title: Forget The Playoffs: Can The Ravens Achieve These 5 Lesser Goals In Final 8 Games?
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are one of the more deficient football teams in the NFL right now.
They have allowed four more touchdowns than they have scored this season and been outscored by nearly 70 points in the last four games alone. They have almost no ascending players and coaches on either roster. Their first half was a failure and playing the rest of the season without two-time MVP Lamar Jackson, almost certainly the case , is a recipe for disaster (7-15 without him).
This was a rebuilding year all along with a coaching staff that appears to be mightily out of its depth thus far and that’s unlikely to change under the pressure of trying to salvage a season with a QB who was just demoted to third string in Arizona, where they are absolutely rebuilding. As much as everyone in The Castle seems utterly delusional about the state of this franchise and how far removed it is for competing or anything real (even with a healthy Jackson), as evidenced by their abysmal trade deadline , we keep it real in these parts.
So, the standings and postseason are not going to be our guide anymore. We are setting hopes and expectations far below that standard (let alone the Super Bowl talk going around Owings Mills as the AFC’s preseason favorite). Nope, we are more concerned with five far lesser objective for the rest of the season.
Let’s see if this flailing organization can manager to check a few of these boxes:
This can’t be the “Zay And Pray” passing game forever. They sunk the middle of this draft into receivers and tight ends – can one of them have a half-meaningful rookie season? That too much to ask? Can Ja’Kobi Lane or Matthew Hibner or Josh Cuevas show enough in some regular-season NFL football games that make you feel good about their ability to make an impact in 2027?
Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is underwater in many respects, but player development is supposed to be where these young coaches would succeed where John Harbaugh, owner Steve Bisciotti put it, failed (real problem is the GM is pretty awful at his job, but the owner claims he “bats .800” ). Somebody from this group has to show something with Jacoby Brissett slinging it downfield in games that won’t end up meaning much in the standings.
“I can do a better job of putting them in better positions and making sure that they're able to go out and execute,” Doyle said of his players last week. This offense will be cooked next season unless one of these youngsters is legit.
Hamilton is not a playmaker on passing downs in any way shape or form. They don’t need another run stuffer – that’s all they have on this defense. Let’s see him affect he QB before he delivers the ball or after it, being around the football in flight. This was supposed to be the embodiment of Jesse Minter’s next-level defense, and it’s been anything but .
Slamming him into offensive linemen and running backs and hanging out in the blue tent every Sunday feels like a dangerous game to be playing in a lost season. Fashion a role for him that makes more impact, that hopefully can carry into next season.
“If I'm out there, I need to be putting good stuff out there on tape,” Hamilton said after the ugly loss to the Bills in Week 8. “Me, myself personally, I don't think I did that. Doesn't matter the situation I'm in. If I'm out there, I need to be doing my best to get the job done."
Minter talked on Monday about “re-establishing” key tenants on his defense. Sorry, outside of consistently proving to be the worst second-half defense in the NFL and displaying an unrivaled ability to blow any second-half lead at any time, Minter hasn’t established anything here as a coach or coordinator.
He better establish an identity, fast, or get ready to keep fielding more questions about horrendous second-half play calling and lack of adjustments . His secondary stinks and his pass rush is limp and his dime coverages are picked apart by bad QBs and he doesn’t get home when he blitzes … They can stop the run some, but who cares when the middle of the field is always wide open in the passing game.
“A couple days gives you a chance to really look and really dig deep,” Minter said after a weekend off. “I think first and foremost, making sure that the identity that we talk about that we want is not just talk. Sometimes that can get lost as you're racing each week to try to get a game plan in and do things. I'm excited for us to sort of re-establish our identity.”
Good luck with that with this roster.
Could anyone besides linebacker Trenton Simpson make the case for a new contract? Too much to ask? Can’t have a team with only three blue-chip players signed beyond 2027 (Nnamdi Madubuike, Hamilton, Flowers) and no one else you need to pay at the same time. Won’t work.
That would be a sign of a bogus front office.
Simpson should be groomed to replace Roquan Smith, now, and every effort made to pay him, now . Will anyone else – Nate Wiggins, Devontez Walker – be performing at a level that would make you want to do the same by January? I wouldn’t bet on it.
The Ravens have championed their roster for years, and the media carries their water, but it’s not very good with massive room for improvement. Now under .500 by some margin since last Thanksgiving, they get better active on waiver claims.
How about finding a player that way? How about plundering someone who can play a little on another practice squad? How about constantly churning the bottom of the roster the way bad football teams do – this has been a bad football team for quite a while. Living off a false reputation and constantly firing coaches who are scapegoated for poor rosters is one thing; doing almost nothing to help them in-season (outside of ridiculously desperate trades that will only set the entire franchise back just makes it even worse.
“When’s the last time they found a football player on a Tuesday?” offered one longtime NFL personnel exec, noting the workouts to fill roster spots that usually take place that day. “Do they think that’s beneath them too? Like (selling at) the trade deadline?
“There’s never anybody on waivers who is better than their 53? When’s the last time they stole somebody who could play off a practice squad? What do the pro personnel guys do over there?”
They might be fooling the access jockeys in the media, and the people who grade offseasons and drafts. But not their peers around the league and any veteran evaluators really paying attention, who see right through this failing front office.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Are Roquan Smith, Derrick Henry, Mark Andrews Back With Ravens in '27? NFL Contract Expert Predicts
full_text:
The Ravens’ ugly payroll and salary-cap situation is born primarily of their inability to act like a functional NFL front office when it comes to extending the contract of their franchise quarterback.
Lamar Jackson has been forced to take a truly unique negotiating path through roughly a decade in the NFL, and it’s not because he chose to represent himself (something increasingly common place in his locker room and around the NFL). Baltimore is staring at a $75M dead cap on Jackson for 2027, and an $84M cap hit is he plays out the final year on his deal with all those poison pills, with no easy way out.
Our pal Mark Levin, who ran the salary cap and agent administration department for the NFLPA for roughly 25 years (as foremost an expert on NFL contracts and structure and cap and the collective bargain agreement as there is on the planet), was also quite involved in Jackson’s last contract with the Ravens. And he explained why there is every reason to be skeptical about Jackson’s future in Baltimore after this season.
But Levin, who ran the salary cap and was the chief negotiator for the Washington Commanders prior to taking the role with the NFLPA, also spent hours recently pouring over Baltimore’s entire current and future cap situation and studying the critical contracts while trying to find ways to get Baltimore under the 2027 cap (they project $50M over it currently ).
Levin, who took a buyout from the union and now runs Pro Football Consulting assisting agents negotiating deals, knows how general managers and cap gurus and owners think and he has a unique portal into Baltimore’s front office from being on the inside of Jackson’s last deal. He also explained on “The Daily Flock” what he thinks the Ravens will do with a score of other pressing contract matters (Roquan Smith, Ronnie Stanley, Derrick Henry, Mark Andrews, Rashod Bateman).
PSA: Marlon Humphrey isn’t in this exercise because he is a UFA in 2027, but he’ll still count $12M against Baltimore’s cap either way; quite a parting gift).
·       Pre 6/1 (Cut/ Trade): $13M ( Save $20M )  / $13M ( Save $20M )
·       Post 6/1 (Cut/Trade): $13M ( Save $20M) / $32M ( Save $20M )
·       Base Salary: $15M  ($4M bonus due March)
Smith has been in steep decline for years, and Trenton Simpson is the rare player making the case for a contract extension on this roster, who might be the next-man up. Smith is being paid like Fred Warner and he is worth maybe a third of that and has a cap hit $14M higher than anyone else in the NFL at his position. He’ll be 30 with 3000 snaps under his belt come ’27 and mobility and acceleration have become a big issue.
Levin: “They're not gonna pay a player four million and then cut him. They're gonna cut him before they have to pay the four million.”
Prediction : They offer Smith a bargain 2027 contract and he declines becoming a free agent at start of league year.
Suggestion: Now’s the time see what Simpson, Teddye Buchanan and Kyle Hamilton can do on the field together (30 snaps all season thus far).
·       2027 Cap/Dead Cap: $24M / $28M
·       Pre 6/1 (Cut/ Trade): $28M / $28M
·       Post 6/1 (Cut/Trade): $8M ( Save $16M ) / $8M ( Save $16M )
He thought his career might be over years ago and extreme medical concerns led him to come back to Baltimore with no real market in free agency. His play is declining, left tackle is a massive need in the draft and the voidable years have made this a brutal cap bind. But remember, cash is king, owner Steve Biscciotti is paying a team-record $370M for his awful product this year, and shedding that $16M base salary is a big deal.
Levin : “Ronnie Stanley would be somebody that you might be able to absorb that extra $4 million hit (from $24M to $28M) and just cut him right away in March.”
Prediction: I could see them saving the $4M and designating him a post-June 1 cut and letting him test the market early.
Suggestion : Don’t get cute in the draft and wait to draft a successor with this awful OL a constant problem.
·       2027 Cap/Dead Cap: $16M / $15M
·       Pre 6/1 (Cut/ Trade): $15M / $15M
·       Post 6/1 (Cut/Trade): $12M ( Save $4M ) / $12M ( Save $4M)
·       Base Salary: $11M ($1M Bonus Due March)
He will be 33, beyond the end for almost everyone who has ever played his position and he’s being ridden into the ground by rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle this year. Without a quality OL and Lamar Jackson, he doesn’t really fit, but the fact this front office wouldn’t do the obvious thing and deal him at the deadline was telling, too. The fumbles are a growing concern.
Levin: “I would lean probably towards keeping him.
Prediction: The King is back in 2027, even on a rebuilding team.
Suggestion: Find a viable complimentary back worthy of 10-15 touches a game
·       2027 Cap/Dead Cap: $15M / $16M
·       Pre 6/1 (Cut/ Trade): $16M / $11M (Save $4M )
·       Post 6/1 (Cut/Trade): $16M / $11M ( Save $4M )
·       Base Salary: $9M ($5M fully guaranteed)
The decision to take the money Isaiah Likely turned down in negotiations last season – wanting to see what the market would bear (perfectly logical and reasonable by Likely) – is the kind of thing that gets you fired by an engaged owner who is driven to win (this one gaslights fans about a GM he says “bats .800” on his transactions). It was a petty and bratty move in realtime and has come to exemplify how this team operates. Andrews is one of the worst tight ends in the NFL the last two season and he cannot run, jump or catch, but leads the NFL in drop percentage at his position and false starts.
Levin: “They could possibly trade him, but I would think more likely he's probably going to be on their roster next year.”
Prediction: They couldn’t get a 4th round pick for him after 2024, when he was just a marginal TE but not a broken one. No trade, and the $5M guarantee means he’s back. He also will retire without a playoff TD in his career.
Suggestion : Get a new front office.
·       2027 Cap/Dead Cap: $11M / $8M
·       Pre 6/1 (Cut/ Trade): $8M ( Save $3M ) / $8M ( Save $3M )
·       Post 6/1 (Cut/Trade): $3M (Save $8M) / $3M ( Save $8M )
·       Base Salary: $13M Base ($3.5M guar for injury)
One of Eric DeCosta’s all-time favorites and yet another first-round bust who he kept around way too long , who added almost nothing on the field, and absolutely nothing in terms of winning traits in the locker room or on the sidelines. Jackson has his worst passer rating throwing to him and highest interception rate and Bateman doesn’t have 300 receiving yards yet this season.
Levin: “He would be a good candidate for a post-June 1 designation for sure.”
Prediction : He joins Stanley as a post-June 1 guy.
Suggestion : Start benching him to protect that injury guarantee and maybe try getting your fourth-round pick (receiver Elijah Sarratt) active on game day in your lost season.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Report: Ravens Sign Two Kickers Following Loss Of Jake Moody
full_text:
After placing struggling second-year kicker Tyler Loop on injured reserve last week, the only healthy player at the position left on the Baltimore Ravens roster was fourth-year pro Jake Moody until he was signed off their practice squad by the Atlanta Falcons earlier this week.
With Loop out at a minimum of three more games, the front office and player personnel staff had to act fast and bring in reinforcements ahead of their Week 10 primetime matchup with the winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football.
The Ravens brought in a pair of veteran kickers for workouts on Wednesday and are reportedly signing them both. According to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo, they added former Miami Dolphins kicker Riley Patterson to the active 53-man roster that same night, with the intention of having him kick against the Chargers. Per his NFL Network colleague, Ian Rapoport, they are also bringing in former Los Angeles Rams kicker Harrison Mevis to the practice squad.
The #Ravens also signed former #Rams kicker Harrison Mevis to their practice squad, in addition to Riley Patterson to their 53-man roster, per me and @MikeGarafolo . All eyes on the kicking game in practice this week. pic.twitter.com/xnHxGCyiz2
Adding both specialists, who were released by their former teams after dealing with some early-season struggles, likely means that they want them to continue to compete for the job in practice or want to have insurance in case Patterson struggles in his debut.
As far as why one got added to the practice squad and the other to the active roster, the Ravens had multiple spots on the 53, and they might've had more competition for Patterson's services and didn't want to risk losing him in a similar fashion to how they lost Moody.
Patterson spent the first five games and all of last season with the Dolphins but was released on Oct. 20 after struggling to consistently kick touchbacks when instructed. As a result, Miami went with their resident practice squad signee, Zane Gonzalez.
When it came to executing on field goals, Patterson converted 7-of-9 attempts this season (77.7%), and last season, his 93.1% conversion rate was the fourth-highest among all NFL kickers with at least 10 attempts after going 27-of-29 in 17 games.
Mevis had been the Rams' kicker since about midway through last season when he replaced a struggling Joshua Karty. He spent the final nine games of the regular season and all three in the playoffs kicking for the 2025 NFC runner-ups, who came into this year as the presumptive Super Bowl favorites.
Since expectations for the Rams as a team were so high and they played in so many primetime and stand-alone games early in the season, it meant that Mevis' struggles were that much more significant. While he was perfect on all 14 of his extra-point attempts in the first five games, he missed four of his first nine field goal attempts, two of which came in an overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 5, which was the final straw and led to his release.
Both Patterson and Mevis are former undrafted free agents who entered the league in 2021 and 2024, respectively, and have played for or at least signed with three or more teams since then.
The Ravens rightfully caught a lot of flak and public blowback for losing Moody, who drilled his lone field goal attempt and extra point in last week's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . After all, they had ample time to sign him to the 53-man roster and could've even done so as a corresponding move after placing Loop on injured reserve.
However, there is more to the story than just general manager Eric DeCosta fumbling the ball on this one, according to head coach Jesse Minter. (The Ravens could have signed Moody to the active roster at any point, including after Thursday's game, which would have precluded any team from contacting him).
"Moody had a chance to be here," Minter said. "He had a choice to make and went somewhere else, [and I'll] leave it at that."
Instead of continuing to be Loops' stand-in and understudy until he got healthy again, the former third-round pick with Super Bowl experience opted to be the No. 1 choice for a Falcons team that plays five of its final eight games inside stadiums, as opposed to remaining with the Ravens, who only play indoors once in their final eight games.
Kickers prefer to kick in enclosed, climate-controlled environments instead of outside, where weather conditions could vastly impact their ability to perform, especially late in the season as fall fades and winter approaches.
"We feel great about our personnel department and us having a really good kicker available on Monday," Minter said.

title: Jesse Minter's Arrival Was Supposed To Immediately Elevate Kyle Hamilton's Game. It Has Not
full_text:
Of all the many things that the arrival of defensive mastermind Jesse Minter was supposed to signal, the further emergence of hybrid weapon Kyle Hamilton was second to none.
Minter had done wonders to reverse the course of the career of Derwin James (one of the few athletic comps for Hamilton on the planet) with the Chargers and he had the same secret sauce in the secondary as Mike Macdonald, who Hamilton had his best season under in Baltimore, and this was part of the reason the rookie coach was allegedly such a great and unique fit with the Ravens .
Except the thing is, on to way to immediately showing he could blow second-half, double-digit leads with more vigor than even John Harbaugh could, and one the way to tying a franchise low allowing 33 points or more in three straight games and during a four-game losing streak in which someone in The Castle should have relieved Minter of play calling duties for a while so they can find out if he can be a head coach, he’s also managed to bring out the worst in most of his roster .
And he hasn’t come close to bringing out the best in Hamilton, who was supposed to become such a gravitational force that it lifted all those around him.
Hamilton has been fine, he’s been good, he’s anything but a problem on defense that is loaded with major ones at all three levels of the defense. But he hasn’t sniffed taking any major leap in this new scheme, which he called a close “cousin” of Macdonald’s this summer, and he’s part of a secondary that has no abundant playmaking flair whatsoever.
In fact, outside of Trenton Simpson (who this failing front office better be trying to extend , now) no one has taken a major step forward. Corner Nate Wiggins has gone backwards, edge rusher Mike Green has made incremental gains, Malaki Starks doesn’t look like he has any business playing free safety at all. And Hamilton has played good football, but certainly not spectacular football, and most of his work has shown up against the run on early downs … which is about the only part of this defense that isn’t broken.
It’s been anything but a breakout, and while Hamilton deserves kudos for being the voice and conscious of this defense, willing to say what needs to be said in a manner in which Minter has shied away from, they were whispering about a Defensive Player Of The Year type campaign for Hamilton, and it’s been anything but.
“If I'm out there, I need to be putting good stuff out there on tape,” Hamilton said after the ugly loss to the Bills in Week 8. “Me, myself personally, I don't think I did that. Doesn't matter the situation I'm in. If I'm out there, I need to be doing my best to get the job done."
This is an area where he was supposed to take a leap. We explained in detail what Minter did deploy James from the slot and as an extra end and from the A Gap to turn him into a projectile who impacted the quarterback in profound ways. Just has not happened this year, the scheme has been less creative as the season wore on and problems arose at every level, and while the volume of pass rush is there, the impact has been scant.
Hamilton set a career high with 65 pass rush snaps last season; he has 51 this season already without a sack. Signing $60M “alleged closer” Trey Hendrickson was supposed to make it easy for Hamilton to get home from the other side, but that’s been money set on fire to this point and Hendrickson has had zero impact in the fourth quarter all season (they will regret not trying to get out of this contract at the deadline ).
Despite Hendrickson’s all-powerful presence and Minter’s brilliance, Hamilton’s pressure rate is egregiously low (he has just five pressures all season):
2026: 9.8%      2025: 18.5%     2024: 29.3%     2023: 38.9%      2022: 26.7%
It’s yet another area in which ridiculed former defensive coordinator Zach Orr is outshining Minter and yet another reason somebody better rethink Minter wearing all these hats come 2027 if this continues. All the blitzing takes him out of coverage, and the Ravens do not have a corner or safety on the roster who can make a play on the football.
Hamilton is basically used as a linebacker in coverage and he got his sole interception as a linebacker in coverage, when washed back-up quarterback Tua Tagovailoa threw the ball to him in overtime at Atlanta. Hamilton is allowing 77% completions – his highest since his rookie season when he was used far more often deeper downfield in coverage.
The Ravens have been carved up by tight ends in the limited amount teams have thrown to them against Baltimore (that’s often his assignment). Opposing QBs have only attempted 55 passes to tight ends against them (seventh-lowest in NFL), but have a 128.6 rating doing so – 30th in the NFL – and expect to see a lot of more of it moving forward.
Hamilton has just two pass breakups (on par with his average of four per year) and the idea of him being any sort of remote ballhawk 20-plus yards downfield just it not going to happen. I did mention that no one playing safety or corner has a pick for this team through nine games despite facing a legion of terrible QBs, did I not?
On a team that has lost its jam up front and with a $20M middle linebacker who stopped being a true thumper years ago, Hamilton shows up with big hits around the line of scrimmage … But he also has a lean/mean body type, seems to suffer a stinger/shoulder/neck situation every other week and is being used in a high-collision areas more than he probably should in what’s realistically already shaped up as a lost season.
Minter better start rethinking some of this calculus because he is in the blue medical tent way too frequently. Hamilton has played 199 snaps against the run already (338 is his career high), his 13.6% tackle rate is basically his career average, and this team badly needs help on the back end.
"Yeah, it's certainly something that's discussed,” defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said recently about getting Hamilton out of the box more. “I believe Jesse's very calculated in the times that he does pressure him. Most of the time we try to bring him on the edge just for that very reason.
“Occasionally, again in high-leverage situations, he may blitz him up the middle, but it's certainly something that we're cognizant of. If you asked Kyle, he's probably like, 'Stop, just keep sending me and putting me around the ball.' But it's certainly something we're aware of as coaches."
With the defense in triage mode and Minter looking less tuned in and willing to lean into pre-snap subterfuge and mixing coverages, expecting a leap from Hamilton this season seems silly. If it doesn’t happen next year, count it among the reasons this team is going to find out real quickly why so many franchises burn through so many aspiring head coaches who are really just coordinators.
Orr got lit up for far less than this 2026 disaster, without the hype and without $160M invested in the defensive roster.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Winners and Losers After Trade Deadline: Underachieving Veterans Stay Empowered
full_text:
The Ravens had a unique opportunity to reset their roster and reposition for the future amid a second straight embarrassing season. They categorically abstained.
There will be ramifications. There always are.
The longer the franchise clings to tropes like “Play Like A Raven,” and mythologize any recent accomplishments, the worse it will get for many involved. They do themselves and, especially, those who spend their money to support this product, no favors by pretending they are something they clearly are not. And they will continue to get humbled and torn down while playing without Lamar Jackson for the rest of the season (trust us and the cap guru who helped Jackson negotiate his last deal). Instead of clearing a path for youngsters  to take over and accept that rookie head coach Jesse Minter and his novice staff have a steep learning curve before anyone sniffs a Lombardi Trophy, they are selling a parable (through words and deeds) that the tanking Cardinals third-string QB is going to save this season.
Instead of loading up on draft picks, they gave them away in droves at an alarming and desperate rate, and the Cam Jurgens deal in October (that’s as much a deadline-deal as any) threatens to haunt them for years to come . And so general manager Eric DeCosta, with a fairly dreadful drafting record, will have fewer opportunities than usual to throw darts at draft picks, and we’ll see if owner Steve Bisciotti is willing to gush again about his GM “batting .800” in his transactions after back-to-back stupefying seasons.
Fans : They really do take you for fools, both pro sports teams in this team. They think you are too simple to see the truth for yourself and believe they can obfuscate with sleight of hand and empty rhetoric. The franchise is in steep and steady decline, they can’t even figure out how to add a kicker to their 53-man roster the right way , they can’t win at home, and they are the NFL’s unmitigated premier choking dogs since DeCosta took over in 2019 no matter who the coaches and coordinators are.
Minter: The front office could have helped empower him and amplify his (quite muted to this point) voice by kicking some of the gross under-achievers out at the deadline and making it easier him to bench others. They could have let the fanbase know that they accept this mess for what it is and stop scapegoating coaches and hanging them out to dry , and started going young for the future. Was a good time to alter expectations that this is some kind of a franchise anywhere close to a Super Bowl – you know startup coaching staff, with more startup starters. But that would take humility and maturity and dignity from a front office.
Derrick Henry/Calais Campbell: Even if they wanted to stick around here to be a part of the rest of this lost season, they will regret that over time. This could be the end for both of them, and they both should be first-ballot Hall of Famers. Being 32 for a RB and 40 for a DL is unreal, neither has a chance to win or standout much individually the rest of this season and Henry, in particular, could carry such a physical toll (he was leading the NFL in carries after playing Week 9) it wrecks whatever might have been left for 2027 . Would be amazing to see them get a shot at playoff glory, but that ain’t happening in Baltimore.
Tyler Loop: The Falcons were not the only team sniffing around former Ravens kicker Jake Moody, as we hear it and they didn’t just immediately take a shine to him. Too gross negligence for the Ravens to lose him, and there is a decent chance Moody kicks quite well for rebuilding Falcons with no pressure and in a dome … Injury to Loop or not, his performance was about to get him benched for Moody, and if Moody had done the job, Loop wasn’t coming off IR. Now the youngster, who clearly has not been the same since missing the kick in Week 18 to knock the Ravens out of the playoffs, gets another chance to maybe send a positive message before the offseason.
Over-entitled veterans : Send a message to Marlon Humphrey and eat some of his contract to send him someplace he wouldn’t want to be? Nah. Clear a path for Trenton Simpson – the only youngster on the entire roster really making a case for a contract extension – by doing something with aged Roquan Smith? Nope. Minter couldn’t even come out and criticize them by name this week with the media (saves that for Loop only, apparently). Expect them to continue to keep these overmatched coaches under their heels.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Grading The Ravens Trade Deadline: F For Failing To Accept Who They Are
full_text:
The Ravens do a great job of marketing their past and keeping former legends close to the front office and boasting about their accomplishments.
There is a sentimentality and hubris that has been woven into their roster decisions for years now – like not realizing after his third season in the NFL that Lamar Jackson meant more to their success and their roster well-being than any player meant to any team in the league, and immediately paying him that way the moment they could . It was implied in them bucking what anyone in the industry would have said about extending rapidly-descending tight end Mark Andrews a year ago or paying $19.3M to bring bottom five starting corner Marlon Humphrey back at that price in 2026.
General manager Eric DeCosta continually gets the media to tell you how great his rosters are and how powerful of a Super Bowl contender this is … but they have one meaningful playoff run since he took over for icon Ozzie Newsome in 2019, and they are bottoming out under his hand-picked rookie head coach and novice staff . They're already doing things no Ravens team has ever done before (failing to score 14 points in four straight games) and only one Ravens team has done before (allow 33 points or more in three straight; DeCosta’s horrid 2025 defense did that as well).
Meantime, the coaches they kicked out of the building, like John Harbaugh (Giants) and Todd Monken (Browns) are shattering expectations right away. The Ravens had three quarterbacks suffer injuries in the equivalent of one quarter of football in Buffalo two weeks ago, and overmatched head coach Jesse Minter is being asked about divesting himself of defensive play-calling duties nine games into his career.
The Ravens are far more likely to be picking in the top 10 the next two years than they are to flirting with anything close to a home playoff game, they have at best the second-worst overpriced payroll in the NFL (to Dallas) and the worst cap situation in the NFL now and moving forward . Given all of that, finding a way to lose their starting kicker (Jake Moody) through a totally unforced error , and making a second straight bizarre trade for a starting center after getting utterly fleeced by the Eagles for Cam Jurgens just a month ago, is a total failure at the trade deadline.
The Ravens won’t start turning things around until they acknowledge that they are a failing front office; when owner Steve Bisciotti starts to hold personnel guys accountable in ways he always did his coaches, instead of throwing out ridiculous platitudes about DeCosta “batting .800.” They have been getting called out around the league since pulling out of the Maxx Crosby trade in March, and we were reporting even before the deadline what would happen.
But they seem to always get a pass in Owings Mills, where it really matters (or on the yacht in Florida).
There were numerous football trades that could have been made if the Ravens got real and started marketing Derrick Henry and Ronnie Stanley and Rashod Bateman and Calais Campbell to others. Instead, they traded basically a fourth-round pick for the rebuilding Cardinals third-string QB (Jacoby Brissett), a potential top 40 pick for a concussed offensive lineman the Eagles were going to bench, and added starting center from the Falcons (Ryan Neuzil) who is probably a back-up here who they should have landed in the spring given all their machinations at center.
“There were trades they could have made, but they were never going to make them,” one GM told me. “DeCosta would never sell.”
Indeed, the NFL believed the Ravens would think starting to reposition for the future and shedding players – most have no future here anyway – was beneath them. It’s what losing franchises do.
But that’s exactly what this is – in steep decline since losing to the Chiefs in the 2023 playoffs, churning through coaches and coordinators like bad teams do, and 6-9 since last Thanksgiving like bad teams are. They are headed for a second-straight losing season, and are 3-9 in their last 12 at home and 3-7 in their last 10 against winning teams.
All the pretending isn’t fooling anyone.
And it’s not serving the fans, or the few young blue-chip players on this roster who might still be here whenever this franchise does remotely resemble a real contender again.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Jesse Minter Shares Expectations For Jacoby Brissett As Ravens Stop-Gap Starter
full_text:
Whether it's until Lamar Jackson is healthy enough and willing to return to action or for the remainder of the 2026 season, Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter made it clear that the recently acquired veteran Jacoby Brissett will be the team's starter moving forward.
After a month of watching his offense struggle and fail to score 14 points during their four-game losing streak, he believes the 11th-year veteran can reignite what was one of the most explosive units to open the 2026 season before injuries began to ravage the roster at the most important position.
"He's played for a bunch of different teams, been in a bunch of different systems. I think he'll operate our offense at a level required to be successful," Minter said. "He'll get the ball out on time. He'll be able to run the whole thing. He'll be a leader. He'll hold guys accountable. I'm just excited about the addition, the chance that gives us to kind of spark this thing."
This marks the second time in Brissett's career that he's been traded and the first in nearly a decade since he was shipped off to the Indianapolis Colts from the New England Patriots. Fortunately for him, his wealth of experience, with 73 career starts under his belt, and familiarity with Ravens quarterback coach Israel Woolfork, whom he worked with last year in Arizona, his acclimation process should be smooth.
"I expect him to hit the ground running," Minter said. "We'll pick up kind of an extra day with the guys (Tuesday), begin kind of a normal week of practice on Wednesday to get a day ahead [and] pick up an extra day later in the week. I think, especially with us playing on Monday, for his circumstance it's good to allow him as much time as possible."
While his new teammates had the weekend off, Brissett was around the Under Armour Performance Center getting up to speed with the new playbook and getting used to his new surroundings.
"We're really excited about the addition, and he's just a very mature pro that I think will bring a leadership style to our offense from the quarterback position," Minter said.
Unlike the other two quarterbacks whom the Ravens trotted out or were forced to play in place of their two-time MVP regular starter, Brissett gives them the ability to push the ball down the field and open up the passing game more. This will also aid in the improvement of the running game since opposing defenses won't be able to load the box nearly as much for fear of giving up big plays through the air.
Fully expect a return to form for some of the Ravens' biggest stars on the offensive side of the ball and the potential emergence of promising young talent with Brissett. The two most prominent are two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers, who totaled just six receiving yards in his last two games after averaging just over 101 yards in his first six, and five-time Pro Bowl running back Derrick Henry, who's been held to under 100 rushing yards in four straight games.
After losing both Jackson and primary backup Tyler Huntley in the first half of their Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills, before they traded for Brissett, the Ravens had no other choice but to have undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finish that game and make his first career start on a short week.
Going up against one of the best teams not only in the conference but in the entire league, the Jacksonville Jaguars, in primetime, the first-year signal caller had the odds stacked against him and an injured ankle but didn't blink or back down in a 33-10 drubbing at home , which resonated with his coaches and teammates alike,
"That guy earned a lot of respect in the locker room for going out there on Thursday night and dealing with what he was dealing with physically and playing and gutting through it and giving us everything that he had," Minter said.
Fagnano went 10-of-18 for 60 passing yards, threw two interceptions and no touchdowns, with a passer rating of 22.7. One of the additional benefits of adding such a seasoned veteran like Brissett to the position group is that the rookie can watch and soak up as much knowledge as he can about what it takes to become considered one of the best backups, stop-gap starters and possible bridge quarterbacks in he league.
"He's well aware of how we feel about him. I think he gets a chance now, again, as another guy that can honestly benefit from a guy like Jacoby coming in," Minter said. "This is the type of role that he could have for a long time if he takes this opportunity and really learns from it."

title: Ravens Week 9 Rookie Report: Vega Ioane Returns From Injury, Joe Fagnano Struggles
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in last Thursday's 33-10 road loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9 . They are in an AFC North division in which every other team has a record above .500, and after falling to 4-5, they deservedly sit at the bottom of the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. The only rookie who was a healthy scratch was fourth-round wide receiver Elijah Sarratt, while fifth-round running back Adam Randall wasn't activated from short-term injured reserve in his fifth week of eligibility. Seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
The first-round interior offensive lineman made his return to the lineup much sooner than expected after only missing one game with an MCL sprain. Ioane played all 56 of the Ravens' snaps on offense and didn't look hobbled when executing his blocking assignments on runs, screens and in pass protection.
Good work on the frontside. Just a tough reach for Vega Ioane to get playside shoulder of the 0T. Not sure who it is, but he tilts his body and gets his playside shoulder into the gap that makes overtaking damn near impossible. Still a solid run pic.twitter.com/5NwMH5rjgt
The second-rounder saw a reduction in his playing time on defense, with his 22 snaps in that phase of the game being the third lowest of the season. While Young didn't fill up or even log a stat in the box score, his underrated grunt work as a stalwart run defender didn't go unnoticed as he played a key role in limiting the Jaguars' rushing attack to a season-low 77 yards.
Despite playing nearly 60% of the Ravens' total offensive snaps with 32, the third-rounder didn't get any chances to make plays in the passing game, as it marked his first game without being targeted. Lane didn't play on special teams at all and was called for a false start once. The scope of the passing game was quite limited, overall.
The fourth-rounder was back to playing near his average number of offensive snaps for the season, with 30, and recorded his first reception since Week 4, before he sustained a hand injury. Hibner reeled in the first of his two targets for a five-yard gain and first down on the Ravens' second drive of the game. His second target came on what would've been the Ravens' biggest play through the air of the game on a trick play, but he wasn't able to corral the pass after it got tipped on its way to him.
With starting outside corner Nate Wiggins inactive with an illness , the fifth-rounder dressed for the game after being a healthy scratch last week, but didn't log any playing time on defense in his third straight appearance. Rivers was only on the field for a single snap on special teams and made it count by recording his second assisted tackle of the season on the last kickoff of the game in the fourth quarter.
The fifth-rounder played his fewest offensive snaps since Week 2 for the third week in a row with just nine, and he had his four-game streak of recording at least one target and one reception snapped. While he didn't log either, Cuevas saw the field for nine snaps on special teams, tied for the second-most of his career.
The sixth-round specialist had another strong outing with five punts for 241 yards, with an average of 48.2 yards per punt and a long of 55. Eckley had one touchback and was able to pin the Jaguars back inside their own 20-yard line three times, with the deepest being at the opposing three-yard line on his very first boot.
The undrafted free agent went from being thrust into his first regular-season action off the bench in Week 8 after both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley went down with injuries in the first half to making his first career start on a short week. As if the odds weren't already stacked against him, he was dealing with an ankle injury of his own, inclement weather, and the Ravens' offensive line struggled to run the ball or hold up in pass protection long enough for him to regularly get through his progressions in obvious passing situations. Fagnano went 10-of-18 for 60 passing yards, no touchdowns, two interceptions and a passer rating of 22.7. Despite being hobbled, he was able to pick up a pair of first downs with his legs, with one coming on a surprise zone read and the other on a nine-yard scramble where he made a defender miss in space.
Fagnano takes it himself and the family was loving it ❤️ JAXvsBAL on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3DX2OXT7JT
The undrafted free agent saw a slight reduction in playing time from last week but still saw the field for the second-most defensive snaps of the season with 25, which accounted for a season-high 44.6% of the team's total. His 23 snaps on special teams ranked first among all rookies and were the third-most on the team. Burke was very impressive as an edge setter against the run, where he consistently stacked and shed blockers on his way to recording three total tackles, including a pair of solos.

title: The Expert Who Helped Lamar Jackson Negotiate His Last Ravens Contract Believes End Could Be Near
full_text:
Almost no one was privy to the inner-workings of the Ravens’ long-and-arduous contract negotiations with Lamar Jackson, dating back to 2020, with an MVP already to his name, once eligible for his first contract extension.
General manager Eric DeCosta, now having quite a miserable time building a sustained winner, led the charge on a process that would take years to complete and was unlike any other first-time QB extension for a superstar in NFL history. It would include a non-exclusive franchise tag and trade demand and collusion case along the way. DeCosta was aided by cap chief Nick Matteo – who has authored some of the ugliest contract structures in the NFL in recent years ( hence the worst cap situation in the NFL ) and team president Sashi Brown, once he took over for legendary steward Dick Cass after he retired.
As for the other side of the table, it was and still is just Lamar Jackson and his mom.
No agent. No marketing guru. No other voice.
And Jackson was seeking counsel from DeMaurice Smith, head of the NFLPA at the time, and Mark Levin, who for roughly 25 years oversaw the Salary Cap and Agent Administration department of the union, in charge of regulating agents and helping them negotiate deals and serving as the PA’s foremost expert on the Collective Bargaining Agreement that governs economic engagement between labor and management.
Levin was Team Jackson’s de-facto agent in the process and a beacon available to them to discuss comparable contracts around the league and structures and guarantees and intricate language. He was available on the other end of the Zoom when they wanted to mull no-trade clauses and no-franchise tag clauses (both of which they successfully obtained) and when they got an $84M poison pill cap charge for 2027 (with a $75M dead cap) that effectively makes Jackson a free-agent after the 2026 season.
Levin was as plugged in on cap and contract matters are anyone on the planet for a generation, and even after retiring from the NFLPA last year, top agents seek his counsel regularly and he assists many more formally as head of Pro Football Consulting. Before taking over the salary cap department at the NFLPA, he oversaw the salary cap and contract negotiations for the Washington Commanders and understands these matters from all perspectives.
He’s continued to follow Jackson’s ongoing saga with the Ravens closely , and their inability to make even a modicum of headway on getting him extended to a new deal back in March of 2025, when it was imperative on the heels of Josh Allen’s extension in Buffalo. Levin predicted basically everything that was to come this summer and fall when he joined me on “The Daily Flock Show” in May to analyze Jackson’s stalemate with the Ravens.
So, with Jackson injured again and the Ravens noncompetitive without him, with a bloated roster that should have been purged before the trade deadline and one of the worst offensive lines and some of the least-proven overall offensive talent in the NFL looking forward, Levin has a strong feeling about what’s next between this two-time MVP, and the Ravens.
Levin knows these individuals quite well and how they operate and was inside these talks and how personal it got at times, unlike almost anyone else on the planet. Like other experts who have discussed this matter with us, it seems obvious to Levin that Jackson will command $70M a season or more, with massive guarantees (even despite his injuries; didn’t impede Dak Prescott, for instance), and Jackson can and will call his own shot in regard to where he plays.
“I would be surprised if he's on the team next year,” Levin told me on “The Daily Flock” this week. “I'd be surprised … Unless the Ravens change their course and agree to make him the highest paid or the second highest paid quarterback on a on a legit structure, legit deal - not with a lot of fluff and window dressing - I just don't see him on the roster next year.
“I think they're just going to have to, you know, for the Ravens’ sake, hopefully trade him and get some good compensation for him, as opposed to just outright cutting him and not getting anything. But I just don't see him on the roster this year. And I think that, based on what's happened this year, you know, it might be time for the Ravens fans to buckle up … and look at a rebuild. They're in a bit of a pickle.”
I’d put Levin’s assessment of the situation up against anyone’s.
Jackson has simply smiled and check-mated the Ravens all along, DeCosta reverted to a trite talking point about being “optimistic” about signing Jackson before the season even as the QB spurned him again, and if the Ravens haven’t paid him what it would take to secure his services by now, it’s beyond fair to suspect they might never again.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: America Shows Up for Josh Allen-led Bills in Primetime, Four More Chances Await
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are a legitimate Super Bowl contender with arguably the NFL's best player as their quarterback.
As a result, the Bills (7-1) are appointment television for football fans across America . With that in mind, the schedule-makers placed Buffalo and five-time NFL MVP finalist Josh Allen in the maximum number of primetime windows this season.
Through the season's first nine weeks, which included a bye, the Bills have enjoyed three primetime exposures. Buffalo went 3-0 in those games, all three of which were against NFC opponents.
"Are the Bills going to be one of the teams that are at or near the max in terms of prime time games and national television appearances? Yeah, as long as that guy is your quarterback. Yeah," said NFL VP for broadcast planning Mike North this past April on the It's Always Gameday In Buffalo podcast.
The Bills delivered for the NFL and ESPN in Week 9, attracting a record number of viewers for this point in the season. Per ESPN PR, the Bills' road victory over the Minnesota Vikings totaled 21.7 million viewers across all platforms.
Since ESPN took ownership of the Monday Night Football franchise in 2006, the November 9 broadcast accounted for the most-watched Week 9 game ever over a 21-game sample.
It was the Bills' second Monday night exposure this season. Buffalo posted a 37-34 overtime victory over the Rams in Los Angeles on October 12. That game attracted 19.8 million viewers, and it's worth noting no Week 5 primetime game managed to crack the 20 million mark this season.
The Bills' home opener, which kicked off Prime Video's Thursday Night Football package in Week 2, pulled in 18.6 million viewers - a monster number for a premium streaming service. It was higher than the 15.33 million viewers Prime averaged per game during the 2025 season.
The Bills will take center stage four more times over the season's final nine weeks, including featured games on Thanksgiving night and Christmas Day.
The Bills will host the Kansas City Chiefs in November 26 for an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff carried live by NBC.
Then, it'll be three consecutive standalone exposures in Weeks 14, 15 and 16.
Buffalo visits the Green Bay Packers for Sunday Night Football on December 13. Six days later, the Bills host the Chicago Bears in a Saturday night window. Capping the three-game stretch, the Bills travel to the Denver Broncos for a Christmas special on Netflix .

title: How Bills' Defensive Upgrade Made Jim Leonhard One of Four NFL Trade Deadline Winners
full_text:
It's arguably the perfect addition, at the perfect position, for his defense.
As Buffalo Bills ' defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard fine tunes his unit for the stretch run, the former NFL safety received a new piece to work with prior to this past Tuesday's trade deadline.
The Bills pried veteran safety Amani Hooker away from the Tennessee Titans, and Leonhard is being viewed as the top beneficiary in the equation.
Sports Illustrated senior writer Conor Orr named post-deadline winners and losers , and Leonhard was included amongst the former. The Bills' defensive coordinator was one of four winners named. Orr also called out five losers, including Dallas Cowboys' owner Jerry Jones.
Orr, admittedly, has been a fan of the Leonhard hire from the start.
"I’ll admit that I can become overly excited about a new position coach turned coordinator and develop a massive blind spot. But I think there is so much more ahead for Leonhard and the Bills defense—a process that has been accelerated with the acquisition of safety Amani Hooker," said Orr.
While Buffalo's defense started slow, getting shredded through the air over the first six weeks, there are reasons for optimism . Albeit against lesser quarterbacks, the Bills feasted in Weeks 8 and 9. There's a belief that they're talented enough for Leonhard's scheme.
"The Bills generate quarterback pressure on slightly more than 40% of opposing quarterback dropbacks, which is significant especially when you consider the Vikings’ pressure rate currently sits at 48.2. It’s not that big of a difference—the next-highest team, the Jaguars, is at 44%—and shows Buffalo has the horses," said Orr. "There is now top-tier talent at every level of this defense, and Leonhard won’t have to do as much piecing together in the post-C.J. Gardner-Johnson/get-the-most-out-of-Damar-Hamlin era."
Over his first seven-plus seasons with the Titans, Hooker showed plenty of versatility in the secondary. He'll likely fit more of a free safety role for the Bills, but he has the ability to move into the box, if needed.
"Hooker is a pure ball hawk who can take advantage of one of the league’s highest pressure rates and turn bad throws into costly turnovers," said Orr.
The 28-year-old Hooker leads the NFL in interceptions (5) thus far this season. He picked off Cincinnati Bengals' quarterback thrice in Week 8.
"I've been a big fan of his game for a long time. Obviously, it goes back to watching him in the Big Ten [Conference], being rivals there, and then just watching how he's progressed throughout his career in the NFL. I've always felt like he's a complete safety," said Leonhard, who spent six years at Wisconsin.
It's clear that Leonhard already knows how he wants to maximize Hooker's impact in the secondary.
"He can play in space, he can play down by the box, he covers, he tackles, you know, he finds a football. So I've been a fan of his for a long time. I think he makes his defense better," said Leonhard.
NFL writer Doug Farrar went as far as suggesting Hooker's arrival has the potential to get the Bills over the hump in the AFC.
"If we’re crediting this trade as the reason the Bills got to the Super Bowl, I won’t be at all surprised," said Farrar in a X post .
Only time will tell, but it looks like Hooker is just what the doctor ordered for Leonhard and the Bills' defense.

title: How Unlikely Meeting Turned Tide for Bills' GM Brandon Beane in Titans' Amani Hooker Trade
full_text:
Unless someone has been living under a rock for the better part of the last month, the recent move by the Buffalo Bills to acquire Tennessee Titans’ safety Amani Hooker prior to the NFL’s trade deadline should’ve come as no surprise.
The majority of Bills Mafia has been clamoring for some type of transaction to be made by Bills’ general manager Brandon Beane prior to the trade deadline on November 10 for quite some time, specifically on the defensive side of the ball.
And, although it nearly came down to the wire on Tuesday afternoon, Beane also recognized the need to acquire some reinforcements for Jim Leonhard’s unit.
So, he ultimately obliged to the pleas for help from the fanbase by sending a 2027 second-round pick to the struggling Titans, a team in contention for the No. 1 overall pick in the draft next spring, in exchange for the aforementioned Hooker and a fifth-round pick.
Applauded by fans, as well as some outside observers , the move appears to be exactly what the current leader in the AFC needs to make a push toward capturing the No. 1 seed later on in January . . . which should hopefully help first-year head coach Joe Brady’s squad reach Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium in February.
What makes the move even more impressive?
Well, not only is Hooker tied for the league lead in interceptions heading into Week 10, but his addition comes on the heels of back-to-back historic performances from the Bills’ defense during the team’s last two victories over the Baltimore Ravens and Minnesota Vikings, which Bills ON SI promptly covered earlier in the week .
With that said, the thought of what’s to come in Western New York is incredibly intriguing, especially with the way that quarterback Josh Allen is orchestrating the offense right now.
But, keeping that in mind, what if the deal between the Bills and Titans never came to fruition?
Apparently, that was almost the case according to Tennessee’s general manager Mike Borgonzi, who divulged the information to reporters on the day after the move.
In the end, persistence paid off for Beane.
#Titans GM Mike Borgonzi said he’d turned away #Bills GM Brandon Beane on Amani Hooker for a week. Saw him at the Notre Dame-Miami game, said to stay in touch and then the deal came together yesterday. pic.twitter.com/dxQGg0B1KB
“We made a difficult decision to move Amani [Hooker]. . . . We weren’t looking to move ‘Hook’. We had some calls on him. You know, Brandon Beane from Buffalo had called me, really, the last week on it. I said, ‘No’, at the time,” Titans’ general manager Mike Borgonzi said on Wednesday .
“Ran into him at the Notre Dame-Miami game [on November 7] the other night, said he’d stay in touch, and it came together pretty fast. He called me, probably, around 11:30 in the morning [on Tuesday] . . . and he just came up with an offer.
“We went back-and-forth, and we felt like it was the best decision really, at the time, to—much like Jeff [Simmons]—really accumulate draft capital to accelerate the process here. . . . It’s hard moving on from two really good players that have been here a long time, and I want to thank Amani, though.”
Keeping that in mind, Bills’ fans likely want to thank Borgonzi, as well.
Buffalo’s defense had been reeling in more ways than one before the calendar flipped to November, particularly in the secondary.
Releasing fellow veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, although necessary , didn’t make the outlook any less bleak, either.
So, as Buffalo quickly approaches the toughest part of its 2026 schedule in just a few short weeks, it’s imperative to get Hooker up to speed with his teammates and on the field for Jim Leonhard’s defensive unit as quickly as possible . . . maybe even as soon as this weekend versus the New York Jets ?
Time will tell, but that’s the plan according to the newest playmaking safety in Orchard Park.
“It’s amazing. That’s all, really, I can say because, I mean, I’ve been on a team that hasn’t been winning. So, I’m obviously very grateful for the Titans and what they did for me, but in the past we haven’t been winning.
“And, to be on a team that’s putting up points with a quarterback and offensive guys that are [great]—they’re on fire—and a great defense, like, I’m just excited to be here,” Bills’ 28-year-old veteran defensive back Amani Hooker said at One Bills Drive on Wednesday .
“I [will] play on Sunday. Yeah. I’ll be ready to go.”
Kickoff between the Bills and Jets is slated for 1:00 p.m. ET on Sunday at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

title: Who Is Former Syracuse QB That Bills Will Face When Dolphins Visit Orchard Park?
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills own the Miami Dolphins, having won 14 of 17 games against them in the Josh Allen era. Miami has started four quarterbacks over that span, and that will change to five come November 22, but it won't be the one Buffalo expected.
Malik Willis, who signed a two-year deal with the Dolphins in free agency, was placed on injured reserve on Tuesday with a groin injury, leading them to turn to a QB who some Bills fans who also follow the Syracuse Orange in upstate New York may know well.
That man is Kyle McCord, a sixth-round pick of the Philadelphia Eagles in 2025 who has yet to take a regular-season NFL snap. However, his pedigree offers talking points that could provide a surprising test for a Bills secondary that just added safety Amani Hooker at the trade deadline.
Kyle McCord #Syracuse Opposite-hash back-shoulder target off a seven-step drop with PA component and pressure up the middle. #NFLdraft pic.twitter.com/lRpJWyWWjN
Before being drafted by his hometown Eagles, McCord was rated a five-star recruit by Rivals (No. 5 QB, No. 25 overall) out of St. Joseph's Prep in Philadelphia in the 2021 class, which includes NFL stars like Caleb Williams and Drake Maye and 2025 Bills draftees Jordan Hancock and Landon Jackson.
McCord began his collegiate career at Ohio State, sitting behind C.J. Stroud for two seasons before taking the reins in 2023. That year, he threw 24 touchdowns to six interceptions, helping lead the Buckeyes to a Cotton Bowl appearance.
McCord did not play in that game, though, as he entered the transfer portal and signed with Syracuse. In 2024, he led the FBS with 4,779 passing yards , throwing 34 TDs to 12 picks and leading the Orange to a 10-3 record, including a Holiday Bowl victory over Washington State, before entering the draft.
Kyle McCord threads the needle to Will Sheppard 🪡 GBvsDEN on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MwIrm3X9la
As McCord entered the NFL , scouts noted his quick release, accuracy and pocket presence, while adding that he struggled with decision-making and had limited mobility.
McCord went 24 of 56 for 192 yards, a touchdown and a pair of interceptions in three preseason games in 2025, but he erupted in the 2026 preseason, going 46 of 70 for 440 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions with the Green Bay Packers.
Following the 2026 preseason, Green Bay shipped McCord to the Dolphins for a 2028 sixth-round pick, and he will make his first start on Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts before going to Buffalo.
In Week 10 of 2025, running back De'Von Achane ran for a season-high 174 yards against Buffalo on 22 carries, including a 59-yard touchdown. He also led Miami with 67 catches, notching 488 yards and four touchdowns in the process. However, his season was cut short three games in.
Achane tore his ACL in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs, meaning McCord will be hard-pressed to find a consistent target to throw to against a Bills defense that has improved greatly in its last two games.
Right now, Caleb Douglas, a third-round rookie out of Texas Tech, is Miami's top receiver. He leads Miami with 15.6 yards per reception, with 19 receptions for 296 yards and two touchdowns despite missing three games with an ankle injury.
Elsewhere, Malik Washington leads Miami with 33 catches and 350 yards, while tight end Greg Dulcich and fellow rookies Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr. are Miami's other main options.
McCord may be well-received by the Buffalo faifthful, but the Bills' defense will make sure his first trip to Western New York is anything but that.

title: Bills 'Trade That Should Have Happened' Would've Welcomed Khalil Mack Back to Buffalo
full_text:
It almost made too much sense for both sides, and it would have been a homecoming of sorts for the player.
As to why it never materialized, only general managers Brandon Beane and Joe Hortiz know.
The Buffalo Bills , who rank 24th overall in sack rate (5.67%), could have beefed up their pass rush for the stretch run by trading for Los Angeles Chargers' veteran Khalil Mack .
For some reason, the winless Chargers decided to hold on to the 35-year-old Mack , who played collegiately for the University at Buffalo prior to being drafted at No. 5 overall in 2014.
In his 13th season, Mack remains a starter. The nine-time Pro Bowl selection has 3.0 sacks through eight games, which is more than Bills' free agent addition Bradley Chubb can say at this point in the season.
After the deadline passed, Sports Illustrated identified "five trades that should have happened, but didn't, at the deadline," and one of them was " Khalil Mack to the Bills ."
From a Chargers' perspective, Mack was seemingly the ideal player to trade away for draft capital. The season is officially lost, and Los Angeles gets nothing by letting the aging Mack walk in free agency.
"Their [the Chargers'] most enticing trade chip was Khalil Mack, who is on just a one-year deal and is still producing at a high level in his age-35 season—as evidenced by his 22 tackles, five tackles for loss and three sacks to begin the year," said writer Mike Kadlick, who named Buffalo a sensible landing spot for Mack last month..
Furthermore, presuming the Chargers were willing at some point, it would have been a feasible move for the Bills to make.
With Mack playing on a one-year contract reportedly worth $18 million, the Bills could have found a way to tensing salary cap compliant, especially considering they just freed up an additional $5.3 million in space by performing a salary conversion with Dion Dawkins. As for trade capital , the Bills have three mid-round picks in the upcoming draft with an additional fourth-round compensatory selection likely.
"An intriguing landing spot for Mack would have been the Bills. Through nine weeks, Buffalo’s defense has logged the 11th-lowest pressure rate at 34.1% and the 11th-fewest sacks with 17. Adding Mack to a room alongside the lines of Greg Rousseau and Bradley Chubb would only help the Bills improve upon those numbers in their quest for the franchise’s first Super Bowl title," said Kadlick.
It's worth noting that Mack's 3.0 sacks this season are more than every Bills' edge rusher besides Greg Rousseau.

title: Bills' Injury Report (Jets Week): Four OL Starters Listed, Christian Benford Added
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills listed two new additions on their first Week 10 injury report.
Furthermore, two carryovers remain on the list, but with new injuries.
Coming out of Monday night's road victory , as expected, starting cornerback Christian Benford appeared on Wednesday's practice report. Benford jammed his wrist while tackling Minnesota Vikings' wide receiver Justin Jefferson. He left, returned and left again during the 23-6 win.
Meanwhile, starting center Connor McGovern, somewhat surprisingly, popped up amongst the injured with a neck problem as the Bills began preparations for their November 15 road game against the New York Jets by holding a walkthrough.
McGovern's addition means four of Buffalo's five starting offensive linemen are dealing with injuries in Week 10. Left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson were unavailable for the November 9 primetime affair .
Appearing to finally move past issues that bothered them over the past few weeks, right tackle Spencer Brown and tight end Dalton Kincaid suffered new injuries on Monday night . Brown was dealing with a back problem while Kincaid fought through a chest issue. Now, both are nursing ankle injuries.
"That was a physical game on Monday night and we kinda knew that [would be the case]," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady on Wednesday in Orchard Park. "Right now it's really like, we're two days out of the game so we're walking today at practice. We're gonna have to kinda get a feel of where everybody is, and I'll have a better answer for you guys come Friday."
The good news is that Benford, McGovern, Brown, Kincaid, Dawkins and Anderson all managed to earn a limited designation on Wednesday. Practice status is only estimated, however, being that the Bills held a walkthrough.
Brown apparently sprained his ankle while blocking for James Cook on the Bills' second possession against the Vikings. He didn't leave the game until the final three kneel-downs by Kyle Allen.
"I'm just playing football right now. It's a tough sport. That's why I play it. That's why I love to play it. I look forward to next week and getting back out there again," said Brown postgame.
Kincaid ankle was twisted up as he went to the ground while blocking for DJ Moore on a wide receiver screen play down the sideline. After being taped up, the tight end returned to make a key third-down catch later during the drive.
Benford was forced out of the game late in the second quarter, going to the locker room for X-rays and subsequently being cleared to return. He was on the field to start the second half, but the Bills eventually pulled him before the night was through.
Neither wide receiver's name appears on the Week 10 injury report. It's a highly encouraging development considering both wore red non-contact jerseys during practice last week.
For Moore, it marks his long-awaited return to full strength following a Week 2 shoulder injury . He missed back-to-back games going into Buffalo's Week 7 bye. The 29-year-old wide receiver was back in the lineup against the Ravens on November 1.
Coleman landed on the injury report following the Week 8 win with a shoulder. He was limited in practice every day leading up to the Monday Night Football affair, but did not carry a designation on the final injury report. Against the Vikings, Coleman led all Bills' wide receivers in snaps .

title: How Team-First Dion Dawkins Made Bills' Trade for Amani Hooker Possible
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills were seeking help on the defensive side of the ball, and they needed an offensive tackle to help make it happen.
The Bills traded for Tennessee Titans' safety Amani Hooker prior to Tuesday's NFL deadline, but there was one minor issue that needed resolution before the deal became official. Buffalo needed $4.4 million in available salary cap space to accommodate the addition.
Per Spotrac, the Bills opened the day with only $3.8 million in room against the spending limit. That's where starting left tackle Dion Dawkins entered the equation.
Buffalo requested a salary conversion for Dawkins as a means of creating cap space. Per Spotrac, the Bills converted $7 million of his 2026 salary into a signing bonus. That transaction frees $5.3 million in room in addition to the $3.8 million in space that already existed.
With Hooker essentially being a replacement for Chauncey Gardner-Johnson, who quickly wore out his welcome, it's worth noting that Buffalo is absorbing a $2.3 million of dead money on this year's cap due to the failed free agent signing.
After playing a road game on Monday night, and not arriving home until the wee hours of Tuesday morning, the players had the day off while Bills' general manager Brandon Beane was busy working the phones.
"We had to restructure Dion today to make that happen. And so, appreciate Dion," said Beane. "He was out at a community event. My man [Manager of Football Admin and Ops] Ryan Moore tracked him down and we got it, we got it done. As soon as we knew that this was getting close to the finish line, we sent Ryan to where Dion was."
There was some confusion in public circles about the salary conversion deadline. The Bills processed the conversion for Dawkins on Tuesday as Monday's deadline was only for players who were changing teams in a trade.
Dawkins is currently in the second season of a three-year contract extension worth $60.06 million. The 32-year-old Dawkins was selected in Round 2 by the Bills at the 2017 NFL Draft.
"Appreciate Dion and his reps helping us out and getting this to the finish line," said Beane.
In a rare occurrence , Dawkins was inactive on Monday night against the Minnesota Vikings. He did not practice last week and was scratched due to a ribs injury .

title: Dalton Kincaid, Spencer Brown Fighting New Injuries After Bills' Primetime Week 9 Win
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills posted a 23-6 road win on Monday Night Football in Week 9, but it didn't come without a few bumps and bruises along the way .
Starting right tackle Spencer Brown and tight end Dalton Kincaid were already battling injuries that popped up during the Bills' two-week swing through Los Angeles and Las Vegas.
Despite nearing full strength heading into the November 9 road game against the Minnesota Vikings, Brown and Kincaid remain on the injury report in Week 10 thanks to new problems.
Both players apparently sprained an ankle going up against the Vikings' vaunted defense.
"That was a physical game on Monday night and we kinda knew that [would be the case]," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady prior to Wednesday's walkthrough practice in Orchard Park. "Right now it's really like, we're two days out of the game so we're walking today at practice. We're gonna have to kinda get a feel of where everybody is, and I'll have a better answer for you guys come Friday."
Kincaid and Brown were listed as limited participants on the week's first official injury report with the ankle issues. The Bills are technically on a short week with a road game against the New York Jets set for Sunday, November 15 at 1 p.m. ET.
The Bills' primary pass-catching tight end went down early in the fourth quarter while blocking for wide receiver DJ Moore along the sideline.
Kincaid left the game for a quick evaluation, and he returned with his ankle taped later on the same possession. With 8:12 remaining in the game, Kincaid snagged a short pass to convert a 3rd-and-3 in Vikings' territory.
The good news is Kincaid appears to be completely in the clear concerning the ribs/chest injury that popped up during the third quarter on October 18. He was a full participant for Buffalo's last two Week 9 practices, and he also ditched the red non-contact jersey.
After missing the November 1 game due to back issues, the fear was that Brown reaggravated the problem on Monday night against the Vikings.
Although he appeared wincing in pain following a couple different plays throughout the night, his ankle, and not his back, was the culprit. Brown apparently suffered the sprain during the Bills' second possession blocking for a James Cook carry.
"I'm just playing football right now. It's a tough sport. That's why I play it. That's why I love to play it. I look forward to next week and getting back out there again," said Brown after the win .
Brown played 77 snaps in the victory, sitting it only the final three kneel-downs by backup quarterback Kyle Allen.

title: Will Amani Hooker Play in Week 10? What New Bills Safety Said About Potential Debut
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills made a huge addition to their defense right before the trade deadline with the trade for Amani Hooker.
With a little over an hour to go before the deadline stuck, general manager Brandon Beane completed a trade with the Tennessee Titans for Hooker, giving up a second-round pick while also receiving a fifth-rounder in return.
The trade was mostly well-received by experts , and it was almost universally well-received from a Bills fan base that has been yearning for that kind of move for years now.
With Hooker now in the fold, the next question is: will he make his Bills debut in Week 10 against the New York Jets?
Hooker spoke to the media on Wednesday for the first time since the trade and he made a definitive statement about his status against the Jets.
“Oh I’m gonna play on Sunday. Yeah. I’ll be ready to go," Hooker said .
It'll be a quick turnaround for Hooker, who will have just five days to prepare to take the field. But he's a smart player, so he should have a fairly good grasp of the playbook by Sunday.
While we know he's going to suit up, what we don't know is if Hooker will play a full complement of snaps. That will likely be determined as the game wears on.
Hooker has been a mainstay on the field during his career.
Over seven games with the Titans this season, the veteran safety has played on a whopping 99% of snaps, and the last time Hooker played fewer than 90% of snaps in a season was his sophomore campaign in 2020.
It didn't take long for Hooker to see just how much Bills fans love their team. In fact, he said he felt it as soon as he stepped off the plane and saw all of the people wearing Bills gear.
“I can just really feel the love here for this team," Hooker said.
Hooker is going from a Titans fan base that has been criticized for not having enough passion for its team, to a Bills fan base that is one of the most dedicated in the NFL.
Hooker is a versatile safety, but he does his best work on the back end as a free safety, where he's solid in coverage and has a nose for the football, as evidenced by his five picks this season and 17 interceptions over his career.
That's a perfect fit for the Bills , who haven't gotten much turnover production from their safeties. In fact, C.J. Gardner-Johnson is the only Bills safety to record a pick this season and he's no longer on the team.
Buffalo also sports the fourth-worst pass defense in the NFL and has given up 28 completions of 20-plus yards this season. Hooker should help the Bills there, also.
