title: Grading Chicago Bears 2026 Free Agent Additions at Midseason
full_text:
The Chicago Bears currently sit atop the loaded NFC North with a 6-2 record. They've built a roster that looks prepared for a deep playoff run. While it was largely built through the draft, they've also found some success in free agency over the past few offseasons.
The Bears entered the offseason in a precarious cap situation, but a flurry of moves ahead of free agency changed their fortune. Drew Dalman's sudden retirement, Tremaine Edmunds' release, and their decision to trade DJ Moore to Buffalo opened up $44 million in available cap space.
Those moves allowed Chicago to make noise in March . They promptly took advantage, bringing in eight new players and re-signing a few homegrown ones.
How has the free agent class fared over the first half of the season?
Devin Bush's season has been a tale of two halves thus far. Aside from a sack in their Week 4 matchup against the Jets (a game where it would've been tough for him to find a rhythm based on how few snaps they played), he had an uneventful first month of the campaign. He was invisible, which was especially concerning against the run .
Bush has seemingly turned the corner from there, though. He's been far more disruptive in recent weeks, and has 35 tackles over the past five games. The 28-year-old has consistently made plays from sideline to sideline, and has looked like the player the Bears thought they were getting when they signed him.
Coby Bryant suffered a left knee hyperextension, bone bruise, and small fracture on August 3, and has been sidelined ever since. He's expected to return to the lineup next month or when the playoffs kick off in January.
The Bears had high hopes for Bryant, and it's safe to assume they still do. He's extremely versatile, with extensive experience playing virtually everywhere in the secondary. He'll provide a big boost to the secondary when he's good to go, but there's no other way to grade this one than "incomplete" at this point.
Bryant's injury opened the door for someone to play a key role at the other safety spot opposite Dillon Thieneman, and Cam Lewis ran with that opportunity. He's been one of the team's biggest surprises over the first half of the season. Like Bryant, Lewis brought a healthy amount of versatility, and it has been on full display.
He's made the brunt of his impact at safety, but he's also seen some time at nickelback when injuries struck others in the secondary. While Lewis hasn't been perfect (their Week 7 matchup against New England set his low water mark), they're not paying him to be. He's also shown strong playmaking chops in recent weeks. He's been a perfect addition at a bargain-bin price .
Kalif Raymond was another home run bargain-bin addition by Ryan Poles and Co. While he hasn't maintained the breakneck pace over the first three weeks (when he had 19 catches for 214 yards), he's still on pace for a career-high campaign. Raymond has earned Caleb Williams' trust and has gotten the Bears out of a few binds over the first half of the season.
The 32-year-old has also had a few great punt returns. He's also become a respected voice for a young receiver room yearning for leadership. Basically, he's been exactly what Chicago needed , and they acquired him on a cheap deal.
Their decision to sign Neville Gallimore to a two-year, $10 million deal (initially announced as a one-year, $12 million deal) was questionable at the time , and it's aged even worse. He's played the fourth-most defensive snaps among all DTs, and two guys ahead of him both missed a game.
Aside from one TFL in the Week 5 loss against Green Bay, he's been relatively invisible. They definitely expected him to make more of an impact when they brought him in.
James Lynch, on the other hand, has been somewhat of a revelation. Despite signing for near-veteran minimum salary, he's played the second-most snaps among all defensive tackles (221). That was with him being a surprise healthy scratch in Week 4 against the Jets.
Lynch's 19 tackles rank second among all defensive linemen, and he's shown a knack for getting his hands up to knock down passes, deflecting two passes at the line (and intercepting another against Seattle). He's also shown some versatility, occasionally playing on the edge. Basically, he's provided the impact many expected Jordan van den Berg to after his impressive preseason performance.
Lynch wasn't the only quality bargain bin pickup along the defensive line. Kentavius Street was actually named the starter next to Grady Jarrett after training camp, and he held his own for the most part. He flashed some potential and is still the only true DT with a full sack aside from Jeffery Simmons (Grady Jarrett was credited with a half-sack against Tampa Bay).
Unfortunately, Street's season got cut short when he suffered a season-ending knee injury in the team's Week 8 contest against Seattle. While he wasn't nearly as impactful as Lynch (he had only 9 tackles despite playing a similar number of snaps) before he got hurt, he still proved to be a great value addition.
Jack Sanborn has only played nine defensive snaps (and they were unforgettable snaps when the Bears temporarily pulled their starters against Atlanta). However, he wasn't signed to play defense. He's a special teams ace, and he's played 160 snaps in the third phase over the first half of the season.
Sanborn hasn't made any splashy plays, though. His five tackles also rank no better than fifth on the team in special teams takedowns. His false start on the fake punt against Tampa Bay was also a net negative, even if it ultimately saved them.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: How Caleb Williams Rates as a Potential Super Bowl Quarterback
full_text:
Bears coach Ben Johnson earlier this week attempted to squash some postgame criticism of Caleb Williams' performance against Tampa Bay.
He diluted it somewhat by spreading out the blame over the full team for four interceptions thrown.
"For 17 games in a season, there are going to be games where every one of us is not at our best, and we need those around us to pick up the slack," Johnson said.
Four interceptions the way Williams threw them wasn't necessarily all on the rest of the team. He had a few terrible decisions and at least one bad throw.
Caleb Williams is just toying with us. pic.twitter.com/rKS0LXcln6
"As a unit, the offense didn't quite perform the way that we're capable of performing," Johnson said. "I think there are a number of individuals that would tell you that was not their best game, certainly this year, and yet as a collective, other guys were able to fill the void.
"We keep talking about how we just have to find a way to score one more point than the opponent, and we did that.”
The important thing for Williams is not this one game as the defense found a way to bail everyone out most of the night and then Williams did deliver in the end. Rather, the focus should be on big picture for Williams with the Bears at the midpoint. His improvement has been obvious. The question is whether it's been good enough to get the Bears to a Super Bowl.
"There are 6 quarterbacks in this league that are just different... Caleb's the only one that doesn't have to carry something. He's got the most complete team." @colincowherd on Caleb Williams & the Bears' Super Bowl chances pic.twitter.com/GZ8mnz2CmS
Super Bowl quarterbacks tend to hit specific statistical levels on their way to playing for the Lombardi Trophy.
Looking at the last 10 Super Bowl QBs dating back to the win by the Rams over the Bengals five years ago, Williams' numbers are largely within the parameters necessary for being a QB in "the big game."
The last performance dropped him down a few notches and in some cases below where he needed to be to reach the levels Sam Darnold, Drake May, Jalen Hurts, Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy, Joe Burrow and Matthew Stafford were at for their Super Bowl appearances.
Here's where Williams sits after his six starts with three missed games due to injury compared to how those passers did in their Super Bowl years.
Bust: #Bears WR Rome Odunze can’t catch this. pic.twitter.com/3YSepVRW68
The analytic EPA that Johnson places so much emphasis on continues to be a Williams strength, even if he slid down a bit last game. Williams is sixth in EPA/dropback at .19. Of the last 10 QBs, no one has been below 10th among starters. Williams' .19 would be better than five of the last 10 Super Bowl QBs. Only Drake Maye (.32) last year, Brock Purdy (.31) in 2023, and Patrick Mahomes (.29) in 2022 were better. His .19 is the same as Matthew Stafford in 2021.
The average for the 10 QBs was 68.3% and Williams is at 68.7 after his interception-plagued game knocked him down from over 70%. There were four Super Bowl QBs better than 68.3%. The 68.3% is much better than last year's 58.1%, though. Drake Maye last season had the highest completion percentage of the 10 Super Bowl QBs at 72%.
Pains me to say this, but I believe Caleb Williams, talent wise, is better than peak Patrick Mahomes. He makes some insane plays consistently. Faster, stronger arm, elite accuracy, no Tyreek Hill, no Travis Kelce - arguably two of the most dangerous players at position during…
Williams' average for six games played is 257 and he doesn't hit the 260-yard average of the other 10 but it is better than four of the Super Bowl QBs averaged. Especially considering how much emphasis the Bears place on running the ball, it is well within the right range. Patrick Mahomes' average of 308.2 yards in 2022 was phenomenal but the range dipped as low as Jalen Hurts' 193.5 in 2024. That total didn't hurt Hurts because he and the Eagles ran the ball so well, much like Johnson wants to see from the Bears and anticipates in the second half.
Caleb Williams has his worst career game and the Bears STILL win. Best team in football. Ice Man 🥶 pic.twitter.com/spmWercY1g
One place Williams and the offense need to pick it up somewhat is here, although he still has been better than a few of the 10 Super Bowl QBs were. Williams is at 7.9 yards per attempt. Only Mahomes in 2024 and 2023 was lower. Last year was a rarity when both QBs came in well above 8.0 at 8.9 for Maye and 8.5 for Sam Darnold.
Caleb Williams is averaging 282.5 passing yards per game in games he finishes. That pace would have him at 2,258 total passing yards through 8 games, placing him 1st on this list. That pace would also have Caleb at 4,798.5 yards for a full season. And all of this while… https://t.co/7L32rzEJ1g pic.twitter.com/4yNubXNHDn
Williams was well on track here until Sunday night's pick fest. Now his ratio of 4.1 TDs to 2.6 interceptions comes in below all of the last 10 QBs.  Mahomes' 2023 mark of 4.5/2.3 was the worst of the 10. Darnold wasn't very good at 5.2/2.9 last year. Williams always points out how he hasn't been a QB to throw interceptions, so perhaps there's a chance he improves this ratio. It would also help if Rome Odunze quits dropping TD passes.
Caleb Williams is everything Patrick Mahomes was supposed to be.
Williams' passer rating too a huge nosedive from lofty status in the 100s to 95.4 but it's still his career best by 5.3 points and better than Mahomes in 2024 (93.5) and 2023 (92.6). He'll be hard-pressed to get back up in the area of some of these passers now, such as Purdy's 113.0 in 2023, Maye's 113.5 last year or Burrow's 108.3 in 2021.
Caleb Williams has thrown 11 INTs and 15 TDs in his last 10 games The guy is in the best situation of any QB in the league. Most time to throw, top 3 run game, and the best play caller in Ben Johnson Ben Johnson should put him back in the box and call screen and 5 yard hitches… https://t.co/XBpWLPRi4b
This is one area where he might never have a shot at being in the same class as some of these QBs. Johnson's offense stresses running so much that many of their first downs will come on the ground. Williams has only 67 passing first downs and the lows were by Hurts at 171 in 2022 and 174 in 2024. This is a number more reflective of the type of offense than a QB's passing.
A success rate means gaining 40% of yardage to the sticks on first down, 60% on second down and 100% on third or fourth down. Williams' success rate of 49.3% doesn't look scintillating on the face of it but Hurts never hit 47% in his two Super Bowl season and a 49.3 is actually better than almost all of the other QBs.
I don’t want to be prisoner of the moment, but is Caleb Williams the best QB in the league right now

title: Jeffery Simmons' Leadership, Trash Talk on Display in Mic'd Up Video From Bears vs. Bucs
full_text:
Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons was mic'd up for his second game with the Chicago Bears when they took on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night in Week 9.
Not only was it his second game with the Bears, but also the first Simmons has played as a member of the home team at Soldier Field.
In the video shared by the Bears, we see a bunch of notable things, including how thrilled Simmons is to be in Chicago.
We also get to hear Big Jeff trash-talking Bucs offensive linemen for their inability to stop him despite double- and triple-teaming him, and we get a good idea of the leadership Simmons brings.
Check out the full video below.
The Bears went on to win the game , 27-24, in what was a too-close-for-comfort finish.
Chicago looked to be in control early, but the Bucs slowly climbed their way back into the game as Caleb Williams struggled en route to tossing four picks .
Luckily, Simmons and the defense played at a high level and kept the Bucs from fully taking advantage of Williams' turnovers.
Simmons once again made a massive impact, with the superstar defensive lineman notching four tackles, one sack, one QB hit, three pressures, one pass defensed and one tackle for loss.
Simmons now has two sacks in two games for the Bears, which is one more than Bears interior defenders had combined in the first seven games.
He's also proving to be a huge asset when it comes to helping the guys around him, as the double teams he draws are freeing other defenders up to make plays.
With each snap, the Bears' decision to give up a historic package for Simmons is looking better and better.
As we noted, the Simmons trade was historic. That's because no team in the common draft era (since 1967) had ever traded multiple first-round picks for a defensive tackle.
As the trade deadline came and went, the Bears did not make another trade despite being linked to interest in cornerbacks .
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Wednesday that the trade for Simmons definitely played a part in Chicago's quiet deadline day.
"For the Bears, once they did the Jeffery Simmons deal, that was kind of it," Rapoport said . "That was kind of the only draft compensation they were gonna give up."
A quiet deadline would normally anger fans, but when it comes to Bears fans, they are so thrilled with the acquisition of Simmons that it's hard to have an issue this time around.
Fans wanted to see an all-in move from general manager Ryan Poles and they got exactly that. As a result, Poles is going to receive a lot more grace moving forward.
The one need we would have liked to see the Bears address was at cornerback, where Jaylon Johnson's struggles leave a major concern.
But Johnson did notch a pick-six against the Bucs, so maybe that will be enough to get him going. And, having Simmons getting after the quarterback should help the back end, also.

title: There's Actually More to Transformed Bears Defense Than Jeffery Simmons
full_text:
The Jeffery Simmons effect has been noticeable for the Bears defense in the last two games , as their own four-man pressure amps up and yards per rush against them declines.
There is more rush making the coverage aspect of rush-and-cover easier.
"He presents a physical presence on the inside of our defense, run and pass, and that's a good feeling to have," defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said.
Still, before Simmons this never was a defense struggling to simply get by while being propped up by the Bears offense, as many suggested during the last few weeks prior to the Simmons trade. It's reflected in their defensive team statistics. The trend was already positive for this group before Simmons and it only figures to improve in the second half.
Jeffery Simmons is a PROBLEM. 💪 📺 Sunday Night Football: Buccaneers at Bears on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/82MjdDopdn
Last year takeaways saved the Bears defense when it lacked the ability to stop the run or defend the pass. This year they've improved at both and haven't needed  takeaways to rescue them. This is where the critics of their offseason improvement failed to show any foresight whatsoever. They were saying the Bears couldn't repeat last year's "lucky" defense that took it away so much but they didn't see past the end of their noses to realize the defense was improved and wouldn't need to rely only on takeaways.
In fact, the Bears defense has been so good that they've been able to withstand an offense that has turned the ball over the third most times in the league (17).
JAYLON JOHNSON HOUSE CALL ☎️ 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/FVkfIjPwvQ
Considering how much criticism Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson receiver, or their supposed lack of a pass rush prior to Simmons was cited, they are ninth overall at 310.9 yards allowed per game, up 20 spots from last year when they were 29th at 361.8 yards allowed per game. Also, they're better against the run by far, at 91.3 rushing yards allowed per game for sixth in the league, 43.2 yards per game better than last year when they were 27th.
While their run defense needs to be better than 22nd in yards allowed per carry at 4.4, they are greatly improved there from 29th last year at 5.0. And they're trending up here because they have allowed just 82.4 yards rushing over the last five games and 4.0 per rush in the last five, which is 14th in the league. With Simmons now added, it only figures to improve.
OK defense this is more fun: I'm gonna start with a general pass D cutup. Lotta their staples. Mugs with c2 behind it, more quarters, some man. It has become very varied. Tons of execution errors by Baker/pass catchers too though. I liked our front/LBs play, as well as Lewis pic.twitter.com/eyTrdgDoC8
The end result of all of this has been a phenomenal improvement in third-down defense from 40.84% and 22nd in the NFL to No. 1 by a very wide margin. At 22.83%, the Bears are a whopping 7.75% better than Seattle, the next-best team. It makes up for fewer takeaways but more importantly fixes the league-high 17 turnovers their offense has committed.
Expect more of the same approach from Allen as the season goes on as in recent games. They'll continue to blitz, though not at the ninth-highest level in the league like they have (31.3%).
"I think in a perfect world scenario the more resources you can send back there in coverage and still be able to affect the quarterback, I think that's, you know, probably the greatest advantage and yet I think you have to have a combination and mixture of both," Allen said.
Jeffery Simmons doing some talking after that last third down stop for the Bears' defense. pic.twitter.com/6rTMd1GhRR
The defense is better because of better people. Beside Simmons, linebacker Devin Bush has gradually improved and finished the first half with three strong games.
"Our big guys are running out of the stack chasing after the ball; we have our little guys playing big and making tackless on the perimeter," coach Ben Johnson said Tuesday while making an appearance on Fox Sports' First Take with Danny Parkins. "I think its really raising the level of play from our whole unit."
Besides better overall play and Allen's defensive scheming between pressure and no pressure, there could be an added factor that has helped the Bears defense rise to ninth overall at 310.9 yards a game. Johnson talked about it in his First Take appearance.
Devin Bush hit pic.twitter.com/wXZgsXveya
"You know, you talk about being the head coach and certainly as the offensive play caller I'm more inclined on that side, and yet trying to bring all three phases together to play a complete game, I think that's where certainly I've grown from Year 1 to Year 2," Johnson said. "But having great, strong leadership on the pther phases really makes my job easier, as well."
With effective direction and impactful coaching, the Bears' defense is heading in the direction it needs going into the second half five four tough NFC North games to come in their final eight.
And it doesn't hurt having someone doing what Simmons has shown, whether he's running upfield chasing a quarterback or chasing a ball carrier downfield as he did so effectively to prevent Tampa Bay receiver Emeka Egbuka from scoring on a screen pass on Sunday.
@DannyParkins : “Does any part of you hesitate knowing that [wanting shutouts] is going to put a target on you and your team’s back?” Ben Johnson: “Absolutely not. If there’s any other offensive play caller in the league that doesn’t feel that way, then they’re full of BS." pic.twitter.com/UMXuIKeczK

title: Cincinnati Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase Gives 2, Um, Thumbs Up to Disrespecting Steelers
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals 2022 season opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers is most known for Joe Burrow’s four turnovers and the loss of long snapper Clark Harris, resulting in missed game-winning kicks at the end of regulation and in overtime of a 23-20 loss.
Wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase remembers the game for something else.
Actually, two of something else – both of his middle fingers.
Chase infamously threw double birds in the face of Pittsburgh safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, and the gesture was immortalized by a photographer. And that picture has been printed and made into shirts, blankets and other mementos that often find their way back to Chase.
The receiver said he’s often asked to sign items with the photo on them.
“Because I want to do it again,” Chase said. “But I don’t want to get fined. But I love it. It’s a cool picture, honestly.”
The display in 2022 resulted in the first fine of Chase’s career, as the NFL docked him $23,870 for “multiple unsportsmanlike conducts.”
The double birds didn’t draw a flag on the field, but he was penalized 15 yards for taunting after an incomplete pass on fourth and 2 with 1:51 remaining and the Bengals trailing 20-14.
Chase has been fined five other times in his career, although the one for obscene gestures in Week 2 against Houston was rescinded.
He also drew a $15,914 taunting penalty and fine later in 2022 against Kansas City; a $31,599 fine for verbally abusing an official in 2024 at Kansas City; a $19,697 fine for an obscene gesture against Baltimore in 2024; and a one-game suspension that amounted to a loss of $507,156 for spitting on Pittsburgh’s Jalen Ramsey last year.
Sunday’s game against the Steelers will be two days shy of the one-year anniversary of that incident.
While Chase said he doesn’t want to get fined again, he said he would accept the punishment and flash the double birds to another team in the right situation.
“If it was the Super Bowl, yes,” he said. “I would definitely do it again.”
What about an AFC Championship Game against the Steelers.
“I might have to call Chad (Johnson) for that one,” he said.
While Chase won his appeal of the fine in Houston this year, he knew there was no way he would win an appeal after the double birds in 2022.
“There's no appealing that fine because I'm red handed in photos. It's hard to get out of that one.”

title: Ja’Marr Chase Delivers Brutally Honest Take on Bengals-Steelers Rivalry
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers enter Sunday night's game tied for the top spot in the AFC North at 6-2.
It's one of the biggest regular season meetings between the teams in years, but Ja'Marr Chase still puts the Bengals' rivalry with the Kansas City Chiefs a tier above it.
Asked where Pittsburgh ranked among the rivalries he's been part of in his career, Chase said on Thursday that it was "pretty up there." The Bengals superstar stopped short of picking a No. 1, saying, "I don't have nobody number one."
The follow-up yielded a more definitive answer from Chase. When asked whether the Pittsburgh rivalry was on par with Cincinnati's rivalry with Kansas City when both teams were rolling, Chase replied, "No, no, no." He put the Chiefs rivalry "way higher."
Some of the biggest games of Chase's career came against Kansas City, and the first one produced one of his best individual performances. As a rookie, he caught 11 passes for 266 yards and three touchdowns in a 34-31 win over the Chiefs. The Bengals overcame three separate 14-point deficits that afternoon and clinched the AFC North on Evan McPherson's field goal as time expired.
Four weeks later, the teams met again at Arrowhead Stadium, with a Super Bowl berth on the line. Cincinnati fell behind 21-3 but rallied to win 27-24 in overtime. The following season, Kansas City earned a rematch in the AFC Championship Game and won 23-20 with a field goal as time expired.
In just over a year, the teams had played a game that clinched a division title and two others that determined who would represent the AFC in the Super Bowl.
Sunday's meeting with Pittsburgh has its own stakes, though they aren't as high as the stakes in the matchups with the Chiefs.
These AFC North rivals are both 6-2, which is the best combined winning percentage for a Bengals-Steelers matchup this late in the season since 2009 according to NBC. The winner will also take sole possession of first place in the AFC North.
The Bengals are trying to win their fifth-straight game and avoid being swept by Pittsburgh for the first time since 2023.

title: Bengals Add 4 Players to Thursday's Injury Report, but That's Actually Good News
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals had four players on the injury report Wednesday. Today there were eight.
But that’s a good thing, because three of the additions are there because the team opened their 21-day practice window to return from Injured Reserve.
Cornerback Jalen Davis, wide receiver Andrei Iosivas and rookie guard Brian Parker II were all listed as full participants in their practice in several weeks.
The fourth addition was defensive tackle B.J. Hill, who was limited with a Non-Injury Related-rest designation.
Parker, the team’s fifth-round pick out of Duke, has been on IR since Aug. 30 with a knee injury. His return to practice coincides with a pectoral injury to Dylan Fairchild, but the starting left guard was upgraded to a full participant after going limited Wednesday.
Iosivas has been on IR since Sept. 26 with a thumb injury. He had three catches for 19 yards before suffering the injury in Week 2 at Houston.
"I had a great practice today," Iosivassaid. "I'm not like shying away from the ball at all. Even if it hurts, whatever. I'm still attacking it the way that I want to. So I'm pretty happy with that. Yeah, it's pretty good.”
Davis went on IR on Sept. 30 with a hamstring injury suffered in the first meeting with the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3.
Josh “Fig” Newton got his first start of the year Sunday in Madrid against the Falcons, and defensive coordinator Al Golden said he was mostly impressed by how the 2024 fifth-round pick played.
“(Cornerbacks coach Chuck Burks) did a great job with him just bringing him along to the point where, OK, he's ready to do it. Let's see what it looks like,” Golden said. “And then Fig did the rest.
“Fig has great energy. Smart player. And he's vocal. He's a good communicator,” Golden said. “I thought he played really hard. There's some plays I know that he would like to have back, but overall, he really, really responded well.”
Golden praised head coach Zac Taylor for the way he has handled the long trip to Spain and quick turnaround, along with all of the other ways he has schedule practice and recovery throughout the offseason and training camp.
“I think Zac is on the front end, if not pioneering in terms of how to take care of the players during the season,” Golden said. “How do you respond as a player, or as in our case, the defensive unit or by position, at the end of the day.
“If he's taking care of us physically, we better be on the game plan,” Golden added. “The walkthrough's got to be great. Overcommunicate. Whatever you have to do to establish that you know exactly what you need to do.
In addition to recovering from an overseas trip, the Bengals are facing a Pittsburgh team coming off a bye.
Since the international series began, there have been five instances where a team returning from an overseas game played a team coming off a bye.
The teams coming off the bye are 5-0.
"I don't know what the stats are. I just know they're not great. I honestly can't even give you a ballpark of what they are," Taylor said. "I just think common sense would tell you it's probably a little challenging. But I think we have a great mindset right now."

title: Three Bengals Players on IR Take First Step Toward Return as Team Opens Practice Windows
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have opened the practice window for three players who are on Injured Reserve.
Cornerback Jalen Davis, wide receiver Andrei Iosivas and rookie guard Brian Parker II will practice today, and the Bengals will have 21 days to reinstate each player to the 53-man roster.
No corresponding move will need to be made for the first of the three to be activated, as the roster currently has just 52 players.
Parker, the team’s fifth-round pick out of Duke, has been on IR since Aug. 30 with a knee injury. His return to practice coincides with a possible need at left guard after starter Dylan Fairchild suffered a pectoral injury at the end of the 34-17 win against the Falcons in Madrid.
Fairchild practiced in Wednesday’s walk-through but was listed as limited.
Iosivas has been on IR since Sept. 26 with a thumb injury. He had three catches for 19 yards before suffering the injury in Week 2 at Houston.
Davis went on IR on Sept. 30 with a hamstring injury suffered in the first meeting with the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3.
The Bengals have been shuffling players in and out of the slot corner position since Davis went down. Josh Newton made his first career start Sunday in Madrid, but Davis likely will return to the starting role once he’s activated.
Newton had an up-and-down performance against the Falcons, but defensive coordinator Al Golden was mostly positive in his assessment.
“(Cornerbacks coach Chuck Burks) did a great job with him just bringing him along to the point where, OK, he's ready to do it. Let's see what it looks like,” Golden said. “And then Fig did the rest.
“Fig has great energy. Smart player. And he's vocal. He's a good communicator,” Golden said. “I thought he played really hard. There's some plays I know that he would like to have back, but overall, he really, really responded well.”

title: Joe Burrow Makes Bold Statement About Bengals’ ‘Lights Out’ O-Line
full_text:
Joe Burrow thinks that the Cincinnati Bengals' offensive line is playing some of the best football in the NFL.
The likely MVP frontrunner through the first half of the season said the team's protection is a major reason Cincinnati's offense has become more explosive. Burrow ranks first among all quarterbacks in EPA, completion percentage, and passing touchdowns, and second in passing yards and passer rating. Clearly, something is working — and Burrow credits the cohesion and trust among the big men up front.
“The guys that we have, I mean, they're lights out,” Burrow said on Wednesday. “They're playing some of the best football in the league, and got to continue to get better and continue to improve. But we're in a really good spot.”
One of the key reasons the Bengals have been able to push the ball downfield, according to Burrow, is his protection holding for an extra second on second-and-a-half.
“You can find ways to do it, but it's a lot harder,” Burrow said.
The Bengals are coming off a 34-17 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid and their offensive line entered the week with Pro Football Focus' third-highest pass-blocking grade , behind only the San Francisco 49ers and Detroit Lions.
The protection also helps explain Cincinnati's success on third down. It's about having a plan, as Burrow noted — one that manages pressure and gives his receivers time to win their matchups.
“We've got a really good scheme. Our guys are protecting at a really high level. That's what third down is,” Burrow said.
“You've got to be able to pick up all the different pressures, and you got to be able to pass twists off, and you got to develop a protection plan that is going to pick up all those pressures and not make you throw hot.”
Of course, standout wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins can win one-on-one battles and turn 50-50 balls into 75-25, but it still comes back to the linemen for Burrow.
"It starts with protection, though,” Burrow said.
Cincinnati's next challenge comes Sunday night at Paycor Stadium, where the Bengals will face the Pittsburgh Steelers, with first place in the AFC North on the line.
Pittsburgh hung on for a 30-27 victory in Week 3, the first matchup of the season between the two teams, but Burrow expects the Steelers to change their looks from the first meeting. They're expected to test him with disguised coverage and pressure packages.
Still, the star QB has utmost confidence in his offensive linemen to help Cincinnati flip the script on Sunday night.

title: Joe Burrow Set for Rare First With Mike Tomlin, Last With Aaron Rodgers on SNF
full_text:
The Sunday Night Football game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers will mark just the third – and likely final – meeting between Joe Burrow and Aaron Rodgers.
Rodgers has said this will be his final season, so barring a meeting the playoffs, Sunday will be Burrow’s last chance to add him to the list of quarterbacks he’s beaten.
Burrow is 0-2 against Rodgers, losing to him and the Packers 25-22 in overtime in 2021, in addition to the 30-27 loss in Pittsburgh earlier this season in Week 3.
Despite it likely being a final meeting, Burrow said he doesn’t think he’ll ask the future Hall of Famer for a jersey swap.
“Probably not,” Burrow said when asked. “Don’t really think about that too much.”
He has, however, given a lot of thought to how well Rodgers has played throughout his career and especially in 2026.
“He’s one of the greatest that’s ever done it,” Burrow said. “He’s 41 or 42 and still doing it at a high level. I would have trouble calling it quits if I’m still playing like that, at that age.
“I’ve enjoyed watching him for a long time,” he added. “And this year, I think he’s playing so well. He really played great in that last game we played. Dang near perfect. I had to be perfect the whole time, too.”
While Sunday could be Burrow’s final game against Rodgers, he’s already faced Mike Tomlin for the final time, presuming the coach doesn’t return to the profession.
Burrow went 4-3 against Tomlin. Among quarterbacks with at least four starts against the future Hall of Fame coach, Burrow is one of only three to boast a winning record. The others are Josh Allen (4-1) and Tom Brady (7-3).
Tomlin stepped away from the Steelers at the end of last year and moved to NBC, the network that will broadcast Sunday night’s game.
That means Burrow will sit with Tomlin and the rest of the NBC crew for a production meeting ahead of the game.
“I didn’t even think about that,” Burrow said before heaping praise on Tomlin, who will be working his first Steelers game since leaving the coaching profession.
“I've always loved how he sees the game and attacks coaching,” Burrow added. “He's always attacked it with a lot of intensity that I have a lot of respect for. So to be able to get to know him in a setting like that, I think will be a little exciting for me.”
Those production meetings typically involve the television crew asking the players and coaches questions to get as much information as possible to use on the broadcast.
But they can be conversational at times.
Burrow was asked if there were any questions he would like to ask Tomlin after all the battles they have had against each other.
“Certainly,” he said with a grin. “Maybe more of an offseason off-the-record session than a production meeting.”

title: Bengals Injury Report: Dylan Fairchild's Practice Status Revealed Ahead of Primetime Showdown
full_text:
The Bengals returned to practice today as the roster works through the lingering jet lag from last week's trip to Spain. Cincinnati is pretty healthy coming out of the first half of the season, and the latest injury report largely reflected that.

title: Zac Taylor Reveals Uncomfortable Message Duke Tobin Asked Him to Deliver After Bengals Trade Debacle
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals did not make de facto general manager Duke Tobin available following Tuesday’s trade fiasco and instead had head coach Zac Taylor address it during his Wednesday news conference.
Despite admitting it made him uncomfortable, Taylor addressed the subject without specifically being asked about it, responding to a question about the team’s depth at defensive end.
“Obviously we tried something yesterday, and Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me of how he wanted this portrayed,” Taylor said. “I’m not comfortable doing it, but I’m going to do what he asked.
“We did make an effort to kind of put some depth in there in place of Cashius (Howell),” Taylor continued. “As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. So he's really apologetic about it.”
With rookie second-round pick Cashius Howell on Injured Reserve due to wrist surgery, the Bengals agreed to trade a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for defensive end Arnold Ebiketie.
But because the Eagles acquired Ebiketie in free agency this past offseason, he would have counted against the Bengals in the compensatory pick formula, negating the third-round pick they are due to receive for losing Trey Hendrickson.
So the trade essentially would have been Ebiketie for a third and a sixth.
The Bengals backed out of the trade after compensatory pick expert Nick Korte posted on X that the team would lose their third-round pick as well.
Taylor said Tobin didn’t say when he became aware of the added cost, and Taylor didn’t ask, but it’s clear the front office was totally unaware until after Korte’s post. Otherwise, why even venture into trade talks for a player who would affect the comp pick formula.
“I certainly have a ton of confidence in our front office and how they do things, and they've given us the players that have allowed us to be 6-2 right now and playing at such a high level,” Taylor said.
“So we'll put that behind us and move forward,” he added. “Our locker room is in a great place right now.”
Taylor said Howell is still considered week to week following the wrist surgery after suffering the injury in Week 8 against Tennessee.
He said the injury won’t be season ending, but the timeline for Howell’s return is unclear.
The injury was the impetus for trying to acquire a depth piece such as Ebiketie, a 2022 second-round pick who has 16.5 career sacks in 76 games.
Taylor said he doesn’t expect the attempt to add Ebiketie to affect the other edge rushers who would have lost playing time after the acquisition.
“I would hope that everybody in our locker room wants us to be at our very best and trust that we're always doing things to make sure we're as good as possible,” Taylor said. “And we had an open roster spot, so it wasn't going to be addition and subtraction. It was just going to be (for) somebody that we've already put on IR.”
The botched trade could have an impact in Philadelphia, where Ebiketie remains, knowing the team tried to deal him.
The Eagles can’t be happy with how everything played out, and Taylor attempted to smooth over that relationship as well, saying that was another thing Tobin wanted him to convey rather than the director of player personnel addressing it himself.
“(Tobin) wants to make clear Philly was a great trade partner,” Taylor said. “It was on our end. And that's just the way things go.
“We're always looking at the waiver wire every single week. We're always looking for practice squad additions, subtractions,” Taylor continued. “The trade deadline is obviously the biggest thing that can impact your season.
“We’re in a great spot where we’re at with our roster, where we’re at with our health. Obviously it's not perfect with the health, but it's about as good as you can ask for getting through Week 8. All that’s behind us. We have a tremendous opportunity Sunday here at home, and our focus should be on that right now.”

title: Zac Taylor Shares Encouraging Injury Updates on Several Bengals Players
full_text:
Zac Taylor confirmed on Wednesday that starting left guard Dylan Fairchild is day-to-day after suffering an apparent shoulder injury during the waning moments of the Bengals' victory over the Falcons. Fairchild appeared to suffer the injury just before the two-minute warning in Madrid and attempted to finish the game afterwards, though he tapped out immediately afterwards.
Taylor also shared an update on rookie pass rusher Cashius Howell, refusing to rule Howell out for the season and instead labeling him week-to-week. The Bengals placed him on injured reserve after he sustained a wrist injury that required surgery in Week 8 against the Titans. He is eligible to return from IR after the team's Week 12 game against the Saints on 11/29, though Taylor said Howell will miss time beyond that.
"Right now he's just on IR and we'll just see how the recovery process goes as we get down the road here, but that time tables to be determined," Taylor said. "Still weeks for him, lets clear through the IR window and it'll definitely go beyond that, and we'll gather more information as the season goes."
Taylor also updated the media on the possible return of several key players from injured reserve this week, leaving the door open for names such as Andrei Iosivas to return to the active roster.
"We're close, not today specifically but very shortly, those are some conversations we've had, a couple of those guys we'll see where it's at," Taylor said.
Rumors have surfaced that Iosivas could return soon after having thumb surgery earlier in the season. He is the most likely candidate for a return from injured reserve at the moment, with names such as Jalen Davis, Ja'Sir Taylor, and Brian Parker II also getting close to a possible return.
Davis landed on IR after sustaining a hamstring injury against the Steelers in Week 3, whereas the team placed Taylor and Parker on the list before the start of the season on August 30th.
The return of either Davis or Taylor would provide a solid boost to a corner room that is missing any sort of stability at nickel corner, as Dax Hill and Josh Newton have filled that role since Davis' injury.
As for Parker, his return may happen at the perfect time. If Fairchild misses any time, Jacob Bayer would likely slot into the left guard spot with Parker also in the mix.

title: Referee Report: Among Active White Hats, Sunday's Has Worked More Bengals Games Than Any
full_text:
No active NFL referee has called more Cincinnati Bengals games than the man who will be on the assignment in Week 10 against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football.
This will be Clete Blakeman’s 18th Bengals game since he became a head referee in 2010.
While Cincinnati is 8-9 with Blakeman on the call, the team has a three-game losing streak with the veteran referee, with all three games being memorable losses.
The most recent was last year in Week 9, the 47-42 loss to the Chicago Bears. Prior to that was the Thursday night game at Baltimore in 2024 when quarterback Joe Burrow was hit in the head with no penalty called on a two-point conversion attempt that would have won the game. Instead, the Ravens prevailed 35-34.
And in 2023, Blakeman worked the season opener in Cleveland when the Bengals couldn’t master the Browns or the rain and dropped a 24-3 decision.

Blakeman and his crew are tied for first with six roughing the passer penalties this season. Their 11 defensive holding penalties also are tied for most in the league.
The crew has had at least 16 accepted penalties in five of the last six games.
Blakeman has earned postseason assignments in 12 of his 16 seasons as a referee, including Super 50 in 2015, the AFC Championship Game last year and the 2023 NFC Championship Game.

title: Todd Monken Gives One Concerning Update on the Browns' Offensive Line
full_text:
As the Cleveland Browns get ready to try and cut a two-game losing streak that would throw them back in the thick of the race for the playoffs, the offensive line’s play will be heavily scrutinized over the second half of the season.
No position group received more attention on the open market during the offseason than the O-Line, and after the first nine games, it’s safe to say the experiment isn’t working.
The Browns' offensive line ranks among the bottom-dwellers in the league when it comes to yards before first contact in the run game, and things look even worse in the passing game. Cleveland’s two starting tackles, Tytus Howard and rookie Spencer Fano, have the two highest pressure rates allowed in the entire NFL, and as a whole, Cleveland is the team that has allowed the most sacks (38) for the year, too.
Here's a look at the worst 10 starting tackles in the NFL right now when it comes to pressures allowed. And man, do I have bad news for the Browns... pic.twitter.com/Mby8wczjTd
To top things off, Howard leads the league with seven false start penalties , while guards Zion Johnson and rookie Austin Barber are among the six players tied for second place in holding penalties, with four apiece.
But if you were expecting to see some personnel changes for the second half of the season, don’t hold your breath.
Monken told reporters on Wednesday that his offensive line is set, and he isn’t planning on making any changes along the unit.
“I don’t see it that way. I mean, our starters are the starters. We addressed it again today: who the biggest culprits are. And they’re our guys. And they’re like, like we said before, I mean, they’re like our kids. We’re not going to just change out our kids. I mean, we’re not going to change out our players. They’re our best players. We got to get our best players. And we have a very diligent team. We have a lot of guys that love playing football, but the stats are what they are. I mean, we’ve got to look in the mirror and say, ‘at some point, this is it.’ I mean, that we just can’t continue down this road.”
When pressed about not reaching the point where changes are needed, Monken doubled down on his stance.
“I haven’t reached that point. We can’t change out our starters. I mean, I’m not changing out our starters. I mean, they’re either going to, they’re either going to buy into those types of things and the mental stamina that it takes to hold their water on defense or for us to have discipline offensively. But we’re not going to be the team we can be, because there are starters for a reason, right? If the other guys we thought gave us a better chance to win, they’d be in there.
"So, it’s all of us. How do we coach it better? How do we get our guys to dial in in the most critical moments, when it matters most?”
The Browns understandably didn’t want to pour more resources into this unit before the trade deadline after an offseason deal for Howard, adding Johnson and Elgton Jenkins in free agency, and then spending two draft picks, including a one inside the Top-10 on the group, but staying this course will lead nowhere... fast.
But zero roster changes doesn’t necessarily mean no changes at all . At some point in the preseason, Teven Jenkins was projected as the team’s starting right tackle before a back injury opened the door for Barber, who hasn’t looked back since. And there were some doubts about Fano too, with Monken acknowledging at one time that Dawand Jones could open the season at left tackle.
If that’s the case, then it’s not like the five current starters have always been head and shoulders above the rest.
And who’s to say Fano wouldn’t actually play better at right tackle than Howard? And Barber better than Fano on the left side? Both are coming off playing those positions in college for Utah and Florida, respectively. Those moves could open the right guard spot for Jenkins, as it seemed was intended.
Finally, Monken admitted during the offseason that he’d prefer to see Elgton Jenkins at guard instead of center, so there’s another possible piece that could be moved in search of a better fit overall.
Because at the end of the day, you do want your five best players on the field, but you also want them playing in their best possible spots, and sometimes leaving out one of the top five players for a better fit in one specific position maximizes the talent of the unit.
Alas, with Monken steadfast in keeping his “kids” where they are, and reinserting Deshaun Watson and his elongated dropbacks at quarterback --not that Shedeur Sanders fared much better in avoiding sacks against the Saints-- the inevitable result for Cleveland is written on the wall.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Why Browns Didn’t Move Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns chose not to make any moves at the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, surprising many who expected them to trade a quarterback, especially with four currently on their active roster. With injuries surging across the league, demand for quarterbacks is higher than ever.
While it was clear that Deshaun Watson and Taylen Green weren’t going anywhere, players like Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel could have been potential trade candidates.
The Browns likely didn’t receive the price they wanted to trade either Gabriel or Sanders, so they decided it was wiser to maintain their quarterback depth instead.
Cleveland selected Gabriel in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Although he may not seem like the franchise’s future quarterback, he could still play a backup role in 2027 and 2028. Sanders, another 2025 draft pick, just started a game against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.
While he might not be the ideal candidate for the starting quarterback position, the Browns likely want to give him a fair evaluation before the next season.
The Minnesota Vikings were in urgent need of quarterback assistance at the trade deadline but ultimately opted for veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders. They probably had no intention of trading for either Sanders or Gabriel, which is another reason the Browns didn’t make any moves; teams in need of quarterbacks were unlikely to reach out to them.
With a 6-2 record, the Vikings weren't going to consider Sanders or Gabriel, since neither has made a significant impact in the NFL. They were searching for someone who could lead them to the Super Bowl immediately.
However, the Browns may still part ways with Sanders or Gabriel during the offseason. Cleveland is likely to draft a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft and intends to keep Green in the quarterback room. They will probably need to sign a veteran quarterback to start, at least until the rookie is ready.
This could lead to five quarterbacks in the room, making it unlikely that the Browns will carry all five into training camp next season. Therefore, either Sanders or Gabriel is likely to be the odd one out.
Sanders still has an opportunity to start a few more games this season. The Browns could enter their bye week 5-5 if they lose to the Houston Texans on Sunday. This situation might prompt head coach Todd Monken to change quarterbacks and move away from Watson.

title: Browns Have 3 Major Offseason Needs That Their Trade Deadline Silence Made Clear
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline passed at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, and the Browns made zero moves. Cleveland finds itself in a strange position with a 5-4 record; however, the Browns aren't in "win-now" mode like many teams that were active at the deadline.
There were a few position groups the Browns could have considered trading for, but since they didn't make a move, here are three offseason needs that Cleveland must address in 2027.
The Browns have one of the best pass-catching tight ends in the NFL in Harold Fannin Jr., but the lack of depth behind him is concerning. Cleveland has only two tight ends on the active 53-man roster: Fannin and Blake Whiteheart. Many teams carry four to five tight ends, so the Browns need to figure out how to add more depth at the position next offseason.
The good news is that the Browns don’t need to add a high-level tight end since they have Fannin. But they should look for additional blocking tight ends so Fannin can focus more on the passing game instead of having to stay in to chip-block. It’s also important to have tight ends who can contribute in the running game.
Expect the Browns to sign a veteran tight end in free agency and to draft one in the first four rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft.
The Browns faced challenges coming into the season, particularly on defense, after trading away the NFL's best pass rusher, Myles Garrett, to the Rams and getting Jared Verse in the deal. Verse performed solidly during his two seasons with Los Angeles, recording 12 sacks in 34 games. But this season, he has yet to register a single sack in nine games.
Additionally, the Browns' second-best pass rusher entering the season was expected to be Alex Wright, who unfortunately tore his Achilles during training camp.
Cleveland will need to address the pass rusher position in the offseason. The Browns may consider making a move in the first or second round of the draft and could also sign a veteran free agent at a lower cost.
The Browns have two strong starting linebackers in Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, but like their tight end position, there isn’t much depth behind them. If the Browns lose Schwesinger or Williams for any length of time during the season, the defense could take a significant hit.
They have struggled to stop the run in recent weeks, allowing an average of 130.6 rushing yards per game, which ranks among the worst in the NFL.
Cleveland needs to add more depth at linebacker. This would let it use three or even four linebacker sets at times to improve its chances of stopping the run game.

title: Browns' Jared Verse Opens Up On Health Questions Amid Strugglesome 2026 Season
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season h as not been kind to Cleveland Browns edge rusher Jared Verse.
After joining the team this past offseason in a blockbuster trade with the Los Angeles Rams, the expectations were set high for Verse, especially with the Browns giving up future Hall of Famer Myles Garrett in the process.
But through the first nine weeks of the season, Verse has struggled greatly.
On Thursday, Nov. 12, he gave an update on where his health was at and if it was affecting his play at all, while also giving Browns fans some grace on their frustrations with him.
"I am upset with the way I have been playing," he said. "I don't think it is anything physical. There's nothing wrong with my body. I don't think it is anything like that. I think it is the mental aspect of the game, and I think I attacked it."
If the 26-year-old had been dealing with some sort of injury, it would have made sense to see him with just 20 combined tackles and four for a loss.
But instead, it looks like it is just something upstairs he is trying to work through.
"I think it was definitely a mental block," he said. "I train my body every day to push myself to the limits of what I am physically capable of doing...I think I have taken the steps to figure out what it was after meeting with a couple of people and everything like that."
Verse went on to defend Browns fans who have been frustrated with his lack of productivity, as the criticism that has come his way as of late has been heavy.
"...We can be here all day, and I can talk to you about each key play we have played all season... It is just simple to say the Browns fans are upset about it; I am upset about it; we all have a reason to be upset about it," he said about Browns fans being upset with his play. "I just haven't done enough, and I think that I have taken the time to figure out what the issue was and attacked it. I think I am ready for this week."
Whether or not he wants to admit it, that likely is also playing a part in his mental state. Having to fill such big shoes that Garrett once had in Cleveland is a tough task, and with his slow start to the year, his lack of production has to be weighing on him.
Either way, Cleveland needs the 2024 Defensive Rookie of the Year to return to that dominant form he once displayed, not just to show that the trade wasn't a complete flop on the Browns' end, but also to help guide this team to a playoff spot in the back half of the season.
The Browns return to the field on Sunday, Nov. 14, from Huntington Bank Field against the Houston Texans. The two sides play at 1:00 p.m. EST.
Against a dynamic and mobile quarterback like CJ Stroud, all eyes will be on how Verse can disrupt their passing attack.

title: Inside Browns 2027 NFL Draft Plan After a Quiet Trade Deadline
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has passed, and the Cleveland Browns did not make a single move despite a couple of glaring holes in the roster.
With the likelihood of Deshaun Watson getting a new contract in the offseason, the Browns are set to make most roster upgrades in the 2027 NFL Draft
The good news for Cleveland is that they are coming off of back-to-back incredible draft classes, and have 11 total picks in 2027.
Let's take a way too early look at a potential draft plan for the Browns next year.
As it stands, the Browns not only have their own first-round pick, but also the one from the Los Angeles Rams thanks to this summer's blockbuster Myles Garrett trade.
While there is still lots of season left, it looks like the Browns won't have a top 10 pick despite the two selections.
Looking at the needs, the Browns could use Tackle, Edge, and Cornerback. Depending on where they end up, we could see these picks used at best available.
But don't be shocked if one first is used on a quarterback.
For the past few years, the 2027 NFL draft class has been hyped up as "one of the best", and is headlined by multiple QBs.
Once again, if the fit is there, espescially with two firsts, it may not be the most shocking thing if the Browns try and find their franchise guy.
🚨 TRADE 🚨 #Chiefs get: • #6 overall #Browns get: • #9 overall • #74 overall • #148 overall
Over the past two drafts, Browns General Manager Andrew Berry has made numerous trades.
In 2026, he gave up pick number six to gain a third-rounder from Kansas City, only to move back three spots. The Browns ended up still getting their guy, Spencer Fano, whom they would have drafted at six.
Looking into round two, the Browns had one selection and used it on Denzel Boston. This was until Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was still available at pick 58, which Andrew Berry traded up into to select the safety out of Toledo.
So what does this mean for 2027?
Having two first-round picks gives Cleveland endless possibilities. If they really have their eyes set on a guy, they could package both picks to move up and take him.
On the opposite side of the boat, Berry could once again trade back and grab assets for either later in the draft or in drafts to follow in later years.
The Browns really don't need many more "generational talents".
Instead, they really could have used some trades to bolster weak positions like the Edge Rusher or Cornerback.
With that being said, trading picks for more experienced players is still on the table. However, the Browns will now have to wait until the 2026 season has concluded before they explore any of those options.

title: Browns Stood Still at Deadline, But Could Still Target These 2 Free Agents in 2027
full_text:
Well, it certainly wasn't a memorable 2026 NFL Trade Deadline for the Cleveland Browns.
After weeks of waiting to see what the Browns' front office would do at the deadline, the day came and went, and nothing was done . Not a single outgoing move or incoming addition, leaving just the same 53 guys that marched to a 5-4 record to try and create a playoff push in the second half of the season.
But that doesn't mean the Browns are a perfect squad. Honestly, they are far from it.
With holes on both sides of the ball, Cleveland obviously isn't in a contending spot, with the front office more inclined to carry their draft capital into the upcoming offseason.
Instead of making moves now, the Browns will likely explore what becomes available this offseason as a way to strengthen the group, especially considering the front office will have a much better feel of where big-time additions are needed.
Here are two 2027 NFL Free Agents the Browns could target this offseason:
Quenton Nelson ended up being traded at the deadline , going from the Indianapolis Colts to the Seattle Seahawks.
While Nelson is likely going to become a Hall of Famer by the time his career comes to a close, the Colts are actively entering a rebuilding period, and the contract Nelson is going to command is far greater than they feel comfortable paying.
If the Seahawks keep slipping down the NFC West standings, all while Nelson remains injured for the next couple of weeks, the two sides could call the deal a wash and part ways this offseason. After all, Seattle only gave up a third- and fifth-round pick, and if Nelson is asking too much money to be trusted after injury, he could enter the open market.
But that isn't something that should deter the Browns.
Instead, they should go in and make an offer for the 30-year-old to come to Cleveland.
For the past few years, the Browns have been trying to build the next era of an offensive line that was once anchored by the legendary Joe Thomas. While they seem to have two strong rookies in Austin Barber and Spencer Fano, they need someone to slide in and lead them.
Nelson would be the perfect fit, not just because of his experience and leadership, but because even if he takes a slight decline, he is a major upgrade to the Browns' lackluster group they currently have.
Quarterback Deshaun Watson is likely leaving this offseason, so the Browns will have much more flexibility in offering a free agent like Nelson a nice contract.
Whether or not the Browns really want to have a cornerback on their mind this offseason, they will have to.
Denzel Ward is continuing to age, all while Tyson Campbell and the rest of the squad continue to be rocky, Sunday-in and Sunday-out. The front office has attempted to build a relatively young, impressionable group over the past couple of years, but injuries and inconsistencies have broken up that group just as quickly as it formed.
This offseason, the Browns should make it a priority to at least sign one cornerback in free agency and take another in the 2027 NFL Draft.
In the case of free agency, Dallas Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant stands out as a big-time target.
Currently on a $5.5 million deal, Durant is expected to command a bigger deal after a one-year rental with the Cowboys. With where the market is right now, and based on his current play, the 28-year-old should see a three-to-four-year deal worth roughly $18-24 million in total. That would net him anywhere from $6-to-8 million a season.
Durant is having an okay season, making 10 tackles, two pass deflections and one forced fumble across five games, but has struggled to stay on the field due to injury.
As long as he finishes the year strong, he may be able to shoot that value up even more.
But as long as the price doesn't shoot too high, the Browns should look to sign Durant and make him one of the staples for the back half of Ward's career in the Orange and Brown.

title: Todd Monken Explains Comments on Shedeur Sanders and What That Means for the QB Position
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns cannot get out of their own way when it comes to quarterback controversies. Deshaun Watson cleared the concussion protocol before their game in New Orleans, but was still replaced by Shedeur Sanders. He led a fourth-quarter comeback that resulted in an overtime period where he marched the offense down for a touchdown.
However, Todd Monken would not commit to a starting quarterback for the next game until Wednesday.
During Sanders’ start, Monken told a sideline reporter that when he and Sanders were discussing which plays he wanted to run, Sanders requested plays that were not in the playbook. Monken had a playful tone that brought levity to the story, but that did not stop speculation that Sanders did not understand the offense.
Monken called for a quarterback competition between Watson and Sanders in training camp before eventually naming Watson the starter. He liked Watson’s “operations” of the offense and it was believed that Sanders needed more time to grasp the concepts. Sunday’s anecdote furthered that narrative.
#Browns HC Todd Monken was asked about the sideline report from Sunday's game regarding Monken joking about Shedeur Sanders suggesting things he liked that weren't in the playbook: "It's hilarious that it's gone this far. 'Shedeur, what do you like?' 'Well, I like this, this and… pic.twitter.com/0eNhUYeZfV
On Wednesday, Monken had an opportunity to clear the air on his game planning with Sanders. “I think it’s hilarious it’s gone this far,” Monken told the press. “I get a big kick out of it because it was really just a normal day-to-day of what a quarterback likes … It really isn’t a big deal.”
Monken chose to hand the offense to Watson instead of Sanders with just one game before the bye week. Watson’s late-game heroics had the Browns at 5-3, and Sanders’ play did not warrant a permanent change. The Browns are one seed out of the playoffs due to a tiebreaker.
The Houston Texans come to town in a crucial week for playoff implications.
The team is not interested in evaluating for the future, as they play in the now and the season is far from over. Monken is a first-time head coach, with any future opportunities very unlikely. He needs to gather as many wins as possible to prove his case to keep his job through tough times.
Starting Watson shows that Monken believes he gives them the best chance to win.
Monken has been open with the media and has been a stark contrast to previous head coaches. He tends to use bad phrasing as he speaks in the moment, and he clarified that any pre-game discussions did not factor into his decision to return to Watson.
The Browns need a win to start their four-game homestand to keep pace in the wild-card race.  He is most comfortable with Watson, as he has taken the first-team reps all year. They have struggled to run the ball the entire season, and his legs provide an opportunity to get anything going on the ground.
Watson may be on a short hook with the bye week looming . If they lose and Watson starts slowly again, they could make a change with the extra week of practice. This was reportedly the case in Week 2, but the team won, and Watson won enough games to keep his job.
Although the sideline report and the decision not to name a starter until Wednesday suggested a quarterback controversy, Monken made it clear that his only mission is to win.

title: 'The Intention Was For Deshaun To Start': Browns Open Up on Recent QB Decisions
full_text:
“I had no intention of Deshaun not being our starter."
All the speculation seems to have been for nothing.
Even though second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders showed up and showed out in a Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints in overtime , the Cleveland Browns never planned to give him another shot.
On Wednesday, Nov. 11, Browns head coach Todd Monken confirmed publicly that the plan was for Deshaun Watson to remain Cleveland's starter after he returned from concussion protocol.
"Everything you're considering, but ultimately Deshaun's done a really good job for us," he said in an X post from ESPN NFL Insider. "5-3 as a starter, and he's worked awfully hard to get back. There's a high belief in that ... the intention was for Deshaun to start. It's just when you come in on that Monday, you haven't really even met as a staff. You've just gone through the film, you've got with ownership and I just wanted to make sure we talked through as a staff, this is the way we're going forward.
"Great. That's all it was. It was pretty simple."
Todd Monken on if he gave real consideration to starting Shedeur Sanders this week: "Everything you're considering, but ultimately Deshaun's done a really good job for us. 5-3 as a starter, and he's worked awfully hard to get back. There's a high belief in that ... the intention… https://t.co/9HKHCzQKM1
Following Sunday's one-point loss, though, Monken's comments led to intense speculation, and understandably so. He had shared that he was not willing to talk about who the starting quarterback would be moving forward, which seemingly left the door open for Sanders.
He clarified why he said that on Wednesday.
"That was my intention," Monken said about eventually backing Watson. "I just wanted to make sure to run it by the staff before I said it publicly. I don't even know why I have to say it publicly, because it's really only our business in terms of who's going to play and who's not going to play. But he played well enough to still be our starter."
Monken: "That was my intention. I just wanted to make sure to run it by the staff before I said it publicly. I don't even know why I have to say it publicly, because it's really only our business in terms of who's going to play and who's not going to play. But he played well… https://t.co/9kHio8Vva4
This season, Watson has thrown for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions on a whopping 249 attempts. He has completed 65.5% of his passes , which is currently the fourth-best mark of his career across the last eight years.
While he still isn't looking like the former Houston Texans Pro Bowler, he is slowly but surely returning to that dynamic quarterback he once was.
On the ground, Watson has flashed his versatility, taking 51 carries for 217 yards and one score, which is the most since 2020.
If Cleveland really wants to get something out of Watson before his contract expires at the end of the year, continuing to let him thrive out on the gridiron is the best option. However, that would mean the Browns have some sort of belief that he will be around the team for the foreseeable future. Because why else would you then turn your back on the second-year Sanders?
Whatever is happening behind closed doors in the Browns' building has left a lot up for interpretation this season, especially at the quarterback position.
The only hope now is that Watson and the Browns don't waste the 2026 campaign and instead put together a strong push to make the playoffs.
The team returns to the field this weekend against the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland.
The two sides clash at 1:00 p.m. EST, with Watson getting a taste of his former side.
"It's a big opportunity for us to get back on the winning track, especially in front of our home fans," Watson said. "That's the ultimate focus is focus on that. On the outside things, going against my former team, that stuff was in the past. Four or five years ago, yeah, it was a big deal, but now I think both sides have moved on.
"We're just both trying to find ways to win and continue to put ourselves in position for later on down the road."

title: Browns Trade Deadline Update Sheds Light into Front Office's Decision To Stay Quiet
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline came and went.
And the Cleveland Browns remained quiet.
On Wednesday, Nov. 11, ESPN NFL Insider Jeremy Fowler released an update on where the Browns' headspace was at during the trade deadline. According to his report , the Browns were feeling out the market, but nothing ended up coming together by the time 4:00 p.m. EST rolled around.
The team was in the market for an extra edge rusher to pair with a squad that has been up-and-down this season, while also exploring the need for a blocking tight end.
Obviously, the Browns have one of the league's most exciting youngsters in Harold Fannin Jr., but he is better known for his pass-catching abilities and athleticism, not his ability to block. Landing a blocking tight end would have given him more flexibility and less strain on that end.
On the defensive side, Jared Verse takes most of the attention; however, he has struggled to begin the year. Adding another body across from him could have opened up more opportunities for him to get in the backfield.
According to @JFowlerESPN , the Browns “put out several feelers” for an extra edge rusher and blocking tight end, but nothing came together at the trade deadline. https://t.co/Nz8Pkt3jFh
"The Browns looked for an extra edge rusher and a blocking tight end and put out several feelers, but nothing came together," Fowler's report read . "This was the rare cycle in which Cleveland did not make a move."
And the latter is correct.
In recent years, the Browns' decisions to trade away wide receiver Amari Cooper in 2024 and trade for edge rusher Za'Darius Smith in 2023 stand out as team-altering moves. Cooper obviously went on to decline over the next few years due to age, but he could still have served a purpose in Cleveland, while Smith would end up becoming a nice complement to the Browns' pass rush.
Even if the Browns had shipped a few players out as they had in the past, with all four quarterbacks and wideout Jerry Jeudy being rumored to be on the block, it would have made things interesting.
But if the front office were really interested in shaking things up, they would have.
As Fowler mentioned, feelers being sent out shows that they were at least exploring different options and trade targets, but nothing coming to fruition means that either their own or others' values weren't met.
No trades for #Browns + a review of their 23-22 OT loss to the #Saints with @LanceReisland . What went wrong on the 2-point try? Did Shedeur Sanders give Todd Monken something to think about? What's going on the the defense late in games and more! WATCH: https://t.co/wLd95Bm9WS
Instead, the Browns are just going to keep the locker room intact and see if the 5-4 record through the first nine weeks was a fluke or not.
They did end up adding two players to the practice squad, increasing a bit of the depth, but neither is an eye-popping move. They signed tight end Zaire Mitchell-Paden and punter Wes Pahl, releasing tight end John FitzPatrick and defensive tackle Eric Johnson II in the process.
The #Browns have signed TE Zaire Mitchell-Paden and P Wes Pahl to the practice squad. The team also released TE John FitzPatrick and DT Eric Johnson II from the practice squad.
Neither are expected to play a big impact on the 53-man roster, but if injuries arise they may get a chance to play on Sundays.
Looking to put a Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints behind them, the Browns will look to chase the top spot in the AFC North this weekend when they meet up against the Houston Texans.
The two sides will play at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland.

title: Cowboys QB Dak Prescott Calls Out DeMarvion Overshown After Foolish Penalty
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys came away with a much-needed 27-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 9 at Lucas Oil Stadium despite nearly blowing another double-digit lead.
It was another up-and-down showing for Dallas, but despite all of the wackiness, the Cowboys came away victorious and kept themselves alive for the NFC East title and a playoff spot.
However, the win was preceded by a ton of interesting moments, some of which proved to be a microcosm of how dysfunctional the Cowboys have been this season.
Most notable among these was a bone-headed penalty from Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who ran onto the field in street clothes to celebrate a fumble recovery by Shemar James in the fourth quarter. It didn't end up costing Dallas in a significant way, but the optics of Overshown's mistake didn't sit well with Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott.
While speaking with reporters on Thursday ahead of Week 10's matchup with the San Francisco 49ers, Prescott didn't hesitate to admit that he was upset after witnessing Overshown's penalty against the Colts.
“I was pissed," Prescott said, per NFL insider Ed Werder. "I spoke my mind, and I don't think I've ever been short or shy in a moment when it's you know truly, truly bothered me. And yeah, that was just a big play … the turnover happened and a flag comes out andit's just like we did some great stuff here, let's not minimize it.”
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer met with Overshown to discuss his mistake. Overshown also apologized to his teammates.
While Prescott has never shied away from being the leader of the franchise and a guiding voice for his teammates, he's making it clear that he shouldn't have to speak up when it comes to avoiding obvious dumb mistakes that have nothing to do with the actual game.
Prescott didn't mention Overshown specifically, but in general, he feels that the NFL isn't the place for people that need their hand held.
“If you need to somebody to tell you what you should and shouldn't do I don't know if this is the business for you," Prescott said.
The truth hurts, and Prescott is right. Overshown has already faced enough criticism for constant injury issues that are due to no fault of his own, but his foolish penalty certainly didn't improve the public perception the Dallas fans have of him.
Hopefully Overshown can return from injury soon and redeem himself with production on the field for the Dallas defense.
