title: Detroit Lions Had 'Hard Conversations' With OL Christian Mahogany
full_text:
Detroit Lions left guard Christian Mahogany has accepted responsibility for breaking team rules and vowed to make it up to his teammates and the coaching staff.
Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, speaking to local reporters before the team departed for Germany, addressed his level of faith in the former sixth-round draft pick moving forward.
“I'm not going to speak to the specific conversation, but again, I think there are some hard conversations," said Petzing. "You’ve got to challenge some people, but I think he responded and was really pleased with the way he handled it and looking forward to see what he does going forward.”
Mahogany was benched against the Miami Dolphins after repeatedly violating team rules. Head coach Dan Campbell the decision had to be made, given he has clear expectations for the roster.
Despite missing a game, the expectation is Mahogany will return to the starting lineup against the New England Patriots.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Was 2026 Season Ruined Due to Brad Holmes Inactivity at Trade Deadline?
Petzing does not see the game off taking away from the 26-year-old's ability to produce at a high level this week and moving forward.
“I think one of the things he has done when he's been in there which has been great is he's played hard," said Petzing. "Hasn't always been perfect, but he's playing at a hundred miles an hour and I think that's so important up front.”
Mahogany was disappointed in himself, but understood what needed to occur moving forward to avoid further disciplinary actions. He has already spoken to Petzing, head coach Dan Campbell and offensive line coach Hank Fraley.
"I’m not going to either. I’m not going to disobey him," Mahogany said, via the team's social media channel. "It sucks what happened, but I have to grow up and I have to stop breaking team rules. It is what it is. I let my teammates down, I let my organization down and it won’t ever happen again."
He later added, "You just gotta eat it on the chin. That’s who I am. I’m not a person that’s gonna sulk. It sucked not being out there, because I let my teammates down. I don’t want to do that, I did, and that’s on me."

title: Spot the Ball: 10 Thoughts Ahead of Detroit Lions Matchup With Patriots
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are getting ready for an overseas journey and a marquee matchup.
On Sunday, while Lions fans in Detroit are waking up, the team will be getting set to take on the New England Patriots. Kickoff is set for 9:30 E.T., with the Lions as the dedicated home team for the game at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.
Here are 10 thoughts surrounding the Lions' Week 10 matchup with the Patriots.
Coming into Sunday's game, quarterback Drake Maye is tied for the NFL lead in interceptions with 11. As a result, the Lions' defense could be in a position to be opportunistic and take the ball away, setting their offense up in good field position in the process.
My eyes are on Brian Branch, who already has an interception to his name in the three games he's played this season. Because of his versatility, he could be in a position to take the ball away at some point throughout Sunday's game.
Since coming back from the Achilles injury that ended his season last year, Branch has looked increasingly comfortable over his three games. He played every snap last week, and looked capable of being a leader for the defense that is missing one of its captains.
The Lions will be playing their first game on foreign soil since 2015, as they have only played two overseas games prior to Sunday. Both were in London, and they took place in back-to-back years starting in 2014.
In their first appearance overseas, that 2014 game against the Atlanta Falcons, they were able to rally and stage a thrilling comeback victory. They won that game 22-21 thanks to a last-second field goal from Matt Prater.
The following year, the Lions returned to Wembley Stadium and took on the Kansas City Chiefs. The results were not as favorable that time, as they were defeated 45-10 by the Chiefs.
The Patriots have dominated the history between these two teams, with the Lions winning just two of those matchups since 2000. Much of that time was in the Tom Brady era, a likely first-ballot Hall of Fame quarterback who led the Patriots from 2001-19.
Detroit defeated New England in November of 2000, and again on Sunday Night Football in 2018 for Matt Patricia's first win as the team's head coach. However, the Patriots won the other five meetings in that time frame leading up to this season.
If the Lions were to win on international soil, it would be a big win and their fifth in a row. A five-game win streak would be the longest for Detroit since the 2024 season, when they ripped off 11 wins in a row.
The Lions did make one trade at the deadline, and while there will be ire for the lack of aggressiveness, general manager Brad Holmes did add some depth in the secondary by acquiring Andre Cisco.
The former New York Jet will provide depth at the safety position, and has experience both playing as a free safety as well as in the box. He could pair nicely with Brian Branch, or supplement Branch by working some in the box in certain packages.
It appears likely that Cisco will make his Lions debut on Sunday and make the trip to Germany with the team.
The performance of Drake Maye has been a huge storyline for the Patriots throughout the season. For a player who finished second in MVP voting last year, the showing through the first eight games has been less than stellar.
Through three games, Maye had just one touchdown pass against six interceptions. While he has rebounded somewhat, his turnover numbers remain jarring after he threw eight interceptions all of last season.
Maye is coming off a disastrous first half performance against Green Bay, where he threw three interceptions before the break before bouncing back in the second half.
If the Lions want to continue their recent stretch of strong defensive play, keeping Maye uncomfortable is a good place to start. In addition to his 11 interceptions, he has also been sacked 20 times and has struggled with consistency.
The NFC North has been the best division in football up to this point in the season. All four teams are at least three games over .500, with the Chicago Bears leading the way at 7-2. Detroit is right behind them along with Minnesota as both teams are 6-2, while the Packers sit in fourth at 6-3.
Part of the reason the division has been so good is how well they've handled opponents outside the division. Through Week 9, the NFC North is 20-4 against teams outside of their own division. Ironically, two of those losses belong to the Lions, who are the only undefeated team in divisional play.
Meanwhile, the Bears are 7-0 against teams outside the division, but have yet to win a game within the NFC North. If the Lions are going to keep pace in the divisional race, they need to keep up with their peers and continue handling business against teams outside the North.
Detroit got a spike in production from rookie Derrick Moore , who recorded the first two sacks of his NFL career against Miami. Moore saw an increased workload with DJ Wonnum ruled out, and even with Wonnum potentially finding his way back into the mix on Sunday Moore has made a claim for more snaps.
Elsewhere on the injury front, Dan Campbell said Wednesday that D.J. Reed and Cade Mays both have small chances of playing, while Kerby Joseph will wait at least one more week for his debut.
If Mays and Reed are both unable to play, it will mean another start for Juice Scruggs at center and more opportunities for the likes of Rock Ya-Sin and Ennis Rakestraw alone with Roger McCreary at cornerback.
The Lions are one of the NFL's most popular teams in Germany, and the local fans will be hoping to see them put on a show. In their best-case scenario, the offense finishes the first drive with a touchdown as opposed to a field goal, setting the tone with an explosive play early.
Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams are both actively involved in the offense, while Jared Goff keeps the ball moving with crisp passes to both as well as Sam LaPorta. As with any Lions game that goes according to plan, Jahmyr Gibbs feasts in the second half and grinds away the clock in a comfortable win.
While Maye has struggled in his third NFL season up to this point, he still has the arm talent to make a defense pay. With Reed potentially out, the Patriots could make the Lions secondary pay through the air.
If the Lions are inconssistent on offense, it puts more pressure on the defense. While Kelvin Sheppard's defense has been solid as of late, they could revert back to their early season ways in this worst-case scenario.
Ultimately, if the Lions start slow and allow New England to build a two-score lead, they would struggle to get enough stops to give their offense a chance to come back late.
Sunday's game will be a homecoming of sorts for Amon-Ra St. Brown, whose mother was born in Germany. He has developed a strong reputation in the country, which has fans excited to watch him live in action on Sunday.
Because of the strong ties he has to the area, I think the Lions will do everything they can to have him have a big game. They've shown some interesting looks for St. Brown in recent weeks with coordinator Drew Petzing, and he could have another big day in store.
It won't be easy, but I believe the Lions will ultimately scheme up a way for St. Brown to approach double-digit catches, and as a result he could go over 150 yards against the Patriot defense.

title: Odds Detroit Lions Beat New England Patriots in Week 10
full_text:
The Detroit Lions travel overseas to take on the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, on Sunday morning (9:30 a.m. EST).
The Patriots, which are off to a 5-4 start, are coming off a 45-27 defeat at the hands of Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. Meanwhile, the Lions, which are sitting at 6-2, defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9, in their Week 9 tilt .
New England – led by Mike Vrabel on the sidelines – has lost two of its last three games, including to the Chicago Bears in Week 7. Additionally, it sits basically in the middle of the pack in both points scored (23.4/game) and points allowed (23.0/g).
Yet, the Patriots still possess a myriad of talent on both sides of the ball.
On offense, they're led under center by third-year passer Drake Maye, who has thrown for 18 touchdowns, 2,282 yards and a league-high 11 interceptions through nine games. He's coming off a three-interception performance against the Packers in which he completed a season-low 55.3 percent of his passes.
Maye's top target this year has been veteran tight end Hunter Henry, who has amassed 32 catches, 361 yards and two touchdowns through the season's first nine games. And on the ground, the Patriots are spearheaded by sixth-year back Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson, a fourth-round pick of New England, has accumulated 399 yards and two touchdowns, and is presently averaging 3.9 yards per carry.
Then, on the defensive side of the ball, the Patriots have received strong performances this season from the likes of EDGE defenders Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder, cornerback Carlton Davis III and linebacker Christian Elliss.
Ponder, a second-year pro , has already recorded 7.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss and 13 QB hits, and has returned a fumble for a touchdown. And for his efforts, he's earned a 75.0 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, the 23rd-best overall grade among 110 qualified players at the position.
The Patriots will not, however, have the services of Davis (knee) for this Week 10 international affair. Plus, they will also be down starting left guard Ben Brown (knee), and are expected to be without Stevenson (knee). Stevenson, the team's No. 1 back, suffered a plantaris tendon tear last week against the Packers.
Those are three significant losses for Vrabel's squad going into its matchup with Detroit.
As for the Lions, they will also be down multiple starters in Week 10: linebacker Jack Campbell (neck), center Cade Mays (ankle) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip). Plus, safety Kerby Joseph, who has yet to play a single game in 2026, will not be making his season debut in Germany.
While both teams are rather significantly banged up, I still believe this matchup favors Detroit.
At this present juncture, I believe the Lions have a 59 percent chance to secure their fifth straight victory.

title: Detroit Lions Draw Lenient Official For Second Time This Season
full_text:
The officiating crew for the Detroit Lions ' Week 10 game against the New England Patriots in Munich has been revealed.
When the Lions take the field at 9:30 a.m. E.T., their game will be reffed by Clay Martin and his crew. It will be Martin's second Lions game of the season, with the first being their Week 4 loss to the Carolina Panthers.
In that game, there were 17 penalties with nine on the Panthers and eight on the Lions. Detroit was penalized for four false starts, a defensive pass interference, an offensive holding and two delay of game penalties during the loss.
Martin is coming off a Week 9 game where he threw a career-high in penalty flags with 23 penalties between the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys. It was the first game where his crew had called 20 or more penalties, as he hadn't had a game with more than 17 up to that point.
The veteran official has actually presided over two games where there have been less than 10 total penalties. For the season, his crew ranks fifth amongst all officiating crews in terms of penalties called.
However, that number is skewed by the fact that he hasn't had a bye week yet, as his per-game count of 13.44 is fifth-lowest. As a result, it can be inferred that Martin's crew could be a bit more lenient for Sunday's international contest. Martin ranks sixth in the league in dismissed flags per game at 2.56.
Martin's two most frequent whistles are for offensive holding and false start. He has called 29 offensive holding penalties, and 22 false starts. As a result, it can be inferred that there will be plenty of eyes on the line of scrimmage in Sunday's game.
Detroit is tied-for-18th in offensive holding penalties this year with 12, which equates to 1.5 a game through the eight games they've played this year. As for false starts, the Lions are tied-for-seventh in the league with 15.
New England is just ahead of Detroit in holding penalties with 14, while they have had less false start penalties with 12.
The Lions are now 5-6 with Martin as the head official in his career after the loss to the Panthers earlier this season.

title: Detroit Lions QB Jared Goff Surprisingly Lands on Week 10 Injury Report
full_text:
Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff surprisingly popped up on the initial Week 10 injury report.
Goff was listed as limited due to a chest injury. Others listed as non-participants included Cade Mays, D.J. Reed and Sione Vaki. There is no indication the 32-year-old will miss the game in Germany.
Following a victory against the Miami Dolphins, the coaching staff decided to conduct a walkthrough practice on Wednesday at the teams Allen Park Performance Center.
The participation levels reported are an estimate of a players participation level, had the practice been traditionally conducted.
Others limited included Amon-Ra St. Brown, Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch.
Detroit's offensive line had their struggles early in the Week 9 contest against the AFC East squad. Miles Frazier did not have the best showing in his first appearance this season as a starter.
The former No. 1 overall pick was subjected to early hits , as Miami's defense brought pressure and were also able to able to secure an interception.
“Yeah, just settle in a little bit. I thought they did a good job up front applying some of that pressure and forcing a turnover," said Goff. "I wish I would have eaten that probably or checked it down, probably would have served us better there. But yeah, they did a good job, and I thought we just settled in eventually and started running the ball well, had those two explosives back-to-back on that one drive.”
Goff credited the defense postgame for keeping the team in the game, as the offense struggled to find the end zone.
“They've been playing so well," Goff said. "They deserve so much credit and figuring it out and going through the storm that they were going through early on, and now playing at such an elite level. And really keeping us in these games and allowing us to kind of find our footing at times, certainly today, they deserve so much credit.”

title: Arrogance of Detroit Lions GM Brad Holmes May Be His Ultimate Downfall
full_text:
Detroit Lions GM Brad Holmes proved various fans and pundits right on Tuesday; he chose to stand pat at the NFL trade deadline instead of upgrading multiple positions of need, particularly on defense.
To be fair, Holmes did acquire N.Y. Jets safety Andre Cisco on Monday. However, the 26-year-old is much more of a solid depth piece than an impact-level defensive back. Consequently, he's not the type of defender who's going to take Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit to the next level.
Holmes direly needed to come out of the deadline with more than just a thrift store-esque acquisition like Cisco. He had several holes to plug across the defensive side of the ball, which were made even more glaring by the recent injuries to cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) and linebacker Jack Campbell (neck). Plus, you can easily argue that Detroit's once again void of a reliable EDGE counterpart for Pro Bowler Aidan Hutchinson, especially with DJ Wonnum being sidelined.
Yet, Holmes decided that the Lions’ roster, as currently structured, is good enough as is. That, to me, was a miscalculation of epic proportions by the sixth-year GM.
Holmes' contract with the Lions ends following the conclusion of the 2027 season. He may earn an extension this summer, but if the team fails to make a deep run in the postseason, it is certain his seat will be getting warmer and warmer.
Fans are not interested in being teased, especially at the current exuberant price of season tickets.
Sure, the Lions are on a four-game win streak, which has certainly been aided by the improved play of the defense. However, that does not mean Sheppard's unit is going to remain productive the rest of the 2026 campaign. More than likely, that's not going to be the case, and I'm willing to predict it will have some hiccups in the weeks ahead, including against Ben Johnson's NFC North-leading Chicago Bears.
It furthers the reason why Holmes should have done everything in his power to add reinforcements to that side of the ball, no matter the valuable draft capital it may have cost.
If Holmes would have been serious about upgrading Detroit's 53-man roster, he would have made an ultra aggressive pursuit of impact defenders like Miami Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks and L.A. Chargers EDGE Khalil Mack. But, did he? No, at least per the reports that came out in the hours leading up to the deadline.
And think about it, Brooks and Mack are exactly the type of difference-making talents that could have elevated the play of Sheppard's unit. However, another deadline came and went where Holmes & Co. erroneously decided that they're all good.
And because of such, the Lions will now be reliant upon a variety of depth pieces – e.g. defensive backs Roger McCreary and Rock Ya-Sin and linebackers Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske – in their attempt to catapult the Bears for the NFC North crown . That's hardly a recipe for success.
Once again, Holmes has fallen victim to the “smartest man in the room” syndrome, impeding the Lions’ efforts to take the next step as a franchise.
Detroit does not possess a Super Bowl-caliber roster, and it only has one person to blame for that being the case: Brad Holmes.

title: Detroit Lions Injury Updates: DJ Wonnum, D.J. Reed, Cade Mays
full_text:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell provided health updates on key defenders DJ Wonnum and D.J. Reed, as well as center Cade Mays, ahead of the teams Week 10 contest against the New England Patriots.
The former NFL tight end said Wonnum will participate in practice on Wednesday afternoon. Barring any setbacks, the veteran defender should be ready to play this week against the AFC East powerhouse.
Mays and Reed are considered doubtful at best for the game set to take place overseas in Germany.
When asked, the sixth-year head man said left guard Christian Mahogany will be back with the starters along the offensive line at practice today.
Appearing on 97.1 The Ticket earlier this week, Campbell indicated he needed to stand by his word when addressing the rules broken on multiple times by the former sixth-round draft pick.
Mahogany did not play any offensive snaps against the Dolphins, as he was disciplined for violating team rules.
"Look, if you say you’re gonna do something, you better hold up to it, otherwise you’re gonna lose respect of the people around you," said Campbell. "Because if I’m sitting in that seat and I say one thing and then I don’t do it, I would immediately lose respect for that person. So we stick by what we say we’re gonna do here."
Quarterback Jared Goff noted, following the Lions 19-9 victory against Miami, how their Week 9 opponent stifled the offense in the first half, prior to adjustments being made.
“I thought defensively, I thought they did a good job against us and played with good depth, made us keep the ball underneath. I thought they rushed really well and tackled really well," said Goff. "They did a good job, and we certainly had our opportunities to blow it open a little bit earlier than that and didn't take advantage of them. Some self-inflicted wounds, some penalties pre-snap and took us a minute to get going there, obviously, but when we did, did enough to win."
Goff later added, "It has been six different ways and four in a row now in four different ways, and that's the hallmark of a good team is when you're able to find different ways to win repeatedly and just sticking in it. Defense played well, I thought, all day, but I can only speak for us offensively. Like just one more time, chop wood one more time, chop wood one more time. It doesn't matter who you're playing, what their record is, this is NFL and they were giving us all we could handle . We just kept chopping wood, kept chopping wood and felt good about the way we finished it.”
Coach Campbell with injury updates on DJ Wonnum, D.J. Reed and Cade Mays. pic.twitter.com/frXwqG6c1a

title: 4 Winners, 2 Losers After 2026 Detroit Lions Trade Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has come and gone.
For the Detroit Lions , the hours leading up to the deadline saw the addition of former New York Jets safety Andre Cisco. Now in his sixth NFL season, Cisco has logged valuable experience playing multiple spots in the secondary for the Jets and Jacksonville Jaguars.
Detroit's inactivity otherwise left the fan base wanting more, as the team did not address its needs at the cornerback and linebacker position. In particular, the team elected to not add a linebacker after the injury to Jack Campbell.
Here are winners and losers from the Lions' trade deadline decisions.
Detroit's defensive coordinator has his group trending up over the team's four-game winning streak. They capped off this recent run of success with a strong performance in which they didn't allow a touchdown against the Dolphins.
Now, he gets another option in the secondary with Cisco that he can utilize in a number of different ways. It adds more depth to the group, and could also allow him to be flexible with the usage of players like Keith Abney II and Brian Branch.
While the Lions didn't make a splash addition at the cornerback or linebacker spot like some believed they would, Sheppard ultimately got another playmaker that could help the defense.
Because the Lions didn't add a big name cornerback , Rakestraw and company will likely continue to be utilized in a rotation. Rakestraw's playing time has been up-and-down at points this year, but he has worked into a pretty stable role since the Lions went to a rotation in Week 7 against Green Bay.
Now in his third season, Rakestraw has already logged a career-high in defensive snaps played and has shown flashes of being the player Detroit hoped he'd be when they drafted him in the second-round of the 2024 draft.
With no new faces joining the cornerback room, Rakestraw will continue to get opportunities to prove himself in what is a pivotal third season.
With Jack Campbell's injury being a dominant headline over the last week, the Lions were believed to be in the mix to fortify their linebacker room. However, they elected to stand pat and this is a vote of confidence in the Oklahoma State product.
Rodriguez played a season-high in snaps on Sunday, which was the first game without Campbell, and will presumably continue to play a big role for Detroit's defense moving forward.
Furthermore, the addition of K.J. Britt off the Patriots' practice squad feels like more of an upgrade on special teams, so Britt's presence may not cut into Rodriguez's workload even as he acclimates more to the scheme.
There were questions about whether or not the Lions may be willing to listen to trade offers for LaPorta amidst what appears to be a contract standoff. LaPorta has made his desire to get a hefty contract public, and because the Lions haven't done that deal it appeared as though they thought they would be willing to consider a potential blockbuster.
However, reports Monday indicated that the Lions in fact were not willing to listen to these offers and instead still have plans of getting a long-term extension done. This means a pay-day could be coming from the Lions for the talented tight end, even if it's not right away.
Joseph has already been ruled out for the Lions' Week 10 game against New England, which will push the decision of whether or not to activate him right up to the 21-day deadline of his return to practice window.
The safety, who led the NFL in interceptions in 2024 and was a First Team All-Pro selection that year, still hasn't played this season and his long-term future remains in doubt at this point.
He could certainly wind up playing a role for Detroit at some point this season, but the addition of Cisco generates questions about just how impactful he'll be.
Izien has seen his role diminish on the defensive end, with Abney taking some of his safety reps as well as Branch getitng back into the mix. With Cisco now in the fold, it's hard to imagine Izien finding a role on the defensive side of the ball barring an injury.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: Grading Lions NFL Trade Deadline: Did Brad Holmes Ruin 2026 Team?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions made one move before the NFL trade deadline.
On Monday, the Lions swung a deal to acquire defensive back Andre Cisco from the New York Jets. While the move is intriguing, many believed that an additional move could be coming to help fortify their defense in particular.
Ultimately, the Lions elected to stand pat aside from the Cisco trade and elected to not make another move before the 4 p.m. deadline on Tuesday. This came as something of a surprise given how active other teams in the mix were.
As the Lions look to make a push for a third NFC North title in four years and a return to the postseason, their relative inactivity at the deadline appears to be a vote of confidence in their roster along with the addition of Cisco.
Around them, the San Francisco 49ers, Minnesota Vikings, Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks were all active in making moves prior to the deadline. The 49ers added a defensive end in De'Forest Buckner, the Vikings added a quarterback in Kirk Cousins, the Bears brought in defensive lineman Jeffrey Simmons and the Seahawks bolstered their offensive line with Quinten Nelson.
Now, the Lions will be tasked with running the divisional gauntlet with Cisco providing defensive depth. It will be interesting to see where Cisco fits within their secondary, as Brian Branch is back in the fold and Kerby Joseph is working toward a return.
Cisco has experience playing both as a box safety and a free safety, so he will provide valuable depth even if Joseph is able to return and play at a high level. Joseph won't play against New England in Week 10, meaning the Lions will have to activate him before their Week 11 game or elect to keep him on the Physically Unable to Perform list for the remainder of the season.
Detroit could also elect to activate Joseph and keep him as an inactive if they don't feel that he's able to play right away. Still, Cisco will give them some options even with Branch and veteran Chuck Clark both playing well.
The Lions didn't make the flashiest move at the deadline amongst their NFC counterparts, and these big trade deadline moves have mixed results over the past several seasons.
Additionally, the Lions have a need at the linebacker position after Jack Campbell suffered a significant injury. He leaves a big hole in terms of production as an All-Pro a season ago, and many believed the Lions could be looking to add a linebacker moving forward.
However, they elected not to and thus provided a vote of confidence in the likes of Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske.
Because of how valuable Campbell was to Detroit's defense, the Lions may wind up regretting not adding an option to the linebacker room.
It's hard to call the Lions' decisions at the deadline an abject failure. Their biggest need was the cornerback position, and there wasn't a single cornerback dealt at the deadline. Joey Porter Jr. was the only cornerback traded in season, while the others who were believed to be on the market ultimately remain with their current teams.
Because there wasn't a market for players at Detroit's biggest position of need, it appears as though the Lions made the right move holding on to their valuable draft capital. They were able to make an addition that will help them moving forward, but didn't make the level of splash that a team like the Bears did.
Ultimately, the roster as constructed has been good enough to win two divisional games amidst a 6-2 start. Their cards are now on the table, and it's up to Dan Campbell's team to prove their leadership right.

title: Packers-Vikings Thursday Injury Report: Three Promising Updates for Green Bay
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Javon Bullard, the Green Bay Packers’ standout nickel defender, missed a second consecutive day of practice on Thursday. Does that put his status for Sunday’s showdown against the Minnesota Vikings in doubt?
“I ain’t missing no game. I ain’t missing no game, man,” Bullard said after practice. “I care about this team. I care about my brothers, man. So, I’m definitely going to play Sunday. For sure.”
After the team conducted a job-through practice on Wednesday, Bullard was one of five starters who did not practice on Thursday – the big workday of the week with the players in pads.
The Packers lost to the Vikings in Week 1 but enter Sunday’s game having won five of their last six games to improve to 6-3. The Vikings started 6-0 but have lost two consecutive games, though they acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins on Tuesday to perhaps right the ship.
“I think, honestly, that’s a good football team over there,” Bullard said. “They well coached and got a lot of good players. I think they’re out of rhythm right now, just truthfully from what we’re seeing on film, and I think we got to capitalize on it. I think we got to capitalize on them not being in-sync right now.
“I think offensively it’s all about rhythm. If you clicking and moving on the offensive side of the ball, it’s really all about rhythm. Because at one point of time, our offense wasn’t clicking and now look at them. So, it’s all about rhythm. We know they got the players to do so. I think it’s all about one play at a time, dialing into our job and doing what we need to do. We don’t take them lightly at all. That’s a good football team over there, despite their offensive struggles and recent happenings, but that’s a great football team there so we can’t take them lightly.”
Along with Bullard’s optimism, kicker Trey Smack progressed from limited participation to full participation due to an injured right calf. He was the only change on the injury report.
Finally, with the team working in pads, Micah Parsons was on the field. The plan was for him to be integrated into team drills this week. That happened, as Tucker Kraft happened to mention when talking about the growth of the offense.
Micah Parsons races Dani Dennis-Sutton. pic.twitter.com/Ibaf1Ss4dG
“I'd say our offensive line, for sure. We've come together as a unit a lot more – a lot more gel now with these reps and some of the guys we brought in,” Kraft said. “Going to get Sean (Rhyan) back soon, but John (Williams has) been playing great. I'd say our defense right now is on a roll, and we're awaiting the comeback of Micah.”
And then came the money line.
“It's been good out there pressing against Micah. Took on a bull rush from him today. He's trying to back me into Jordan (Love's) lap. … No comment. Maybe it was a stalemate. I'm going to say it's a stalemate. Yeah, he'll be making his return soon. He's looking great, but our defense is rolling, and we just hope that they can remain consistent.”
Along with Bullard, linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and edge Lukas Van Ness (back) did not practice. Those five players aren’t just starters but important starters.
Franklin, who was inactive for the last three games, and Rhyan, who was inactive the last two games, would seem to be long shots to get ready for Sunday given their extended absences. Jacobs will have surgery on Friday, at which point the team will have a more definitive timeline.
The wild card is Van Ness; coach Matt LaFleur gave him a chance to practice on Thursday. That didn’t happen, obviously, but it signals that he is perhaps close.
Josh Jacobs won’t play, but the expectation is Chris Brooks will be activated from injured reserve.
That will be a key return. He’s carved out his niche in the NFL as a pass-protecting back, and that obviously will be vital against a Vikings defense that will blitz from the first game to the last.
However, Kaleb Johnson gave the Packers a breakthrough rushing performance against the Patriots, when MarShawn Lloyd was inactive with a knee injury. Lloyd isn’t on the injury report this week. Plus, Pierre Strong’s versatility has been an asset.
“I think the running game, especially the later you go in the season, the more important it is,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “As the weather turns, especially at home, you better be able to run the football.”
MarShawn Lloyd is not on the injury report. pic.twitter.com/dsfjl3UgvF
One of the Vikings’ best players, linebacker Blake Cashman, did not practice against due to a concussion.
Cashman was one of four Vikings who did not practice. Tight end T.J. Hockenson, defensive end Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins and safety Theo Jackson were the others. Versatile backup Kyle Van Noy did not practice, either.
Their injury report was unchanged from Wednesday.
Thursday's #Vikings injury report pic.twitter.com/DIuwcsd49i
Did not participate: S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), LB Zaire Franklin (shin), RB Josh Jacobs (finger), C Sean Rhyan (ankle), edge Lukas Van Ness (back), TE Josh Whyle (concussion).
Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/hip), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), G/T Travis Glover (knee), LB Ty’Ron Hopper (illness), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), WR Savion Williams (groin), G Kevin Zeitler (ankle).
Full participation: WR Bo Melton (gameday concussion evaluation), K Trey Smack (right calf).
Note: Brooks, Moore and Parsons have been designated to return and are within their 21-day practice window.
Same as yesterday, Packers not practicing today: Bullard Jacobs Franklin Rhyan Whyle Van Ness Here is Micah Parsons. pic.twitter.com/xHScvBXWhK
Did not participate: LB Blake Cashman (concussion), TE T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest), DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), WR Jauan Jennings (calf), QB Kyler Murray (hamstring), OLB Kyle Van Noy (calf).
Limited participation: S Jay Ward (knee), QB Carson Wentz (ankle).
Full participation: S Theo Jackson (quad).

title: Packers Thursday Update From Practice: Parsons, Smack, OL, Injured Starters
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – With the biggest game of the season looming on Sunday, the Green Bay Packers kicked off Vikings Week with a season-high 16 players on the injury report. Five of those players are starters.
Plus, rookie kicker Trey Smack was among a long list of players who were listed as limited participation on Wednesday. Smack is dealing with an injured right calf, but coach Matt LaFleur was not concerned.
“Not on what I saw yesterday,” LaFleur said before practice on Thursday. “He went out there and did a good job, so I think he should be full go today.”
The Packers did not have a true practice on Wednesday. If they would have, five starters would not have participated. At Thursday’s practice:
Edge Lukas Van Ness (back), who leads the team in sacks, worked in the rehab group but was not on the field for the start of practice.
“Potentially,” LaFleur said when asked if Van Ness would practice. “We’ll try to loosen him up and see where he’s at.”
S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee) also stretched but did not go out for practice. He played in every game last season and the first nine games of this season. He is fourth on the team with 43 tackles, tied for fifth with four tackles for losses and tied for second with seven passes defensed.
LB Zaire Franklin (shin) missed the last three games following an injury sustained at practice before the Detroit game. He did not practice and seems destined to miss another game.
With Edgerrin Cooper on injured reserve, Franklin inactive and Ty’Ron Hopper missing almost all the game with what was called a chest injury, the Packers essentially played last week with their No. 3 (Isaiah McDuffie) and No. 5 (Nick Niemann) linebackers. Hopper was limited participation on Wednesday – due to illness, not injury – and practiced again on Thursday.
C Sean Rhyan (ankle) went down during the opening series at Detroit, then missed the last two games. LaFleur called him “day-to-day” on Wednesday but he did not practice on Thursday. John Williams, presumably, will start again.
RB Josh Jacobs (finger) will have surgery on Friday, LaFleur said. That’s when the team will have a better handle on his timeline; the early indication is it was a “clean” break and he might be back after missing only two games.
Here’s Zeitler and Belton working a combo drill today. pic.twitter.com/zHrLGjgQbr
Jordan Morgan will start at left tackle, Anthony Belton will start at right tackle and John Williams probably will start at center.
What about the guard positions? Based on the start of practice, it might be Laken Tomlinson at left guard and Kevin Zeitler at right guard, though that comes with the enormous asterisk that whatever the team shows at practice might not be (and oftentimes has not been) the same as how the team lines up in the game.
“Interested to see how it plays out this week with Zeitler, Laken, all of that and just how that’ll shake out,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said on Tuesday. “That’s going to be big, but I like what I’ve seen from Zeitler in there. When he went in and played, he did a really nice job. So, it’ll be interesting to see how it plays out.”
Same as yesterday, Packers not practicing today: Bullard Jacobs Franklin Rhyan Whyle Van Ness Here is Micah Parsons. pic.twitter.com/xHScvBXWhK
Star edge rusher Micah Parsons went through drills with reporters present on Thursday. The goal was to have him take part in team drills this week; the Packers worked in full pads, so this would be a big day.
Parsons and running back Chris Brooks had their return-to-play window opened last week and receiver/returner Skyy Moore had his opened this week. They also were on the practice field.
“Well, he’s a big-time weapon, so if he’s able to go, that will definitely boost our returns, and then also we’ll see how we use him on offense,” LaFleur said of Moore.
The Vikings signed running back Damon Bankston to their practice squad. He served two stints on the Packers’ practice squad so might be willing to share a little intel.
On Wednesday, Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley explained why they reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins at Tuesday’s trade deadline.
“He made sense for a lot of reasons,” he said. “There's familiarity with the offense, with the organization, with the coaching staff. His level of play; his production to this season; and everything just aligned. The quarterback position is one that can impact the entire team, and this roster, in all honesty, has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing.”
The teams will release updated injury reports after they are done practicing on Thursday. Until then, here are the reports from Wednesday.
Packers Wednesday Injury Report
Did not participate: S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), LB Zaire Franklin (shin), RB Josh Jacobs (finger), C Sean Rhyan (ankle), edge Lukas Van Ness (back), TE Josh Whyle (concussion).
Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/hip), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), G/T Travis Glover (knee), LB Ty’Ron Hopper (illness), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), K Trey Smack (right calf), WR Savion Williams (groin), G Kevin Zeitler (ankle).

Note: Brooks, Moore and Parsons have been designated to return and are within their 21-day practice window.

Limited participation: S Jay Ward (knee), QB Carson Wentz (ankle).
Full participation: S Theo Jackson (quad).

title: Here Are Packers’ 2027 Draft Picks After Potential Double-Whammy
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers reaped the rewards from the excellent additions in their 2022 draft class, then hoped to benefit even further from their departures in free agency.
This past offseason, the Packers let linebacker Quay Walker, receiver Romeo Doubs and left tackle Rasheed Walker go in free agency. Along with quarterback Malik Willis, who provided two superlative seasons as the backup quarterback after being acquired for a seventh-round pick, the Packers hoped they’d benefit from four top compensatory picks.
It hasn’t quite worked out the way the Packers were hoping.
Willis, as expected, signed a big contract with the Dolphins in free agency. Based on the $22.5 million average of his three-year contract, the Packers were in line to get a third-round compensatory pick.
Doubs was the odd man out at receiver, with the Packers choosing to give second contracts to Christian Watson and Jayden Reed rather than Doubs. He signed a four-year contract worth $17 million per season with the Patriots, which put the Packers in line to gain a fourth-round compensatory pick.
The Packers opted to go older and cheaper at linebacker with Zaire Franklin, so they let Quay Walker sign a three-year contract worth $13.5 million per season with the Raiders. That was projected to net the Packers a fifth-round compensatory pick.
Left tackle is a premium position – and is paid like one – so the Packers believed Rasheed Walker would land a big contract in free agency that would fetch them at least a fourth-round pick and possibly a third-round pick.
Compensatory picks are awarded by the league via a secret formula. Nick Korte of OverTheCap.com has mostly cracked that code – so much so that his expertise wound up killing a trade . Comp picks are based mostly on average annual salary but playing time is a factor.
Injuries have taken a bite out of the playing time for Willis and Doubs, and it might cost the Packers.
Malik Willis going on IR could be very problematic for the Packers' 2027 compensatory picks. Missing at least 4 games looks like it could be enough to knock down the round the Packers get for Willis going to Miami from the 3rd round to the 4th round. https://t.co/IxAqOG0doB
The Dolphins placed Willis on injured reserve this week due to a groin injury that had him looking like a shell of himself in the loss to the Lions. The hope is he’ll be back in four weeks, but there’s no guarantee.
“The injury had progressed enough where the medical team believed he needed the rest,” Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley told reporters. “It started as a groin injury that worked to his core. I'm not going to get into medical details because that's not my expertise. He'll get second opinions this week. You're going to ask questions, surgery, non-surgery. He's going to get more input this week and make a decision in our hopes that he'll be back after his four weeks. Which in time, if healthy, he'll return.”
In the latest projections at OverTheCap.com , the Packers are in line to get a fourth-round pick for Willis. A prolonged absence wouldn’t move the pick back another round but it would practically guarantee it wouldn’t rebound back into the third.
That’s huge. A third-round compensatory pick would have landed at around No. 101 overall. This year, the first of the fourth-round compensatory picks was made at No. 133.
Doubs spent last week’s Packers-Patriots game on injured reserve. Because he will miss at least four games, his compensatory pick fell from the fourth round to the fifth round. This year, the last of the fourth-round comp picks was at No. 140 and the first of the fifth-round comp picks was at No. 173.
Quay Walker has started all nine games for the Raiders, so the Packers remain in line to get a fifth-round pick.
In one of the more surprising developments in free agency, there was no market at all for Rasheed Walker. He wound up signing with the Panthers; his contract wasn’t even big enough to merit a compensatory pick.
So, the Packers hit the maximum of four compensatory picks with edge Kingsley Enagbare, whose one-year, $10 million deal with the Jets was projected to be worth a sixth-round pick. He’s started all eight games so that pick has stayed in the sixth round.
Once upon a time, the Packers were in line to have perhaps six of the top 140 picks in the loaded 2027 draft class.
They had no first-round pick from the Micah Parsons trade, but they had one pick in the second round, two picks in the third round (their pick and the Willis pick), three picks in the fourth round (their pick, the Rashan Gary trade and the Doubs pick) and two picks in the fifth round (their pick and the Quay Walker pick).
Now, based on OTC’s projected draft order through Week 9 , these could be their picks.
Second round: No. 53 (their pick).
Third round: No. 85 (their pick).
Fourth round: No. 112 (Rashan Gary trade), No. 120 (their pick) and No. 133 (Willis pick).
Fifth round: No. 158 (their pick), No. 171 (Doubs pick), No. 173 (Quay Walker pick).
Sixth round: No. 184 (Dontayvion Wicks trade), No. 214 (Enagbare pick).
Seventh round: No. 241 (their pick).
At the end of training camp in 2025, the Packers acquired offensive tackle Darian Kinnard from the Eagles for a sixth-round pick in 2027. Before this year’s draft, the Packers traded receiver Dontayvion Wicks to the Eagles for a fifth-round pick in 2026 and a sixth-round pick in 2027. The Eagles have one of the worst records in the NFL, so Green Bay could wind up picking near the top of the sixth round.
At the end of training camp this year, the Packers acquired running back Kaleb Johnson from the Steelers for a sixth-round pick in 2028 and tight end Mark Redman from the Rams for seventh-round pick in 2028. So, those trades will have no impact on the upcoming draft.

title: Packers-Vikings Wednesday Injury Report: Huge List Filled With Big Names
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers kicked off their biggest week of the season with their longest injury report of the year.
Officially, the Packers did not practice on Wednesday as they get ready for Sunday’s showdown against the Minnesota Vikings. If they would have, five starters would not have practiced and a total of 16 players were dealing with one issue or another.
Nickel Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), edge Lukas Van Ness (back) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) would not have practiced.
Rhyan was injured during the opening series at Detroit. So, he missed most of that game and then the next two games. Coach Matt LaFleur said Rhyan could “potentially” return this week, but that he would not have practiced on Wednesday might not be a good sign for Sunday.
That means John Williams could be in line for his third career start – and his first against the most aggressive defense in the league.
“Banked reps and experience, you can't beat that,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “If we were on a away game, it would be even more critical because sometimes John having his head between his legs, those are the guys that got to communicate a lot of looks. So, it'll be good for John to be at home, he'll be able to see everything and make all those calls.”
Franklin has missed the last three games due to an injury sustained at practice before the Detroit game.
Finally, Van Ness was a noteworthy addition. He played 32 of the 63 snaps against New England and contributed one tackle. He leads the team with 4.5 sacks.
The questions on the offensive line run deeper than center. Left guard Aaron Banks (knee/hip) would have been limited participation, a continuation of a season filled with injuries. He’s played only 137 snaps. Of his three starts, he was unable to go the distance against the Jets in Week 2 or the Patriots last week.
When Banks was knocked out of the New England game, Kevin Zeitler made his Packers debut. Well, he would have been limited participation, as well, with an ankle injury.
Linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper, who played only two defensive snaps vs. the Patriots due to a pregame chest injury, would have been limited due to illness; the chest is not mentioned on the injury report.
Kicker Trey Smack (right calf) and receiver Savion Williams (groin) were listed as limited participation, as well.
One starter not on the injury report is Love. He was knocked to the turf at one point last week and got up flexing his left hand.
“It was just one of those weird ones where it just get hits, so it’s fine,” he said.
Receiver Skyy Moore was designated for return after missing the last four games with an ankle injury. He is averaging 16.0 yards per punt return, highlighted by a 63-yarder against the Jets, and 27.5 yards per kickoff return. Both figures lead the team.
On offense, he caught seven passes for only 35 yards.
“He's been such a great returner for us,” Love said. “It'll definitely be huge to get him back and I'm grateful that we're able to get him back this week.”
Running back Chris Brooks (ankle) and edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), who are entering their second week of practice after being designated for return, would have been limited. Brooks would be a big addition against the Vikings’ blitzing defense.
The big news in Minnesota – other than trading for Kirk Cousins – is that star linebacker Blake Cashman is in the concussion protocol. That’s never good news for any team or player, but that’s especially noteworthy considering the Vikings are coming off a Monday night game, so Cashman will have a day less to recover.
“He had the stinger evaluation going on and then did end up taking a hit, or more than likely giving a hit, later on in that game. He is currently in the concussion protocol,” Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters. “Obviously, short week. He's doing really, really well, but I'll keep you guys posted on him as we go through the week.”
Cashman leads the Vikings with 76 tackles, including seven tackles and two tackles for losses in Week 1. He’s in the top three on the team with 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for losses, 10 quarterback hits and seven passes defensed. Cashman is 10th in the league in tackles. From that group, nobody has more sacks, tackles for losses, quarterback hits or pass breakups.
In fact, no player with even 50 tackles has 10 quarterback hits. Cashman and Tampa Bay’s Josiah Trotter (70 tackles) are the only players with 60-plus tackles and seven PBUs. He is an elite player.
“Cash is an important part of our defense,” defensive coordinator Brian Flores said last season. “He’s a big part of what we do defensively from a communication standpoint, just an athleticism, football acumen. Getting other guys in the right positions, leadership. He does a great job.”
Did not participate: S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), LB Zaire Franklin (shin), RB Josh Jacobs (finger), C Sean Rhyan (ankle), edge Lukas Van Ness (back), TE Josh Whyle (concussion).
Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/hip), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), G/T Travis Glover (knee), LB Ty’Ron Hopper (illness), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), K Trey Smack (right calf), WR Savion Williams (groin), G Kevin Zeitler (ankle).
Full participation: WR Bo Melton (gameday concussion evaluation).
Note: Brooks, Moore and Parsons have been designated to return and are within their 21-day practice window.
Did not participate: LB Blake Cashman (concussion), TE T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest), DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), WR Jauan Jennings (calf), QB Kyler Murray (hamstring), OLB Kyle Van Noy (calf).
Limited participation: S Jay Ward (knee), QB Carson Wentz (ankle).
Full participation: S Theo Jackson (quad).

title: Packers Wednesday Practice Update: Walking Fine Line With Blitzing Vikings
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur scrapped Wednesday’s practice in favor of a jog-through. That means less time on the practice field to get the offensive line in order for Sunday’s showdown against the Minnesota Vikings.
There’s no doubt that Jordan Morgan will start at left tackle and Anthony Belton will start at right tackle. After that, it’s anyone’s guess.
Well, not anyone’s guess. LaFleur has a handle on who will be the starting guards for the NFC North showdown at Lambeau Field. Will it be Aaron Banks at left guard and Laken Tomlinson at right guard with the No. 1 line for a third consecutive week? Or will Kevin Zeitler start at right guard, Tomlinson shift back to left guard and Banks move to the bench?
“We have an idea where we’re going to go. I’m going to hold that ‘til Sunday,” LaFleur said.
Plus, center Sean Rhyan, who suffered an ankle injury during the opening series at Detroit, could return to the practice field after essentially missing the last three games. John Williams has filled in admirably – and, obviously, could start against the Vikings given the team will have only two real practices this week.
“I think there’s a reason that we brought Sean back here and paid him, because I think he was playing really good football, and so he’s a starter for a reason,” LaFleur said. “Not to take anything away from John, I think the job John’s done is remarkable. To be able to come in there with little to no experience and to be able to play the way he’s done and set the table for the rest of the front and the guys on offense, I think it’s been remarkable.
So, to review, the Packers could have new starters at each of the interior positions. That lack of cohesion could be a factor against the Vikings. According to Stat Rankings, they blitz 75.3 percent of the time. The Buccaneers are a distant second at 45.4 percent.
Rhyan has a couple games of experience with Tomlinson at left guard. He has none with Zeitler at right guard. The Packers haven’t played a single snap this season with Rhyan joined by any combination of Banks/Tomlinson/Zeitler.
The Packers, of course, haven’t been able to build any continuity on the offensive line all season. Continuity is a big thing, especially in their biggest defensive test since the Week 1 loss to the Vikings. But talent is a big thing, too.
In that first game, the starting guards were Donovan Jennings and Jacob Monk. They entered that game with one career start – Monk at center at Minnesota in Week 18 of last season. Whoever the Packers will turn to on Sunday will have infinitely more experience.
“I think the biggest thing is just getting all 11 on the same page with all the different looks that you get,” LaFleur said. “You’re going to get pressure, and you’re probably going to get pressure in almost every situation.
“Just getting all those guys, up front especially, on the same page – we had some meltdowns at the end of the game that really cost us, where we didn’t have our guys on the same page, and one, we got knocked off a block, one of the sack/fumbles we miscommunicated protection.”
Micah Parsons returned to practice last week, where he was limited to individual drills for all three practices. The plan is for Parsons to progress to team drills this week. He won’t be on the field on Wednesday, though, due to illness.
Speaking of injured players, receiver/returner Skyy Moore spent the last four games on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain and linebacker/captain Zaire Franklin missed the last three games due to an injured shin. LaFleur said he is “hopeful” they will return this week.
The Vikings beat the Packers in Week 1 with Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz as their quarterbacks. Their offense is among the worst in the league, though, ranking 27th with just 18.3 points per game. So, they sent a third-round pick to Las Vegas to bring back Kirk Cousins, who started for Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell in 2022 and the first half of 2023 before he sustained a torn Achilles in the Packers-Vikings game at Lambeau.
“Yeah, he’ll be out there,” said LaFleur, who coached Cousins while they were in Washington. “He’ll be starting, I’m fairly confident of that. Obviously, he’s got familiarity with their system. Even if he didn’t, he’s a really intelligent guy, and I think he’s been playing at a high level. I’m surprised they didn’t get more for him, quite honestly. I was shocked when I saw what they traded him for. It was mind blowing to me.”
Cousins is 5-4-1 with the Vikings against the Packers. He has seven games of a passer rating of at least 118.
In eight starts with the Raiders, Cousins ranks 11th in the league in passer rating, fifth in passing yards and second in touchdowns. For some perspective, Jordan Love is ninth in rating, first in yards and third in touchdowns.

title: Packers Rookie Stock Report: Regrading the Draft Class at Midseason
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Dynamite comes in small packages. The Green Bay Packers’ six-man draft class was small but has been dynamic, even without a first-round pick.
Dane Brugler’s midseason all-rookie team for The Athletic, for instance, listed second-round pick Brandon Cisse as a first-team cornerback, third-round pick Chris McClellan as an honorable mention at defensive tackle and fourth-round pick Dani Dennis-Sutton as a second-team choice at edge.
Here’s a closer look at each of the draft picks with nine of the season’s 18 weeks complete.
Stock up: The 52nd pick of the draft has been excellent. He’s started every game and seemingly gotten better by the week. He’s allowed one or two catches in six games and less than 50 yards in seven. He is tied for the rookie lead with nine passes defensed.
Only 10 rookie cornerbacks have played at least 100 coverage snaps. That alone tells you the challenge for a first-year player. From that group, Cisse ranks second with 14.5 coverage snaps per reception allowed, according to Pro Football Focus. Among the 72 cornerbacks overall who have played at least 150 coverage snaps, he is 18th in snaps per reception and 37th in passer rating allowed (88.7). He’s missed too many tackles, but the mentality is obviously there.
“Remember you guys asked me where can he go, and I said I’ll tell you when I see some balls get caught on him. Week 1, he got a bomb caught on him and he responded the right way,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said on Tuesday. “So, that was huge to me. That was kind of the first measuring stick of when we get into the season how is this guy going to be? He’s got quite a bit of resilience about his game.”
Cisse was the NFL’s Defensive Rookie of the Month for October. A serious player who prefers to look ahead, Cisse enjoyed the honor – for a moment.
“I think that comes with it,” he said. “I feel like you can’t be always so hyperfocused on not celebrating those things because those things don’t come around often and it’s hard to even win in this league, so I celebrate the wins. So, take a little bit of time to enjoy it, but now I’m onto this week.”
Stock up: As is the case at cornerback, defensive tackle is a tough position for rookies to break through. Only 11 have played 100 snaps this season. That McClellan leads all rookie defensive tackles in snaps is quite a feat.
Statistically, he hasn’t done much with five solo tackles, 16 total tackles, zero sacks, two quarterback hits and six pressures, but he seems to be playing better every week. The Packers have needed him with Javon Hargrave, Warren Brinson and Jonathan Ford on injured reserve, and he’s delivered while playing at least 24 snaps in every game.
“Honestly, more mental than physical,” he said of his growth. “I feel like physically, I definitely can see I've gotten a little stronger, just the way I can handle blocks now compared to back in the spring. But mentally, formation rec(ognition), and knowing when certain things are coming, knowing how to play blocks better, and just knowing when to do certain things, I feel like I've evolved a lot more in that aspect.”
The Packers drafted him because he’s not just a big, two-gapping defensive tackle but because he can be that player while also getting after the quarterback. There have been plenty of flashes of that potential.
Stock up: With Micah Parsons (and Collin Oliver) sidelined by injuries all season, the Packers desperately needed Dennis-Sutton to be a key player in a four-man rotation with Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell and Brenton Cox. He has delivered week after week after week.
Edge is a position where rookies should make an immediate impact. Indeed, 18 have played at least 100 snaps, with Dennis-Sutton ranking fourth in that group with 280. He is third with 23 tackles (behind first-round picks David Bailey and Akheem Mesidor) and third with 21 pressures (behind Bailey and Gabe Jacas).
Dennis-Sutton is tied for second on the team with three sacks. Just as importantly, he’s been strong against the run and even made some plays in coverage because of his instincts and athleticism.
“I feel like it’s starting to slow down for me a little bit,” he said last week. “But just got so much more to work on and continue to grow. But, yes, I feel like I am getting to know the game a little bit better and knowing what's coming.”
Simply put, the Packers thought they got a steal at the time and they were right.
Stock down: Burton was thrown into the fire during the second half against the Jets in Week 2 and started in Week 3 against the Falcons. He was horrendous against Atlanta. The Packers responded by signing three veterans, meaning he hasn’t been heard from again aside from eight garbage-time snaps at the end of last week’s blowout win.
Burton has played 97 snaps. Among the 15 rookie guards/centers to play at least that many snaps, he ranks last by a significant margin in PFF’s pass-blocking efficiency, which measures sacks, hits and hurries allowed.
Grade: F, with the obvious caveat that one bad game by a rookie doesn’t mean he will be bad for the rest of his career.
Stock down: The Packers, with Keisean Nixon and Carrington Valentine set to be free agents at the end of the season, doubled down on cornerback by taking a flier on Jackson, a former top high school recruit who had an up-and-down college career.
Jackson didn’t make the 53-man roster, landed on the practice squad and hasn’t played in a game.
Grade: F , with the important caveat that he missed all of the offseason practices and the start of training camp due to core-muscle surgery, so was behind the 8-ball from the start.
Stock up: The stock up/stock down portion of this could vary by the minute. For now, let’s go stock up because he made every kick at New England, including a 51-yard field goal.
Smack was the only kicker drafted and one of three full-time rookies. The Giants’ Dominic Zvada is 13-of-13 on extra points and 17-of-22 on field goals, the Commanders’ Drew Stevens is 12-of-15 on extra points and 16-of-19 on field goals and Smack is 20-of-23 on extra points and 14-of-19 on field goals.
By percentages among the rookies, he is second in extra points and last in field goals. Overall, out of 29 kickers who have attempted at least 10 field goals, Smack is 25th in field-goal percentage and 26th in extra-point percentage.
“I think the ball striking was improved,” special teams coordinator Cam Achord said on Tuesday. “It’s still not back to where we exactly want it. So, we’ll continue to work with it, and the more we can get out there on the field in practice, I think we’ll get the result we want moving forward.”

title: Latest NFC Playoff Standings, Projections Show Enormity of Packers-Vikings Showdown
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It’s just one game.
The Green Bay Packers will host the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. It will be an enormous game for the Packers, who have won five of their last six games to improve to 6-3 but are still stuck in last place in the juggernaut NFC North.
“Yeah, you’ve got to bring it every week. You’ve got to be your best,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Monday. “There’s not a lot of room for error in our division right now, and that’s just the reality of it. And I think it puts a healthy kind of pressure on you, to make sure that you’re present each and every day, and you’re pouring everything you can into this thing.
“Because, the one thing that is definitely true about our league is, anybody can be anybody. It doesn’t matter who you’re playing, when you’re playing, where you’re playing. You’ve got to bring it, and if you don’t, you will get beat.”
Here’s a look at the playoff standings entering Week 10 and what the computer models say about the importance of Sunday’s rivalry rematch.
1. San Francisco 49ers, 7-1.
3. New York Giants, 5-2-1.
4. Carolina Panthers, 3-5.
Death, taxes, the NFC North is good at football pic.twitter.com/BCPzyESFAX
The Three Wild-Card Front-Runners
6. Minnesota Vikings, 6-2.
7. Green Bay Packers, 6-3.
11. New Orleans Saints, 3-5.
12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 3-6.
The NFC North has the same number of wins as the entire NFC South and NFC East COMBINED pic.twitter.com/DSPyFJ3z7F
14. Arizona Cardinals, 3-6.
15. Washington Commanders, 2-5-1.
16. Philadelphia Eagles, 2-7.
The Packers would be in a familiar spot and play a familiar team, entering the playoffs as the No. 7 seed and facing the rival Chicago Bears in the wild-card round.
The seventh seed is practically a death sentence. If the No. 7 can beat the No. 2 on the road, then the reward is a game at the No. 1, which is San Francisco. A win would get the Packers to 7-3, a half-game ahead of the Vikings.
To win, the Packers are going to have to do a better job handling the Vikings’ relentless blitz packages than they did in Week 1. Offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich was multitasking when the Vikings played the Bills on Monday night.
“You’re kind of doing your prep for game planning and then you got the game on in the background, so you’re kind of watching the situational stuff and just, ‘Oh, it’s third down. Let me check in on it and see what’s going on,’” he said. “It’s kind of the same thing with Minnesota’s defense. They’re aggressive, they’re good and they do a really nice job, so it’s going to be a big challenge for us.”
According to Tankathon , the Packers have the second-toughest remaining strength of schedule. That’s life in the NFC North, of course, with Sunday’s game against the Vikings being one of their three remaining division games.
The Bears have the toughest remaining slate, with their eight opponents having a .631 winning percentage. They have four division games left along with matchups against Buffalo and Jacksonville.
The Packers are next at .576, with games against each NFC North team along with Buffalo and the Rams. The Lions are third at .558, with two games against the Packers and one each against the Vikings, Packers, Giants and Patriots. The Rams are fourth at .557, with two games against Seattle and one against the 49ers, Chiefs and Packers. The Vikings are sixth at .539, with games against each of the division teams as well as the 49ers and Patriots.
The remaining opponents for the Seahawks, who are one game behind the Packers, have a .514 winning percentage.
Here’s what the computers say about the Packers’ playoff chances.
At ESPN , the Packers have a 62 percent chance of reaching the playoffs. With a win, that would climb to 75 percent. With a loss, that would fall to 45 percent. That’s a 30-point swing in one game. They have an 11 percent chance of winning the NFC North.
According to The Athletic’s Playoff Predictor , the Packers have a 64 percent chance of qualifying for the playoffs, with a 13 percent chance of winning the division. The last-place Packers have the lowest playoff odds among the division teams, with the Bears at 88 percent, Vikings at 75 percent and Lions at 72 percent.
The Packers’ playoff chances would surge to 76 percent with a win but fall to 46 percent with a loss. If they can sweep the Vikings and Rams, they’d be at 90 percent.
At NFL.com , the Packers have a 62 percent chance of reaching the playoffs. That would improve to 74 percent with a win but fall to 45 percent with a loss, a 29-point swing.
At Playoff Status , the Packers have a 66 percent chance of reaching the playoffs. The other NFC North teams are over 80 percent, led by the Vikings at 87 percent. With a win, Green Bay would climb to 77 percent. With a loss, it would fall to 56 percent.
Using Stick to the Model ’s Playoff Machine, the Packers have a 62 percent chance of reaching the playoffs. That would improve to 72 percent with a win but fall to 40 percent with a loss – a wild 32-point swing that is the largest in the league this week.
“We talk about the same thing every time. We got to take a mindset of one week at a time,” quarterback Jordan Love said after crushing the Patriots. “You want to stack wins. So, got two wins here.
“Obviously, we got Minnesota coming to our house next week, someone who we lost to earlier in the season. So, we got to be able to regroup, have a great week of prep, and go and attack that week. And then, obviously, we got the bye coming up after that. But I think the mindset’s just got to be all complete focus and preparation on Minnesota. And you know you can’t let one game kind of lull you to sleep.”

title: Winners and Losers as Packers’ Long NFL Trade Deadline Streak Continues
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The streak goes on.
The Green Bay Packers haven’t been buyers at the trade deadline since the Super Bowl season of 2010. While there were reasons to believe it might be different this year, general manager Brian Gutekunst once again saw a good team and believed it was good enough.
Here are the winners and losers from a trade deadline (presumably) filled with talk but, once again, no action.
There was one good reason for general manager Brian Gutekunst to not make a trade. The team is tight against the salary cap, with the outlook not being especially better next season. Good teams are filled with good players; good players make a lot of money (or will make a lot of money).
So, that Gutekunst didn’t try to shoehorn a high-priced veteran onto the roster was probably good news for Russ Ball, who would have had to tie himself into about a dozen pretzels to make it fit for the rest of 2026 and beyond.
Green Bay Packers Salary Cap Update: 11/08/2026 🚨Trade Deadline Edition!!🚨 Salary Cap: 💰Current: $6.03m 💵Effective: $4.31m Roster: 83 🏈Active: 53/53 📋Practice: 16/17 🩹Injured: 12 🩼PUP: 2 Meaningful Restructures Available: 🔄Jordan Love: $3.44m -end of list- pic.twitter.com/jQAsawPqXL
Aaron Rodgers can probably feel Jordan Love’s pain.
For more than a decade after winning the Super Bowl, Rodgers slipped on Superman’s cape and did everything humanly possible to lead the team into a good spot in the playoff race at the trade deadline, only for the general manager – either Ted Thompson or Brian Gutekunst – to not make that one final move to perhaps push the Packers over the top.
The Packers are 6-3 through nine games due in large part to the superhuman play of Love. No Micah Parsons? Too many dropped passes? No running game? A leaky offensive line? Too many penalties?
Now, he’ll have to overcome a general manager who didn’t follow in the footsteps of the men in charge of the Seahawks, Bears, 49ers and Vikings.
Adding a player in a trade would have meant a player losing his spot on the roster.
So, the Packers didn’t trade for a defensive tackle. That’s good news for Anthony Campbell or Jonathan Ford. The Packers didn’t add a running back. That’s good news for Kaleb Johnson or Pierre Strong. The Packers didn’t add a receiver. That’s good news for J. Michael Sturdivant. Even with a wave of injuries, the Packers didn’t add a linebacker. That’s good news for Kristian Welch. Ditto for tight end and the offensive line.
This one has nothing to do with the lack of roster moves made by Brian Gutekunst. Instead, the Vikings traded a third-round pick to the Raiders to acquire Kirk Cousins.
Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon no doubt would have loved to face Carson Wentz or Max Brosmer, the two quarterbacks who were showered with boos as the Vikings were demolished by the Bills on Monday night. Instead, he’ll almost certainly have to face Cousins, who is on pace to throw for 4,420 yards and 38 touchdowns after a productive half-season with the Raiders.
“You need to have a plan ready to go for anybody that they put out there,” Gannon said before the trade was made public.
Kaleb Johnson had a breakout performance last week against the Patriots. With Josh Jacobs out after suffering a broken finger, Johnson carried the ball 14 times for 68 yards. The Packers were averaging less than 61 rushing yards per game entering the game.
“I was excited about him coming into the game,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said on Tuesday. “He had some really nice practices leading up to the game and he ran hard. That was the good thing about it. That's what we've been challenging him, is he's a big, physical, fast guy. Just run hard. Run angry. And I thought he did a nice job with that, for sure.”
The Colts did not trade Jonathan Taylor and the Titans did not trade Tony Pollard. Had the Packers acquired either, Johnson almost certainly would have been one of the odd men out in the backfield. Instead, with Jacobs out for at least a couple games, Johnson will have a chance to be the top back for the short term and perhaps earn a key role for the stretch run.
The Seahawks traded for receiver/returner Rashid Shaheen at the trade deadline last year, and he became a key player in their run to a Super Bowl championship.
Before this year’s trade deadline, the Seahawks traded for All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson. The 49ers traded for veteran defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. The Bears traded for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. The 49ers doubled down with aging receiver Keenan Allen. The Vikings made their big move at quarterback with Kirk Cousins.
Well, they did nothing. No starters were added. No depth pieces were acquired. Nothing. Now as always, help is not on the way.
The Packers don’t have a first-round pick due to the Micah Parsons trade. Because they didn’t make a trade, they’ll at least have their second- and third-round picks, plus their projected four compensatory picks as well as the fourth-round pick from the Rashan Gary trade.
(As an aside, OverTheCap.com is projecting the Packers will go from a third-round pick for quarterback Malik Willis and a fourth-round pick for receiver Romeo Doubs to a fourth-round pick for Willis and a fifth-round pick for Doubs because they are on injured reserve. Compensatory picks are awarded based mostly on salary but also on playing time.)
The 2027 draft class is supposed to be loaded. Gutekunst will have his full arsenal of picks (other than the first round) to add some young, cheap talent to a top-heavy roster.
There’s no word to describe what last year’s trade for Micah Parsons meant to the locker room. Excited, fired up – none of that fits the jolt that trade provided to the rest of the players on the roster.
No trade made on Tuesday would have had that visceral impact. And it’s not as if the players are pouting that no trades were made at the deadline.
Still, Green Bay’s players – especially the veteran players – understand what happened over the last week. The Seahawks added a Hall of Fame lineman. The Bears added a potential Hall of Fame defensive lineman. The 49ers made two trades. The Vikings did what they had to at quarterback.
And their boss did nothing. Getting to and winning the Super Bowl is incredibly hard. Seahawks general manager John Schneider was aggressive, as always, in his quest to go back-to-back. Bears general manager Ryan Poles had built the best roster in the NFC North, then added a true game-wrecker. 49ers general manager John Lynch’s team had the best record in the NFC, then added two useful veterans.
If you’re a member of the Packers, it would be hard not to reflect on what happened this week and not think the Lombardi Trophy got just a bit further out of reach.
