title: Chiefs Week 10 Injury Report: Two Key Trenches Players Remain Absent From Practice
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs handily defeated the New York Jets last Sunday, several offensive starters came away with injuries. There seemed to be a good chance that KC would be without several contributors for this week's matchup against the Falcons.
Patrick Mahomes (elbow/knee) and Xavier Worthy (hamstring) have fully participated in practice the past two days, suggesting they are trending toward playing. However, a pair of key players in the trenches are currently in danger of missing the Week 10 contest. Two Chiefs were listed as nonparticipants on Thursday's injury report , those players being right tackle Jaylon Moore and defensive tackle Peter Woods. All signs indicate they won't be cleared to return by Sunday.
Amid the messy Josh Simmons fiasco , Moore has been thrust into a full-time role at right tackle while undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson mans the left side. The 28-year-old has started all but one game for the Chiefs this season, his only absence coming in Week 7 when he was in the NFL's concussion protocol .
Now, the veteran swing tackle is dealing with an ankle ailment that forced him to exit the Jets win in the second half. In his place, Joshua Ezeudu stepped in on the outside, and he could be in line for his second start as a Chief if Moore doesn't take part in Friday's practice session.
Meanwhile, rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods continues to work his way back from a neck stinger that has plagued him for nearly a month. It was not initially considered a long-term issue when he first sustained it , but he's now on track to miss his second consecutive week for KC.
Many Chiefs fans have eagerly awaited the return of Omarr Norman-Lott, the franchise's second-round draft pick last year. He tore his ACL in Week 7 of his rookie year and has been rehabbing back since. Kansas City designated him to return from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list on Oct. 28. The Chiefs have listed him as a limited participant on Wednesday and Thursday, signaling his long-awaited 2026 debut may be nearing. Regardless, time is running out for Norman-Lott to be activated before his 21-day practice window closes.
Although Norman-Lott does not technically need to return for the Chiefs' upcoming game, he only has until Nov. 18 to be added to the 53-man roster. Otherwise, he will revert to the reserve list permanently for the remainder of the year, closing any avenue for him to get back into game action.
Considering Woods is likely to be unavailable against Atlanta, Norman-Lott's presence would do a lot for the pass rush , which recently broke out with a five-sack outing versus New York.

title: Josh Downs’ Biggest Goal After Joining Chiefs Should Be Music to Fans’ Ears
full_text:
Whenever a team acquires a player at the NFL trade deadline , it always opens the door for exciting possibilities the rest of the way that season. It also presents an obstacle or two, however, and the Kansas City Chiefs have shown that as much as any club in recent years.
In reality, 2024 might be the most apt example of that. Wide receiver DeAndre Hopkins was heavily involved early on, only to see his production taper off over time, and defensive end Josh Uche never carved out a real role after coming over to his new organization. Kansas City-specific additions frequently encounter steep learning curves and adjustment periods.
The prized newcomer of 2026, wide receiver Josh Downs , is trying his best to ensure his transition is as seamless as possible.
As a short-area savant who operates primarily out of the slot, Downs figures to compete for some of the work tight end Travis Kelce and fellow wideout Rashee Rice are getting. That includes a variety of concepts and potential choice or option routes, giving the fourth-year man plenty to absorb as he enters a new system.
Heck, not quite having complete mastery of the offense is part of the reason why rookie Cyrus Allen's involvement has lagged behind the hype nine games into his Chiefs tenure. Can Downs catch on quicker and make a good impression with quarterback Patrick Mahomes?
Speaking to the media this week, he said that's what he's setting out to do.
"Build that relationship with him and then on the field, when he throws me the ball, just catch it," Downs said. "And keep making plays when he throws it to me. Just do anything I can to learn the offense as fast as possible. I don't want to be a guy that's asking everybody what the play is [or] what the formation is. I feel like that's when you kind of get left behind, so I want to do everything I can to learn as fast as possible."
Downs also opened up on going from the 2-7 Colts, who have already lost to Kansas City this season, to a 6-2 club that anticipates both qualifying for the postseason and making a run at the Super Bowl.
"It's great to join a team like this with so much history and so much winning in their past, and even now," Downs said. "So I'm excited to be able to be a part of a group like this and contribute where I can."
In three-and-a-half years as a Colt, Downs was targeted an even 350 times in the passing game and managed to log 231 receptions for 2,494 yards and 12 touchdowns. That came with a 66.0% catch rate and 50.6% success rate, although his sophomore effort may have been his best in totality. Downs was effective last year despite playing 6% fewer snaps than the campaign prior.
After requesting a trade and having that ask met by his old franchise, Downs has nothing but love for Indianapolis and is ready to hit the ground running for his new one.
"I know they made a decision based off the betterment of their organization," Downs said. "I respect them for sending me to an organization like this. Those are great people over there, and I feel like they did right by me. This is the choice they made."
If Downs can accomplish his goal and grasp the playbook with efficiency while also earning Mahomes' trust, both he and the Chiefs will be all the better for it.

title: What Does Chiefs’ Reported CB Trade Interest Before Deadline Say About the Secondary?
full_text:
The only trade the Kansas City Chiefs made at the deadline saw them acquire former Colts receiver Josh Downs to bolster the receiving corps. However, that wasn't the only position group Brett Veach hoped to improve on the open market.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Chiefs held substantial interest in adding a cornerback before Tuesday's deadline. While no deal came to fruition, it may have revealed how the front office views the defensive backfield and its confidence in the current personnel. In the last two games, KC has primarily operated with Nohl Williams and Kristian Fulton on the outside, mixing in Chris Roland-Wallace as the primary slot corner. That rotation would look significantly different if it weren't for the injuries to the secondary.
Although he has been a full participant in practice this week and is expected to return against the Falcons, Mansoor Delane's shoulder has has been a recurring problem all year long. He suffered a hairline fracture in his right shoulder blade during OTAs in the offseason, forcing him to wear a non-contact jersey throughout most of training camp. The LSU product reaggravated it in his NFL debut after coming down with an interception, and a setback in practice last month forced him to miss the past two contests .
The concern with Delane isn't how he's performed, as he's been quite effective during his rookie season. Despite having missed three games, he holds the highest Pro Football Focus defensive grade (79.7) among all NFL rookie cornerbacks, allowing just 14 receptions for 227 yards in coverage.
Still, it shouldn't come as a surprise that the Chiefs were exploring their options given the depleted state of their defensive backs. Since placing L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve with a knee strain, Kansas City's pass defense has been compromised by a lack of continuity.
Fowler's report didn't provide much insight into the caliber of player the Chiefs were pursuing, but the lack of a move doesn't necessarily mean they are comfortable with their current group. It's possible the franchise views Delane's shoulder ailment as an ongoing question mark for the remainder of the season. Part of Kansas City's reluctance to overpay for a cornerback could be attributed to Fulton's unexpected resurgence. While he was an afterthought coming off a lackluster first season in the red and gold, Fulton has surprisingly looked like a lockdown corner since being thrust into a bigger role this season.
Kristian Fulton has allowed just 50 receiving yards over 8 catches (15 targets) this season Qbs are registering a 32.6 passer rating when targeting KC's veteran CB
Having Fulton as a dependable depth piece has benefited KC tremendously. Regardless, the Chiefs may not have complete confidence in him as the secondary boundary cornerback starting in a playoff game should Delane's injury worsen at some point.
Williams has served as a stabilizing presence all year and has emerged as a real star in his second NFL season . The good news is that his strong play has helped offset concerns about Delane's availability.
Steve Spagnuolo is confident in the cornerbacks on his roster, and the Chiefs' interest in making an addition was probably more a product of their injury concerns than dissatisfaction with the players' performances. Either way, this group is only a season-ending injury away from being dangerously thin, and Kansas City didn't do anything at the deadline to provide insurance.

title: Chiefs’ Kicker Decision for Week 10 Is Bordering on Blind Faith
full_text:
With nine weeks of play and the NFL trade deadline in the books, the Kansas City Chiefs are in good standing overall but have some potential red flags. One of them is in a lesser-appreciated realm, but it could continue to loom large if not resolved in time for the postseason.
Head coach Andy Reid's squad and Dave Toub's special teams unit still can't rely on the kicking game to produce quality results. Longtime starter Harrison Butker's nightmare season rolled on in last weekend's win over the New York Jets, presumably making his seat even hotter with another subpar performance.
Is that actually the case, though? Despite former Pro Bowler Justin Tucker being ready to go on a moment's notice, KC has yet to make a swap at the position. Those expecting a changing of the guard on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons will have to wait at least one more week.
Speaking to the media on Wednesday, Reid announced that he's trotting Butker out again in Week 10.
"As far as the kicking part goes, I'm going to stick with Butker this week," Reid said. "We'll go from there."
Reid and Toub have remained consistent in their backing of Butker , routinely pointing to his past accomplishments as justification for the unwavering faith. Instead of a new norm, the coaching staff is echoing that this is merely a cold spell of sorts.
"Listen, Harrison's done such a great job for us over time here," Reid said. "Sometimes, you go through these little peak and valley things. You give him a chance to work through them; we'll see how things go."
Another week of Butker highlights a multitude of concerns with the club's current approach to rectifying the ongoing kicking woes.
First and foremost, believing Butker is going to return to prime form borders on blind faith. The 31-year-old is perfectly fine on kicks inside the 50-yard line, going 10-for-11 on the year, but it's his long-range ability that — at least statistically — seems unlikely to come back.
After going 2-for-5 on field goals of 50-plus yards in 2024, he "rebounded" to post a 5-for-8 mark last season and is a career-worst 2-for-8 this year. In a sport where more and more kickers seem to be gaining either distance or accuracy, Kansas City's go-to man is losing both. This doesn't pass the smell test of someone who, in Reid's words , is "off a bit."
There's also the Tucker aspect of it all. If the Chiefs were so confident in a Butker resurgence, why would they bring in competition on the practice squad and keep him around for this long? That's on top of the reality that Tucker is in as a 36-year-old player who hasn't kicked in a game since the 2024 season and made only 73.3% of his tries, including converting on six of 11 attempts from that all-important long distance.
Maybe there is a world where Butker levels out. He found his stride, to some degree, in 2025-26 after a slow start out of the gate. Perhaps even if he doesn't, there's a concession from the coaching staff and Tucker proves to be closer to his 2023 self than the version we last saw. It's improbable, albeit not impossible.
But this comes off as a team hoping to catch lightning in a bottle rather than one that's truly getting to the bottom of a pressing issue.

title: Chiefs Winners and Losers After the Trade Deadline: Actually a New-Look WR Room?
full_text:
The unofficial second half of the 2026-27 NFL campaign is here, which coincides with the passing of the annual trade deadline . Several teams capitalized on opportunities to add to their respective rosters, with the Kansas City Chiefs being among the group of perceived winners.
By acquiring wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts, Kansas City improved the route-running quality of its skill players while also maintaining some flexibility for the future. Whether the move can raise the upside of the offense or is worth the cost is another argument, but there's no denying that at least trying to get better was a good call in a vacuum.
In this post-deadline world, where do the Chiefs stand on an individual front? Let's dive into who should benefit from the move, as well as whose roles might be changed in negative ways.
The following players should benefit from the Downs trade by way of either increased production, decreased pressure, or both.
What better way to start than with the man himself? It feels like forever ago that the Colts' offense was viewed as football's best, but the reality is that was only a calendar year ago. Through 10 weeks of play in the 2025 campaign, per RBSDM , Indianapolis led the sport in EPA per play on that end (0.183) and was second to only the Los Angeles Rams in success rate.
Everyone knows what a horrific collapse Indianapolis had down the stretch, partially due to getting exposed but also because quarterback Daniel Jones tore his Achilles tendon. Despite Jones' return for the 2026-27 season, things still haven't gone even close to smoothly for head coach Shane Steichen's crew.
It's safe to say that going from catching passes from Jones to Patrick Mahomes could have a positive effect on the fourth-year wideout's prospects.
Josh Downs went from Daniel Jones to Patrick Mahomes - here is how they stack up in catchable aimed pass attempts in 2026 🎯 Catchable pass rate (rank of 29 QBs): 0-9 yds: Jones 83% (24th) → Mahomes 91% (2nd) 10-19: 59% (26th) → 68% (12th) 20+: 21% (29th) → 45% (17th) pic.twitter.com/acJg1HA8ai
Speaking of which, having another reliable pass catcher figures to come to Mahomes' aid as well. It's a two-way street.
Coming into the season, Kansas City was banking on several things to happen at the receiver spot. Not only did Xavier Worthy need to look more like he did as a rookie — or perhaps even better — but Rashee Rice was supposed to return to his pre-injury form and Tyquan Thornton was expected to take a step forward. It's safe to say that plan, which was on thin ice to begin with, hasn't worked.
If anything, Worthy has regressed and now has a bum hamstring . Rice sustained a hamstring injury of his own in Week 4 and isn't remotely as productive on a volume basis as he was last year. Thornton, who was actually living up to the hype, is done for most or all of this season with a dislocated ankle . Enter Downs, who now might be the best separator and technician Mahomes has had in years at the receiver position.
WR percentile separation & YPRR vs man coverage pic.twitter.com/NWbBKMMNRi
No. 15 has still managed to turn in a good season, throwing for 14 touchdowns and four interceptions, but his life's been much more difficult than is needed. This move should assist him on all downs and make the offense hum more efficiently as a result.
On a per-target basis, tight end Travis Kelce's been more effective in 2026 than he has in several years. He's producing a career-high 14.6 yards per reception and 10.0 yards per target, paired with an average of 10.0 yards after catch per reception. Kansas City isn't force-feeding him volume, instead allowing him to pick his spots while playing 4% fewer snaps than he was last season.
Had Kelce been at or near his peak involvement, he'd be a bit more of a loser than a winner with Downs coming to the Chiefs. Because his catches cut deeper this campaign, though, it's hard to not see him either maintaining his current output or reaching new heights in what could be the final stretch of his first-ballot Hall of Fame career.
The jury is out in the "losers" category, as the welcoming of Downs to the lineup likely changes some things moving forward.
After a slow start while recovering from offseason knee surgery , Rice went off for seven receptions and 88 yards in Week 3. Since returning from injury in Week 8, he's averaged six receptions and 51 yards across two games while also scoring a touchdown. Whatever momentum he had from a stat-sheet-stuffing standpoint may be slowing down with another peer to compete with, however.
Josh Downs averages 0.23 EPA/target this season, per @SumerSports Rashee Rice entered today with the highest EPA/target among Chiefs WRs at 0.15
Adding to the SumerSports data , Rice is 29th out of 111 wideouts with at least 100 routes at a 2.0 yards per route run mark. Downs is way down at 76th at 1.14, but that number is pretty deceiving given the injuries to the Colts' receiver unit and how inept the offense has been. If Downs gets the looks from Mahomes many are expecting, it means Rice's ceiling is capped.
There's also the element of these two thriving in similar areas of the field. According to Pro Football Focus , 46.7% of Rice's targets are coming within 0-9 yards of the line of scrimmage. That threshold is 61.5% for Downs.
After combining for 19 offensive snaps in his first five games, rookie fifth-rounder Cyrus Allen's figures were 16, 31 and 19 over his next three outings. Week 9 marked a regression for the former Cincinnati standout, unfortunately, as he fumbled on a kickoff return and also went without a catch on offense. Worthy's injury didn't see him get unleashed, either, so his stock was already down .
It's virtually impossible for a true breakout to happen as long as the trio of Rice, Downs and Worthy is healthy and available. Allen can still perhaps make a couple plays a game as a supporting piece, although that isn't the rest-of-season path some wanted him to take. Chalk that up to a classic tug-of-war between expectations and reality.
This one is unfortunate, but it's sometimes simply a numbers game when it comes to roster math. The Chiefs needed to make room for a better player, which meant special teams ace Nikko Remigio got the boot by way of being waived on Wednesday morning.
Remigio has several years of teams experience, on top of a thorough understanding of the offensive system, but it became clear when Rice was out in both 2025 and 2026 that he was never going to find an expanded role. Downs having his name added to the depth chart essentially signaled the complete extinguishment of those hopes for the former undrafted free agent.
Side note: Downs was spotted warming up with the punt team in Wednesday's practice. I'm still hard-pressed to believe he'll take many of Remigio's old reps, especially with this being more of a standard procedure during the week than anything else.
I struggled with where to put Worthy. While it seems likely that his overall workload and involvement in the offense will decline with Downs in the fold, it could take some pressure off him and make him a more impactful player overall. We'll wait and see.

title: Grading the Chiefs' Trade for Josh Downs: The Move KC Had to Make
full_text:
As the 2026 NFL trade deadline approached, everyone knew that the Kansas City Chiefs were in the market for wide receiver help . Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs was the player most often mocked to Kansas City, even as other receivers were rumored to be on the market .
On Tuesday, only two wide receivers were actually traded, and they both came from Indianapolis. The Colts sent Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round pick, while the Chiefs added Downs (and a late seventh-rounder) in exchange for a fourth- and fifth-round pick in the '27 draft.
Recent reports have indicated that the Chiefs were willing to give up a fourth-round pick for Downs well before deadline day, but the Colts held firm until Tuesday, when the Chiefs added the fifth-rounder to seal the deal.
So, how did the Chiefs ultimately fare in the agreement that brought a much-needed pass catcher to Kansas City?
Before any Chiefs fans take offense to "just" a B, hear me out: I think this is a good move that Kansas City had to make. If I were in general manager Brett Veach's shoes as the clock ticked down on deadline day, I would have accepted this same final offer. Still, the Colts got very fair value for their 2023 third-round pick.
A simple trade of Downs for a fourth-rounder would have felt like a better deal for the Chiefs, but I also vastly prefer the way the Chiefs packaged the fourth- and fifth-rounders as opposed to sending a single third-round pick to Indianapolis in the transaction. Meanwhile, the Colts had some leverage because the entire league knew that the Chiefs were in desperate need of a starting-caliber wide receiver.
That point is one of the reasons I struggle to lift the Chiefs' grade above a "B." After an offseason of discussion about how badly Kansas City needed to invest in their wide receiver room, they were left scrambling in November because their current group of pass catchers hasn't been good enough (or healthy enough) to keep the offense afloat.
Tyquan Thornton was looking excellent before his serious ankle injury, and Rashee Rice has been solid when he's been healthy (which may still be a work in progress), but Xavier Worthy hasn't taken a third-year jump, while Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong haven't made much of their respective workloads. Rookie Cyrus Allen hasn't had a serious role, despite his training camp hype. This was a predictable problem with the Chiefs' roster well before the season began.
There's one other major unknown in Downs' future that will ultimately determine how this trade is viewed. Right now, Downs is only guaranteed to be in Kansas City through the remainder of this season. He's in the final year of his rookie contract and is scheduled to hit free agency in the spring. That, of course, is part of the reason he was available for roughly a third-round value, while players like Brian Thomas Jr., with additional team control on their current contracts, didn't get moved at the deadline. There was no urgency for many of those other teams and players.
The Colts essentially had to trade Downs on Tuesday, and the Chiefs essentially had to add a receiver. Therefore, the leverage game evened out and both sides got what they wanted.
You'd also be well within your rights to ask me why I care about a fifth-round pick at all. The NFL Draft is always a bit of a guessing game, and Day 3 draftees rarely become impact players. That's all completely fair—it's also one of the reasons I'd be a pick-hoarder as a general manager. Keeping more picks means taking more swings on players who could round out your roster at very low salaries for years to come.
In the 2026 NFL Draft, the Chiefs had two fifth-round picks: running back Emmett Johnson, who has flashed budding-star potential , and the aforementioned Allen, who had plenty of training camp hype but has only five catches so far this season.
In 2025, the Chiefs' fourth- and fifth-rounders were Royals and linebacker Jeffrey Bassa: two players who haven't yet made an impact in the pros.
What about 2024's Jared Wiley, Jaden Hicks, and Hunter Nourzad? Hicks is carrying that group as KC's third safety, while the others are organizational depth. 2023's Chamarri Conner and BJ Thompson? Conner is a valued starter in the final year of his rookie deal, while Thompson never stuck. 2020's L'Jarius Sneed and Mike Danna? Those were massive hits, but they came many, many draft classes ago.
All of that is to reiterate why I'd always like to have a few more draft picks, given the opportunity, but I am certainly not bent out of shape about the extra selection needed to seal the deal to bring Downs to KC.
Much like any overachieving student, perhaps you're not content with a "B" and would like to raise your grade later in the year with some extra credit. The Chiefs can do that, too!
If the Chiefs enjoy their time with Downs throughout the second half of this 2026 season (and if Downs is willing to forego full-on free agency for the sake of pairing up with Patrick Mahomes for the next act of his career), Kansas City could pay Downs and ensure that he won't just be a half-season rental. Even if Downs does leave in free agency, the Chiefs would be able to recoup some value with his addition to the compensatory pick formula, which would soften the blow.
The Chiefs absolutely did not get ripped off. The Colts certainly didn't get swindled. This is about as fair of a mid-level trade as you'll find between a contender and a rebuilder, and both teams are better off now than they were on Tuesday morning.

title: Chiefs Cut Ties With Special Teams Ace, Shuffle Roster and Cap After Josh Downs Trade
full_text:
It's been a busy week for the Kansas City Chiefs as they attempt to move on from a win over the New York Jets and gear up for a road contest versus the Atlanta Falcons. Although the 2026 NFL trade deadline is in the books, general manager Brett Veach's work is far from done.
On Wednesday, Kansas City completed some roster moves and also appears to have made a tweak to the salary cap sheet in response to the club's trade for former Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs.
Let's dive into the latest Chiefs transactions and what they could mean for the rest of the season.
In a Wednesday morning tweet on X, the Chiefs announced that the Downs trade is official. It's him and a 2027 seventh-round pick coming to KC in exchange for fourth- and fifth-round picks in the same NFL Draft.
In order to make room for Downs on the 53-man roster, wide receiver Nikko Remigio was waived. The 2023 undrafted free agent is now available to be claimed by all 31 other NFL teams but could always pursue a return to Kansas City if he clears waivers.
We have traded for WR Josh Downs. We have waived WR Nikko Remigio and DE Jack Pyburn. pic.twitter.com/bdZIgClbIW
Remigio, who turned 27 a week ago, was in his fourth year with the team. The former Fresno State standout has 72 offensive snaps and 202 special teams reps to his name as a Chief, including respective marks of two and 55 in 2026. Remigio played in five regular-season games in 2024 before seeing that total increase to 14 last campaign. He'd appeared in all eight contests to date this season.
Assuming it isn't Remigio being back on the practice squad and elevated for game day, it'll be interesting to see who handles the return duties for the Chiefs. Remigio had 12 kickoff returns and 14 punt returns this year, including a big-time 69-yard return that was wiped by a penalty on Sunday.
Options for the vacant special teams role include rookies Cyrus Allen and Emmett Johnson, as well as running back Brashard Smith once he comes off injured reserve . Downs has 32 punt returns and a pair of kickoff returns on his resume, although his projected role on offense could keep him out of special teams dealings.
The Chiefs have also waived defensive end Jack Pyburn, whom the franchise originally claimed off waivers at the end of August when roster cuts were happening. Like Remigio, he may be a practice squad candidate.
No corresponding addition has been revealed as of the publishing of this article, but reading the tea leaves could hint at defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott officially rejoining the 53-man roster from the physically unable to perform list.
Veach and company found themselves strapped for cash at the deadline, leaving Downs as one of the more affordable and sensible pieces that wouldn't require a ton of cap gymnastics to fit under the league-allotted threshold.
Kansas City wound up pulling the contract lever of linebacker Nick Bolton to make sufficient room for Downs' expiring rookie deal.
Shared by Michael Ginnitti of Spotrac , $6.76M of Bolton's salary was converted into a signing bonus, giving the team another $3.3M in space to work with. The polarizing defensive stopper now carries a 2027 cap hit of $22.6M with $7.6M in dead money if released, further signaling that he's in the club's plans for next season.
The #Chiefs converted $6.76M of LB Nick Bolton's salary into signing bonus, creating $3.3M of 2026 cap space. Updated Cap Hits (dead) 2026: $15.8M ($23.5M) 2027: $22.6M ($7.6M)
If the Chiefs wanted to lower that number to below $20M, they could always sign Bolton to an offseason contract extension. Considering that he's still only 26 years old, that outlook seems to be favorable.

title: Chiefs Have Another Potential WR Trick Up Their Sleeve After Josh Downs Trade
full_text:
Although it was more anticlimactic than fans had hoped, the Kansas City Chiefs' trade deadline was still a net success. They acquired Josh Downs, an elite slot separator , from the Colts without having to surrender significant draft capital to do so.
With Tyquan Thornton out for most of the season and Xavier Worthy potentially missing time with a hamstring injury, general manager Brett Veach had little choice but to bolster the receiving corps. However, KC isn't exactly out of options with its current group. The Chiefs could still make a highly anticipated addition in free agency, as rumors have linked former Kansas City star Tyreek Hill to his old team for months. While he recently faced a civil trial for domestic violence allegations and is working his way back from a gruesome knee dislocation that has kept him out of the NFL for over a year, a recent report suggests a signing could come sooner rather than later.
According to Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, the veteran receiver is close to being medically cleared to return to football. It's certainly not out of the question that Hill could be suiting up in a red and gold uniform sometime in December.
"As soon as Tyreek is healthy and cleared medically, I'm letting teams know, 'Hey, remember, you may not have to trade for a receiver, you can just go sign Tyreek,' whenever we get that medical clearance, which we hope will be soon," Rosenhaus said on The Pat McAfee Show yesterday. "I do think he's close to getting cleared. When he gets that OK, I expect him to be playing and making things happen this season."
"As soon as Tyreek Hill is healthy and cleared medically I'm letting teams know they can sign him.. I think he's close and I think he's gonna make a great comeback.. I expect him to be playing and making things happen this season" ~ @DrewJRosenhaus #PMSLive https://t.co/COoR7ksIqD pic.twitter.com/EsBmjrnFJ8
After being traded to the Dolphins during the 2022 offseason, Hill spent four seasons in Miami before being released to free up cap space as he continued recovering from his injury. His expected return has been pushed back several times, as Rosenhaus previously suggested he could be ready to return in October . However, Hill's extensive rehab process has delayed his potential comeback.
Hill won Super Bowl LIV with the Chiefs in 2020 and spent six seasons with the franchise, establishing himself as one of Patrick Mahomes' favorite targets. The two built a strong rapport over the years, and a reunion would certainly be an intriguing development as KC looks to revitalize its downfield passing game.
At 32 and coming off what many thought to be a career-ending injury, it's difficult to envision exactly where Hill would fit into a receiver room that now features Rashee Rice, Worthy, and Downs . He'd likely come at a relatively low cost, though, and could potentially offer more to the team than backups like Jalen Royals or Cyrus Allen at this stage of the season.
All of this remains fluid given the uncertainty surrounding the aftermath of Hill's legal dispute and the question of whether he'll actually be physically capable to contribute once he returns. Regardless, the possibility of bringing back one of Mahomes' most dynamic former weapons is something worth keeping an eye on, especially if Downs doesn't make an immediate impact with his new squad.

title: Chiefs Rookie and Sophomore Power Rankings: What's the Deal With Cyrus Allen?
full_text:
With the dust officially having settled on Week 9 and the NFL trade deadline , the Kansas City Chiefs are one step closer to figuring out who they are ahead of the most important stretch of the season.
Sunday's victory over the New York Jets featured a return to dominance for most of the game, although it was likely just an example of a good team taking care of business against a bad one. With that said, it served as a prime opportunity for some of the club's young players to continue developing.
Following Week 9, let's break down the Chiefs' rookies and sophomores by ranking each qualifying 53-man roster member in tiers. Be sure to return to this series each week to see who's moving and shaking.
Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott, whose practice window was opened a while back, isn't included while he's still on the physically unable to perform list .
Left tackle Josh Simmons remains off the list after going to injured reserve . The same exemption applies to running back Brashard Smith .
Nohl Williams just keeps on proving why he's one of the best cornerback building blocks on a rookie deal. His breakout year rolled on in Week 9, as he dominated in coverage against the Jets' banged-up receiver room and did exactly what he should've on the afternoon. If he's rejoined by Mansoor Delane this weekend versus the Atlanta Falcons, which is expected , it could be tough sledding for the home offense.
The further that second-year defensive end Ashton Gillotte gets from his plantar fascia injury , the more he looks like a somewhat reliable starter opposite George Karlaftis. At the very least, he's a nice one-two punch with rookie R Mason Thomas, although the former received 44 snaps in Week 9 to the latter's 28. According to Pro Football Focus , Gilotte finished with a pair of pressures and a stop on Sunday to Thomas' respective marks of one and zero.
A week after going 5-for-5 on targets and receptions for 128 yards and the first touchdown of his NFL career, rookie running back Emmett Johnson rushed for a career-high 34 yards and his first-ever score on the ground. Being in a blowout game allowed the Nebraska product to get some more work in the run game, and he certainly delivered.
It's impossible to move rookie tackle Kahlil Benson down a tier, so he's stuck in this one until he improves his play. Considering the back half of Kansas City's schedule, that doesn't seem probable . The former CFP National Championship winner from Indiana gave up more pressures (five) than any Chiefs lineman over the weekend, which doesn't bode well for his long-term prospects.
The wide receiver room is suddenly in an interesting position. Jalen Royals made the most of both of his targets on late downs on Sunday, although there may not be a ton more to his role at this juncture and he's now battling an ankle issue.
Fifth-round rookie Cyrus Allen fumbled on special teams and didn't see an expanded workload on offense, which may be something to monitor given that Josh Downs was acquired at the deadline. The next few weeks could be a make-or-break stretch for Allen's debut year in the Chiefs' wideout ranks.
Defensive tackle Peter Woods is far from an empty snaps player, but he hasn't made too many high-impact plays as of late and also didn't play in Week 9 because of a neck injury. The Chiefs anticipate him back in Week 10. Bryson Eason, who played 20 snaps in Week 8 when Woods first got hurt, saw his total drop all the way down to five.
Fourth-round cornerback Jadon Canady has experienced a tale of two games in Weeks 8 and 9, going from flashing his playmaking upside to being a special teams liability. The good news for this category is that tight end Jake Briningstool receives a promotion after logging season-high thresholds for offensive snaps (15) and targets (two).
Linebacker Jeffrey Bassa still isn't going to crack the rotation on defense, but he made his second big-time special teams play of the year when he recovered Allen's fumble on the Chiefs' opening kickoff return. At the safety spot, Xavier Nwankpa went over the 20-snap mark for Dave Toub's unit for the second consecutive game.
Not a ton to see here. With backup quarterback Justin Fields not being moved at the deadline, rookie Garrett Nussmeier will remain the emergency third signal-caller on game days for the remainder of the year. In fairness, there was never any smoke surrounding a Fields trade.
Offensive tackle Diego Pounds and defensive end Jack Pyburn are safe on the 53-man roster for the time being.

title: Sean Payton’s History Makes Failed Chargers Trade Suspicious
full_text:
The world of NFL front offices is built on relationships, connections and ultimately trust. George Paton may be the general manager for the Denver Broncos but head coach Sean Payton has a less than stellar history when it comes to trust, trickery and gamesmanship in the NFL.
The Los Angeles Chargers had a trade agreement in place for their homegrown starting linebacker, Daiyan Henley, to send him to the Denver Broncos. The trade that was finalized at the 11th hour before the trade deadline came to pass was for a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-rounder pick.
Late Wednesday night, the Broncos decided to pull the plug on the trade after trying to renegotiate the trade compensation after getting Henley in the building in Colorado. The Broncos cited a failed physical designation for Henley and specifically cited arthritis in his knee which immediately raised eyebrows and suspicions. The Chargers are now left to deal with the fallout .
Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk raised concerns with the Broncos' evaluation and mentioned arthritis being a common issue for NFL linebackers.
"The Broncos discovered an issue with Henley’s knee. It has, we’re told, arthritis. (As one source with neither the Chargers nor the Broncos told PFT, most if not all starting linebackers in the NFL have some degree of arthritis in their knees.)" - Mike Florio
The entire situation smells fishy. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is asking the NFL to look into how the loophole, which allows trades to be adjusted by compensation past the deadline. Harbaugh pointed out the obvious issue with how this trade fell apart, the Broncos did not fail Daiyan Henley for his physical, they were only going to pass him if the trade compensation was reduced.
HC Jim Harbaugh says Denver failed Henley's physical to back out. "The Broncos based a pass/fail on a medical grade on whether we would take less compensation." Harbaugh says the Broncos would pass Henley's physical if the picks were downgraded from the agreed upon 4th + 5th. pic.twitter.com/xwoVCILJyl
The Chargers are 0-8 and had not made any other moves at the deadline. Henley was one of the few trade assets the Chargers had that could net any relatively significant draft capital. If this sounds shady and suspicious, there is good reason.
Sean Payton has a long history of holding grudges and operating on the margins of good and bad faith. Payton was famously suspended for a full season for his role in the New Orleans Saints Bountygate scandal.
Payton has a longstanding beef with the Minnesota Vikings going back to Bountygate and the 2009 NFC Championship and later to the Minnesota Miracle game in 2018 playoffs. He later took credit for and bragged to reporters about playing a game of smoke and mirrors to trick the Vikings in the 2024 NFL draft.
Sean Payton and Jim Harbaugh may not have a full-on beef with each other but they do have history. Back in 2011, there was a preseason controversy between Payton and Harbaugh over an unspoken gentleman's angreement , that Payton took as a slight, on how to handle their preseason matchup.
Payton took a year off from coaching and was working in media during the 2022 season. During the season, Payton was agressively pushing for the Chargers head coaching job, the job that went to Harbaugh the following year.
Did Sean Payton and the Broncos operate in bad faith in regards to Daiyan Henley and the trade? Did they try to use a loophole to leverage the Chargers and steal a player for less draft capital? The entire situation seems suspicious, and Sean Payton's track record does little to calm those suspicions.

title: Jim Harbaugh Calls For League Action After Rival Broncos Cancel Daiyan Henley Trade
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers, being 0-8 with a failing roster, seemed to have made the correct decision at the trade deadline and decided to trade away one of their valuable assets, Daiyan Henley. This decision was controversial for the fan base , but it finally showed that the team was willing to accept their fate and look toward future seasons for success.
However, fitting for the rest of the year, they found a way to lose out on something else, this time in a trade. The initial agreement between Los Angeles and Denver was to send LB Daiyan Henley in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
Generally speaking, this is a solid return for a LB in a contract year who has yet to return to his 2024 breakout form. It is important to highlight the off-the-field reasons for his lesser play, but unfortunately, that does not change the fact that his current level of play has not been to the same standard.
With this return, the Bolts were happy to look toward the 2027 NFL Draft and see second-year LB Marlowe Wax play an increased number of snaps.
Then the news of the trade being rescinded hit the media, changing everything (and nothing) at the same time.
Once the NFL trade deadline passed, it was reported that Henley did not pass Broncos physicals, yielding George Paton and the Broncos to cancel the trade, sending Henley back to Los Angeles and taking back their draft selections.
This is obviously a whirlwind of events for fans, media, coaches, players, especially Henley. Players like Tony Jefferson and Denzel Perryman were shocked and sad to see him go, just for them to be excited to see him return. Henley briefly spoke out on Twitter, with a GIF depicting confusion.
pic.twitter.com/T4vwHML4yN
One of the coaches with the most to say on the matter is the usually secretive/nondescript coach, Jim Harbaugh. When prompted about the process today, Harbaugh said:
"The Broncos based a pass/fail on a medical grade on whether we would take less compensation." Harbaugh added that the Broncos would pass Henley's physical if the picks were downgraded from the agreed upon 4th + 5th. (Quote courtesy of Alex Insdorf)
Harbaugh also mentioned that the Chargers refused to accept less compensation and that this transaction is bad precedent for the league, and they (the league) should look into it.
Now, the aftermath is the awkward nature of Henley's return, with him likely being frustrated with the entire situation, likely essentially ending his chances of returning to the Chargers on a new contract after the 2026 season. He is expected to play the rest of the season in Los Angeles.

title: The Potential Locker Room Impact of the Chargers' Latest Trade Drama
full_text:
Well, the Los Angeles Chargers had yet another bad thing happen. Not because of the overall trade, but because of the repercussions that come with it.
A trade falling through can have consequences that stretch well beyond the front office. For a team trying to build something together, situations like this can create questions about trust, commitment and the relationships between players. Following the failed Daiyan Henley trade, there is an interesting conversation to be had about what this could mean inside the locker room moving forward.
This feels like a classic Chargers moment, everything this season has been on the negative side of things. Things just keep getting worse, looking towards the future might be the best option after all.
Football is built around relationships, communication and the understanding that everyone in the room is working toward the same goal. Players spend countless hours together, pushing one another through practices, meetings and the everyday demands of an NFL season. That kind of environment takes time to establish, and maintaining it requires a level of trust between teammates.
When a trade involving a prominent player falls apart, it can introduce an uncomfortable element into that environment. Even when players understand that the NFL is a business, seeing how quickly circumstances can change is a reminder that nobody is completely protected from the decisions made above them. It can leave players wondering how secure their own positions really are and whether the organization views them as part of its long-term plans.
For the players who remain, the challenge is making sure that outside circumstances do not become a distraction from what is happening on the field. A failed transaction does not automatically create division, nor does it mean teammates suddenly view one another differently. However, situations like this can test the relationships that a team has spent an entire offseason trying to strengthen. There is also a leadership element to consider. Veterans and established voices in the locker room have an opportunity to keep everyone focused on football rather than allowing front-office decisions to become the center of attention. The strongest locker rooms are often the ones that can handle uncomfortable situations without allowing them to affect the way players approach their responsibilities.
The business side of football will never disappear. What matters now is whether the brotherhood inside the locker room remains stronger than the circumstances surrounding it.

title: Denver Pulls Plug on Daiyan Henley Trade, Chargers Face a Massive Fallout
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers created plenty of frustration across the NFL with their approach to trade deadline despite carrying an 0-8 record. In the end, the team has been playing awful football and did not get offers worthwhile to move on from their veteran players, but they did make one trade in the final hours.
Just hours before the deadline it was announced that the Chargers and rival Denver Broncos had agreed to a trade for starting linebacker Daiyan Henley. Henley a former third-round pick of the Chargers out of the 2023 draft has been an emotional leader and backbone of the Chargers defense but unfortunately has seen inconsistencies in his play. Following a breakout in 2024, Henley had to survive a storm of challenges both physically and mentally in 2025 and it unfortunately created significant challenges for his performance.
The defense has been the lone relative bright spot for the Chargers this season and Henley has had some displays of elite skill. However, some of the inconsistencies have continued into 2026. Henley was one of the few trade assets the Chargers had that could net relatively significant draft capital. Unlike teams such as the Indianapolis Colts, the Chargers were not loaded with players such as Quenton Nelson or Jonathan Taylor
The trade compensation for Henley did feature a slight in division tax with a 2028 fifth-round pick added on to the 2027 fourth-round selection. However, the basis of the deal was similar in compensation to the trade that sent linebacker Ernest Jones IV from the Tennessee Titans to the Seattle Seahawks.
pic.twitter.com/vFJ7MYS2UN
All of the compensation and discussion over the trade deadline is not all for naught. The Denver Broncos pulled the plug on the trade, presumably for a failed physical, and Henley will now remain with the Chargers for the duration of the 2026 season. If Henley did fail the physical, it will be on the transaction wire on Thursday unless it is publicly acknowledged beforehand.
The Chargers may have an awkward reunion on their hands. Daiyan Henley is beloved by his teammates and already safety Tony Jefferson is joking and celebrating the news on social media. Henley just went through a whirlwind and now is apparently injured and heading back to Los Angeles to rejoin an 0-8 team.
The defense is already struggling to stay motivated and are side-eyeing the offense who continue to struggle to score points. How will this botched trade affect the group will be very interesting to monitor.
The Chargers will now lose the additional draft capital as they try to rebuild and regroup in 2027. Henley, based on the trade, is likely not in the Chargers long term plans and will likely walk in free agency in the offseason. If he signs a strong enough contract, he can factor into the compensatory pick formula for 2028.
The Chargers will also now have to decide how to handle the roster with Denzel Perryman's practice window opened and no open roster spot with Henley's return. Defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary, as a first-year play caller, is faced with a tough task in managing the in-house ramifications of this trade falling through.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh is in a spot he has never been in before. The team is 0-8 and is seemingly unable to find any answers to their current struggles. Now a botched trade of a homegrown locker room favorite, to a division rival, has a fallen through and looms over the entire team. How does the team respond?
Can Harbaugh keep the train on the tracks with a nationally televised game against a wounded Baltimore Ravens team? Monday night suddenly has become a massive test for this regime and organization.

title: Chargers Had Trade Deadline Options Like 49ers for Khalil Mack
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers sent some odd messages to fans at the NFL trade deadline.
On the topic of Khalil Mack, the Chargers remained true and didn’t move him, seemingly aligning with his wishes on the matter.
But the Chargers did go out and trade away Daiyan Henley , one of the core locker room leaders and prominent personalities on the team only outmatched by the likes of Derwin James.
Not trading obvious candidates to move while rebuilding, but sending away a 50-50 to stay player seemed to align with the wishy-washy stance of general manager Joe Hortiz and the front office overall. It just creates even more questions about how they attack change next offseason.
For now, though? We know the Chargers certainly had offers on the table for Mack.
Presumably, the Chargers had more than a few deadline offers for Mack, no matter what their public posturing through leaks and otherwise said.
One team with interest was the San Francisco 49ers, according to Steven Haglund of the GAC Podcast.
Should the Chargers have fired off a trade? Such a move would’ve kept Mack somewhat local and let him go play for a 7-1 contender.
That was the crux of the discussion for Chargers fans, really. Mack pondered retirement last offseason before coming back on his latest one year $18 million fully guaranteed contract. If this is his last season, most Chargers fans would have agreed that shipping him off and letting him get a chance at a title was the right thing to do.
However…those same fans would probably agree that if Mack wished to stay with the winless Chargers no matter what, they should probably honor that, too. There are things outside of football that are important to players, believe it or not.
The Chargers were in a no-win spot here (pun intended, sorry). They were never going to get a good return for Mack. They have no wins and no leverage. If they traded Mack for a sixth-round pick or something, they would've been lambasted for trading away a future Hall of Famer for peanuts.
Instead, they continue to clutch that Hall of Famer on an 0-8 team while whittling away the locker room leadership around him. He’s not under contract for next season, nor is anything about the Chargers, including the entire coaching staff, guaranteed for next season, either.
All Chargers fans can do, really, is enjoy watching Mack do his thing over the back half of the season and hope this is a sign that he comes back in some capacity for one more go next year, no matter what the coaching staff looks like.

title: NFL Rumors Hint at the 1 Team That Called Chargers About Justin Herbert Trade
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers , through reports and otherwise, made it abundantly clear that they wouldn’t be trading away Justin Herbert at the NFL trade deadline.
But everyone knew that wouldn’t stop other teams from picking up the phone and at least asking .
Those Chargers fielded what was likely a huge number of calls at the trade deadline this week. General manager Joe Hortiz and Co. settled on just one semi-controversial move by trading away linebacker Daiyan Henely .
Still, the fact the winless Chargers were in a position to even get trade questions about Herbert speaks volumes to just how off the rails this thing has gone.
A handful of teams probably called the Chargers to get the heat check on the possibility of Herbert being moved.
A report confirms at least one of those teams.
According to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz , the Minnesota Vikings were one of the teams that called and asked about Herbert: “The Chargers, I’m told, immediately shut down all inquiries for Herbert, who also has a no-trade clause.”
Those Vikings went on to trade for Kirk Cousins of the Las Vegas Raiders. The cost was tiny compared to what it would have cost to acquire Herbert, but it speaks to just how desperate other teams will get for quarterback help.
Which speaks to how smart it is to hang onto Herbert, of course. Barring Herbert himself wanting out or the very top of the organization deciding a full reset is necessary, there’s zero sense in moving off a star quarterback who is just 28 years old and in the middle of his prime, even if it doesn’t seem like it right now.
And indeed, Herbert’s five-year, $262.5 million contract extension that boasts $133.7 million fully guaranteed comes with a no-trade clause and north of $80 million in dead money in future years if moved.
These details won’t stop calls from teams or outside speculation, though. One of the biggest pain points of Herbert’s career to date is the never-ending resetting of the offensive coordinators and coaches around him.
That’s probably going to happen again this offseason if and when the Chargers move on from Mike McDaniel. If the Chargers can’t muster a couple of wins, Jim Harbaugh and the entire staff might be gone too, no matter how much money ownership has committed to them in future years.

title: Grading the Chargers NFL Trade Deadline: Beloved Homegrown Star Shipped to Rival
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers approached the 2026 NFL trade deadline with a shocking lack of willingness to engage in trade talks. They finally changed their tune at the 11th hour and were willing to discuss some of their players on expiring contracts.
The Chargers may have hurt themselves with how they approached the deadline and appeared to be in denial of how bad the season was going. There is an argument to why the Chargers may have chosen to be less active at the trade deadline given their lack of true valuable trade assets.
When the dust settled from the trade deadline, Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz did make one move and adjusted the franchise's public plan of standing pat and not moving on from any players. Los Angeles traded starting linebacker Daiyan Henley within the division to the Denver Broncos.
Trading away Henley was one of the top trade assets the Chargers had on the roster alongside veteran edge rusher Khalil Mack. The Chargers found a market for Henley and satisfactory offers came in. There have been reported offers for several other players on the roster, including Mack, but their low value kept the deals from coming to fruition.
Let's examine and grade the deal for Henley and the lack of deals from the trade deadline.
Grade: B+ The Chargers waited until the final hours before the trade deadline to make their first and only move. Moving on from former third-round draft pick and local Los Angeles product Daiyan Henley was not an easy move to make.
Henley has all the talent to be a top-tier linebacker and appeared on his way to achieving that ceiling by the end of the 2024 season. For several reasons, including several outside of Henley's control, he has struggled with consistency since the start of the 2025 season. Henley entering 2026 on the final year of his rookie contract and with his inconsistencies, an offseason extension would have been difficult to navigate.
Henley is also known for his energy and leadership on defense. Being a local with significant ties to the community makes the departure more difficult. The move may be best for Henley's long term career as he can get a fresh start away from his hometown and some of the heavy baggage following him around LA.
The Denver Broncos gave up a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick for Henley. For a player under contract only through the remainder of the 2026 season, that is significant value. The closest comparable trade was in 2024 when the Tennessee Titans traded linebacker Ernest Jones IV to the Seattle Seahawks. Both Jones and Henley were third-round picks in the final year of their rookie contract. Jones was sent to the Seahawks for backup linebacker Jerome Baker and a 2025 fourth-round pick.
The trade makes clear room for the Chargers to give young linebacker Marlowe Wax more playing time down the stretch as they determine how the room will be built in 2027. The 2027 draft class is shaping up to be a very deep class of linebackers. Overall the trade is well-rounded on both sides and the Chargers got the best value they could have for a homegrown player.
Grade: B- The Chargers may have been in denial of how their season was going but if they were going to trade Khalil Mack, the best destination would have been to the Chicago Bears before the Bears made a blockbuster deal to acquire Jeffery Simmons. The amount of capital the Bears gave up for Simmons likely left little on the table to make a move for Mack.
Mack will surely be immortalized in the Hall of Fame when he decides to hang up his cleats. Players of his caliber and with his resume have earned the right to choose their path. By all accounts, Mack wanted to stay in Los Angeles, likely for his family. If the Chargers had an offer for a fourth-round pick, the discussion likely would have been different, but by waiting and standing pat in hopes of turning their season around, that ship sailed.
The value of late-round picks has greatly diminished in the NIL era. Sixth- and seventh-round picks are widely viewed as near throwaway picks with the caliber of players available in that range down from years prior with so many underclassmen staying in school. The Chargers, according to Steven Haglund of the Guilty as Charged Podcast, who has worked with the Chargers in the past, had a sixth-round offer from the San Francisco 49ers for Mack.
Per sources, the 49ers maintained contact with the Chargers throughout the trade deadline process about a potential deal for Khalil Mack but never offered more than a 6th round pick. The Chargers obviously never budged on their desire to keep the future HOFer around. https://t.co/fOqg4c90lr
Is going against a legendary player and his direct wish to stay all for the chance of adding a UDFA level rookie next year worth the effort? No, for a franchise with a checkered past in dealing with top tier veterans, it would have been a bad look and not helpful.
Grade: C The Chargers still have to field a team for the remainder of 2026 and can only trade away so many players with the amount of injuries they have suffered. The Chargers may have had offers for seventh-round picks for a handful of their veteran players. As we have seen on the offensive line, when players who are not at least replacement level are on the field, injury risk goes up for the rest of the players around them.
Is a seventh-round pick or two worth the downstream damage a veteran's absence could create? Likely not. The Chargers have been playing awful football and were not going to have good offers for many of their players.
Did the franchise wait too long to engage in trade discussions? More than likely. They may have missed on opportunities to gain extra capital. It is clear though, unlike other teams around the league like the Colts who had top-tier assets that could net strong draft capital in return, the Chargers do not have a Quenton Nelson or Jonathan Taylor on the roster.
As frustrating as it is to watch the process or lack of process, the simple fact remains, the Chargers have been playing terribly, suffered significant injuries and were not going to get top compensation back. And no, trading franchise quarterback Justin Herbert would never have been an option .

title: Brandon Aiyuk Could be a Fantastic Addition for the Chargers if Released
full_text:
The possibility of Brandon Aiyuk becoming available is something the Los Angeles Chargers should be paying attention to. Regardless of his recent drama, the elite receiver still has a lot left in the tank.
If the San Francisco 49ers decide to release him, there is a legitimate argument to be made for bringing him into the picture.
According to Jordan Schultz , Aiyuk passed his physical and was reinstated. Noting that “The next step is hoping for a release from San Francisco.”
One of the biggest things this offense could benefit from is having another receiver who can consistently win on the outside. The Bolts have desperately needed a player to fill this role since the departure of Mike Williams a few years back.
Aiyuk brings that type of ability. He’s not simply someone who needs to be schemed open or given easy opportunities to make plays. He has the ability to create separation, work against defensive backs and make things happen when the ball comes his way. Those are qualities that make him an interesting option for a team looking to improve its receiving group. A major upside would be adding a legitimate X receiver. Having someone who can line up outside and give opposing defenses another matchup to worry about would be valuable. It would also give the offense more flexibility with how it uses its other receivers.
There’s also something to be said about the timing of a potential opportunity. Good receivers don’t become available every day. Especially ones who have already demonstrated the ability to be productive in this league. Also since the Chargers did not trade for one, this could be a great opportunity.
I don’t think this needs to be viewed as some massive move that would completely change the direction of the franchise. Sometimes, it’s about recognizing an opportunity to improve one area of the roster before the season gets underway. Adding another outside receiver with Aiyuk’s abilities would give the coaching staff another option and potentially make the entire receiving room more versatile. At the end of the day, I think Brandon Aiyuk is a name worth keeping an eye on. There are certainly questions that would need to be answered. However the overall fit is interesting enough to make this worth considering.
If he becomes available and the financial side of things works out, I would have a hard time arguing against making a move for him.
Sources: #49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk passed his physical Monday and was officially reinstated. The next step is hoping for a release from San Francisco, and I’m told at least one NFC team has internally discussed the possibility of adding Aiyuk to its practice squad if and when… pic.twitter.com/PsmPRzZ4Vr
Brennan is sports writer focused on delivering sharp analysis, real-time reactions, and engaging storytelling focused on NFL analysis.  He is passionate about football and breaking down what matters to bring fans closer to the action.  Brennan comes from a family of Chargers fans.

title: Chargers Winners and Losers After the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has finally passed, with all 32 NFL teams now unable to make trades with one another to help improve their current or future rosters. The deadline is often an exciting time, considering that change and, by virtue of it, hope can occur.
This hope was desperately needed from the Bolts, with the team being 0-8 and coming off an absolutely horrid blowout loss to the now 3-5 Houston Texans.
General manager Joe Hortiz opted to make one move at the deadline, trading away Daiyan Henley to divisional rival Denver Broncos in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Henley has been a vocal leader for the Bolts since his breakout season in 2024 but has unfortunately regressed on the field since then. This gave the Chargers the opportunity to trade him away and opt to play other individuals...some of whom will be on this list as a winner.
Marlowe Wax is the first name that should come to mind as a winner for the Chargers post-NFL trade deadline. Before Henley was traded away, Wax was already climbing up the depth chart, playing more and more in the LB rotation.
Now that Henley is gone, Wax should be expected to start and/or see a major increase in playing time, even with Denzel Perryman being expected to return from injured reserve.  So far this season, in his limited snaps (48 total), Wax has recorded 15 tackles and a pass deflection, which resulted in an interception...coincidentally for Henley.
Omarion Hampton is considered a "loser" in this scenario as both Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal both remained on the roster after the trade deadline. Both RBs are young with production, giving reason for them to be traded to a team that could use a rushing threat.
Instead, they remain on the roster, which I believe to be the right move. However, this still means that Hampton will be splitting carries with Mitchell and Vidal, making his sophomore-slump likely to continue for the rest of the NFL season.
RJ Mickens should be considered a winner after the deadline, as he should be expected to see a small uptick in snaps. With Henley being traded away, this will likely prompt the Bolts to play more dime packages or packages that see fellow safety Tony Jefferson playing closer to the line of scrimmage in an LB-esque role, giving Mickens more opportunities on defense.
Akheem Mesidor has been quite solid in his rookie year, showing flashes as the team's third EDGE rusher. Unfortunately, the team is 0-8 and no one is talking about how well he is playing. With more playing time, that could have changed, but for Mesidor, it seems his role will stay the same post-NFL trade deadline due to the Bolts' best and most talked-about trade asset, Khalil Mack, not being traded to a contending team.

title: Rams Officially Place Puka Nacua on Injured Reserve, Make Two Roster Moves
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have officially placed wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve . After Nacua got hurt late in the fourth quarter against the Washington Commanders on Sunday, it was determined that he suffered a sprained PCL and turf toe. While the Rams weren’t initially sure whether they would place Nacua on injured reserve, they made it official on Thursday.
In corresponding moves, the Rams signed wide receiver Brennan Presley to the active roster and added Tyler Scott to the practice squad.
With Nacua on injured reserve, he will miss at least the next four games. While the Rams have a bye next week, that does not count against the time missed. Nacua would have to miss games against the Arizona Cardinals, Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and San Francisco 49ers. That would put Nacua back for Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys at the earliest.
Prior to Thursday, the Rams were unsure whether they would place Nacua on injured reserve . Teams are only allowed eight return designations during the season. The Rams had already used return designations on Keagen Trost, Myles Garrett, Ronnie Rivers, and Terrance Ferguson. They are also likely to use return designations on Kobie Turner and Davante Adams. If they plan on using one on Nacua as well, that would put them at seven of their eight available return designations.
While Nacua is out, the Rams will be relying on Konata Mumpfield , Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, and Xavier Smith to fill in at wide receiver. Additionally, Adams should be back following the Packers game in Week 12.
Now that Nacua is on injured reserve, the Rams are very thin at the wide receiver position. It makes sense to bring up a player like Presley. Presley has spent time on the practice squad the last two years and could provide some special teams value. At Oklahoma State, Presley earned All-Big 12 honors as a kick returner.
The Rams also added Scott to the practice squad. Scott was on the practice squad last year with the Rams and spent all of training camp with the team before being let go as part of final roster cuts.
The additions of Presley and Scott give the Rams some flexibility at wide receiver, but it's difficult to see either player making a significant impact on offense. With the trade deadline already passed, the Rams don't have many options to improve the position. For now, they'll have to hope that their young receivers can provide enough production to keep the offense afloat until Adams and Nacua return.

title: Rams Midweek Report: Are the Playoffs Still Realistic? Puka Nacua to IR, and Trade Deadline Leftovers
full_text:
Just as things were starting to look better and the Los Angeles Rams could see the light at the end of the tunnel, they were hit with another barrage of injuries. Last week, it was expected that the Rams would get Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson back. With Davante Adams set to return in a few weeks, it was looking like as long as the Rams could stay afloat, the playoffs were still within reach.
As quickly as Ferguson returned, he was out again, this time with a hamstring injury that he suffered during his first practice back. During the game against the Washington Commanders, Steve Avila left the game with a hamstring injury and Puka Nacua injured his knee late in the fourth quarter. That doesn’t mention that Trent McDuffie had to miss Sunday’s game with a back injury. It marked the third game in four weeks that McDuffie missed.
At this point, do we need to add that the Rams are without Jaylen Watson for the rest of the season? All season it’s been one step forward and two steps back for the Rams on the injury front. The Rams have remained mostly healthy on the offensive line, but at skill positions, it certainly feels like 2022 all over again.
It’s not all bleak, though. For as injured as the Rams have been, they finally went on a run they needed. With their third straight win last week, the Rams improved to 5-4 and moved above .500 for the first time this season.
Now it becomes a matter of whether the Rams can survive this next wave of injuries to still be in contention for the playoffs come December. According to several metrics, the Rams have one of the more grueling schedules in the NFL over the second half of the season.
So the Rams future schedule... is... sheesh pic.twitter.com/XpSkHTWoHj
Following the Rams’ bye week, they will play the Green Bay Packers and Kansas City Chiefs. The Rams will be without Adams for at least the Packers game and likely Avila as well. With Puka Nacua set to go on injured reserve, they will be without Nacua for those games as well.
The Packers and Chiefs certainly have their flaws, but both have top-10 defenses. Through nine weeks, the Packers rank sixth in defensive EPA per play and the Chiefs rank tenth. The Rams were already inconsistent on offense. With Adams coming off of a hamstring injury and without Nacua and Avila, it could make things even more difficult.
If the Rams beat the Cardinals and then lose back-to-back games to the Packers and Chiefs, that puts them at 6-6. At that point, they’d have to rattle off five straight wins or hope that 10-7 is good enough to make the playoffs in a very difficult NFC.
While it certainly hurts their playoff chances, it doesn’t eliminate them. At that point, the Rams would be mostly healthy going into San Francisco and be in a position to make a run. It doesn’t seem crazy to think that the Rams could win five straight games to finish off the season.
Even if they were to lose to the 49ers, The Athletic’s projection gives them a 72 percent chance to make the postseason. An 11-6 finish puts them at 99 percent.
This isn’t to say the Rams’ season is over or that there’s reason to have a negative outlook. That is a realistic scenario. The Rams managed to show toughness and grit to survive the first half of the season. Now they’ll need to do the same in the second half.
There had been some thought that t he Rams may not place Nacua on injured reserve . The Rams only have eight return designations to use throughout the season. They’ve used one on Keagen Trost, Myles Garrett, Ronnie River, and Terrance Ferguson. The Rams will likely use one on Kobie Turner and Davante Adams. By putting Nacua on injured reserve with the expectation that he will come back, the Rams have one return designation remaining.
With Nacua set to go on injured reserve, he will be out at least four games. The bye week does not count. That means the earliest Nacua can return is Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys on December 20. His absence against the Cardinals, Packers, Chiefs, and 49ers certainly makes things interesting. The Rams need to find a way to survive that stretch.
Following Tuesday’s trade deadline, the Rams came away empty-handed. Despite needing a wide receiver, the Rams opted to hold on to their draft assets. It’s certainly an odd decision considering that the WR1 right now is Konata Mumpfield.
With that said, that doesn’t mean the Rams didn’t try. According to ESPN’s Dan Graziano, the Rams were among the teams that called about Ladd McConkey. The Rams also called on Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman , but wouldn’t give up what was being asked for him. Cleveland Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot reported that the Rams also called on Jerry Jeudy. However, the Browns wanted premium draft picks.
While the Rams made trade calls, nothing ever got serious. The thinking in the building remains that they will get Davante Adams and Puka Nacua back this season and that making a trade and giving up assets wasn't necessary.
It was initially reported that the 49ers were going to release Brandon Aiyuk on Tuesday after he reported to the team. However, with Aiyuk on the Commissioner’s Exempt List, the 49ers are likely to hold on to him for the next two weeks. Once Aiyuk does become available, he’s a low-risk signing that the Rams should consider . He provides a solid WR3 option, and if he can return to his pre-injury form, the Rams would be getting a player who was once a borderline top-10 wide receiver.
Without Adams and Nacua, it will be interesting to see what Sean McVay does on offense. Back in 2018, defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz said,
“The hardest thing gap-control wise is 22 personnel (two backs, two tight ends),” Schwartz says. “Thirteen (one back, three tight ends), if you don’t know exactly what you’re doing on defense, 13 personnel can wear your ass out.”
A serious argument can be made that the best two players on offense for the Rams on Sunday will be Blake Corum and Kyren Williams. It could make sense to get both players on the field. Williams especially has proven to run good routes while Corum has been one of the more efficient running backs in the NFL.
Two weeks ago against the Los Angeles Chargers, it took an entire half before Sean McVay’s hand was forced and he had to play rookie tight end Max Klare. Playing Klare was the best decision McVay made in that game and left some wondering why he hadn’t been playing him previously.
The same can be said about CJ Daniels. By all accounts, Daniels impressed in training camp and the preseason. However, he has played just six snaps on offense. Given the Rams’ current wide receiver situation, that needs to change. It’s time to give Daniels an opportunity .
Not too much changed from Wednesday’s projection. However, tight end Davis Allen was downgraded from a limited participant to DNP with an oblique injury. Additionally, tight end Tyler Higbee was added as a non-participant due to an illness. The biggest thing for the Rams on Thursday was Nacua officially heading to injured reserve.
