title: Rams Film Review: Myles Garrett Could Exploit Major Weakness Against Cardinals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams finally got a glimpse of what a healthy Myles Garrett looks like on their defense against the Washington Commanders. After being out for almost two months with a knee injury, Garrett made his return last week and showed the Rams why they traded for him.
Despite playing only 60 percent of the defensive snaps, Garrett made his impact felt. He played 28 pass rush snaps and finished with three sacks, including one forced fumble. The explosiveness and bend that Garrett lacked in Week 1 were on display against the Commanders.
Just look at that bend around the edge from Myles Garrett. Can tell he was really starting starting to feel like himself and gain confidence as the game went on. pic.twitter.com/P3Xeo1cl5w
In his first game back, Garrett had a 21.4 percent pressure rate and generated six pressures. His 28.6 percent pass rush win rate led all edge rushers for the week as well.  The Rams traded for Garrett to be their closer on defense and two of his three sacks came in the fourth quarter. His third sack was on a 3rd-and-4 to set up a 4th-and-17 and helped stop a late surge by the Commanders offense.
One of the main reasons Aaron Donald came out of retirement was to play alongside Garrett. It took two months, but the wait was worth it. It’s no coincidence that Donald’s best game of the season came with Garrett on the field.
Blocking Myles Garrett: LG, LT, TE Blocking Aaron Donald: RG (kinda), RT, RB Even with Myles Garrett, Donald still managing to get triple teamed 😭😂 pic.twitter.com/QZXxWcdRj5
For much of his career, offenses had to focus all of their attention on Donald. That’s not something they could do with Garrett on the edge. Donald finished Sunday’s game with a season-high four pressures and a 12.9 percent pressure rate.
“Myles obviously did a great job, but I thought ‘AD’ had a couple awesome things that allowed him to be able to get some one-on-ones and get freed up and thought the plan that we had was really beneficial,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Yesterday was the first day that it was on tape of how you're deploying Myles. It may or may not be the same or different as you continue to increase his snap count as he's feeling better and getting back to being able to play that workload that he's been accustomed to throughout his whole career, but it was very impactful as was ‘AD’.”
Using Garrett solely in pass rush situations gave the Rams more flexibility in how they deployed him. Throughout the game, Chris Shula occasionally mugged Garrett over the center. This is something that the Rams did with Verse occasionally, but Garrett also had success doing it in Cleveland.
The Browns defense aligned Myles Garrett over the center on four plays against the Bengals. Here were the results: -Sack -Incompletion -Incompletion -Incompletion Jim Schwartz is weaponizing him by moving him around the front. The entire Steelers OL better come ready to rock. pic.twitter.com/OHqhY2kZWl
Garrett lined up over the center on four plays against the Commanders. On those plays, he had two pressures, created a pressure for Donald on a stunt, and had one sack. Garrett’s size and speed make it very difficult for the average center to block one-on-one.
This is likely something that the Rams will try to take advantage of this week against the Cardinals as well. Hjalte Froholdt and Jon Gaines have been out of practice for the Cardinals with injuries. That would leave Hayden Conner as the third-string center, who is also technically the fourth-string guard.
The Cardinals could be down to their 4th-string center on Sunday. That could be a problem. The Rams situationally put Garrett over the center and had success with it. pic.twitter.com/JFf2EFuYlf
With the Rams down their starting two wide receivers, they may have to rely on their defense more. While the defense had been good for much of the season, Garrett helped take it to the next level that many have been waiting to see . The presence of Garrett could be enough to help carry the Rams over the next month until they get healthy on offense again.

title: How the Rams Offense Can Survive Without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams
full_text:
Over the next few games, the Los Angeles Rams will need to figure out how to manage without their top two wide receivers. Davante Adams is likely out at least the next three weeks and Puka Nacua could be out four. With Adams and Nacua out, the Rams will need to get what they can out of Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell. It’s not necessarily a predicament that the Rams want to be in.
Heading into Week 10, the Rams are one of two teams  that will play without a wide receiver who has even 250 receiving yards in 2026. The other team is the Indianapolis Colts, who traded away their top two wide receivers at the trade deadline.
Throughout the season, the Rams have been inconsistent on offense to say the least. Against the Los Angeles Chargers, they went three-and-out on each of their first five possessions. That’s not something a Rams offense had done this century, and that includes offenses coached by Jeff Fisher. Nacua was in the lineup for those games.
This isn’t to say that the Rams’ offense can’t figure it out or nobody will step up. However, it also wouldn’t be incorrect to believe that being without Adams and Nacua will make things more difficult offensively. That also doesn’t mention the absence of Avila at left guard.
At the end of the day, the Rams will be relying on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and CJ Daniels at wide receiver. Mumpfield is a seventh-round pick, Atwell  likely would have been cut by the Miami Dolphins had the Rams not traded for him, and Daniels has played six snaps on offense. The Rams also re-signed Xavier Smith, who was previously cut back in Week 3.
The Rams’ current wide receiver situation would leave some wishing for the days of Austin Pettis, Chris Givens, and Brandon Gibson. Head coach Sean McVay joked on Wednesday about the possibility of Robert Woods coming out of retirement. It’s bleak to say the least, but that’s where the Rams are at.
For as much as the Rams may want to lean on the defense and run game, they will have to be able to prove they can still throw the ball. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers won a game this season in which Baker Mayfield didn’t complete a pass. However, it’s highly unlikely that the Rams get blessed with monsoon conditions at State Farm Stadium on Sunday or back at SoFi following the bye.
This season, the Rams’ entire offense has been Puka Nacua. Nacua has 715 yards receiving. All other Rams wide receivers that have recorded a catch this season have combined for 753. Mumpfield and Atwell have a combined 261 receiving yards this season. Nacua had 230 yards in the last two weeks alone.
Offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase talked last week about how much the team trusts the wide receiver group behind Nacua. “I think the encouragement that we have is we have guys that we feel we can put trust in to be able to supplement him in the right ways.”
On Wednesday, quarterback Matthew Stafford also mentioned how much trust he has in that group.
“I still throw those guys every single day in practice and have a ton of trust in what they can do,” Stafford said. “With those guys, trust the route running techniques that they have. Trust themselves to go out there and make plays because these guys are here for a reason. I'm excited for their opportunity.”
Despite what Scheelhaase and Stafford have said, it’s become abundantly clear that they don’t have trust in that group. Mumpfield leads the Rams’ wide receiver depth with a 6.8 percent target share on the season. Among players who have run at least 100 routes, that ranks 101st out of 111 wide receivers.
Just in the last three weeks without Adams, Nacua has a 43.2 percent target share. Only CeeDee Lamb’s is higher. Mumpfield’s target share of 6.3 percent ranks 72nd out of 75 qualifying players. Atwell’s 9.5 percent ranks 63rd.
While some will say that Stafford has simply locked onto Nacua, you only have to look at the receivers around him to understand why that might be the case. Mumpfield has a targeted success rate of 39.1 percent. Atwell remains limited as a route runner. Almost half of his routes are deep corner or go routes.
For as much as Xavier Smith struggles as the team’s punt returner, he did show some upside at receiver last season. There’s a reason he was getting snaps over Atwell. Smith led the Rams in EPA per target and was only behind Nacua in targeted success rate and yards per route run. There is at least some logic to why the Rams brought him back with him having some success and being familiar in the system.
Again, Daniels has six snaps on offense this season. While he was a training camp and preseason standout, he hasn’t been able to see the field. McVay has shown in the past that if a rookie wide receiver displays an understanding of the offense, they’ll play. That has not been the case up to this point with Daniels.
Last week, McVay hinted at a larger role for Daniels . He played one offensive snap. With three healthy wide receivers, now seems as good of a time as any for Daniels to get his chance. At this point, it’s hard to understand why Daniels hasn’t gotten more involved given that Adams has been out the last three weeks.
As the game progressed, you really saw Ty Simpson start to get comfortable. With be interested if Rams let him off the reigns a little bit next week. Tight coverage on CJ Daniels and Simpson throws an accurate ball. pic.twitter.com/ZPOUISGzac
“I don't know that I could really say any areas of improvement until he truly gets his opportunity,” McVay said on Monday. “He is a guy that, no question about it, will get an opportunity to play more snaps moving forward.”
“C.J. has done a hell of a job,” added Stafford. “I'm excited to get some chances to throw with him, get it out there on Sunday, and just get his feet wet. It's an opportunity, like I said, for a lot of guys in this situation that we're in. I'm just excited to go be a part of it.”
The Rams have done a lot of talking about how much they trust their wide receiver depth and how good of a job they’ve done, but it’s time for them to turn words into action.
Outside of the wide receivers, the Rams could look to use their tight ends as well. The Rams will likely operate heavily out of 13 personnel. However, that could limit the passing game with Terrance Ferguson out nursing a hamstring. Tyler Higbee has shown some of his limitations as he’s gotten older. Without Ferguson at tight end, the rest of the group lacks explosiveness.
Throughout his tenure, McVay has devised one-off gameplans in these exact types of situations. In 2021, when the Rams were hit by COVID, McVay used six offensive linemen. When the Rams were injured for the Jacksonville Jaguars game last season, he implemented 13 personnel that has since become the identity of the offense.
If there is any head coach that can figure out how to run an offense with limited options at wide receiver, it’s McVay. The two best offensive players on the field against the Cardinals will likely be Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. It may be unlikely, but operating out of 22 personnel with two tight ends and two running backs wouldn’t be a crazy idea.
Without Nacua and Adams, an argument can be made that Williams is the best receiving option on the team. Williams’ 1.34 yards per route run is higher than Mumpfield or Atwell’s. Corum isn’t perfect as a pass catcher, but still averages 1.74 yards per route run, which also ranks seventh among running backs. Both Williams and Corum also rank inside the top 15 among qualifying running backs in first downs per route run.
Even if the Rams don’t go to the extreme and use 22 personnel, both will likely be used often in the passing game to some capacity. Williams had 10 receptions in Week 4 against the Eagles. Without Nacua in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos, Williams had six receptions.
The Rams are going to have to get creative in the passing game until Nacua and Adams return. It’s also possible they look at wide receiver options as they become available as well. McVay will need to…

title: Rams vs. Cardinals Prediction: Preview, Key Matchups, and What to Watch
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be looking to get their first division win on Sunday in Week 10 as they take on the Arizona Cardinals for the second time this season. Both teams will enter Sunday dealing with their own set of injuries . The Rams will have to manage without Puka Nacua, among others, while the Cardinals will be without Gardner Minshew at quarterback.
Since losing to the Cardinals back in Week 6, the Rams have won three straight games. The loss to the Cardinals marked rock bottom, but they’ve managed to climb back to .500 for the first time in 2026. However, the Rams continue to get bombarded with injuries. Along with Nacua, the Rams could be without Steve Avila, Trent McDuffie, and others in addition to the players already on injured reserve.
Carson Beck will be making his first career start for the Cardinals on Sunday, and it won’t be easy for him. The Cardinals will be without Michael Wilson and could be down to their fourth-string center. Beck will also be facing a Rams defense that looked good with Myles Garrett back last week.
Back in Week 6, the Rams were without Alaric Jackson at left tackle, and the Cardinals took advantage, blitzing Stafford relentlessly.For the most part, McVay was outcoached by defensive coordinator Nick Rallis. With Avila out and the Rams not having Nacua , it wouldn’t be surprising to see a similar game plan from the Cardinals.
The Rams will be one of just two teams in Week 10 playing without a wide receiver who has recorded at least 250 receiving yards in 2026. Throughout the season, the Rams have been inconsistent on offense, and that was with Nacua. It’s going to be much more difficult when the top wide receiver options are Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell. At some point, the Rams are going to have to be able to beat teams in the passing game and will need to prove they can still do so.
In the first game against the Cardinals, the Rams didn’t allow a single touchdown. However, they did allow long drives that ended in field goals. They allowed the Cardinals to play keep away and control the game. It wouldn’t be surprising to see the Cardinals come out with a similar game plan as they look to keep things simple for Beck in his first start.
Jayden Williams has allowed an 8.3 percent pressure rate this season. Among qualifying offensive linemen, that’s the 10th-highest in the NFL. The Rams got Myles Garrett back last week, and he made his presence felt with three sacks and a forced fumble. Chris Shula will likely move Garrett around and line him up over the center occasionally, but he should be set up to have another strong performance.
Given the amount of injuries on both sides, this is looking like it could be an ugly game. Both teams will be rolling out preseason-caliber options at wide receiver. With that said, Beck is making his first start and the Cardinals haven’t won at home since early last year. The Rams need a win going into their bye week to set themselves up well for the second half of the season. Without Nacua, the Rams will need to lean on the defense and run game. Prediction: Rams 16, Cardinals 10

title: Rams Injury Report: Trent McDuffie Status Uncertain as Rams Face More Injury Troubles
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could be significantly short-handed on Sunday as they get ready for their Week 6 rematch against the Arizona Cardinals. Steve Avila, Puka Nacua, Trent McDuffie, Kam Curl, and Terrance Ferguson were all projected as non-participants in Wednesday’s walkthrough, with most of them likely to miss the game.
One player that the Rams will hope to get back this week is cornerback Trent McDuffie. After McDuffie returned against the Los Angeles Chargers, he missed last week’s game with a back injury.
“I think we're optimistic that this week he will be able to go,” said head coach Sean McVay. “With the injury that he sustained, it's weird because you have these muscles around it in the back, which in some of the movement, especially at his position. He's so damn tough but you want to make sure that you're putting him in a position to have a successful outcome.”
The Rams are set to be without Puka Nacua, Steve Avila, and Terrance Ferguson against the Cardinals. McVay noted on Wednesday that the Rams won’t place Nacua on injured reserve due to the limited return designations they have available. With Avila and Ferguson, the Rams are expecting both to be out a few weeks.
Also showing up on Wednesday’s injury report were Joe Cardona, Davis Allen, Colby Parkinson, and Myles Garrett, who were all projected as limited participants. Cardona has missed the last two games with an ankle injury. Allen and Parkinson will be players to monitor throughout the week. While Garrett showed up on the injury report, that shouldn’t be surprising going forward. The Rams will likely manage him during the week to ensure that he’s ready for gameday.
Despite the Rams being as injured as they are, the Cardinals might be in a worse spot. The Cardinals are set to be without Gardner Minshew, meaning Carson Beck will get his first career start against the Rams. Additionally, Michael Wilson injured his neck and will be out.
Hjalte Froholdt (concussion), Jon Gaines (ankle), and Roy Lopez (toe/ankle) were all non-participants for the Cardinals on Wednesday as well.
The Rams have dealt with injuries throughout the season, but the situation has become especially challenging over the last few weeks. With several key starters expected to miss Sunday's game, the Rams will once again have to rely on their depth to avoid getting swept by the Cardinals. They’ve managed to win three straight games despite their injuries, but continuing that success without players like Nacua and Avila won’t be easy.

title: Rams Make Surprising Puka Nacua Injury Decision as Sean McVay Provides Update on Davante Adams Return
full_text:
After some speculation that the Los Angeles Rams could put wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve , head coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that wouldn’t be the case. The Rams are set to keep Nacua on the active roster as he misses time with a knee injury. Additionally, McVay added some clarity on Davante Adams’ return and noted that the team expects him back following the game against the Green Bay Packers.
Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that the team will not place Puka Nacua on injured reserve due to roster mechanics, but that the WR still will be out for a “significant period of time.” pic.twitter.com/QggesIr2Nh
The Rams deciding not to place Nacua on injured reserve is certainly an interesting choice. Had Nacua been placed on injured reserve, the soonest he could come back would be for Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys. By not placing Nacua on IR, the Rams can hope to get him back for their Week 14 rematch against the San Francisco 49ers.
While the Rams may be hopeful that Nacua is back in time for Week 14, that’s not likely the reason why he was kept off of injured reserve. During the regular season, teams are only allowed eight return designations off of IR.
As it stands, the Rams have already used return designations on Terrance Ferguson, Myles Garrett, Ronnie Rivers and Keagen Trost. With Adams set to return, that brings their total to five. The Rams will also likely use a return designation on Kobie Turner when he’s healthy. That gives the Rams two spots for the remainder of the season.
If Nacua is expected back on the shorter end of four weeks, it makes sense to just eat that roster spot instead of using a return designation when it might be needed later. It also looms large that the Rams used one of their return designations on Rivers last week.
With the second half of the season still to come, the Rams will likely try to preserve an injured reserve spot if they need it. If the Rams make the playoffs, they will be given two more return designations.
Heading into the week, there was some thought that Adams could be back after the bye week to go up against his former team. However, McVay said on Wednesday that the team expects him back after the Packers’ game. Adams was initially given a 6-10 week timeline, but was expected back on the shorter end of that. After the Packers game would have put Adams right at six weeks.
Additionally, the Rams will be without Steve Avila for a handful of weeks, but are hoping to avoid injured reserve with him as well.
The Rams have been hit hard by injuries this season, and that has forced them to be strategic with how they manage the roster. While keeping Nacua off injured reserve limits their flexibility in the short term, it could pay off later in the season. The Rams will have to survive the next few weeks without Nacua and Adams, but the hope remains that both will be back in time to help the team make a playoff push.

title: Rams Missed Chance to Add Wide Receiver at Trade Deadline, But Brandon Aiyuk Could Be the Answer
full_text:
The trade deadline came and went on Tuesday with the Los Angeles Rams not making a move for a wide receiver . After losing Puka Nacua to injury and already down Davante Adams, it was expected that the Rams would try to acquire a player at the deadline.
While the Rams had conversations for players, nothing got serious and they stood pat with their current options on the roster. Over the next few weeks, the Rams will be without Adams and Nacua. With Jordan Whittington on injured reserve, the Rams will be relying on Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, and Xavier Smith as their top receiving options.
After not making a trade at the deadline, the Rams could hope for players to become available. In 2021 and 2022, the Rams benefitted as they signed Odell Beckham Jr. and Baker Mayfield after they were cut.
The Rams will continue to try and get healthy, but they could still supplement the roster as players become available. If the Washington Commanders continue to lose, Stefon Diggs may ask for his release. While the process is being dragged out by the San Francisco 49ers, the Rams could also look to sign Brandon Aiyuk .
It was expected that the 49ers would release Aiyuk on Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET, but a clause in the CBA changed the dynamic. According to Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk, the 49ers don’t have to pay Aiyuk while he’s on the Commissioner Exempt List. That pushes their deadline for avoiding owing him a game check until Tuesday, November 24. It’s likely at that point the Rams would consider signing Aiyuk. That’s also one day before their game against the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.
Signing Aiyuk is certainly complicated. He brings a lot of off-field issues that he’s created himself over the last year. At the same time, the 49ers aren’t innocent either. Holding on to Aiyuk at this point seems petty. The only reason not to release him would be to hamper his ability to join another team.
The 49ers are holding onto Brandon Aiyuk for one reason — because they can. pic.twitter.com/MZja4AiMbV
For all of his off-field problems, the Rams may not have a choice when it comes to Aiyuk. Beggars can’t be choosers and the Rams aren’t in a position to be picky when it comes to their wide receiver options. Again, as it stands, their top wide receiver is Mumpfield. Aiyuk had more receiving yards in his shortened 2024 season than Mumpfield has the last two years.
Aiyuk is also simply a player who makes sense as he fits the Rams archetype at receiver and is proven to fit the system. He’s a good route runner, separator, and blocker and provides YAC potential.
A big reason why the Rams didn’t want to trade for a wide receiver was because of their limited 2027 draft capital. Aiyuk wouldn’t cost that. After not playing for two years, the Rams could likely sign him to a veteran minimum deal with incentives for more.
Additionally, the Rams are set to play the 49ers in five weeks. Aiyuk will certainly be motivated to play against his former team that has kept him off the field for much of the last two years. The wide receiver the Rams should want for that matchup is one that has been publicly frustrated and feels like he has been wronged by the 49ers over the past year.
There is certainly risk with Aiyuk given his injury history and the fact that he hasn’t played since 2024. At this point, it seems like a risk worth taking. The Rams don’t have anything to lose by adding Aiyuk to the roster. If he doesn’t work, the Rams can cut him or move on after the season. In the case he plays well, they can try to re-sign him.
Given the Rams’ current situation at wide receiver, it seems like an option the Rams should at least explore. Adding Aiyuk would give the Rams a chance to make up for what they didn’t do at the trade deadline.
With the margins getting thin, the Rams can’t sit around and hope to get healthy. That was the plan going into the bye week, and they lost Nacua as soon as they got back Myles Garrett. Simply banking on getting healthy isn’t a luxury that this Rams team seems to have.
The Rams made the decision not to trade for a wide receiver at the deadline. Signing Aiyuk wouldn't erase that mistake, but it would at least show that the Rams recognize the urgency of their situation. The Rams need someone who can help keep their season afloat until Nacua and Adams return. Given the circumstances, Aiyuk may be their best opportunity to do that.

title: Rams Legend Steven Jackson Reflects on His Career, Kyren Williams and Playoff Hopes
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have a strong history at the running back position, and one of the best within the last 20 years was Steven Jackson. While Jackson didn’t necessarily play on many good Rams teams, he was always one of the bright spots and remained incredibly consistent. Jackson remains one of six running backs in NFL history to rush for 1,000 yards in eight consecutive seasons.
Throughout the years, Jackson has remained involved in the Rams community. With Los Angeles sitting at 5-4 and on a three-game winning streak, Jackson recently talked with Rams On SI to share his thoughts on the team's current running back duo and playoff chances as it starts to get healthy.
Prior to the Rams’ game against the Los Angeles Chargers two weeks ago, Jackson took part in a Rams community event in partnership with Edwards Lifesciences and their Off the Sidelines Initiative, encouraging fans to take charge of their heart health through free heart valve screenings and education.
“At Edwards Lifesciences, we're committed to advancing heart health and helping more people understand the importance of early detection,” said Evan Webber, Vice President of Marketing at Edwards Lifesciences. “Through our Off the Sidelines partnership with the Los Angeles Rams, we're making heart valve failure education and screening more accessible to the community. Together, we're encouraging adults 50 and older to be proactive about their heart health, talk to their healthcare provider, and get screened.”
Jackson joined Torry Holt and Eric Dickerson for the event after previously participating in the initiative during training camp.
“I actually participated a couple of times this year with Edwards LifeSciences. I was screened myself to make sure that my heart passages are clear or if there's any concern to be brought to notice,” said Jackson. “It could be a silent killer…There are the conditions like this heart disease that could kill us quietly if we're not aware of it and not getting checked up…Early screening only takes 5 minutes of people’s time.”
Just met the great Steven Jackson!!! @sj39 🔥🔥🔥 #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/4wgmP2ndrD
While Jackson and Williams have different running styles, the emotion and heart that they play with are very similar. It’s widely known that Williams grew up a Rams fan and there’s a photo of him as a kid in the Edward Jones Dome with Jackson.
The rookie and the legend. 🤝 pic.twitter.com/zYQYDvk2Qq
Williams has since followed in Jackson’s footsteps as a Rams running back and has been a similar model of consistency. Over the past three seasons, Williams has eclipsed the 1,000-yard mark. He is the only Rams running back since Jackson to rush for 1,000 yards in three consecutive seasons.
“Anytime you can have an influence on anybody's life in a positive way, you know, it's one of those things that's a feel-good story,” said Jackson. “I'm happy that my interaction with Kyren has left him in the sense that he thinks fondly of me. And then to go on and see him have his own career and be very, very successful in his own right is even more rewarding to see that just compounding interest and just doing right by people.”
Throughout Jackson’s career, he was a true bell cow at running back. He started his career behind Marshall Faulk, but eventually took over as the lead player in the Rams’ backfield.
However, over the last two years, the Rams have used a running back by committee approach with Williams and Blake Corum. Williams has remained the steady presence while Corum has provided some elusiveness.
“Having Corum back him up, you see why the longevity of why they use them interchangeably and why you try to bring them both to the postseason healthy,” Jackson said. “They're both dynamic runners, but Kyren does an unbelievable job of finding the end zone.”
During Jackson’s career with the Rams, he didn’t experience a lot of team success. The Rams made the playoffs in Jackson’s rookie season, but never had a winning record. Still, Jackson was a model of consistency despite not always getting the individual recognition.
In 2009, the Rams went 1-15 and Jackson had one of the best years of his career. Jackson ranked third in the NFL in rushing yards with 1,416 and scored four touchdowns. In their lone win, Jackson rushed for 149 yards and scored the game-winning touchdown against the Detroit Lions.
“There are certain things that we have a standard or we have beliefs or something in our inner core that we live to and hope to be a beacon of and we try to aspire to be that each and every day,” Jackson said. “For me as a kid that grew up wanting to play professional football, wanting to be an NFL running back, and having that answered and having that given to me with the opportunity, I didn't think it would be right in honoring what I worked so hard for and praised for to then take it for granted.”
Some of the more fun battles to watch throughout Jackson’s career were his yearly matchups with San Francisco 49ers linebacker Patrick Willis. The two players faced off 17 times between 2007 and 2012.
While the Rams-49ers rivalry has taken on new life since the Rams moved back to Los Angeles, Jackson and Willis had their battles.
“I view playing against Patrick Willis and the 49ers defense as that me giving me the chance to rise to the occasion against someone that's a Hall of Famer,” said Jackson. “When you play with the passion that I try to show up with each and every Sunday, It lets everyone know that, you know, there's pride taken into what we put on the field. And that's how I carry myself in my career.”
The Rams have had an up-and-down season to say the least. They’ve dealt with injuries and lost some close games. However, after beating the Washington Commanders, they have won three straight and are above .500 for the first time this year.
Despite losing Puka Nacua to injury, the Rams also got Myles Garrett back and should continue to get healthy over the next few weeks and after their bye. At 5-4, the Rams control their own destiny and should have a good chance to make a late-season push at the playoffs.
“The Rams definitely had some tough losses, right? You know, you had the longer week one travel to Australia, and then you had a couple of games where you could say officiating was something to be raised,” Jackson said. “When you think about a head coach, a quarterback, a general manager, all the decision makers, you have the right people in the right places. And I think as far as a roster, you're having guys get back healthy, speaking mostly about Myles Garrett, getting ready to come back to make a late push in this run.”

title: Rams Restructure Pair of Contracts, But Could Another Move Be Coming?
full_text:
Following Tuesday’s trade deadline , the Los Angeles Rams opened up cap space on Wednesday as they restructured two contracts. According to Spotrac, The Rams converted $2 million of Kyren Williams’ salary into a signing bonus, adding two void years to create $1.7 million in cap space. The Rams did the same with Kam Curl’s contract, creating $1.3 million in cap space.
Despite restructuring the contracts, the Rams still have flexibility with both. They have an out with Williams’ deal following the 2027 season, while Curl’s contract also provides flexibility after 2027.
With both moves, the Rams have opened up around $3 million in cap space. While it’s natural to look at the moves and wonder if the Rams have a pending move planned, this was always inevitable. The Rams have consistently been among the teams with the least amount of available cap space this season. They have spent a large portion of the season cap-strapped and under $1 million. They were under $10,000 at one point.
It was never going to be sustainable for the Rams to go the rest of the year with that little amount of cap space. Throughout the season, the Rams have dealt with several injuries, forcing them to make weekly roster moves.
With eight games remaining, it was always unlikely that they would get through the rest of the season without needing to make additional, low-level signings. Whether that's signing a player to the active roster, adding depth at an injury-riddled position, or elevating someone from the practice squad, those moves require cap space. At some point, the Rams were going to have to restructure at least one contract.
These moves also show why the Rams' limited cap space was never going to prevent them from making a trade at the deadline. While the Rams didn’t have a lot of cap space to work with, there were ways to open up space as needed.
Now, that isn’t to say that the Rams can’t still sign a big-name player if they become available. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Rams are interested in Brandon Aiyuk when the San Francisco 49ers eventually cut him. If Aiyuk signs for the veteran minimum with incentives, that’s a move the Rams could afford. The same can be said if Stefon Diggs demands a release out of Washington.
At the very least, it gives the Rams flexibility to make a late in-season signing if that’s something they want to do. Previously, that would not have been an option.
The timing of these moves may raise some eyebrows, especially coming one day after the trade deadline and Aiyuk’s pending release. However, this was more about necessity than anything else. The Rams simply couldn't continue operating with so little cap space. While the additional flexibility could allow them to make a move if the right opportunity presents itself, the restructures were something the Rams needed to do regardless.

title: 3 Things Fernando Mendoza Can't Control in First Raiders Start
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are set to finally take the field with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza leading the way. After a long wait, Las Vegas will roll out what they hope will be their last starting quarterback for many seasons to come. First, the Raiders must get through Sunday.
The Raiders' Week 10 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks will present its fair share of challenges. Las Vegas will need to execute at a high level and hope the ball bounces their way a time or two.
Below are three things the Raiders' rookie quarterback cannot control in his very first start, or in general, for that matter.
Las Vegas' offensive line has struggled to open up running lanes this season. Overall, the unit has done relatively well by many statistical measures. Still, the offensive line has spent the past few months working with Kirk Cousins under center; there will naturally be a few hiccups along the way.
If the Raiders' offensive line continues to pass block well and improves their run blocking, Las Vegas quietly has a chance to surprise the Seahawks on Sunday. If the line does not play well, Mendoza, like any quarterback in the league, will also struggle.
The offensive line has its deficiencies, but it probably deserves more credit overall than it has received this season. Some would likely be shocked by how well the unit has graded through nine games. The unit likely ranked even higher before last Sunday's loss.
No matter how the unit performs, it is not on Mendoza. If anything, it is the other way around. Las Vegas' offensive line must protect its rookie quarterback even better than it did for Cousins. Mendoza's mobility should bode well for the unit too, should he use it when possible.
Through the first half, Las Vegas is once again one of the league's worst rushing teams. They are nine games away from that being the case for the fourth straight season. The Raiders' inability to run the ball has hurt the offense and the team as a whole, especially Las Vegas' defense.
In their five losses, the Raiders' offense has been unable to sustain drives, let alone score points, while the game was still competitive. A large part of the reason the offense has struggled is that they can't run the ball. This will eventually negatively impact Mendoza, likely as soon as Sunday.
That problem has plagued the Raiders long before Mendoza or any of the coaches and running backs on the roster arrived.
It would be unreasonable to expect Las Vegas to magically run the ball well consistently simply because Mendoza is starting. If the Raiders cannot get their ground game going, at least marginally better than it has been in the season's first nine games, Mendoza will have a tall task.
The Raiders must get their ground game going on Sunday against the Seahawks, even if that means Mendoza adding two or three runs. Running the ball with Mendoza would give future opposing defenses a legitimate concern that has not been there this season.
In their losses, Las Vegas' defense has failed to play well, and it has been glaringly bad. However, in their wins, the Raiders' defense has shone. The unit has forced the fourth-most turnovers of any defense in the league this season. That is what Mendoza and the Raiders will need on Sunday.
At the very least, Las Vegas' defense has to keep the Seahawks from scoring touchdowns and hope Mendoza finds a rhythm. The unit cannot afford to fall behind early and hope the rookie can beat a Seahawks defense that is playing with a big lead, as has been the case for the Raiders this season.
Regardless of how well the Raiders' defense plays on Sunday, their performance is not on Mendoza, nor is it the rookie's responsibility to compensate should Las Vegas' defense underperform in Week 10.
That said, even though the Seahawks are the better team, I am interested to see how the Raiders' defense responds if Mendoza gets the offense going in the first half. Las Vegas' defense plays better when they know their teammates on offense have their back with points and long drives.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders Receive More Fantastic Injury Report News Ahead of Seahawks
full_text:
Jimmy Garoppolo, Brian Hoyer, Aidan O'Connell, Desmond Ridder, Geno Smith, Kenny Pickett, Kirk Cousins.
The Las Vegas Raiders have had a revolving door at quarterback in recent seasons, starting eight different quarterbacks since 2023. The Raiders' roster finally bottomed out in 2025, registering its second straight season with a 10-game losing streak and securing the No. 1 overall pick.
After eclipsing last season's win total in the first half of the season, the Raiders were presented with a chance to smoothly transition into the Mendoza era. Trading Cousins gave Las Vegas' front office a third-round draft pick for a player who was unlikely to be on the team next season.
Despite the natural buzz that comes with the No. 1 overall pick finally getting to start, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was sure to emphasize the importance of Las Vegas doing what is necessary as a team to make the fact that they're starting a rookie quarterback an afterthought.
“I think the most important thing, like every week, is that you spend a lot of time worrying about you, worrying about your technique, worrying about studying, worrying about watching tape. Yes, we got to prepare them as coaches for what they’re going to see on the practice field, but as a player, you got to make sure you don’t overlook yourself first," Kubiak said earlier this week.
The Raiders returned to the practice field on Thursday ahead of Mendoza's first career start. With Sunday's matchup against the Seattle Seahawks just days away, Las Vegas appears to be about as healthy as it has been at any point this season.
The Raiders' injury report was light on Wednesday , as Thomas Booker, Trey Zuhn, and Foley Fatukasi participated in a limited fashion. Ian Thomas was listed but participated fully. Zuhn's participation, despite being listed with a concussion-related issue, was promising.
On Thursday, the injury report took another promising turn, as Zuhn practiced again. Booker and Zuhn were limited. Fatukasi and Thomas fully participated. The Raiders cannot get much healthier than that halfway through the season. This should work in their favor on Sunday against the Seahawks.
Although in a small sample size, Zuhn looks to be the best offensive guard on the roster this season. The Raiders have their hands full with him, but Sunday will be a long day for the unit without Zuhn. Still, Las Vegas must prepare for what happens if Zuhn can't play or leaves the game early.
Mendoza took another step toward his first professional start and now gets starter-level reps in practice. In addition to the half-season he has had to learn, this week's practices are invaluable ahead of Week 10 . The Raiders hope it gives them a spark under center on Sunday.
The rookie will have his growing pains , as all rookie quarterbacks do. However, with eight games remaining and the Raiders within striking distance of a possible playoff spot, now is the time to turn to the player they have already invested so much in.
The Heisman Trophy, National Championship-winning quarterback knows he has a lot to learn but refuses to be overwhelmed by the moment. Las Vegas' front office used the draft's top pick on Mendoza, in part, because of his poise in big moments. Sunday will be the first test of that poise professionally.
“I believe starting an NFL game is a new step, but a whirlwind? No. I would agree with Coach [Klint] Kubiak. Coach Kubiak, Coach [Andrew] Janocko, and Coach [Mike] Sullivan, and everyone in the quarterback room, including Kirk [Cousins], have done a fantastic job in aiding my development, and I can’t thank them enough. And now it’s my turn to do my 1/11th . And we have such a great offensive staff, and we have such a great offense,” Mendoza said on Wednesday.
Sunday is quietly an important day in the Raiders' storied history, regardless of whether they win the game. Las Vegas' Week 10 matchup against Klint Kubiak's old team signifies the Raiders fully turning the page and moving into the future, for better or worse. It is finally Mendoza season.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: 2 Reasons Why Raiders Playoff Hopes Are Still Alive
full_text:
With a 4-5 record, the Las Vegas Raiders have been viewed as an afterthought when evaluating the AFC playoff picture.
While the Raiders have an uphill battle to reach the playoffs, crazier things have happened in this league. With that in mind, here are a couple of reasons why Las Vegas can challenge for a wildcard spot.
As things currently stand, I would say the top six spots in the AFC playoff picture are solidified, with the Bills, Broncos, Jaguars, Steelers, Chiefs, and Bengals occupying those spots. There will be some movement among those spots, but those six teams feel cemented. That leaves the No. 7 seed and the final wildcard spot.
At the moment, the New England Patriots take up that slot with a 5-4 record. For context, the Raiders are 4-5, so they're right there. The Cleveland Browns are also 5-4 at the No. 8 seed in the AFC. Yes, Las Vegas' upcoming three games are daunting, but the Patriots still have five games against teams above .500. Meanwhile, the Browns aren't trustworthy with Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders at quarterback. Not to mention, Las Vegas faces Cleveland in a few weeks.
The Houston Texans are a sleeper team to watch, despite being 3-5. Houston has a manageable schedule. Nevertheless, barring a substantial drop-off by one of the top six teams in the AFC, four teams are vying for one spot. That said, there's a chance the Raiders squeak in. All four of these teams battling for the No. 7 spot are vulnerable.
The next two weeks are very difficult matchups for the Raiders, with contests against the Seahawks and Broncos. So, by this time in a couple of weeks, Las Vegas' playoff aspirations could be bleak. However, considering that Seattle may have a quarterback issue on Sunday and Denver always allows opponents to hang around, the Raiders could split those two games, which would be monumental in maintaining ground in the playoff race.
After that, the Raiders face the Browns, Chargers, Broncos, Titans, Cardinals, and Chiefs. As mentioned, the Browns are always susceptible to a collapse with their quarterback situation. Meanwhile, Los Angeles, Tennessee, and Arizona are all teams the Raiders should beat. Now, Kansas City is the polarizing variable, as that game takes place in Week 18. It will be a road game, but depending on the playoff picture entering the season finale, the Chiefs could be resting their starters.
If that's the case, and the Raiders' playoff hopes are still alive, that could be a "free win" for the Silver and Black. Las Vegas' hopes are contingent on the next three weeks before the bye. Going 2-1 during that span, the Raiders are in legitimate contention for the wildcard, assuming none of the other three teams - Texans, Browns, and Patriots - create significant separation.

title: How Raiders' Mendoza Can Use Early Learning Opportunities to Advantage
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are about to begin a new era against the Seattle Seahawks this Sunday.
Rookie quarterback and 2026 No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start after the Raiders traded veteran Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a third-round pick. This beckoning has lit up Raider Nation with excitement ahead of Sunday's matchup against the defending Super Bowl champions.
As Mendoza and the Raiders prepare for a historic moment for the organization, the former college football legend from Indiana shared his growth and development, from the early days of OTAs to as early as last week's game against the San Francisco 49ers.
When Mendoza first stepped into the Intermountain Health Performance Center, it was go-time. Working with Cousins, Aidan O'Connell, and quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan, all of whom have a significant number of years playing or coaching in the NFL, has allowed Mendoza to gain more confidence as a quarterback at this level, and he feels more developed than he did in the spring, especially working from under center, chemistry with his pass-catchers, and the scheme.
"In the quarterback room, sometimes Coach Sully will reference back to Spring Fernando," Mendoza explained to reporters. "I don’t want to talk about myself in the third person, but it just shows how much improvement there’s been, and I’m a lot more confident as a quarterback, and feel like more developed."
"Whether it’s under center, connecting with teammates, understanding an NFL scheme, there’s so many areas that I’ve improved on, and I look forward to keep on improving because there’s still a lot of work to do.”
With head coach Klint Kubiak, who may be the biggest key to Mendoza's success in Las Vegas, stating that the playbook would not be limited, it doesn't come as a surprise to the first-year quarterback. In fact, the players in the room go by a motto to always stay ready and prepared.
"And that’s something that all three of the quarterbacks, when we were all here, we always, all three of us, prepared like the starter," Mendoza said. "We were all in there doing our routine, doing it together, watching film together, going over the game plan together, tweaking and seeing which adjustments we’d like to make."
For much of the season, Mendoza would be seen on the sideline with his helmet on, almost as if he were ready to hit the field with the starters. However, it's so that he's hearing the calls in real time, taking in critical mental reps by watching Cousins on the field.
Now that Cousins is off to the Vikings, Mendoza has called the reps with O'Connell and Sullivan crucial. Learning what Cousins saw on the field, talking to his coaches, including offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko on the sideline after drives, has allowed Mendoza to digest a lot of information that has allowed him to take critical steps in his mental growth as a quarterback.
"They were great. However, there’s nothing like game experience and game reps because the best vision is when you’re in the pocket rather than adjacent on the sideline, just to process information," Mendoza said. "So, it’s obviously a lot of post-film study, confirm what we saw on the sideline on film, because sometimes the angles could be a little bit different."
Mendoza is about to accomplish a dream come true, and it will be against an inconsistent Super Bowl champion, the Seahawks, in Kubiak's first time playing against his former team since leaving the organization for Las Vegas. There are a lot of emotions that come with making your first NFL start, and Mendoza felt he had great teachers in Cousins and his offensive coaches.
However, even when you have so many great minds around, a young quarterback is still developing, and mistakes will come along the way. Mendoza understands that, first and foremost.
It has been a long time since I've seen a quarterback come into the league with not just a level head but self-awareness and honesty about his progression as a quarterback publicly. In the long run, this could be incredibly helpful for his career as he goes through the ebbs and flows of being a professional passer at this level.
I can't wait to see Mendoza on the field this Sunday. There will be mistakes, but the time is now for the Raiders to see what they have in their top overall draft selection. The show is about to begin.

title: Analyzing Raiders Under the Microscope Ahead of Week 10
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' Week 10 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks is one of their most important games over the last several seasons. After finishing 3-14 last season, Las Vegas landed the No. 1 overall pick for only the second time in franchise history.
Fast forward a few months, four wins, five losses, and here we are, with the Raiders technically still in the hunt for a playoff spot halfway through the season, which makes this week's happenings even more important.
The Raiders enter Week 10 with a significant change at a significant position. They may also shuffle players around multiple position groups on both sides of the ball heading into Sunday. Several positions will be under the microscope for Las Vegas on Sunday.
Among other reasons, Klint Kubiak was hired because of his ability to lead an offense in today's NFL. With Mendoza finally taking over after having extra time to prepare, all eyes will be on how fluid Las Vegas' offense looks with Mendoza under center.
Kubiak and offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko have called solid games together this season. They will now do so with a quarterback who has the skill set to help run the offense more efficiently and productively. Sunday will be interesting, to say the least.
Las Vegas has a quarterback in Mendoza, tasked with leading the organization forward. Starting Sunday, how well he and Kubiak work together will essentially put both under the microscope.
"I'm very comfortable running our playbook with Fernando [Mendoza]. He’s been through every situation that Kirk [Cousins] has been through in training camp and during OTAs. He just hasn’t had the game reps, but we’re not going to ask him to do anything that we haven’t done in practice."
After years of subpar quarterback play, the Raiders used the No. 1 pick on Mendoza. Then, he sat behind Cousins for the first half of his rookie season. With Cousins gone, the rookie now steps forward to lead the way.
He is the No. 1 overall draft pick playing the most critical position on the field, and a position Las Vegas has been unable to solidify for many years now. No player will be under more of a microscope on Sunday than Mendoza, if for no other reason, to see what he looks like in a meaningful game.
"The coaching staff and I, and personnel staff, we’ve watched, I would say, I’ve watched a good amount of film so far in my routine, especially a routine that I’ve modeled, whether it’s Coach [Andrew] Janocko, Coach [Mike] Sullivan, Coach [Klint] Kubiak, ones that they’ve recommended, and also taking from Kirk [Cousins]’s and Aidan [O’Connell]’s past processes,” Mendoza said on Wednesday when asked about his preparation for Sunday's game.
“And so, we’ve been doing the same process every week. So, continue on keeping the same thing and keeping the main thing the main thing, which is the process. They’re a very impressive team. They’re one of the best defenses in the league, so it’s going to be a great challenge. I’m excited to do my 1/11th out there.”
Mendoza's supporting cast will be important on Sunday, on both sides of the ball. Kubiak and the coaching staff will do what they can to get Mendoza ready. However, Mendoza and the Raiders' offense will need their teammates on defense to turn things around quickly.
The unit needs only a few more stops than they haven't been getting. Las Vegas' defense must get off the field on third down. Stopping the run will naturally be the Raiders' defensive focus heading into the game. Yet they will need their defensive backfield to play significantly better.
The Raiders do not want to get into a shootout with their rookie quarterback in his first start. The Seahawks will also be without their starting quarterback, which should make life a little easier for the defense. Or it could make things more difficult, as they would have less information on the player.
Regardless, the Raiders need their defensive backs to step up this Sunday. A few extra pass breakups can change a game. If the defense can get off the field and give Mendoza a couple of extra possessions, the rookie will have even more breathing room in his first start.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Seahawks vs. Raiders Matchup: Biggest Advantage, Biggest Fear
full_text:
Wednesday's practice marked the official start of the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas. After trading veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins just before the trade deadline, the Las Vegas Raiders have had a smooth transition from Cousins to this year's No. 1 overall draft pick.
The Raiders are 4-5 and will face Klint Kubiak's old team, the Seattle Seahawks, on Sunday. After losing four of their past five games, Las Vegas aims to beat a team with a winning record for the first time this season. Yet it will be another uphill battle for Las Vegas.
In addition to the issues Las Vegas' roster still faces, they will now start a rookie quarterback. Mendoza will face one of the league's better defenses, Kubiak noted.
“Every week in the NFL is tough, and this is the best defense in the NFL. And again, he’s got to go do his job and not worry about a whole lot else. Everybody does their 1/11th , and everyone around him elevates their play,” Kubiak said.
On paper, there will not be many competitive advantages for the Raiders on Sunday. The Seahawks not having Sam Darnold is one of them, as is being at home in front of their home fans after weeks away. Those two things alone should give the Raiders a boost.
Mendoza getting his first start at home, and against his head coach's former team, is a slight competitive advantage for Las Vegas. Kubiak's familiarity with the Seahawks as a whole is undoubtedly a competitive advantage.
The Seahawks have little idea what to expect from Mendoza, as he has hardly played all season. This competitive advantage likely explains why the Raiders did not play Mendoza against the Los Angeles Rams despite being down by three touchdowns entering the fourth quarter.
There are not many, but the Raiders do have a few competitive advantages, however slight. Yet none of that matters without execution. That is the main area Las Vegas must improve upon heading into Week 10. The plays have been there to make; the Raiders have just struggled to make them.
The biggest fear for the Raiders on Sunday will center around their supporting cast. Mendoza is not only a rookie, but few players on the field this Sunday have played less this season, and as a professional, as him. It will be just as much about his teammates as his performance.
“He brings his own unique things, and yes, he’s a young man with some juice in his legs, and he’s got a lot of talent. But in this game on Sunday, it’s going to be about way more than his physical talent,” Kubiak said shortly after Mendoza’s first practice as the team’s starting quarterback.
“It’s going to be about his leadership, his knowledge of the offense, his ability to read defense, and again, I’ll say it, it’s his reliance on his teammates and everybody around him elevating their level of play. We’re not putting it all on him.”
Another significant fear for the Raiders will be Mendoza's ability to avoid the backbreaking turnover. Up until Week 9, Cousins had done that. Cousins rarely turned the ball over, and when he did, they did not lose a game because of it. Not all turnovers are created equal
Mendoza will have room for error, as no one expects him to be perfect in his first start and first extensive action in the league. However, as long as his mistakes aren't turnovers that are returned for touchdowns, red-zone turnovers, or similar, all is well.
Mendoza can make mistakes; he will, as all rookies do in their first few starts. Mendoza must be himself, since much of Sunday will depend on his performance. If his teammates can execute and play at a high level for four quarters and Mendoza plays well, anything is possible on Sunday.
Kubiak believes his coaching staff has prepared Mendoza well for the moment.
"I think it starts with, it shouldn’t be a whirlwind if he’s been preparing the right way each week. At some point he knew he was going to get an opportunity, and so he’s been preparing that way since April,” Kubiak said.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza Opens Up About His New Opportunity
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) are set to host the defending Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks (5-4), at Allegiant Stadium.
It is truly a baptism by fire for the 2026 No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Fernando Mendoza, whom NFL executives ranked as the best QB prospect in the last four years.
Great, look at @fernandomendoza and his 1st practice as "THE MAN" today pic.twitter.com/dlEIP7uiB8
The Raiders' burgeoning young superstar has blossomed since the Raiders made official what we had reported for months: that they had pegged him as their potential choice.
With the trade of Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday, the franchise has handed the reins to the reigning Heisman Trophy winner, and fans who see their fandom as a way of life couldn’t be happier.
The youngster is well known for the way he handles pressure. He didn’t flinch when his Indiana Hoosiers needed a touchdown to beat the Penn State Nittany Lions, nor in the National Championship game versus the Miami Hurricanes.
In both cases, and multiple others, he has always gone back to his deep-rooted Christian faith for his calm-under-pressure demeanor.
On Sunday, he will fulfill a lifelong dream of starting a game as an NFL franchise QB—certainly another emotional moment in a young career overflowing with them. I asked the rookie if he would handle this moment as he has the previous ones, and despite now being a multi-millionaire nearly 50 times over, he hasn’t changed one bit.
“This is a once in a lifetime opportunity, and I get my strength from Jesus Christ, and I can’t thank everybody that supported me up to this point. And a huge part of that is faith, and that’s my motto – faith, family, and football. So, to have faith and gain strength from my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, it is a fundamental part of my prior success.”
Mocked by some for his genuine demeanor and raw appreciation for life, Mendoza is the real deal in a fake world. That is hard for some to conceptualize because so many are fake and don’t even know who they are.
For his age, he is a rarity in that he isn’t looking for likes and follows on social media; he is focused on doing things the right way. So when asked about Kirk Cousins, his deep emotional bond with the new Vikings starting quarterback was heartfelt.
“Yeah, I wanted to make a statement where I really, truly, from the bottom of my heart, wanted to thank Kirk [Cousins] and the entire Cousins family, whether it was Julie, Cooper, Turner. As a family, they’ve done so much for me. They’ve essentially taken me into their household when they were here, and they welcomed me with open arms.”
The gesture of my friend, Cousins, wasn’t lost on Mendoza. “And it would have been really easy for Kirk, being a veteran quarterback and having already proved everything, to be a little bit more dismissive. But he had me with open arms and has taught me so many things.”
Like what you might ask? He explained, “Whether it’s film study, how to operate as a starting quarterback, all the different multifaceted approaches that have made him so successful throughout his career, he has shared with no restrictions or no constraints. So, I really appreciate him, and it was heartfelt to see him as he was a great mentor.”
Mendoza has always dreamed of piloting his own NFL franchise, but that is only a road sign on his map to success. So, with the emotion of another goal checked off his bucket list, he knows there are far bigger ones down the road, so he is focused on keeping the important things front and center and shutting out the things that aren't.
“I believe in the principles in the quarterback room that Coach [Andrew] Janocko, Coach [Klint] Kubiak, and Coach [Mike] Sullivan always preface is you’re always one play away, always be prepared. And Kirk [Cousins] was a great example and leader of that on how to be prepared and how to make no moment too big. And so those are all lessons that I believe Aidan [O’Connell] and I will take into this next chapter.”
The Raiders loved Mendoza coming out of the NFL Draft, just like the multiple executives that were mentioned above. But that doesn’t compare to what they think of him today.
For nearly three weeks, people inside the building have quietly said he's ready, and as he has grown every day, he has gotten himself to this point.
He reflected on his growth since touching down in the desert.
“In the quarterback room, sometimes Coach Sully [Mike Sullivan] will reference back to Spring Fernando. I don’t want to talk about myself in the third person, but it just shows how much improvement there’s been, and I’m a lot more confident as a quarterback, and I feel more developed."
"Whether it’s under center, connecting with teammates, understanding an NFL scheme, there’s so many areas that I’ve improved on, and I look forward to keep on improving because there’s still a lot of work to do.”
Kirk Cousins taught Mendoza that they weren’t competing against each other, but with each other. That allowed the two to build a close bond, and it helped Mendoza get to where he is today. He explained the concept brilliantly.
“That compete-with approach, I think, was a fundamental part of our relationship and the entire quarterback room’s relationship altogether, and the quarterback room that we have and that we had with Kirk [Cousins] was such a special moment, and it was like a nice family away from home, and so we’re all getting each other better. And honestly, it was more like Kirk and Aidan [O’Connell] giving me tips and tricks. So, I’m forever thankful.”
Klint Kubiak made it clear that Mendoza is the Raiders' starting QB, and with that comes the entire playbook. In fact, it may even expand with Mendoza’s arm and mobility, but the young man is ready for it, and the moment isn’t too big for the protégé who has had many big moments.
“I believe one of our mottos in the quarterback room is to always stay ready and always stay prepared. And that’s something that all three of the quarterbacks, when we were all here, we always, all three of us, prepared like the starter. We were all in there doing our routine, doing it together, watching film together, going over the game plan together, tweaking and seeing which adjustments we’d like to make.”
“I believe one of our mottos in the quarterback room is to always stay ready and always stay prepared. And that’s something that all three of the quarterbacks, when we were all here, we always, all three of us, prepared like the starter. We were all in there doing our routine, doing it together, watching film together, going over the game plan together, tweaking and seeing which adjustments we’d like to make.”
Mendoza wasn’t done; as the leader he is, he reminded people that as Cousins worked with him, he would be working with Aidan O’Connell. “And so, I believe Aidan [O’Connell] and I will continue that rhythm in order to prepare and do our job and execute the offense. Because at the end of the day, the quarterback is only 1/11th, and I need to do my job to best showcase all the other talents we have on the offense and on the team.”
Because of Mendoza’s ever-present faith, the moment isn’t too big because he is grounded. So when asked about the enormity of the moment and the whirlwind around him, he wasn’t buying the narrative.
“I believe starting an NFL game is a new step, but a whirlwind? No. I would agree with Coach [Klint] Kubiak. Coach Kubiak, Coach [Andrew] Janocko, and Coach [Mike] Sullivan, and everyone in the quarterback room, including Kirk [Cousins], have done a fantastic job in aiding my development, and I can’t thank them enough. And now it’s my turn to do my 1/11th. And we have such a great offensive staff, and we have such a great offense.“
He continued to praise this franchise, “Whether it was leaders in the offensive line, leaders in the receiver room, leaders in the tight end room, or leaders in the running back room that I believe that they’re going to help me along the way to…

title: Raiders Get Fantastic News on Injured Starter
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders traded veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings just before the trade deadline on Tuesday. Las Vegas' front office got a top-tier return on their investment in Cousins, as he led them to a 4-5 record with some of the best quarterback play in the league.
The Raiders' front office was able to reel in a third-round pick for a veteran quarterback that was highly unlikely to be on the team past this season. John Spytek and the Raiders' front office have already found great value in the third round of the past two NFL Drafts.
Trading Cousins was a win for all three parties. With Cousins under center, Las Vegas has already won more games in half a season than they did all of last season. They are in position to win as many games as, if not more than, they have in the past two seasons combined and walk away with a third-round pick.
The Vikings get an experienced quarterback the franchise knows well. Cousins returns to the city where he had his best years as a professional. He also goes to a team with a winning record and one that could potentially go on a deep playoff run with the right quarterback.
With Mendoza headed back to Minnesota, the Raiders will finally turn to the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft, Fernando Mendoza. Among other things, Cousins' play over the first half of the season bought the Raiders more time to see what they had under a first-year coaching staff.
The extra time gave the Raiders' brass and coaching staff an extra couple of months to develop Mendoza and work with the rookie quarterback. Instead of throwing him onto the field with a roster filled with questions, Las Vegas can move forward with certainty.
The Raiders' roster still needs significantly more. Las Vegas' remaining roster issues will likely hurt Mendoza at some point. However, with him now the team's starting quarterback, the Raiders can finally take another step toward a brighter future overall.
Mendoza's first start doesn't erase the many problems Las Vegas' roster still has. The rookie will not be enough to overcome a Raiders roster that was the league's worst last season, which is how Mendoza landed in the desert in the first place.
However, the Raiders' final eight games will show how far they've come after an offseason of wholesale changes. Mendoza is the only part of the Raiders' massive offseason haul that hasn't played significant minutes this season.
That will change this Sunday, as Mendoza will get his very first start as a professional against Klint Kubiak's former team, but at Allegiant Stadium. It is hard to miss the irony of it all, or how full-circle a moment Sunday will be for many players and coaches.
Sunday is bigger than just the game or its results, as it marks the official start of a new era in the Raiders' storied history. Yet Wednesday's practice was quietly an important day as well.
Last week, the Raiders' injury report was the lightest it has been this season. Wednesdays are usually the day that Las Vegas' roster gets the most rest in, as most of the players who are listed throughout the week generally play on Sundays. That should still be the case for the most part this week.
The Raiders will need all hands on deck against a solid Seahawks team that, on paper, already possesses most of the game's competitive advantages. On Wednesday, several players were listed on the injury report.
Thomas Booker, Foley Fatukasi, and Trey Zuhn were limited participants on Wednesday. Ian Thomas was listed on the report but was a full participant. Booker and Thomas are dealing with ankle issues. Fatukasi is dealing with a shoulder issue, and Zuhn is dealing with a concussion-related issue.
Zuhn's status will be worth keeping an eye on, as he has started the past two games for the Raiders at right guard. This is despite not being listed on the depth chart as the team's starting guard. “Trey [Zuhn III] will be the starter if he can go," Kubiak confirmed on Wednesday.
Kubiak offered further insight into the guard position, specifically veteran offensive guard Bryce Cabeldue, a former Seahawks offensive lineman the Raiders may have to turn to on Sunday, should Zuhn be unable to play.
"He is doing it, and he’s doing a fantastic job. Since the time he got here, he’s been professional. He’s showing improvement, and he’s just waiting for an opportunity," Kubiak said Wednesday.
The Raiders hope a relatively healthy roster, their home crowd, and a potential spark from Mendoza are enough to catch the Seahawks off guard. Las Vegas is 4-5 but hasn't beaten a team with a winning record this season.
Heading into Week 10, they have several things working in their favor that could be enough to unexpectedly swing momentum in their favor. Cousins played well in his time with the Raiders. However, Mendoza's skill set could be enough to help Las Vegas negate roster deficiencies.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Hondo’s Raiders Mailbag: Fans Make Expectations for Mendoza Clear
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) are staring at a steep climb into the NFL Playoffs, but with the defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks (5-4) coming into town this Sunday, things are far from dismal.
The Raiders traded QB Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings and are ready to embrace the future.
In part because of their No. 1 overall 2026 NFL Draft selection, the young man NFL executives ranked as the best QB prospect of the last four years, Fernando Mendoza. The reigning Heisman Trophy winner has been ready, according to people within the organization, for just over two weeks, allowing the team to make a trade and reassure the locker room of its intention to win.
The players see what Mendoza is doing, and they are pleased.
Every week I ask Raider Nation for their thoughts on the Silver and Black via my X account, @HondoCarpenter, and as always, you responded in masse, even with me spelling Mendoza, “Medoza.” So let’s dig in.
I expect growing pains, a few boneheaded trying-to-do-too-much plays, a handful of wow plays and a 3-5 record or better.
This is a great point. He is a rookie. The next 25 regular-season games for Fernando are about growth and maturity. I can assure you that you will see the wow plays, and conversely, you will see those mistakes as well.
Raider Nation, not all, but many, turned on Ashton Jeanty very hard, even after a good rookie season and an offensive line whose run blocking is offensive.
Just like with the other young players, the rookie head coach, and the offensive and defensive coordinators, the name of the game is to embrace the growth and the process.
Every mistake made this year and next shortens the learning curve. Great take.
This would fall close to my prediction for the year, but I want to add this.
After Sunday, the schedule gets significantly easier. While that does not negate the fact that Mendoza is a rookie, if the underperforming veterans step up, I think things could get very interesting.
To me, the success of these final games has far more to do with veterans than with Mendoza or any other Raiders rookies.
Run game is about to open up. The lack-of is difficult to root for.   If Mendoza is half the qb i think he's gonna be... we're gonna be just fine.
I have said since the Raiders selected the Nandolorian that his mobility is an underrated part of his skill set. The issue will be him learning patience if he runs no more than four times a game; that is ideal.
If he does that, the Raiders will be in great shape. Remember this: if he gets sacked, that counts as a rush on the stat sheet, but not for me. No more than four legitimate runs per game is great for the Raiders and Fernando.

title: Buckle Up: The Fernando Mendoza Era Has Begun For Raiders
full_text:
A few days ago, the Las Vegas Raiders were down in the dumps after their 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, with trade rumors around the organization persisting. As the Minnesota Vikings fell to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night with a putrid quarterback performance, the signs began to show of a potential reunion in the making.
On Tuesday, before the NFL trade deadline, the Raiders ushered in a new era by trading quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Vikings for a third-round pick. It all but handed the offense and franchise to the No. 1 overall pick in the NFL Draft, Fernando Mendoza , who will get his first opportunity to start against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday.
One of the bright spots of the Raiders' offense this season has been their passing game, which is fifth in passing yards per game (259.7). It has been an impressive unit to watch, with head coach Klint Kubiak calling plays and putting the offense in positions for success this season, and Cousins playing a big role .
However, Cousins was never going to keep his starting job, despite throwing for 2,340 yards and 20 touchdowns to begin the season. Kubiak stated a few points this year that Mendoza would get his opportunity when the time was right. Sure enough, the Vikings needed a quarterback and added someone with great familiarity, opening the door for Mendoza to become the starter.
In Tuesday's post-trade press conference, Kubiak and general manager John Spytek noted in the preparation that Mendoza had to be ready for this moment. Both thanked Cousins for his contributions, but Spytek noted the obvious.
"With that, we did want to say and confirm that Fernando [Mendoza] will be the starting quarterback going forward."
Kubiak and Spytek shared similar sentiments about Mendoza's preparation. Spytek told reporters that he "passed every test," while Kubiak noted how well his rookie signal-caller has practiced, acknowledging the work habits that have allowed him to have the opportunity to make his first career start. Those work habits have a direct link to Cousins, as Kubiak shared.
"Work habits, preparation, ways to take care of your body, ways to connect with your teammates, progressions, blitzes to expect, things to expect from coordinators," Kubiak said. "We could go on and on, but there’s a lot more to playing the position than what your coaches tell you in your meeting room, and I think Kirk [Cousins] embodied all the right things there: how to prepare and how to be a professional, and really, when things aren’t going well, what buttons to push on your teammates and what questions to ask your coaches. It’s an endless list of all positive things.”
Cousins was a big piece of the Raiders' offensive puzzle, but it was never permanent, and both Kubiak and Spytek suggested as much before the season and during Tuesday's press conference. Cousins was a great bridge quarterback for the team, providing some great moments during the season with some terrific games against quality opponents. Raider Nation can appreciate those moments.
Moving on from Cousins now is a clear signal that Las Vegas wants to get the evaluation process started for their top draft pick. Mendoza is much more physically gifted as a passer than Cousins and could do more inside and outside the pocket, which could open up the passing game more than we've seen to date.
The arm arrogance, poise, and football intelligence will be on full display this weekend against a vaunted Seahawks defense. I'm excited for what Mendoza could showcase in his first start, but like any rookie quarterback, there will be some rough patches, whether that be standing too long in the pocket, making indecisive reads, making bad throws, etc.
The move also doesn't change the approach for the rest of the season.
"And then the last point to make is, and this is for Raider Nation and for this entire building, this in no way signifies that we are punting on this season or looking forward to 2027," Spytek said. "That is not the intention of this. We have a big game this week against the defending world champs, and we intend to attack it like we would any week."
The Raiders want to compete while growing their foundation and youth in the process. Losing the veteran leadership of Cousins is a blow, but a necessary one. With that, a new era has dawned in the desert.
It is officially time for the Fernando Mendoza era to begin.
