title: Giants-Commanders Rematch: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Thursday Night
full_text:
New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said it best when he described the team’s Thursday night Week 10 matchup with the Washington Commanders as a game in which the Giants had to enter with a “2-0” mindset.
That was because just a little over a month ago, they did not live up to head coach John Harbaugh’s simple yet effective 1-0 motto in their first duel against the Commanders, where Big Blue stormed back from a 14-point deficit yet couldn’t nail the winning score in overtime to leave with a 27-27 tie on their record.
It could have very easily been a grueling loss that might have painted a different brushstroke on the current NFC East standings at the midway point of the season. Still, instead, the Giants snuck out a pseudo-win before a lot shifted in their favor over the next four weeks.
They are standing tall in the division at 5-2-1, while Washington is 2-5-1 and within one game of seeing their chances to pressure the Giants down the second-half stretch vanish.
As such, the rematch carries a double entendre for the Giants, who are seeking to unofficially put the Commanders' season to rest and notch another key divisional win that brings their postseason chase into closer view.
Standing between Harbaugh’s squad and that goal is taking care of business in these three matchups during their second chance from the football gods.
In the first matchup, it was a bit surprising that defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson didn’t use a spy player, preferably Abdul Carter, to keep quarterback Jayden Daniels from stepping upfield with the ball.
Daniels eventually found some creases in the Giants' defense as the game wore on, charging nine times for a team-high 103 yards on the ground to help Washington pile up 202 total rushing yards that marked the largest amount allowed by Wilson’s unit this season.
Along with the Commanders’ unacceptable average haul of 6.7 yards, they also punched in three rushing touchdowns, two of which were authored by Daniels, who took advantage of uncovered gaps to thrash the Giants for 38- and 26-yard foot chases into the end zone that gave Washington a two-score lead.
The reality is that Daniels’ dual-threat ability gives the Commanders a chance to stay productive despite the relentless injuries that have torn up their receiver room and sidelined their top running back, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, for four games.
With very wet conditions expected to engulf East Rutherford during the game, the battle in the trenches could be the factor that determines the final score. Washington has the advantage there, averaging 118.3 rushing yards per contest with the eighth-best 4.5 yards per carry through their first eight games this season.
The Giants’ run defense has improved over their previous two games, allowing under 100 yards to the Texans and Eagles; they held the latter to 92 yards while neutralizing Saquon Barkley’s impact after he opened the game with the Eagles’ lone touchdown.
Still, they find themselves dwelling near the basement in the important rushing metrics. They must be ready for the Commanders to threaten with Daniels' legs, especially near the end zone, where the Giants are ranked dead last in the NFL in red-zone scoring percentage (78.9%).
On the other hand, the Giants backfield has to respond strongly after they were largely disappointing in the win over Philadelphia.
Sure, the Giants, who ran the ball 31 times and only gained 80 yards (2.6 average) on the ground on Sunday, deserve a little benefit of the doubt for not having Cam Skattebo active after he suffered a hamstring injury late in overtime against the Houston Texans in Week 7.
They thought the bye week would give Skattebo enough time to let the hamstring heal before his first return to Lincoln Financial Field since he suffered a season-ending ankle injury on that same turf in Week 8 of 2025.
Instead, the Giants elected to sit Skattebo out for a few extra days of rest before facing the Commanders, and their rushing game struggled without him, posting their second-lowest output this season and a second sub-100-yard performance in four weeks.
Skattebo is expected to suit up as a full participant against Washington, but he still has work to do as he searches for his groove in what could become a run-heavy evening for the Giants offense.
That is protecting the football, something he failed to do in the final minutes of overtime, with the Giants already well-positioned in Dominic Zvada’s field goal range to give their young kicker another shot amid a rough afternoon and seal a come-from-behind victory with his leg.
Skattebo’s biggest mishap led to him playing only a handful of snaps in the Week 6 loss to the Saints before he reignited Harbaugh’s trust with an impressive 124-yard, one-touchdown outing against the Texans to lead a three-score day for the backfield.
It’s the kind of response the Giants will demand of Skattebo on Thursday night, and he must deliver in the trenches to help New York keep the ball moving if poor conditions don’t let J.J. McCarthy and the passing game create a major impact.
Washington, which has forced the second-most turnovers in the league this season, will look to execute the Peanut punch if traffic builds up in the middle of the scrum. The Giants’ running backs must be looking over their shoulder at all times.
It will be a bit surprising if Matt Nagy and the Giants offense can let the football rip through the air at a high volume, given the aforementioned weather conditions that aren’t predicted to favor it.
However, they’ve certainly learned that there might be no other team in the league better to give it a shot against than the Commanders defense, which enters Week 10 ranked 29th in pass attempts and 30th in passing yards allowed.
Granted, the last time these two franchises squared off, Jameis Winston was still the Giants’ starting quarterback and was largely contained to 72 passing yards in the first half before exploding for another 254 yards and three passing touchdowns over the next 30 minutes.
His top target that day was none other than Malik Nabers, who has found a liking for stacking his catch sheet against the Commanders’ porous secondary, including a team-high 11 receptions for 121 yards and a touchdown that became his second of what would be four consecutive 100+ yard games stretching into Week 7.
Nabers is coming off a strange week against the Eagles, where he was held to five catches on nine targets for 43 yards and dropped a perfectly placed ball by McCarthy in the back corner of the end zone that would have helped his team seal the win faster than it did.
There is no doubt he will also want to shake off any remnants of the body-language controversy that followed that game with a strong rebound performance against a defense he is quite familiar with, gaining the upper hand.
Washington will do everything they can to keep Nabers from taking over another game, including lining up cornerback Amik Robertson to help contain him. Robertson was largely successful in his coverage assignments in Week 5, allowing only four catches for 37 yards while forcing a pass deflection in 64 total snaps.
He has easily been the Commanders’ best man coverage defender in top matchups like Nabers, but he is also prone to committing penalties in the process. It will be interesting to see if Nabers can work that to his advantage to create separation from Robertson as the game wears on.
No matter what happens on the field, Nabers will bring his usual energy to every play, and the hope is that he and McCarthy can connect on a few shots that put the Giants in scoring position and pressure Washington’s defense at critical moments.

title: Giants vs. Commanders Week 10: Time, Channel and What to Watch
full_text:
The New York Giants and their fans don’t need a reminder of the last time they were hailed as the victors of the NFC East. Nor of the last year they even had a chance of competing for the title in the second half of the season.
However, with John Harbaugh bringing rapid success in his first year as head coach despite some early injury adversity that ripped away his intended starting quarterback in Jaxson Dart and other key players, that is where the Giants find themselves as the 2026 campaign hits Week 10 in the blink of an eye.
Leading the division at 5-2-1, the Giants, bolstered by their never-say-die mentality, the switch to J.J. McCarthy at quarterback, and a huge pass-rushing resurgence under defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, have put themselves in the driver’s seat by handling their business in several close games that have filled their early slate.
That includes a pair of division victories over the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles, the latter of which the Giants defeated 19-11 this past Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field for the first time in 13 years, going 1-0 in the first half of a critical two-game swing for the franchise.
On the other side are the Washington Commanders, who are set to visit New York on Thursday night at MetLife Stadium for the back half of their regular-season series.
The first meeting in Landover in Week 5 was a rare exception to the trend, as neither team could make enough plays in the critical moments of overtime, including an unfathomable mishap by the Commanders on the final play, when they let the clock run out within kicker Drew Stevens’ field goal range. The result was a grueling 27-27 tie that left the Giants a little dissatisfied.
A rematch on home soil will give Harbaugh’s Giants an opportunity to avenge a win that most players in the locker room would agree they let get away from them, especially against a Washington offense that is reeling from injuries, including a compromised Jayden Daniels, and has struggled to do the right things to finish football games.
The caveat is the weather, which is expected to bring miserable, rainy conditions to East Rutherford in the hours leading up to and during the game, similar to what the Giants faced five weeks earlier during their draw.
It will also be a short week for McCarthy and the offense, which will likely have to ditch a good portion of its playbook and rely on the run game to get the job done. Questions loom about the strength of the Giants’ backfield, including whether McCarthy’s legs will be a factor after he sustained nasty hits during the win over Philadelphia that led to a rib injury.
McCarthy fully expects to play as he steps into his first full home start with the organization. Still, the Giants must play it safe while executing as close to perfection as possible in a game where points could be at a premium and one mishap could determine the outcome.
With the calendar well into November and the hardest part of their schedule yet to be played, the Giants know they need to right their wrongs from their first battle with the Commanders and land the knockout punch that gives them another key win in the NFC East race.
A 3-0-1 divisional record mixed with a few extra victories in softer matchups would likely render any challenger to the Giants’ postseason hopes dead. That is what will linger in the players’ minds as they prepare to come out on top for the second time in five days.
Check out New York Giants on SI for pregame, in-game, and postgame coverage.
This week’s matchup marks the 190th all-time meeting between the Giants and Commanders, the third-most face-offs between the two franchises in NFL history. That long lineage includes two postseason games as well.
After their 27-27 overtime draw in Week 5, New York held a 108-75-6 advantage in the NFC East rivalry series, but the Giants had lost the four previous games dating back to the 2024 season, three of them decided by less than one score.
The Giants’ last victory over Washington came in Week 11 of the 2023 season, when they swept the Commanders for the third time in four years. Their last win at MetLife Stadium came four weeks earlier, when Big Blue defeated the Commanders 14-7 behind then-starting quarterback Tyrod Taylor.
Thursday's contest will air on Amazon Prime Video. Al Michaels will serve as the play-by-play announcer with Kirk Herbstreit working as the analyst and Kaylee Hartung as the sideline reporter.
Fans can listen to the radio broadcast on WFAN 101.9FM. Bob Papa will be the play-by-play announcer and joined by former Giants greats Carl Banks and Howard Cross as analyst and sideline reporter.
Brad Rogers is the designated lead official for Thursday's game. The Lubbock, Texas, native began his officiating career in 1991, working local high school games before moving on to the Southeastern Conference and Conference USA at the college level, then joining the NFL in 2015 for preseason games.
Two years later, Rogers was hired to be a full-time field judge. In 2019, he was promoted to head referee after John Parry's retirement and has yet to officiate any postseason games in his career.

title: Aaron Glenn Must Put His Money Where His Mouth Is After His Will McDonald IV Comments
full_text:
Despite a 2-7 record and a four-game losing streak going into Sunday's divisional game against the Bills, it was a quiet trade deadline for the Jets as they decided to keep their roster together for the second half of the season and try to salvage something from a disastrous start.
Aside from trading safety Andre Cisco to the Lions , which was not all that surprising considering the diminished role and expiring contract he had anyway, the Jets stayed put while other teams like the Jaguars and Vikings went out and made some big moves.
One player who was among those expected to be traded was defensive end Will McDonald IV, who has expressed his frustration over his reduced snap count. That said, the fourth-year DE has the second-most sacks on the team this season (three) behind rookie David Bailey (7.5) and head coach Aaron Glenn believes he has earned a bigger role.
"His pass rush is second to none and he's been in a lot of those situations where he can rush the passer," Glenn said in his Wednesday press conference (h/t SNY Jets ). "And it's just my job to make sure I put him in position to play more because he is improving and I've always said this that you earn the right to play and he's doing that."
Aaron Glenn says Will McDonald has earned a bigger role: "His pass rush is second to none" pic.twitter.com/oWcbE0KqdU
While you could argue that Gang Green's inactive trade deadline was not necessarily a bad thing and said a lot about the Jets' future plans , the inability to get the most out of their best players and put them in a position to succeed has been a recurring issue for Glenn and this coaching staff.
They ultimately decided to keep McDonald around after the frustrated DE requested a trade , but if Glenn is so confident in his pass rush and giving him a bigger role, it is time to prove it on the field by putting McDonald in situations where he can go out there and back his coach's talk up.
While the doors opened after some missed opportunities at the trade headline, McDonald certainly emerged as a clear loser. Although he still has one year remaining on his rookie deal with a fully guaranteed fifth-year option for next season, he has been relegated to more of a situational role this season and has gone from a primary pass rusher to a third-down specialist who has played less than 50% of the team's defensive snaps in 2026.
Since the Jets have shifted to a 3-4 base front that has put more of the attention on Bailey and Kingsley Enagbare, McDonald has not exactly been put in the best positions to effectively rush the passer to be able to utilize his athleticism and make the most of the opportunities he has had through nine weeks.
As someone who can deploy a signature spin move and create a burst off the line of scrimmage, lining McDonald up wider could allow him to use his speed instead of taking on double-teams and being limited in his pass rush.
With the attention that Bailey is rightfully creating due to his elite play so far, pairing McDonald alongside him more frequently in nickel and dime fronts would take some of the focus away from him and free him up to create some pressure.
If Glenn can do that and move him around to make use of his agility against the slower linemen, in addition to keeping McDonald fresh for early downs and passing situations, he could maximize his pass rush skills instead of being put in a precarious position against power run schemes, an area he has struggled in.
Considering the Jets have three first-round draft picks and will most likely use a high-value pick on the edge, McDonald is still at the top of the list of current Jets who could be leaving in the offseason .
It simply would not make much sense for Gang Green to hold onto the former first-rounder if the snap count does not see much of an uptick, but Glenn's comments say otherwise, assuming he actually backs the talk up or is just using coach speak.
Despite playing on a defensive front that has battled its share of injuries this season, McDonald has been nowhere near the 66% of defensive snaps that he played across his last two seasons with the Jets. With an explosive Bills passing attack led by quarterback Josh Allen up next, it is paramount that McDonald resembles a similar snap count to the last two seasons—roughly 60-65%—while taking on a reduced role on special teams to preserve his stamina.
Glenn has doubled down on the process despite possessing a 5-21 record with the Jets. He and McDonald may both be on their way out of Gotham by season's end, but if he truly wants to back up his comments and put his money where his mouth is, he may be wise to let McDonald show what he can do over the final eight games as the season continues to get away from the Jets anyway.

title: Confidence Meter: How Close Are Jets to Firing Aaron Glenn After the Trade Deadline?
full_text:
Disappointing, frustrating, and embarrassing.
Those are just a few words to describe the Jets’ 2026 season. With New York on the verge of missing the playoffs for the 16th consecutive season, head coach Aaron Glenn’s job security has been the main topic of discussion.
While it’s unlikely Glenn remains with the team beyond its regular season finale on Jan. 10, would Gang Green be willing to pull the plug on him before then?
Even though there’s little belief that Glenn will be able to turn things around, there’s practically no chance he'll be fired mid-season
After an historically bad 2025 season, Glenn entered Year 2 with one goal: improving. However, the Jets haven’t made much progress, as many of last year's issues persist.
New York has the same record through nine games this year as it did last year. The team continues to struggle with poor execution, questionable coaching decisions, and an inability to make proper in-game adjustments.
One embarrassing stat line that keeps popping up is their performance in the final two minutes of the first half, where they’ve been outscored 107-9 in Glenn’s tenure.
While Geno Smith has been night-and-day better than Justin Fields, the offense hasn’t significantly improved, averaging 20.2 points per game compared to 17.6 last year. Additionally, they continue to struggle in the red zone, ranking 31st in red-zone scoring rate (40.7%). Whether it’s play-calling or poor execution, the offense has consistently found ways to hold itself back.
Defensively, the Jets haven’t been any better. Despite calling play-calling his “superpower”, the unit hasn’t improved under Glenn's watch. While New York ranks fourth in passing yards allowed per game (197.8), it’s surrendered 16 passing touchdowns this season and has only one interception during Glenn’s tenure.
However, their run defense has been the most glaring weakness. Despite overhauling the defensive line during the offseason, the Jets still struggle to stop opposing rushing attacks, ranking 26th in rushing yards allowed per game (128).
These are the type of growing pains you expect from a first-year head coach, not someone in their second season. Ultimately, Gang Green hasn’t done what Glenn set out to do.
Even though the team has shown minimal improvement under Glenn, we shouldn’t expect New York to fire him mid-season.
Since Woody Johnson took over as owner in 2000, he’s fired seven coaches. The only coach he fired during the season was Robert Saleh, who was hired by his brother, Christopher Johnson, while he served as the U.S. Ambassador to the United Kingdom.
With Glenn being Johnson’s pick for head coach, isn't likely to fire him before the season ends. This was evident during the trade deadline, as the Jets didn’t trade any key players despite Will McDonald IV requesting a trade and Breece Hall being involved in trade rumors.
By standing pat, it shows Glenn has the support and backing that he can turn things around in the final eight games.
Glenn may have backing from ownership to finish out the season, but there’s only one way he can convince them he deserves another year, and that’s by winning games.
Since Glenn took over in 2025, New York has posted a 5-21 record, including 0-8 against the AFC East, and is trending towards missing the playoffs for the 16th consecutive season.
You could make a strong argument that the Jets should be 4-5 or 5-4 this season, but they’ve been unable to win tight contests. According to Next Gen Stats , New York is 1-5 in close games.
Some of those games they should’ve won were against the Packers in Week 2, where they had a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter; Week 7 against the Dolphins, where they failed to execute in the red zone; and Week 8 against the Raiders, where they scored on their first six possessions only to surrender 24 second-half points.
New York doesn’t need to miraculously win its remaining games for Glenn to stay a third year. However, the Jets have to beat the bad teams and pick up some division wins to give him a realistic chance of keeping his job.
Looking at their remaining games, there’s no excuse not to beat the Chargers, Dolphins, and Cardinals. Add in a win against the Bills and Patriots, and it would go a long way toward persuading Johnson to give Glenn another season.
Otherwise, we should expect Johnson and company to begin another head coaching search in 2027.

title: The Biggest Jets Mistake Darren Mougey Made at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
General managers make mistakes all the time in the NFL - even the most elite in the league.
What separates a good GM from a great GM, though, is his ability to correct his mistakes and put the team in a position to succeed either now or in the future.
The jury is still out on what kind of general manager Darren Mougey is for the New York Jets. He's made some excellent moves and some head-scratchers. For the most part, he's done his job. The Jets are a better football team because of the talent he has acquired.
But Mougey made one mistake during the NFL trade deadline. One that won't have any long-term implications or isn't even entirely his fault.
As Jets fans begin to turn on their current GM for a lack of moves on Tuesday, it's the one move he isn't going to be able to shake that people are overlooking...yet.
If you ask most Jets fans, Mougey's biggest mistake came when the team failed to move Will McDonald after a trade request. Even McDonald was clear in his demands.
"I just want to clear everything up," McDonald said. "There's no hard feelings with the coaches and staff or anybody here. I just want to play, and I just want to help the team win."
In reality, though, not moving McDonald is not Mougey's mistake.
It's not doing enough to gain full control of the Jets' roster management...yet.
Let's be clear: Mougey and head coach Aaron Glenn have been in lockstep from the very beginning. Both have talked about there being a sort of 50-50 split on personnel matters, and the lack of a McDonald trade is as much a Jets organizational decision as it is a Glenn or owner call.
However, while Glenn has certainly helped the Jets in scouting and roster management, his in-gamecoaching is the team's biggest problem right now. And it shows in his 5-21 record.
Mougey is shielded from that record, especially since the one thing he is tasked with ( building the roster ), he's done a pretty good job. The one thing Glenn is tasked with ( winning ) has not been accomplished.
The reality is that I have a hard time believing the Jets will clear house this offseason if they fail to reach their win goals under Glenn. If they were to fire the coaching staff, the belief is that Mougey would get a chance to not only pick his head coach but also a rookie quarterback.
That's where the lone mistake comes in. Mougey is clearly sharing responsibility with the team right now, with Glenn. He doesn't have full control along the lines of other general managers around the league, like Howie Roseman or Les Snead. That's ok for where the Jets are now. They won't give him full control as long as they want their head coach to succeed.
That said, until Mougey has full control, it will be the one thing missing from his resume. Once he does, the ownership of record and everything else will be under him.
Until that time, the fact that he doesn't have a full 100% say is his biggest mistake. Is it arbitrary? Maybe. But that's to be expected with the Jets having a 2-7 record.

title: Aaron Glenn Doubles Down on Process Despite 5-21 Record
full_text:
There's doubling down on a process that you believe works, even when others doubt you. Then there's doubling down on a process that hasn't worked, and results have shown it.
Can you guess which one New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn has focused on?
New York's head coach is 5-21 since taking over the top job with the team he was a Pro Bowler for during his playing days. Throughout his tenure, Glenn has focused his efforts on celebrating the improvements his team has made over time. In many ways, the coach has focused on building from the ground up.
But as Glenn's mentor Bill Parcells once said, "You are what your record says you are." And Glenn's doubling down on his process, with his record, is only complicating the problem.
There's a reason why the Jets were so high on hiring Aaron Glenn in the first place. His energy, passion, and determination were all easy to buy into. And it is still a major positive trait. Fans can't help but want to see him succeed because he desperately wants to win for the franchise.
But results are what they are. Glenn's passion for a 2-7 club and determination to win his way are the key reasons, especially when he tries to refocus people's anger on the process at hand.
The problem with Glenn's answer isn't the facts. He's right that the Jets have improved and have been in almost every game. Save for two blowouts , there's an argument the Jets should be three to four more wins better than they are.
But therein lies the problem. New York should be better. Glenn's coaching staff and his own in-game decisions are key reasons for the team's struggles. Whether it is the misuse of timeouts, an archaic offensive system, or a total lack of adjustments, the Jets are being outcoached in almost every game.
So when Glenn says he's close, the fanbase only has to point to results and lack of improvement from him to question that very thought.
"We're right on the cusp of trying to break through, and we're going to do everything we can to do that," Glenn said.
Maybe the Jets can turn their misfortune around. Perhaps a late run will be enough to save Glenn's job. But that flip needs to be made now, not in a couple of weeks.
His double down on what hasn't worked isn't helping things either.

title: Breaking Down Jets’ Injury Report Coming Into Week 10 (Who’s Hurt & Who Could Return vs. Bills)
full_text:
The Jets extended their losing streak to four with Sunday’s 35-12 loss to the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium.
While there were few positives to take away from the team’s disappointing performance, one was that New York left Arrowhead Stadium without suffering any significant injuries. Gang Green has constantly had to deal with key players missing time, which has played a small part in the team’s disappointing season.
With that said, let’s take a look at the Jets’ injuries heading into Week 10’s matchup with the Bills.
One reason the Jets struggled against Kansas City was that they were without star receiver Garrett Wilson. The five-year veteran was placed in the concussion protocol after taking a hit to the head on the second-to-last play of New York’s Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
Without Wilson, the Jets’ offense had little success through the air, as the other receivers couldn’t consistently create separation. Although Omar Cooper Jr. recorded a season-high eight receptions on nine targets, the majority of them came on screen passes.
ESPN’s Rich Cimini reported earlier Wednesday that Wilson returned to practice , although he was limited. While this doesn’t guarantee Wilson will play on Sunday against the Bills, it’s a positive update on his recovery.
It’s been a really disappointing year for Joseph Ossai, and injuries have played a large role. A ruptured plantar fascia forced him to miss the first two games. Then an ankle sprain in Week 5’s win against the Browns sidelined him for the last four weeks.
Although Ossai missed last week’s game against Kansas City, he practiced with the team in a limited role leading up to the game, which suggests he’s close to returning. If he can be a full participant in either Thursday's or Friday’s practice, we should expect him to suit up against Buffalo.
But Ossai will have to step up, as he’s been extremely underwhelming in limited action. In just three games (107 defensive snaps), Ossai has recorded nine total tackles and zero pressures, earning a career-low 50.9 pass-rush grade and 54.3 run-defense grade , per Pro Football Focus .
New York must hope that Ossai can turn things around if he returns this week, as the Bills’ offensive line has allowed just 17 sacks.
With Andre Cisco traded to the Lions on Monday, it’s opened an opportunity for VJ Payne to fill his role as the Jets’ backup safety behind Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick.
The 2026 sixth-round selection, who had been on injured reserve with a significant bone bruise since Aug. 30, opened his 21-day practice window last Wednesday and was a full participant in the team’s three practices.
The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt reported that Payne was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice, suggesting he is trending toward making his NFL debut against Buffalo. However, New York must officially activate him to the 53-man roster before he’s eligible to play in Sunday’s matchup.
Harrison Phillips won’t practice today. Omar Cooper, Joe Ossai, Garrett Wilson and Nahshon Wright are all limited. VJ Payne will be a full participant.
If he does play, we should expect to see him primarily on special teams, considering the Jets have leaned on Belton and Fitzpatrick at safety. Payne could potentially earn a rotational role as the season progresses if New York keeps losing.
Missing last Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices with an ankle injury, Harrison Phillips was trending towards being ruled out for last week’s matchup against the Chiefs. However, he was a full participant in Friday’s practice and ultimately suited up in Week 9, recording one total tackle in a season-low 27 snaps.
According to Jets website reporter Eric Allen, Phillips did not participate in Wednesday’s walk-through . While this doesn’t rule him out for Sunday’s game, it suggests he’s still dealing with the injury. If he logs another full participation on Friday, there’s a good chance he plays.
The only other player to miss Wednesday’s walk-through was Trevin Wallace, who’s dealing with a groin injury. Wallace was a limited participant in last Wednesday’s practice, but didn’t participate in the following two practices and was ultimately ruled out for the team’s matchup against Kansas City.
The 23-year-old has been a critical member of New York’s special teams, logging three total tackles and earning a 63.9 special teams grade. With no clear timeline for his return, we should expect the team to be cautious and ease his workload in practice before clearing him to suit up.
David Onyemata was placed on injured reserve after suffering a groin injury in Week 2’s loss to the Packers. The 11-year veteran underwent core muscle surgery and wasn’t initially expected to return until December, but Rosenblatt reported last Friday that Onyemata was at practice working with trainers.
While this is an encouraging step in his recovery, it doesn’t mean he’s close to playing. He’ll have to clear some hurdles before New York inserts him back into the lineup. Fourth-round selection Darrell Jackson Jr. has done well in his absence and has flashed potential to become a key rotational player.
The Jets have a long list of players on the injured reserve.
Kingsley Jonathan, Kiko Mauigoa (quad), Marcelino McCrary-Ball (ankle), Max Mitchell (head/concussion) and T’Vondre Sweat (knee) are all candidates to return this season.
However, we won’t get to see Braiden McGregor (torn pectoral), Arian Smith (torn ACL), and Chip Trayanum (neck) for the rest of the year.

title: Kenyon Sadiq Needs to Be Jets' X-Factor to Help Upset the Bills in Week 10
full_text:
Following a quiet trade deadline that only saw the Jets trade safety Andre Cisco to the Lions and keep the rest of their roster intact, it is time for Gang Green to turn its attention to the second half of the season and make some improvements on the field after a 2-7 start.
Despite the lack of movement ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, it was not entirely bad, as the doors opened for some on the roster amid the missed opportunities . Still, that does not account for the poor coaching that has been the prevailing theme each week and the lack of execution on the field over the course of a full game.
As the Jets take a four-game losing streak into Sunday's home tilt against the 7-1 Bills at MetLife Stadium, head coach Aaron Glenn's 0-8 record against divisional opponents will once again be a talking point. That said, any chance the Jets have of competing in this game and having a shot to pull off the upset could reside on the shoulders of rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq.
While Sadiq has struggled to receive a consistent amount of targets each week since his breakout Week 3 performance when he went off for seven catches, 105 yards and a TD against the Lions, he is coming off his best game since then in the Week 9 loss to the Chiefs when he came down with four receptions for 49 yards.
That is nowhere near the level of performance expected of the talented and athletic TE, but it is important for him to keep his foot on the gas to help the Jets beat the Bills and pull off the stunner.
Granted, the Jets were without WR1 Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Adonai Mitchell had zero catches on seven targets against the Chiefs, so the pass game was essentially nonexistent in the Week 9 loss. That said, Sadiq stepped up when nobody else did, aside from rookie Omar Cooper Jr. (eight catches, 58 yards), and showed that he has still not lost a step amid a crowded receiving room.
There is no denying the freakish athleticism that the No. 16 pick out of Oregon brings to this team and the fact that he was the first offensive player the Jets drafted back in April. If anything, his inconsistent lack of usage has more to do with the coaching staff's lack of creativity in distributing the ball to him and getting each of their playmakers involved each week.
Despite that, Sadiq still has 21 catches (on 31 targets) for 235 yards and one receiving TD, plus a three-yard TD run in the season opener that showcased his versatility in both the pass game and as a physical runner. Simply put, he has shown some bright spots as part of a talented 2026 draft class and his numbers should be even greater if more opportunities were coming his way.
Kenyon Sadiq makin it look easy 📺: #NYJvsKC on @NFLonCBS | @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/VzYXDSx5VU
At the same time, Sadiq has to cut back on his penalties. He was called for a false start in Chiefs' territory on the opening drive of last Sunday's game and was flagged for a facemask penalty on a second-and-five with 53 seconds left in the first half, which negated a seven-yard run from Breece Hall and ultimately led to a missed 53-yard field goal by kicker Jason Sanders.
There are still some growing pains and areas that need to be corrected for the immensely talented TE , but he appeared to get back on track against the Chiefs and showed why he could be key to the team's success going forward when he is more involved and the mistakes are limited.
While a lot of the attention on the Bills has been on their league-leading scoring offense (32 ppg) and the MVP-caliber play from QB Josh Allen, the Buffalo defense ranks in the bottom half of the league in points allowed and gives up the fourth-most passing yards per game (238.8 ypg).
Furthermore, the Bills are allowing the sixth-most yards to TEs and 11.2 yards per catch to the position this season, so this could be an opportunity to capitalize on for a player who is plenty capable of taking advantage. Although Pro Football Focus only gives him the 27th-ranked overall grade (64.3) out of 37 qualified TEs, he has been efficient in picking up yards after the catch and could make the Bills' secondary pay on Sunday.
In Buffalo's last road game, the Bills' secondary allowed a combined 11 catches for 165 receiving yards to Raiders TEs Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer. Perhaps Sadiq and Mason Taylor could have similar success.
While the recently acquired Amani Hooker, who is tied for the league lead in interceptions (five), could give the Bills a boost, Sadiq could be the true difference-maker for the Jets this week. A lot will depend on Wilson's status and how the Jets continue to use Taylor, but if the targets do come his way, Sadiq will need to attack the Bills downfield and wear them down with his sheer athleticism.

title: 3 Jets Likely Leaving in the 2027 Offseason Despite Surviving Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Jets were quiet during the trade deadline compared to years past. The Jets were involved in only one deal despite their 2-7 record. Making only one move has left them with many roster questions that may be answered come the offseason.
Gang Green will look much different going into 2027. They already have 22 players on expiring contracts and a player requesting a trade. As the organization plans for next season, here are three Jets who likely will not be a part of those plans, regardless of their current place on the roster.
The Nahshon Wright experiment has been a failure . The Jets signed the 28-year-old to a one-year, $3.5 million contract after the corner led his position in interceptions in 2025. That success has not followed Wright to Florham Park.
The veteran corner has yet to take a snap for New York . Someone who was supposed to be a game-changer in the secondary has not stepped onto the field for the team. Wright is clearly not in the Jets' plans currently or in the future. While it's surprising not to see him moved at the deadline, the former Bear will likely be a one-season unused rental for New York.
Wright is clearly not a part of head coach Aaron Glenn's plan, and it is hard to believe he would re-sign with a team that didn't let him see the field all season. Wright is coming off the best season of his career; he isn't looking to fade into anonymity in New York.
Even though he wasn't traded, the Jets can expect Wright to be one of the first out the door come the offseason.
Geno Smith was a surprise deadline opportunity when teams started looking for a quarterback. It was always unlikely to see him traded, but the fact that it gained traction shows what trajectory the veteran is on. As the season progresses, it seems increasingly possible that Smith won't be a Jet come 2027.
Smith has been sufficient at QB, but he isn't the long-term answer New York needs. The signal caller is 36, and it's not like the Jets are winning games because of him. The Jets have been looking for a franchise player at the position since before he was on the team the first time, and the second time around, he is still unfortunately not that guy.
New York already has a rookie sitting behind Smith, Cade Klubnik, whom they drafted in the fourth round. As the Jets continue to lose, calls will get louder for Klubnik to get his shot . That doesn't bode well for Smith. Either Klubnik is good, and the Jets roll with the rookie, or he isn't, and the team looks to draft a first-round QB in the upcoming draft.
Either way, it looks like the Jets will be going in a different direction come 2027.
Will McDonald IV's contract isn't out after this year, but the defensive end requested a trade that wasn't granted . He's disgruntled with his role on the Jets, but the team declined to fulfill his request. However, the road to a happy McDonald come 2027 seems more treacherous than the one to a trade.
New York has three first-round picks, which all currently sit in the top 13. It is hard to believe that one of those won't be used on an edge rusher. McDonald is upset about playing time and usage; it seems those issues will only grow as New York continues to rebuild.
McDonald could be on his way out if the Jets are to use a high-value pick on the edge. Holding the former first-rounder hostage for two more years as a second-choice edge rusher just wouldn't be smart. It may not have happened at the deadline, but it would be surprising to see McDonald in Gotham green come 2027.
Barring a change of heart, McDonald looks to be on his way out of New York.

title: What the Jets' Inactive Trade Deadline Says About Their Plans for 2027
full_text:
The Jets stood pat during the trade deadline on Tuesday . It shouldn't come as a surprise, considering head coach Aaron Glenn announced as much following their loss to the Chiefs.
Aaron Glenn on tomorrow's trade deadline: "Never say never, but right now I know we're going to stand pat. Listen, we're in the business of keeping good players. That's how I see it...But you never know what's going to happen." #Jets
But as countless trades poured in over the wire, New York's inactivity, particularly pertaining to several players on expiring deals, left some confused. They didn't trade edge rusher Will McDonald despite a reported trade request; they didn't move Nahshon Wright or Jarvis Brownlee, and watched as other struggling teams moved off key players.
Gang Green's actions were clear. They wanted to keep as much of the talent on the roster to give Glenn the best chance to keep his job.
But is it really that simple? Does failing to trade McDonald actually hurt the Jets' chances beyond 2026?
Many Jets fans were frustrated with the team's lack of moves on Tuesday. But their frustration ignores the reality that the team had been living with over the last several months. Owner Woody Johnson wants Glenn to succeed. Because of that, he wants to give him as much talent as possible.
That means keeping players who are helpful role pieces or borderline starters.
Despite a 2-7 start, the Jets are more comfortable keeping their already heavy treasure trove of draft picks—including three first-rounders in the 2027 draft. In their eyes, Glenn still has eight games remaining to show he's capable of being kept on for a third year.
But the record and on field problems tell a different story.
Few coaches in NFL history have had as bad a start to their careers as Glenn has with New York. He's 5-21 in his first 26 games, has yet to win a division contest, and has few answers for how to fix the problems New York has. Before he was first hired, Glenn was known as someone who could build a great staff full of competent coaches around him, but after dismantling his first failed staff, his second has shown little improvement. If the team continues to lose this season, there can be no argument that Glenn has failed to earn a third season with the team.
The caveat here is that while the Jets are trying to win with Glenn, their inability to do so has shown it doesn't matter how much talent they have. But their push also means a few more things we'll get to.
Many Jets fans have drawn their ire not just at Glenn but also at general manager Darren Mougey for the team's lack of a sell-off as the Colts and Eagles have previously done.
In their minds, Mougey not making a deal is a sign that he and Glenn are a package deal. If Glenn ends up being fired, Mougey's mistakes shouldn't absolve him either.
But that couldn't be further from the truth.
There are several reasons the Jets failed to make any trades at the deadline. Ownership could have voiced their opinions to push one final time behind Glenn, and players may have requested that they still try to openly compete. A general manager has to weigh all of that together when making decisions.
In the case of Will McDonald, for example, New York Post 's Brian Costello reported  that the Jets had offers for as high as a second-round pick . McDonald has a trade request out and played under 50% of the snaps last week in Kansas City. So why didn't Mougey make a move?
What if he did and the Jets' front office opted not to move him? What if Mougey believes in McDonald's abilities as a pass rusher and is willing to keep him on the roster for the team's next head coach? If McDonald is a scheme liability under Glenn, could the Jets hire a coordinator with a 4-3 background who incorporates the wide-nine approach? All of a sudden, McDonald could be seen as an important piece again.
The idea that Mougey failed at the deadline is a farce. New York is set up for success now just as much as they were last week. Trades for later picks would have done nothing to change that.
If anything, the lack of moves shows the Jets still value Glenn's input on the roster, and it is as much a 50-50 split with Mougey as once originally thought. Should the team continue to bottom out, Mougey will have plenty more to point to as a way to show he should be given more responsibility over the roster and the head coach.
Here's what many people forget:
The Jets are a bad football team. They will remain a bad football team even after the trade deadline . While it would've been nice to ship off players on expiring deals, the team still has plenty of cap space and three first-round picks—more than enough ammo to entice a strong coach and come away with impact players to alter the team's fortune.
New York's desired defense of Glenn should also matter little to the fanbase at this point. The coach has proven himself incapable of putting a team in a position to win football games; the best way forward for the team to actually lose for the remainder of the season is to keep everything the way it is, however harsh or realistic that may be.
By the end of the year, it's expected that the Jets will move on from Glenn and his coaching staff. Mougey will have an opportunity to bring in a coach who fits his vision for the roster. The trade deadline will mean very little when it comes to these outcomes.
Especially with the Colts (the team the Jets own the first-round pick of) already selling off key starters across both sides of the ball.

title: Jets Winners & Losers After the Trade Deadline: Doors Open Amid Missed Opportunities
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has officially passed , and while the Jaguars and Vikings made some big moves and the Colts continued to clean house, the Jets remained quiet and kept their roster mostly intact despite a frustrating 2-7 start to the season.
Even though players like Harrison Phillips, Will McDonald IV and Jarvis Brownlee Jr. were on the list of those who could be traded, safety Andre Cisco was the only Jet let go, as he was acquired by the Lions . While that did not come as much of a surprise given his diminished role and expiring contract, it was a little shocking to see the rest of the roster go unchanged amid a four-game losing streak.
Coming off their latest blunder against the Chiefs in a 35-12 loss , it is now or never for the Jets to show what they've got at the season's midway point. With that in mind, here are the biggest winners and losers following the trade deadline.
Although Moore has primarily played on special teams this season and has been productive in that role with eight tackles, he has only played nine defensive snaps in eight games and has clearly taken on a reduced role due to the additions of Minkah Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton.
Combine that with Cisco also being on the roster until he was traded, and Moore essentially became an afterthought in the secondary despite recording the second-most tackles on the team during his rookie season (101). While Cisco's departure could also open the door for rookie VJ Payne to get some opportunities after starting the season on injured reserve due to a bone bruise in his knee, Moore is in line to be the direct backup behind Belton and Fitzpatrick.
Fitzpatrick may have picked up the team's lone interception earlier this season, but the secondary has been a weak spot for the Jets with numerous blown coverages and undisciplined play. As Moore moves up the depth chart, he should see an uptick in sub-package defensive snaps and have some additional opportunities to try and build on the bright spots he showed last season.
Even though McDonald still has another year remaining on his contract and appeared to be someone who was going to be packing his bags before the deadline , that ultimately did not come to fruition as he remains in Gotham. For someone with 24.5 sacks in just three-and-a-half seasons, it is understandable that New York would want to hold onto him.
That said, the 2023 first-rounder out of Iowa State has played less than 50% of the snaps for the defense this season and has been relegated to more of a situational role. While McDonald expressed his frustration about wanting to take his talents somewhere else, head coach Aaron Glenn addressed the deadline uncertainty with a vote of confidence toward his DE.
" I just know we're in the business of keeping good players, so Will's going to be here ," Glenn said, per Jets on SI's Nick Faria.
Still, McDonald has gone from a primary pass rusher to a third-down specialist with fewer opportunities. While some of that is on a coaching staff that continues to mismanage its roster, a lot also has to do with the emergence of rookie David Bailey and the fact that he is receiving more snaps as a result
The Jets may have kept their pieces in place despite not making any significant trade deadline moves, but that is not necessarily a bad thing for their long-term future. They already have three first-round picks (their own, the Colts' and the higher of the Cowboys' two picks), and they only benefited that much more as the 2-7 Colts have gone through a fire sale by trading away most of their top players and likely getting an even higher pick by season's end.
Even teams like the Eagles and Jaguars could be playing a role for the Jets as it relates to the draft. Given the needs the Eagles currently have and the likelihood that they stick with Jalen Hurts at QB, combined with the fact that Atlanta only has one first-round pick, the Jets could still be sneaky winners with the power they currently have in their draft capital.
Wright was signed to a one-year, $3.5 million deal in the offseason following a breakout 2025 campaign that featured a career-high five interceptions and his first Pro Bowl nod. However, he was expected to see his way out the door from Gotham after being a healthy scratch in more games than he's played this season.
Instead, the Jets decided to keep him around, perhaps with the hope that his playmaking abilities and tendency to create takeaways in his career could prove beneficial for a defense that has struggled in that area. Therefore, it seemed like a no-brainer move for the Jets to get him into the lineup for Week 9 against the Chiefs, even if that ended up being far from the case.
That said, Wright remains mired on the depth chart, looking for playing opportunities. An interested party would have only needed $833,333 in cap space to make a deal work, per Spotrac , but the Jets did not budge and chose to keep him on the roster, even if his opportunities remain few and far between.
While execution on both sides of the ball continues to plague Glenn this season , particularly his lack of aggressiveness and inability to adjust to what is happening on the field, he was certainly one of the biggest winners to emerge from the trade deadline due to the quiet approach the Jets took.
He may only be 5-21 during his brief tenure in Gang Green and 0-8 within the AFC East, a clear sign of a coach who is just getting by at this point until the Jets eventually let him go. The decision to retain QB Geno Smith and RB1 Breece Hall, specifically, gives him the best possible roster to try and finish out the season with some positives.
The talent, as we have seen, does not mean anything if the coaching does not utilize it correctly and execute in key situations. The writing may already be on the wall for Glenn, regardless of what happens for the rest of the season, but at least he gets the benefit of having a talented roster that is essentially the same as when the season began.

title: Jets Report Card: Regrading 2026 Draft Class Halfway Through First Season
full_text:
We're past the midway point of the 2026 NFL season, and the Jets should have a pretty good indication of where their rookie class is at this time.
Spoiler alert: they've been very encouraging .
From late-round production to the team's top talent early, the Jets have gotten everything they should want to see from their deep rookie class. So let's take out the report cards and see who has stood out the most.
The debate between if the Jets should've taken David Bailey or Arvell Reese will go on for many years beyond their rookie season.
Through nine games, though, it's clear the Jets made the right choice for them. Bailey has had a transcendent start to his first season with the team, recording 7.5 sacks and forcing five fumbles. His run defense isn't the greatest, but it's light-years better than what people originally thought it would be like coming out of college.
Bailey remains a blue-chip talent for the team going forward. As he develops, he could be the next great pass rusher this league is waiting to see. It's been a joy to watch him make big plays whenever he steps on the field.
It's been a frustrating year to judge Sadiq. Not because of what he's put on the field, but because of the lack of creativity in getting him the football from the Jets' coaching staff. They seemingly aren't entirely sure how to coordinate their offense with so much talent to choose from.
Because of that, Sadiq's numbers are a bit overlooked. The 16th overall pick has recorded 21 receptions for 235 yards and a touchdown. It should be more, though, if the team understood how to use his freakish athleticism.
Much like many players on this list, Omar Cooper Jr. has had a case of the injury bug early in the year. That said, his production while on the field has been superb. He was the first Jets receiver with back-to-back 100-yard receiving games since 1985, and he is already showing his skill set to be a big-play playmaker.
On the season, Cooper has recorded 20 receptions for 306 yards and two touchdowns. The more he plays, the better he will be. Cooper is a major part of the Jets' future.
Ponds is a difficult player to judge through his early snaps. The second-round corner out of Indiana missed all of training camp and the start of the season with an injury. Since his return to the field, the Jets have worked Ponds primarily out of the slot, a position he does not have a ton of experience in.
That said, the work we've seen so far from Ponds this season has been solid. He hasn't done enough to generate any coverage grades from Pro Football Focus, but has some solid reps in coverage. He's been penalized twice this year.
As of now, there is more tape on Ponds than some of the other late-round selections, so he'll get an average grade with room to grow moving forward.
New York's struggles with drafting quality day three talent have been well documented. For the first time in years, it seems like they may actually be correcting that mistake.
Jackson has not been dominant or the second coming of a Hall-of-Fame defensive tackle. However, he has been a quality piece to the defensive line rotation and one of the lone bright spots for the entire front seven this season. Jackson led the team in run stops last week in Kansas City and has an above-average grade (58.7) from Pro Football Focus , one of the highest of all current players in the Jets tackle room.
New York should be excited to see his development continue.
Perhaps we eventually see Klubnik out on the field once the season is nearly over (a final two games type of deal), but we aren't there yet. Instead, the Clemson product will have to take solace in sitting behind Geno Smith for the remainder of his first season. There's a lot to like out of Klubnik from his work in the preseason, but still. He gets an incomplete grade until we can actually see him get meaningful snaps.
New York's offensive line is a strength this season, but Cooper hasn't been healthy enough to play. He's been on short-term IR for most of the year. Cooper is a project offensive lineman with the potential to be an impact player in a few years.
Like many late-round rookies, it's unfair to even put a grade on Payne, considering he hasn't been healthy or played at all so far this season. Perhaps he will get some time now that Andre Cisco is no longer with the team , but that remains to be seen.
This has been one of the better draft classes the Jets have enjoyed in recent years. Almost every rookie who has seen playing time has gotten a chance to excel in some way. With stronger coaching and more development, the path is there for the 2026 class to be more impactful in a positive way than the 2022 one was.
There are, of course, questions. What would a new coaching staff do with some of these players? Is there hope they can get the most out of this talent?
But from a sheer report card basis, the Jets' future is very bright with this class.

title: Eagles Week 10: 3 Most Important Games to Watch During Philadelphia's Bye This Weekend
full_text:
Philadelphia's bye week has arrived at an opportune moment . The Eagles will benefit from an extra week of rest and preparation in the midst of a dreadful seven-game losing streak . While the Birds may not be taking the field in Week 10, that doesn't mean they won't be impacted by the final scores.
This weekend's 14-game slate is highlighted by an overseas matchup of playoff contenders and an intense divisional showdown at Lambeau Field. For the Eagles, the contests involving losing squads have much more meaning, though. Here's a look at three Week 10 games to watch during Philly's bye.
Sunday's battle at Nissan Stadium will mark defensive tackle Jordan Davis' first game since he was dealt by the Eagles at the deadline . Philly sent him to Jacksonville in exchange for two high draft picks. The Jaguars are hoping the massive run-stopper can take their elite defense to the next level.
Playmaker incoming 😮‍💨 📺: NFL + | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/pEiVyFUSCE
It'll be intriguing to see how well Davis gels with veteran pros like Arik Armstead and Josh Hines-Allen. Checking in on a former Eagle isn't the sole reason to watch this divisional duel. The Eagles' 2-7 record has them holding on to the No. 5 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft entering Week 10.
Tennessee (1-7) is one of three NFL teams to earn fewer than two victories through nine weeks. An upset win by the Titans would draw them equal with the Eagles in the standings, strengthening Philly's chance of landing a top-five pick. Take note that the Jaguars and Titans will face off again in Week 12.
The focus remains on the 2027 NFL Draft when highlighting a Week 10 clash between the Dolphins and Colts. Philly could rip off a few wins down the stretch, but its chances of making the playoffs are incredibly slim. Wins from teams below the Eagles in the standings suddenly carry notable weight.
Miami (1-7) and Indianapolis (2-7) are two of those four teams. A Colts' victory would catapult them ahead of the Eagles with a 3-7 record. A Dolphins' victory would place them above the Eagles for the moment, due to strength of schedule. Either way, Philly will hold a top-four pick going into Week 11.
Miami quarterback Kyle McCord will make his NFL debut on Sunday, following Malik Willis' groin injury. He grew up an Eagles fan and played high school football at St. Joseph's Prep. McCord was selected by Philly in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, before being waived after the ensuing preseason.
The Chargers join the Titans, Dolphins, and Colts (first-round pick owned by the Jets) as the four teams currently standing in the Eagles' way of the No. 1 overall pick. Los Angeles travels to Baltimore on Monday night as the only winless squad in the NFL. It is the franchise's first 0-8 start since 2000.
It's possible the Ravens could get caught off guard here. Baltimore acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett to be their starter after both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (turf toe) suffered injuries. Wednesday was Brissett's first practice with the team as he aims to get acclimated quickly .
There have been two winless NFL campaigns since the turn of the century. The 2008 Lions and 2017 Browns each struggled to a 0-16 record. No one wants to join that club, so the Chargers should have added motivation to compete. Any Los Angeles win moving forward benefits Philadelphia.

title: Eagles Can't Hide From Bleak Coaching Staff Reality for Much Longer
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - Nick Sirianni says the Eagles won’t change coaches just to change them. Fair enough. But that feels like it's only delaying the inevitable with Sean Mannion, Chris Kuper, and Ryan Mahaffey.
After another flat loss that pushed the Eagles to 2-7 and a seven-game skid into the team’s bye week, Sirianni was asked about potential staff moves. The head coach repeated a version of the same line he’s used before: everything is on the table, but you don’t just change for the sake of changing because the record looks bad.
Sirianni’s premise is that you look at what’s real, you need conviction, and you don’t react to outside noise. He has publicly stuck with Mannion as the play-caller and has defended Kuper in strong terms, saying the new offensive line coach is coaching hard, teaching fundamentals, and giving players tools even if the results on game days haven't show nit.
Mahaffey, the run-game coordinator and tight ends coach Mannion brought over from Green Bay, has largely stayed out of the direct spotlight, but he is part of the same rebuilt offensive group that replaced Kevin Patullo and, more significantly, the long-tenured Jeff Stoutland.
The problem is that the “real” is hard to isolate right now. Attrition has muddied every evaluation. Jalen Hurts is out for the year with blood clots. Lane Johnson retired. The offensive line has dealt with injuries, scheme changes, and the sudden absence of the coach who had been its constant. Saquon Barkley has played through multiple ailments while DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks have missed time at receiver.
The quarterback situation behind Hurts has already flipped from Andy Dalton to Tanner McKee to the Joe Milton experience.
Through it all, the offense keeps failing to generate sustained drives, protect the quarterback, or establish the run. That makes it reasonable to question the scheme, the teaching, and the coordination between Mannion’s calls , Kuper’s line work, and Mahaffey’s run-game plan.
It is also fair to note that the sample is incomplete and chaotic. Injuries and personnel losses make it easier to argue that the coaches haven’t had a clean look—and harder to argue that the current setup is producing anything worth preserving.
Sirianni insists he is results-aware. The results, however, are that the offense has looked disconnected and underwhelming for most of the season under a first-year coordinator.
Claiming you care about results while continuing to operate as if this particular group is the right one creates an obvious tension.
Running it back with Mannion, Kuper, and Mahaffey next season feels increasingly untenable. The body of work, even with the caveats of attrition, has not justified another year of the same voices installing and calling the offense.
That does not mean midseason changes would fix anything. Firing or reassigning coaches now, with the season already lost and the roster battered, is unlikely to produce better football over the remaining schedule.
New voices would still be working with the same depleted personnel, limited practice time, and a quarterback situation that is not ideal.
The practical reality is that you play out the string. You gather whatever additional data you can, you keep the locker room from fracturing further if possible, and you accept that the meaningful decisions—on the offensive coordinator, the line coach, the run-game coordinator, and potentially the head coach himself—belong to the offseason, when there is time to search, hire, and install properly.
Sirianni’s reluctance to change for change’s sake is understandable on its face. But if the evaluation is truly results-driven, the current offensive staff is on thin ice.
While attrition makes the grade incomplete; it does not erase the results. The Eagles can finish the year with the group they have. The harder question is whether they should start the next one with it. The evidence so far suggests they should not.

title: 3 Pending Free Agents Eagles Could Re-Sign After Not Trading Them
full_text:
Jordan Davis was the only player the Philadelphia Eagles traded directly before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. That means the Eagles held onto a plethora of pending free agents, despite the risk of losing them for nothing over the offseason. However, some of the guys they held onto could remain in Philadelphia beyond the current campaign.
Here's a look at three pending free agents the Eagles could re-sign in the offseason after hanging onto them at the deadline.
People have predicted the end of Dallas Goedert's tenure with the Eagles for over a year now. Many didn't expect him to be back with the Eagles after the 2025 season, but he was re-signed over the offseason. And again, there were assumptions that he would be moved prior to the deadline this week.
But the deadline is now in the rearview mirror, and Goedert remains on the roster in Philadelphia, and it isn't impossible to imagine a world where the Eagles decide to bring him back again for the 2027 season.
It's not like the Eagles have another starting-caliber tight end waiting in the wings. Rookie Eli Stowers might be the future at the position, but he's barely touched the field during his first season, so he'll need more time to develop into a reliable starter.
Plus, with all their other needs this offseason, the Eagles won't want to spend big at tight end in free agency, and Goedert would likely be relatively affordable. Also, he's still a productive player. He led the team in touchdown receptions last season and has tallied 308 receiving yards and two TDs this season, despite dealing with injury issues and subpar quarterback play.
At the end of the day, the best option for both Goedert and the Eagles could be to run it back again in 2027.
There was a lot of speculation that the Eagles could trade defensive tackle Moro Ojomo before the deadline since he's playing on the final year of his current contract and is projected to become a whole lot more expensive heading into next season.
But the Eagles surprised everyone and went in a different direction , trading Davis to the Jaguars instead. This should be viewed as a vote of confidence in Ojomo on the part of Philadelphia's front office. Given this decision, it now seems exceedingly likely the Eagles will hold onto Ojomo and sign him to a new contract in the offseason.
The Eagles holding onto Woolen at the deadline, as opposed to trading him , will afford the team an extended opportunity to evaluate him for the future. The Eagles don't have a long-term answer at CB2 alongside Quinyon Mitchell, so all options should be on the table. Woolen has been somewhat underwhelming for the Eagles this season, but he hasn't been terrible, and the defense as a whole has struggled, so it's hard to single him out individually. He does need to be better about committing penalties, though.
It's far from a guarantee that the Eagles will bring back Woolen over the offseason, but if he plays well over the back half of the season, it's certainly not impossible.

title: 5 Necessary Changes the Eagles Must Make After Their Bye Week
full_text:
Eight games remain in an Eagles season that resembles a Talking Heads song: "We’re on the road to nowhere." It will be more than two months since they last won a game when they return from their bye week to play the Steelers on Nov. 22.
Their last win was Sept. 20, when Jalen Hurts led the Eagles on a magnificent game-winning drive against the Titans.
This won’t help turn things around, but here are five things I’d like to see happen over the Eagles' final eight games once they come out of their bye week.
Even when/if DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks return from injury, the rookie should see a healthy number of targets. He has improved with each game played and is one of the bright spots on this horrid offense.
With Smith missing four of the team’s nine games, Lemon is now the Eagles’ leading receiver with 312 yards, two more than Smith has.
It’s a small sample size, but since Week 7, Lemons has had three straight games with at least six catches and 50-plus yards, joining Puka Nacua and Jaxon Smith-Njigba as the only three on that sort of streak.
That Dallas Goedert wasn’t traded for something—anything—is curious. Maybe nobody wanted to give up anything for the veteran tight end.
Even more curious is why Johnny Mundt and Grant Calcaterra are still on the roster. Maybe Zach Ertz doesn’t have anything left, but wouldn’t fans rather see him out there threatening to break a franchise record for most catches in a career that has stood since 1983, when Harold Carmichael had 589? Ertz has 582.
Second week in a row we are seeing Eli Stowers (No. 87) give this kind of effort blocking a CB Baby steps! pic.twitter.com/l5FhR3fGRI
Even with Goedert still on the roster, Stowers needs more of a role. That the second-round pick only played seven snaps against the Giants in Week 9 is ridiculous.
Goedert played 57 snaps (81 percent). Come on, the odds are he won’t be back on a third straight one-year deal, so why shouldn’t Stowers cut into that kind of workload?
The trade of Jordan Davis will likely make this happen. The defensive tackle has played just 61 defensive snaps in his second season, but has held up well in a rotational role. He needs to play more just to see what the Eagles have in him over the next two years of his rookie contract.
Zion Wilson spent the preseason with the Eagles but was waived on cutdown day despite recording nine tackles, two tackles for loss or no gain, and four QB pressures in three preseason games. He was signed to the practice squad on Oct. 13.
Wilson, who is 6'3" and 315 lbs, was denied another year of college when he tried to transfer from East Carolina to Virginia, so he entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent. In 2025, with East Carolina, he had seven sacks. It would make sense to either elevate him from the practice squad or just sign him to the roster to take Davis’s place.
Barring Joe Milton leading the Eagles to a win or two, play Cole Payton in the final two games. Heck, even if Milton wins a game or two, playing Payton should happen. It’s evaluation time, after all.
Same thing for outside linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby and safety Cole Wisniewski, who has one practice squad elevation remaining. Why play Marcus Epps? He’s not part of the future. James-Newby has done some decent things in limited opportunities.
Then there’s guard Micah Morris. Why not give him some reps, too? He’s a big guy at 6'5" and 335 lbs.
Let’s see what these players have.

title: 3 Eagles Coaches' Jobs Should Be in Jeopardy During the Bye Week
full_text:
Bye weeks are a time for NFL players and coaches to rest and prepare for the second half of the season. For the Eagles, it'll be a time for reevaluation, too. A disastrous seven-game losing streak has Philadelphia sitting at the bottom of the NFC East. Glaring problems remain on both sides of the ball.
The front office can only change the roster so much midway through a season. That move came in the form of trading Jordan Davis to the Jaguars . Bigger changes can be made in the coaching staff. That could be as simple as shifting responsibilities or as impactful as firing someone .
Here's a look at three Eagles coaches whose jobs should be in jeopardy during the bye week.
Moving on from veteran offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland has proven to be more difficult than the Eagles expected. Philadelphia's hire of Chris Kuper wasn't considered a big splash. He took on the same role in Minnesota last season, when the Vikings allowed the second-most sacks in the NFL (60).
Philadelphia is suffering from similar issues, allowing the third-most sacks in the league (30). The Eagles entered Week 9 with the highest percentage of pass plays with unblocked pressure (18.2%). That was before New York's Arvell Reese had a free run to blast quarterback Joe Milton.
The issues go beyond pass blocking. The Eagles rank 27th in both rushing yards per carry (3.7) and rushing yards per game (88.6). This is a team that cruised to a Super Bowl title just two years ago with a historic ground game. Nowadays, Saquon Barkley is lucky to tally a few yards before being leveled.
It's fair to point out that Lane Johnson's retirement, Landon Dickerson's injuries, and Cam Jurgens' trade to Baltimore have made Kuper's job tough. The results on the field go beyond excuses, though. Improvements need to be made, and it has become clear that they won't be with Kuper at the helm.
Special teams should be a part of football that provides a team with an advantage, or at least keeps them in the fight. Instead, the Eagles have been getting undone by their special teams unit on a weekly basis. That includes poor kick/punt coverage, missed field goals, and costly penalties.
There's at least one setback to point out in every game. As of late, a false start penalty turned Jake Elliott's 36-yard field goal make into a 41-yard field goal miss in Week 8. A bad snap from Rocco Underwood forced punter Braden Mann into a rugby-style boot that went -2 yards in Week 9.
Mistakes happen, but constant mistakes show that there's a lack of adjustment. Special teams coordinator Michael Clay has been with the Eagles since 2021. It would make sense to give him a longer leash if Philly were winning games. It isn't. A new voice is needed in special teams meetings.
The hype surrounding offensive coordinator Sean Mannion was real during training camp. The 34-year-old former NFL quarterback was expected to bring a fresh, modern offensive scheme to a team that desperately needed one. However, the offense has looked far from fresh through nine weeks.
The Eagles have averaged 260.2 yards and 16.4 points per game, which are bottom-three marks in the NFL. They also check in below Philly's 2025 marks (311.0 & 22.1). While it's easy to blame injuries, the offense performed poorly even when the roster was fully healthy. It's been a season-long disaster.
Now, firing Mannion would be a much more substantial move than firing either Kuper or Clay. A first-time play-caller should be given the chance to work out the kinks. With that said, the Eagles need to shake up the game plan. Tailoring the system to their personnel would be a good place to start.
