title: Pressure Is Rising for Eagles' Recent Draft Classes Now That the Trade Deadline Is Over
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — With the trade deadline behind them and eight games left in a season gone bust, the Eagles will emerge from the bye week on Nov. 22 with shifting priorities.
The recent trades of Cam Jurgens and Jordan Davis have stripped some veteran production while loading up on future draft capital .
Quarterback Jalen Hurts is likely sidelined for the season. The offense is sputtering under new coordinator Sean Mannion. The defense under Vic Fangio has been uneven. In the midst of seven consecutive losses after a 2-0 start, wins would be nice, but the real work will be evaluating the recent draft classes under live-fire exercises.
Start with the 2026 class, which is already getting meaningful snaps for two of the premium picks.
Makai Lemon, the first-round wide receiver out of USC , is the clearest immediate contributor. After a quiet start, he’s become the most reliable target during the stretch without DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks. Lemon has put together consecutive games with six-plus catches and 50-plus yards, scored his first NFL touchdown against Dallas, and led the team in targets and yards in recent losses to the Commanders and Giants.
In recent weeks, Lemon has shown nice hands (although the concentration drops have been problematic), route-running, and the slot ability the Eagles targeted when they traded up to get him. The yards-per-catch are modest so far. But in a post-A.J. Brown offense that needs a young WR to step forward, Lemon is doing a solid job.
The rest of the season will show whether Lemon can sustain his recent improvement with Smith and Wicks involved as the more important priorities. It's also a test for Mannion to keep Lemon in mind.
Eli Stowers, the second-round tight end from Vanderbilt, is further behind because of early injuries that landed him on injured reserve to start the season.
The athletic former college quarterback has shown some flashes, namely three catches for 53 yards against Washington, including a 34-yarder, albeit in garbage time. You can at least envision the ability to stress linebackers.
Stowers is not displacing Dallas Goedert yet, but the long-term goal is clear. More snaps in 12 personnel or flexed out will tell the staff how quickly the Vandy product can be counted on for a real role in the offense.
Markel Bell, the third-round tackle from Miami, got thrown into the fire at right tackle after Lane Johnson’s retirement. The 6-foot-9, 345-pounder had a rough debut but has somewhat stabilized since. He’s not a finished product by any means—pressures and penalties remain an issue—but the size and improving processing are obvious.
With the offensive line in flux, Bell’s remaining games will serve as an extended audition for whether he can be a long-term starter or settle in as a backup swing tackle.
Evaluating key components of the 2025 class, which is supposed to be further along, is all about piling repetitions on Jihaad Campbell and Andrew Mukuba.
Campbell, a first-round linebacker from Alabama, had a solid rookie year (All-Rookie consideration, productive when starting) and was set for a full-time weakside role next to Zack Baun after Nakobe Dean left in free agency.
Year 2 has been interrupted by lingering hamstring and quad issues, but the tools are there. The questions surrounding Campbell involve his instincts. When healthy, the rest of the season should clarify whether Campbell is a true three-down starter or just an athlete.
Mukuba, the second-round safety from Texas, is already a primary piece in the secondary, but the results have been mixed—missed tackles and coverage lapses have shown up.
Fangio has spoken well of Mukuba’s trajectory, but outsiders often see something different. Mukuba’s remaining snaps will determine how much the coaching staff trusts him in the back end of a defense that needs more consistency.
Ty Robinson, a fourth-round defensive tackle from Nebraska, has been buried on the depth chart behind Jalen Carter, Davis, Moro Ojomo and Byron Young.
In a defensive line room that just lost Davis, Robinson should join the rotation and every snap will help determine if he should stay a part of it in 2027.
Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has always built through the draft. With extra premium picks coming in 2027 and beyond, the next eight weeks are the best chance to separate the keepers from the most recent drafts from those who won’t be part of any solution.
The record might not improve much for the Eagles, but the information gathered on these younger players should help determine the future.

title: 3 Eagles Who Will Likely Be Gone in the Offseason Despite Surviving Trade Deadline
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is now in the rearview mirror, and outside of the surprising trade of star defensive lineman Jordan Davis , it was a relatively quiet deadline for the Eagles.
The Eagles held on to several players who were predicted to be traded away , but that doesn't necessarily mean that those guys are part of the long-term plan in Philly.
Here's a look at three Eagles players who will likely still be gone over the offseason, despite surviving the trade deadline.
The Eagles benching Tanner McKee in favor of Joe Milton after three starts this season tells you everything you really need to know about how the organization views McKee at this point in time. If they viewed McKee as a long-term piece, they would have prioritized his development and allowed him to continue to play in Jalen Hurts' absence, even through some struggles.
Instead, they handed the offense over to a guy who had been on the roster for less than a month.
It should have been obvious that the Eagles were down on McKee when he entered the season as the third QB on the depth chart behind Andy Dalton, but his benching has made things crystal clear. McKee will be a free agent over the offseason, and we shouldn't expect to see him back in Philadelphia next season.
It came as a surprise to many, likely including Brown himself, that the veteran pass-catcher wasn't traded prior to the deadline , but he wasn't, which means he'll finish out the campaign as a member of the Eagles.
Perhaps Brown will be more of a factor for Philly over the final eight games than he was during the first nine, when he tallied just five receptions for 53 yards. Either way, it seems like the writing is already on the wall when it comes to his future in Philly.
There will be a lot of moving parts for the Eagles over the offseason, and bringing back an aging receiver who has had little impact probably won't be a priority for general manager Howie Roseman and company.
The Eagles agreed to trade linebacker Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals prior to the trade deadline, only for the Bengals to back out of the deal after learning that they might lose a compensatory pick as a result.
Bengals are expected to back out of the trade for Arnold Ebiketie. The Bengals would have lost a third-round compensatory pick that they were receiving for Trey Hendrickson signing with Baltimore. Now this trade is expected to fall through. https://t.co/1Enn5jLpDD
So, Ebiketie will remain in Philly for the rest of the season, but the fact that the team tried to flip him for a sixth-round pick is pretty indicative of his future with the franchise.
The Eagles couldn't recoup any value for Ebiketie, but it still seems exceedingly unlikely that they'll bring him back over the offseason. He's as good as gone.

title: Confidence Meter: How Close Are Eagles to Firing Nick Sirianni During Bye Week?
full_text:
The Eagles' 2026 season has spiralled out of control.
The Eagles have lost seven consecutive games heading into their bye week, a streak that dates back to late September, and head coach Nick Sirianni has been unable to stop the bleeding . As a result, some have suggested that the Eagles should move on from Sirianni in the middle of the current campaign, despite the fact that he led the team to a victory in Super Bowl 59 just last year.
But would the Eagles actually make such a drastic move involving the most successful coach in franchise history? That seems very doubtful.
During his first five seasons on the sideline in Philadelphia, Sirianni led the Eagles to five playoff appearances, two Super Bowl berths and one win in the big game. He has the highest regular-season winning percentage in franchise history and the second-most playoff wins.
If nothing else, his previous success should afford Sirianni the dignity of not being fired midseason, especially a season in which injuries have absolutely ravaged the roster. Sirianni hasn't had his starting quarterback for the past month, and a plethora of other key contributors have missed legitimate time due to various ailments. That's not necessarily an excuse, just a fact. Sirianni hasn't been dealt a full deck this season, and while he's been unable to maximize the deck he has been dealt, it's fair to wonder whether that's a fireable offense, especially since we've seen what he can do with a full deck.
The Eagles aren't going anywhere this season, anyway, and they're not in danger of missing out on the franchise's next great coach if they don't act quickly. It's not like there's a mastermind waiting in the wings to take over the team.
On the contrary, firing Sirianni in the middle of the season would do little for the franchise other than to send a message, but the message might not even be one that the organization wants to send. How would other coaches, and potential Sirianni replacements, feel after seeing a Super Bowl-winning coach thrown out the door at the first sign of turbulence? Why would a prime coaching candidate want to come to an organization that treats successful coaches that way? If the Eagles want to move on from Sirianni, they should absolutely wait until the offseason to do so.
Plus, moving on from coaches in the middle of the season simply isn't the Eagles' M.O. under owner Jeffrey Lurie. Since Lurie took over as the owner of the team in 1994, he has fired five head coaches. Four of those coaches—Rich Kotite, Ray Rhodes, Andy Reid and Doug Pederson—were all fired directly after the season came to an end.
Chip Kelly is the only coach who was fired by the Eagles during the season under Lurie. He was fired with just one game remaining in the 2016 season, and he hadn't experienced a fraction of the success with the organization that Sirianni has. So, the decision to move on from Sirianni mid-season would buck a major trend for the Eagles as an organization, which makes the move seem even less likely.
For what it's worth, Sirianni doesn't seem especially concerned about his future in Philly. While speaking prior to Philadelphia's Week 9 game against the Giants, Sirianni stressed that he continues to feel full support from Lurie despite the team's struggles this season.
“I’ve always felt I have nothing but complete support from Mr. Lurie, in everything, through good times, through bad times. That’s huge, right? That’s huge to be able to know that the owner has your back in all these situations," Sirianni said.
He likely wouldn't acknowledge any difference publicly, but it certainly sounds like a midseason firing would come as a surprise to Sirianni himself.
Crazier things have happened, but it would be extremely surprising if the Eagles moved on from Sirianni during the current campaign, both because of his previous success and the lack of other options available at the present time.

title: I’m Shocked the Eagles Didn’t Trade These 3 Players at the Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is officially in the rearview mirror, and it's safe to say that it felt like a normal day for Eagles fans. Outside of a failed deal that would've sent EDGE Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a sixth-round pick, Eagles general manager Howie Roseman stuck with the status quo, deciding Monday's blockbuster Jordan Davis trade with the Jaguars was all that needed to be done.
While the return for Davis was great, it's hard to be too excited about Philadelphia's trade deadline performance. After all, it isn't often that the Eagles have an opportunity to blow things and restock their draft capital, given that they're usually firmly in the Super Bowl conversations.
With that in mind, it's a surprise to see that the Eagles decided to keep this trio rather than trade them when they had the chance.
When it came to potential trade chips, Riq Woolen was among the Eagles' likeliest candidates to be moved . A one-year contract made him the perfect rental option for contending teams, while his Super Bowl-winning experience from his time in Seattle only added to what he could've brought to the table.
Instead, Woolen will remain in Philadelphia until the end of the season, at least. NBC Sports Philadelphia' s Ryan Fowler reported that even though "multiple teams" attempted a trade , "a deal that made sense for both sides never progressed beyond initial conversations."
It'll be interesting to see what Woolen does in the second half of the season; either giving the Eagles more reasons to keep him or walk away in March. His 52.7 coverage grade is a new career-low performance , according to Pro Football Focus , meaning he'll need to seriously step up if Philadelphia doesn't want to regret keeping him.
Despite spending all of his career in Philly, Dallas Goedert was another veteran viewed as one of the Eagles' biggest trade candidates .
Like, Woolen, Goedert is on an expiring deal, and no one would've blamed the team if they had done right by the 31-year-old tight end and trade to a Super Bowl contender. That didn't happen, though, forcing Goedert to spend the rest of the season on one of the more uncompetitive Eagles teams he's played for in the last nine seasons.
Goedert has now played on one-year contracts in back-to-back seasons, so it remains to be seen whether the Eagles will attempt the hat trick. Goedert is averaging career lows in yards per catch (9.9) and success rate (45.2%), so he'll likely need significant improvements if he wants to reach Year 10 in Philly.
With all the changes that the offensive line has undergone, Eagles fans were prepared to see guard Landon Dickerson shipped out of town this week. Several teams around the NFL needed interior O-line help, so why not turn to a former Super Bowl Champion with over 90 games between the regular season and playoffs under his belt?
Fast-forward past the deadline, and Dickerson is still an Eagle as he finishes the first season of his three-year, $58.5 million extension. In theory, that's plenty of time to get back on track, but a 54.4 PFF grade —ranking 54th among 75 qualified OGs—suggests that a fresh start likely would've benefited both sides, especially if Philadelphia could've gotten a decent return.
Given the term remaining on his contract, the Eagles likely want to give Dickerson more time before making a decision to cut ties. Let's hope, for their sake, he turns things around ASAP. Otherwise, not trading him on Tuesday might eventually look like a mistake.

title: McMullen: Jordan Davis Trade Cements Why Howie Roseman Is One of NFL's Best GMs
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Actions always speak louder than words.
Eight months after Howie Roseman handed Jordan Davis a three-year, $78 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid interior defensive linemen in football, the Eagles shipped him to Jacksonville for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round selection.
That isn’t just a roster tweak. It’s a clear signal that Philadelphia would rather build around Moro Ojomo than live with the massive commitment they just made to Davis.
An NFL source confirmed to Eagles On SI what the market already suggested: the Jaguars checked in on Ojomo first. They were told he wasn’t available. From there, the talks evolved to the point that the Eagles were willing to part with Davis , as long as James Gladstone played into his reputation for the overpay.
Behind the scenes, the Eagles’ posture for weeks had been that Ojomo was staying. However, most considered that to be straight out of the Roseman playbook of shooting for the stars in an attempt to generate a second-round pick for the Texas product.
The trade of Davis confirms Philadelphia is choosing the younger, cheaper, more versatile player they can actually keep next to Carter long-term.
This is also a clear indication that the Eagles believe this will be defensive coordinator Vic Fangio’s last season in Philadelphia. Fangio always wants a pure nose tackle he can plug into variable fronts when needed.
Davis was that guy—the space-eating, two-gap presence who lets Fangio play the light-box looks and disguise coverages he’s built his reputation on. When the production didn’t match the contract this year, it makes sense that the organization decided it wasn’t worth locking into that personnel profile for the next three seasons if Fangio isn’t going to be the one drawing it up.
The disappointment in Davis’ 2026 tape is real. After a career year in 2025—career highs in sacks, tackles for loss, and overall disruption—the Eagles thought he had turned the corner as a more complete player. Instead, he’s been a solid-but-limited run-stuffer who has struggled to stay in ideal condition and has barely played on third down unless it’s short-yardage.
Through nine games, he ranked third among Eagles defensive tackles in snaps behind Carter and Ojomo. On obvious passing downs he has been a non-factor for most of his career.
That’s not the profile you pay $26 million a year to keep when you already have Carter locked up on a much bigger deal and a rising player like Ojomo ready to take a bigger role.
Roseman should take a hit for crafting the original extension but recovered quickly by continuing to tap into the same market inefficiency he’s exploited for years: the systematic devaluation of future draft capital.
The 2029 second-round pick is the kind of asset most GMs treat as monopoly money. Roseman treats it like currency .
Ultimately, Davis is a two-down player who generated a little less than what the Titans extracted for Jeffery Simmons—a more accomplished, higher-usage player who fetched two firsts and a fourth.
The Jaguars may win a Super Bowl this year after loading up with Davis, safety Jessie Bates, and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. That doesn’t change the fact that this is one of the biggest overpayments we’ve seen in years. Jacksonville is paying a premium for a two-down player,
Former NFL executive Andrew Brandt noted that a general manager with a business and negotiating background like Roseman will continue to take advantage of GMs whose backgrounds are primarily scouting or personnel.
This trade seems to be the latest example of that.

title: Getting Close: Steelers Could Get Starting WR Back Soon
full_text:
Michael Pittman Jr. doesn't appear to be far away from a return for the Pittsburgh Steelers .
While the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Ray Fittipaldo doesn't expect Pittman Jr. (foot) to be activated from the reserve/injured list in time to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football this week, he may be back shortly after that.
"Do I think it's going to happen this week? No, I don't," Fittipaldo said during an appearance on 93.7 The Fan on November 11. "He hasn't even been among the guys who have been rehabbing during practice. But there's a little bit better feeling about him maybe for the Eagles game. But I think definitely pushing toward Thanksgiving, post-Thanksgiving, I think that's when you could see Pittman return."
Acquired from the Indianapolis Colts alongside a 2026 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2026 sixth-rounder in March, Pittsburgh also signed Pittman Jr. to a three-year, $59 million extension that more or less locked him in as the team's No. 2 wide receiver next to DK Metcalf heading into the season.
Pittman Jr. was out for part of training camp and all of the preseason due to a groin injury he suffered during the Steelers' Saturday Night Lights practice on August 8, though he was ready to go by the time Week 1 rolled around.
After posting 58 yards in his debut for the team, however, he missed their Week 2 game against the New England Patriots with a foot injury.
Pittman Jr. was active in Weeks 3 and 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals and Cleveland Browns, respectively, but he logged a combined 31 yards between those two contests.
He then landed on IR before having a chance to face the Colts for the first time following the trade in Week 5.
There was some fear at points that Pittman Jr. would remain out long-term, if not for all or at least a vast majority of the season, while dealing with plantar fasciitis.
While Pittman Jr. told reporters at the beginning of the Steelers' Week 9 bye that his injury had "morphed into something else" beyond plantar fasciitis, which was a bit ominous, he expressed some optimism regarding his timeline for a return.
"It would be great to be back after the bye week, which is what I would like," Pittman Jr. said. "But I can't go out there if I'm not effective. So, only time will tell."
Pittman Jr. has missed the minimum of four games while on IR, meaning he can be activated at any time.
His 21-day practice window has yet to be opened, and it appears unlikely that he'll play vs. Cincinnati as a result, though he could still very well be back on the field for Pittsburgh in short order.
Pittman Jr. has certainly lost a step at 29 years old, and his foot injury may keep him from being the best version of himself for the rest of the campaign.
Regardless, his return would be huge news for the Steelers when and if it happens. With Roman Wilson (finger) also on IR after suffering his injury vs. Indianapolis, while Ben Skowronek (calf) also hasn't suited up since Week 5, the team has been working with an incredibly short receiver room consisting primarily of DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Brandon Smith for essentially their entire four-game win streak.
Skowronek appears good to go ahead of this week's bout with the Bengals, however, and Wilson will be eligible for activation next week, though whether or not he's back in time to face the Eagles remains to be seen.
Pittman Jr.'s not overly explosive or dynamic as a route-runner at this point of his career, especially with his foot injury, but his size, reliable hands and blocking prowess are all of considerable value to Pittsburgh and will help the offense out once he does play.

title: Steelers Have a New WR to Watch For
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need help at the wide receiver position. After several injuries, the team's depth is depleted, and they're hopeful to get many of their options back , but will it be enough to make their room "good enough"?
Roman Wilson, who's missed the last four weeks with a finger injury, and Michael Pittman Jr., who's dealing with plantar fasciitis in his foot, are hopeful to return this season, but when? That's still up in the air.
Both are working off to the side during practices and progressing toward a return, according to head coach Mike McCarthy. But it's not confirmed when they'll be able to provide the needed help to the position this season.
Then there's Max Hurleman. The practice squad wide receiver has impressed during two training camps and preseason campaigns. Both in 2025 and 2026, he was on the verge of making the 53-man roster but fell just short, likely due to his undersized frame and undrafted status.
But McCarthy isn't overlooking him.
On two occasions, McCarthy has mentioned Hurleman as a candidate to return from Injured Reserve and help his offense move in the right direction.
"I feel great about our guys. I mean, we’re getting guys healthy. Michael [Pittman Jr.] is getting close, obviously, Roman [Wilson] and Max [Hurleman]," McCarthy said about his wideout room after the trade deadline. "So, we’ve got good young guys. Both the Brandons [Smith and Johnson]. So, we’ve got a group that I'm excited to continue to work with."
Even Aaron Rodgers tossed his name out there as a player who can contribute when healthy.
"We've obviously raised up a couple of our P-Squad guys who are talented. Still would love to get some opportunities for Max [Hurleman] at some point whenever he comes off," Rodgers said about players who can contribute at wide receiver. "We have Marquez [Valdes-Scantling], who hasn't been brought up yet, so we have a lot of options. But I'm hopeful that we'll get [Michael Pittman Jr.] and Roman [Wilson] back sooner rather than later."
Never say never, in the words of Mike Tomlin. The practice squad wideout has shown those in the building what he could do for some time now and may finally be getting his opportunity.
He's currently on the practice squad IR list but is eligible to return. When he does, McCarthy may have hinted at him getting an opportunity to prove himself on the active roster.
"I mean, how do you not love Max [Hurleman]? I mean, Max is, he's one of the guys you — as a new coach, new coaching staff, you come in here every day doing everything right," McCarthy said. "GPS was, [he] burned it up. I mean, just, the guy has an incredible workload capacity, work ethic. So, unfortunate that he got hurt when he did. I felt that he truly performed to a level that he deserved a 53-man roster spot. So, it'll be great to get him back and get him back into the fold."
And Hurleman is ready for that opportunity.
"Awesome," Hurleman told Steelers On SI, about being mentioned by Rodgers and McCarthy. "It's very humbling whenever your name gets brought up. I've been working my tail off every day to come back. To get the recognition, that means a lot, but obviously, there's a ton of work to do. Haven't played a game yet, but it's awesome to hear they trust me and see me as an option."
"That's why we play the game, to be out there on Sundays," he added. "Whatever my role has been, I've tried to excel at that. But I've been itching to play."
So, look out for a new addition to Pittsburgh's wide receiver core . And after not adding anyone at the trade deadline, they may be looking at their practice squad for a name they have a lot of excitement about.
Noah Strackbein is a Publisher for On SI, covering the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. title: DK Metcalf Explains How to Fix Steelers Passing Game
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are trying to solve their offensive woes as they begin the second half of the regular season.
At the top of the Steelers' priorities is their passing game. The organization opted against trading for another wide receiver, leaving number-one option DK Metcalf as the only player who can lead this receiving group down the stretch.
Getting Metcalf going has been a problem all year long, however. After posting back-to-back 50+ yard games in Weeks 6 and 7, he posted another blunder of a performance in Week 8 against the Cleveland Browns, finishing with just four receiving yards.
Searching for answers, Metcalf has a simple suggestion that could unlock more production. He thinks moving him around the line of scrimmage more could be the key.
"Just moving around more," he said to Brendan Howe of Steelers Now. "I think that’s pretty much the only answer that we have, because if they know I’m just gonna be back side, they can put just a safety (over), a corner press me and good luck with everybody else."
Coming out of the bye week, both head coach Mike McCarthy and offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio shared a similar sentiment. They expressed frustration with themselves and their playcalling, saying that the coaching staff hasn't given him the right opportunities to produce like a number-one wide receiver.
Metcalf's comments seem to confirm that, but is it true?
According to game data compiled by SumerSports , Metcalf is being used in a limited way. It starts with where he lines up, which is almost exclusively out wide. He's lined up on the outside 86.8% of the time.
That alone isn't a problem, as he works as the primary target in a majority of the passing plays.
The problem is how limited the route tree the Steelers are asking him to run is, despite finding limited success through the first eight games.
It's easy to guess what Metcalf's most frequently run route is - a go ball. According to data from SumerSports, it accounts for 27.6% of his routes, doubling any other route he's run so far.
On those go balls, he's been targeted 18 times. When he makes the reception, he can cause damage, averaging 19 yards per reception. The issue is that he's only hauled in four of those passes.
But still, the Steelers keep asking him to do the same thing. Of the 315 routes he's run this season, 87 have been Metcalf just running straight down the boundary, trying to beat the secondary over the top.
The other routes they are asking him to run most frequently aren't faring much better. His second-most-run route is a hitch, running it 42 times so far. He's been targeted eight times, making seven receptions for 70 yards, but no touchdowns.
His lone touchdown pass came on a crossing route against the Cincinnati Bengals.
All of this points to expanding what they ask Metcalf to do. Things haven't gone perfectly for the team's top wideout, but he stillh as 33 receptions for 378 yards and a score. It's not number one production, but maybe with a bit more versatility in his route tree, Metcalf can return to form in the second half.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Broncos News Makes Steelers Look Way Better
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers didn't make any moves at the NFL trade deadline , leaving their fans feeling more disappointed than optimistic for the back half of the season.
Meanwhile, the Kansas City Chiefs, Jacksonville Jaguars, Buffalo Bills and Denver Broncos all made trades. Or at least we thought.
Two days after the trade deadline, the Broncos announced that their deal with the Los Angeles Chargers for inside linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized. It's believed to be because of a failed physical.
https://t.co/Ewbs7j6Yga pic.twitter.com/QzaZ40ZFF7
All of a sudden, the AFC field felt very different. Yes, the Jaguars made two massive trades, landing Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, and the Buffalo Bills traded for one of the best safeties in the NFL in Amani Hooker, but those were the splash additions.
The Chiefs added Josh Downs, which many Steelers fans were arguing wouldn't be an "all-in" type of move for Pittsburgh, and the Cincinnati Bengals also backed out of a deal.
Maybe it's the sobering of two days passing since the trade deadline, or the news that the Broncos will not be getting better at inside linebacker, but the Steelers feel much more in the mix than they did less than 48 hours ago.
Yes, they will need to get past the Bills and Jaguars, who certainly improved in big ways, but maybe they don't need to get past either.
Sometimes, the NFL playoff bracket is about getting there, then getting lucky.
The Steelers are a comparable team to the Broncos, New England Patriots, and even the Chiefs. The Houston Texans, Cleveland Browns, Baltimore Ravens and Las Vegas Raiders all feel a step below Pittsburgh in terms of talent and ability to win at this point in the season.
Maybe the Steelers don't sit in the same tier as the Jaguars and Bills leaving the deadline, and unless something drastic happens in the next few weeks, they won't be in that tier before the postseason. But they certainly sit in the next tier, and at that point anything can happen.
Pittsburgh is going to get healthier. Derrick Harmon , Roman Wilson, Michael Pittman Jr. and hopefully Sebastian Joseph-Day will all return at some point before Week 18. If they can have a fully loaded roster going into the playoffs, anything can happen.
But as the dust settles from the trade deadline and the Steelers look at their competition, there's not much separation between them and the rest of the AFC, and the Broncos killing a trade with the Chargers brought that to light for everyone to see.

title: Mike Tomlin Reveals Moment He Knew He Was Leaving Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- There has been lots of speculation surrounding former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin. After 19 seasons as the man in charge, he stepped down following their Wild Card loss to the Houston Texans.
In the months since, the Steelers have moved in a new direction under head coach Mike McCarthy, while Tomlin has adjusted seamlessly to life as a television analyst on Sunday Night Football.
Still, there has never been an answer as to why he stepped down when he did. Now, we may finally have an answer after Tomlin appeared on Cam Heyward's Not Just Football podcast. Speaking on his decision to depart the organization, Tomlin shared that he made his mind up about leaving around the time he entered his driveway after that loss, citing an acceptance that he reached the end of his time in Pittsburgh.
"I did probably by the time I pulled in my driveway," Tomlin said when Heyward asked if he knew after the loss that he was retiring.
"I never wanted to stay too long," he admitted. "Also, there's a cumulative component to coaching. I had 19 years of baggage. And sometimes your teams have to carry your bags. And I just thought we had the making of a really good team. A team that is capable of competing for and winning a championship. But when I really started thinking about it, man, my bags might have slowed it down."
"I never wanted to stay too long." Mike Tomlin on his decision to step down as head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers after 19 seasons. pic.twitter.com/Qo9XleOaX2
This entire conversation between Tomlin and Heyward was illuminating, but this specific clip stands out due to the former head coach's admission. Over the final years of his tenure in Pittsburgh, terms like "stale" were frequently used to describe his approach.
The defense was unrelenting in trying to do the same things, regardless of how often opposing offenses figured them out.
The offense couldn't find steady footing either. Despite Tomlin switching offensive coordinators multiple times over his time in Pittsburgh, the offense was no better than average after the end of the "Killer B's" Era of Steelers football.
Tomlin is acknowledging that in this conversation, and it's incredibly refreshing to hear it from him as he reflects on a Hall of Fame run with the Steelers.
It's easy to speculate about Tomlin truly being done as an NFL head coach, and he even admits that. Speaking with the media before the Steelers versus Cincinnati Bengals Sunday Night Football matchup, Tomlin said he has yet to think about his future as a coach, but that he hasn't thought he will never return.
It's a situation he'll address when it reveals itself to him.
"I haven’t given one iota of thought to coaching," Tomlin said . "I’m sure some of that is going to come up in the not-so-distant future. But I’ll cross that bridge when I get there."
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Former Steelers LB Reveals He Once Requested Trade
full_text:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers inside linebacker Vince Williams revealed that he once approached general manager Kevin Colbert and asked for a trade.
On " Steelers Blitz" , Williams stated that after the Steelers drafted Ryan Shazier in the first round of the 2014 NFL Draft, he went to Colbert and asked out. That request was not granted, however.
"I asked to get traded one time," Williams said. "Kevin Colbert was like, 'Get out of my office...' I tried to get traded when Ryan got drafted. When Ryan got drafted, I was like, 'I'm out of here.'
"He was like, 'Get out of here. What are you talking about?' You're a sixth-rounder. You better be hoping that you've got a job tomorrow...' He laughed at me. He never took me serious... I had my agent, and he told my agent, he was like, 'What? Get out of my face.'"
Considering Williams was a late Day 3 pick who was entering his second season in the league when he asked for a trade , it's no surprise that Colbert shut it down immediately and seemingly didn't give even a second of thought towards fulfilling the former's wishes in the moment.
Williams did play more than most sixth-round picks as a rookie, making 11 starts and logging 53 tackles, but Colbert still didn't believe he had any ground to stand on when it came to requesting a trade.
Once Shazier entered the picture, however, Williams' playing time did dwindle.
From 2014 to 2016, Williams made just six starts and recorded a total of 136 tackles with three fumble recoveries and 2.5 sacks while never being on the field for over 26 percent of Pittsburgh's defensive snaps in any of those three seasons (per Pro Football Reference ).
Williams later became more of a focal point for the Steelers' defense, as he started all 30 contests he appeared in between the 2017 and 2018 campaigns while putting up a combined 165 tackles, 12.5 sacks and two interceptions.
He also signed a three-year extension worth $18.60 million ahead of the 2018 season, and after recording 125 tackles with 5.5 sacks between the 2019 and 2020 campaigns, he was cut in March 2021.
Pittsburgh re-signed Williams to a one-year contract one month later in April, though he went on to retire in July right before training camp began.
Colbert first joined Pittsburgh as its director of football operations in 2000 before being named the franchise's first-ever general manager in 2010 and later adding vice president to his ledger in 2016.
In terms of the most noteworthy trades involving players that he made over his 22 years with the organization, sending Antonio Brown to the Oakland Raiders in March 2019 for a 2019 third-round pick (Diontae Johnson) and 2019 fifth-rounder (Zach Gentry) is up there alongside acquiring Minkah Fitzpatrick from the Miami Dolphins in September of that same year for a package headlined by Pittsburgh's 2020 first-rounder.
Colbert also dealt Santonio Holmes to the New York Jets in April 2010 for a 2010 fifth-round pick, and that selection was later flipped to the Arizona Cardinals in order to reacquire Bryant McFadden as well as a sixth-rounder, which was used on Brown.
In terms of trade-ups during the NFL Draft, Colbert slid up in the first round in 2003 to select Troy Polamalu while doing the same in 2006 to land Holmes.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers vs. Super Bowl Champions: One Mark Isn't Good Enough
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers were urged to add to their roster before this year's NFL Trade Deadline. Instead, they stood pat. They made no trades for a pass-catcher or any bolstering additions to an already impressive defense. The front office sent a crystal-clear message: the main pieces they assembled in the offseason are the ones they are relying on to finish the job in 2026.
That could be seen as a vote of confidence or an admission, depending on how you view the Steelers' roster. Now that we know who the team is running with, barring any free-agent additions, it's worth asking if this offense has what it takes to support a postseason run.
Looking through the past 10 teams to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, their offenses all shared one thing in common - they finished the regular season averaging at least 350 yards of offense per game. Sadly, the Steelers' offense isn't there yet, and without any upgrades at the deadline, it's unlikely they reach that point in 2026.
They say defenses win championships, and while that is certainly an important piece of winning in the NFL, having a well-structured and balanced offense is just as important.
The past 10 Super Bowl winners all had that in common. They didn't rank in the top five across all offensive statistical categories, but they did stand out in more than one way.
Total yards were consistent across all 10 winners. Each of those offenses averaged at least 350 yards of total offense per game at the end of the regular season. According to data compiled through ESPN, the Seattle Seahawks and the 2023 Kansas City Chiefs were the lowest-performing offenses in terms of total yards. Both teams averaged just over 351 yards per game. Last season, the Seahawks finished eighth in the NFL with 351.4 yards per game, while the '23 Chiefs finished ninth in the NFL that year with 351.3 yards per game.
The number 350 remains the benchmark for a Super Bowl-winning offense.
Through eight games, the Steelers are not meeting that mark. They have posted a respectable 328 yards per game, currently 16th in the NFL. It's also 23 yards more than they averaged in 2025 and nine yards higher than their 2024 offense.
Even with those improvements, the Steelers are still a bit short on reaching that 350 yards per game.
The best part of the Steelers' offense is undoubtedly the running game. Led by Jaylen Warren , the ground game wears defenses down and consistently puts up yards. Warren has single-handedly posted at least 90 rushing yards and 100 all-purpose yards or more in five of the last six contests.
That's led to the Steelers averaging 117.9 rushing yards per game, which ranks 12th in the NFL. That's the highest they rank in any major offensive category (yards per game, rushing yards per game, passing yards per game and points per game), and it's what the Steelers are putting all of their hope in for a postseason run.
But can the running game add even more to what is already an outstanding performance for the rest of the season?
If the Steelers are serious about a Super Bowl, they need to improve their offensive output by 22 yards per game. The run game might take them there, but a better path to that total yardage is improving their pedestrian passing game.
That's what made the Steelers' inaction at the NFL Trade Deadline so maddening. They have a glaring hole and draft capital that could have filled the void, but they took the passive route.
As a result, they don't have the personnel to reach that next level. So, despite the surprising record and plenty of positives to build on for the second half, it's hard to take this team seriously as a Super Bowl contender after another quiet deadline performance.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Defense Could Get Huge Boost for Bengals Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' defense could be receiving some major reinforcements ahead of a crucial Week 10 matchup on Sunday Night Football against the Cincinnati Bengals.
Head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters that the Steelers are opening the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Derrick Harmon (foot), who is currently on the reserve/injured list.
It's not necessarily a guarantee that Harmon will be activated off of IR in time to play the Bengals, though it's certainly a huge step in the right direction and would signal that there's at least a solid chance that he'll return to the 53-man roster in the coming days.
Harmon was placed on IR after suffering his foot injury in the first half of Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football.
The 2025 first-round pick has missed the required minimum of four contests while on IR, meaning he is eligible to be activated from IR at any time.
Before going down with his injury, Harmon had recorded 12 total tackles and 1.5 sacks. He also has a forced fumble, which came at the end of the fourth quarter vs. Cincinnati in Week 3 on a sack of Joe Burrow and clinched a 30-27 victory for the Steelers.
With Harmon's return appearing rather imminent, Pittsburgh is inching closer to having about as clean of a bill of health as it has had all season long.
Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is making progress while also residing on IR, and the same could be said for fellow wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger).
Wilson cannot be activated until Week 11, though Pittman Jr. has missed the required minimum of four games, just like Harmon.
Pittman Jr.'s practice window has yet to be opened, and it appears as though he is trending towards missing this week's bout with the Bengals, but he should be back in the not-too-distant future.
Gennings Dunker (knee) also could potentially work his way back sooner rather than later, as he's at the end of his initial four-to-six week recovery timeline for an MCL sprain that landed him on IR in Week 3.
Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) might be staring down a long-term absence , perhaps for the entire season after being placed on IR in Week 7, though Harmon's impending return could help offset that loss.
While the Steelers opted not to swing any trades at the deadline, they're still set to supplement their roster in the back-half of their season considering the likes of Harmon, Pittman Jr. and Wilson are all progressing.

title: Ex-Steelers HC Mike Tomlin Leaves Door Open for Coaching Return
full_text:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin isn't thinking about his future in coaching at the moment, though he at least kept the door open for a return in that regard.
During a conference call with NBC correspondents before the Steelers ' Week 10 road matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football, which Tomlin will be in attendance for as part of the network's "Football Night in America" crew, he stated that he hasn't "given one iota" of thought towards returning to an NFL sideline while admitting that it is a topic of discussion that will likely pop up down the line.
"I haven’t given one iota of thought to coaching," Tomlin said. "I’m sure some of that is going to come up in the not-so-distant future. But I’ll cross that bridge when I get there."
While the end of his tenure with the Steelers wasn't always smooth, Tomlin's overall body of work with the franchise will undoubtedly be enough to make the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the future.
In his 19 years at the helm in Pittsburgh before stepping down after the 2025 campaign, not once did Tomlin finish with a losing record while compiling an overall record of 193-114-2 in the regular season.
The Steelers lost seven straight postseason games under Tomlin to close out his run with the team, but that shouldn't take away from the fact that he won Super Bowl XLIII with them in 2008 in addition to notching seven additional victories over 13 total trips to the playoffs.
Tied for the ninth-most head coaching wins in NFL history with fellow Pittsburgh legend Chuck Noll, Tomlin's legendary resume will always stand tall regardless of if he takes another job in the coming years or not.
If Tomlin does decide to jump into the coaching carousel, whether that be in 2027, 2028 or beyond, there's some uncertainty around whether or not Pittsburgh would be able to trade his rights and receive assets in return.
The New Orleans Saints were able to do so when Sean Payton stepped away after the 2021 season and was later hired by the Denver Broncos in 2023, but it's unknown if the Steelers can follow suit.
Should Pittsburgh still retain his contractual rights, it could potentially land a first-round pick (if not more) for Tomlin's services from whichever team hires him, which would greatly aid the organization's potential pursuit of a franchise quarterback.
Even if the Steelers can't trade Tomlin, his destination in the event that he returns to coaching could impact the team if he takes a job in the AFC and thus would have to face the black and gold semi-frequently.

title: Former Steelers Player and Coach Dick Hoak Passes Away
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — Former Pittsburgh Steelers player and coach Dick Hoak passed away at the age of 86.
The native of Jeannette, Pennsylvania spent nearly five decades with the Steelers in some capacity, winning five Super Bowls with the franchise. He earned Pro Bowl honors once over his 10 seasons as a running back in the NFL, and he followed his playing career with a tremendous stint as a coach in the organization, helping the franchise capture five of their six Lombardi Trophies.
The former Pro Bowl running back was a legendary of the franchise’s history, and Steelers President Art Rooney II offered some heartfelt words on Hoak’s passing. The team shared his official statement via their team social media channels.
“We are deeply saddened by the passing of Dick Hoak, a legendary member of the Pittsburgh Steelers family,” he stated. “Dick respresented everything the Steelers stand for with his toughness, loyalty, dedication and an unwavering commitment to the team. First as a player, then as a coach, Dick’s contributions to the organization spanned generations.”
Steelers President Art Rooney II on the passing of Dick Hoak: pic.twitter.com/sPXZk1vtoB
Hoak first entered the Steelers organization during the 1961 NFL season, when the team drafted him out of Penn State in the seventh round of the 1961 NFL Draft.
As a rookie he played in 14 games, kicking off a career that spanned 10 seasons and 135 NFL games played. As a tailback, he amassed over 1,100 carries with the Steelers, producing 3,965 rushing yards and 25 touchdowns. He also added 146 receptions over his career for an additional 1,452 receiving yards and eight touchdowns.
The 1968 was Hoak’s peak season as a player. He ran for 858 rushing yards and three touchdowns, plus 253 receiving yards and another score. Those numbers earned him his sole Pro Bowl selection.
He ranks eighth on the Steelers' all-time rushing leaders.
It didn’t take long for Hoak to find an impact in a new role. He retired from the NFL following the 1970 season, but two years later he was right back with the Steelers. Head coach Chuck Noll hired Hoak as the running backs coach ahead of the 1972 campaign. The team went on to win four Super Bowls under his coaching.
Decades later, Noll retired and was replaced by Bill Cowher . The only position coach Cowher retained was Hoak.
He ended his coaching career with 35 seasons at the helm and earned his place as an inaugural member of the Steelers’ Hall of Honor.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Knowledge of Klint Kubiak 'Definitely Helps' Seahawks Against Raiders
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have an upcoming reunion when they face the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Former Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak is now the head coach of the Raiders, and that means the Seattle defense will face Kubiak’s offense once again.
After practicing against Kubiak’s scheme every day during the 2025 season, both sides have an advantage: Kubiak knows Mike Macdonald’s defense, and the Seahawks’ defense and Macdonald know Kubiak’s offense.
Those may ultimately cancel each other out, but it does add intrigue to the matchup. Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV was asked on Thursday about how their knowledge of Kubiak’s system could impact the game.
“Yeah, I mean, I think that definitely helps,” Jones said. “We were able to get a feel of how he would like to attack us in practice during certain situational periods, and you got a great idea of how he likes to call the games just sitting there watching. I think that’ll help us, but at the end of the day he’s got his own squad; he’s tweaked a lot of things, so we’ve gotta go out there and execute.”
After a 3-0 start, the Raiders have lost five of their last six games. But much of that can be attributed to a horrendous defense that has allowed a league-high 29.8 points and 385.4 yards per game.
Offensively, Las Vegas has been in the middle of the pack under Kubiak. The Raiders are averaging 331 yards (15th) and 26.4 points (eighth) per game. They moved the ball through the air well with Kirk Cousins at quarterback, but their 71.3 rushing yards per game rank 31st in the league.
A lot will change in Week 10, however. Cousins was traded to Minnesota, and No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is taking over the starting quarterback role. He will make his first NFL start against the Seahawks.
“You kind of watch the preseason games; he played a little bit in those,” Jones explained about how they’re game-planning for Mendoza. “Then you go from what they’ve done, the totality of the season; you kind of go in there with expectations of them to kind of keep it the same, but knowing that he’s a young guy … I think they’ll kind of dial it back a little bit. But you’re playing a player [that was] the number one pick and can make all the throws, extremely intelligent guy from the looks of it, so I think we’ve got a challenge ahead of ourselves.”
On paper, the Seahawks’ defense has the big advantage of being the best against the run in the entire league against one of the worst rushing offenses.
But as Jones said, Mendoza leading the offense creates a big question mark about how good the Raiders’ passing offense will be, and that’s what Seattle will be looking to neutralize on Sunday.

title: Seahawks Injury Update: Great News on Star Offensive Lineman
full_text:
When looking at this injury report, the first thing that might stand out is how familiar it all is . Not a lot changed from yesterday, but one of the things that did change is very significant. So, keeping in mind that a Thursday report is much more impactful than a Wednesday one, let’s have a look and take the temperature of this roster’s health at the moment.
The one big news update today concerns starting left tackle Charles Cross (ankle). After not practicing once since his injury against the Kansas City Chiefs a couple weeks ago , Cross was able to squeeze in a limited session today. I don’t think he plays on Sunday, but it’s indicative of a player who will be ready to go after the bye week. So that’s something to be happy about.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who rested yesterday, was a full go today. A.J. Barner (finger) was removed from the report entirely, which is a rare occurrence that indicates they believe he’s completely 100% healthy. Otherwise, all of this will look pretty similar to yesterday. In some cases, that can be a good thing, but for some of these players the lack of progress is bad.
Rashid Shaheed (knee) was a full participant once again , so expect him to suit up on Sunday. Jarran Reed was a DNP again, but the report lists it as being for personal reasons and not an injury. Anthony Bradford (knee), Derick Hall (back), Drew Lock (right elbow, oblique), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), and Connor O’Toole (foot) remained limited.
Sam Darnold (ribs, quadricep), Quenton Nelson (knee), Brandon Pili (back), and Leonard Williams (stinger) remain DNPs, so plan to watch a game without those four participating on Sunday. Darnold and Nelson in particular have been basically declared out this week , and there’s great incentive to wait on returns with the bye week looming.
The Raiders had a report that was also very similar to yesterday. The only change was concerning the status of Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, back), who went from limited to full, indicating he’s ready to roll. Thomas Booker (ankle) and Trey Zuhn (concussion) remained in limited status, and Ian Thomas (ankle) is still practicing in full.
Injuries will likely not play any real factor on the Raiders side of the fence this weekend, as I suspect all of these players will be available. They’re also very light on long-term wounds.

title: Seahawks QB Drew Lock Provides Positive Injury Update Ahead of Week 10
full_text:
With Sam Darnold out again in Week 10, Drew Lock is in line to start for the Seattle Seahawks once again against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.
Lock, however, has been working through elbow and oblique injuries. The elbow was already an issue before his Week 9 start, and he suffered the oblique in that win over the Arizona Cardinals. When speaking to reporters on Thursday, Lock said the oblique isn't too bad.
“Not too much, honestly,” Lock said when asked if he’s been feeling it when throwing. “We talked about it being on the backside, which is way better for a thrower than on the front side. So, grateful for that.”
By the backside, Lock means his right oblique. As a right-handed thrower, that’s preferable with oblique injuries because more power and rotation is initiated by the frontside oblique.
“Mechanic-wise, yeah, you’ve got to use a little bit of the backside. But when you’re rotating and pulling through, it’s all this,” Lock said, motioning to his left oblique. “That’s really when the torque happens; the speed of the arm comes through with that. So, allowing it to be back here [on the right], mechanically speaking, it is a little better.”
It’s not a new injury for Lock, either, as he said he dealt with a worse oblique injury while he was playing for the New York Giants in 2024. That was his gap year away from the Seahawks after backing up Geno Smith in Seattle in 2023.
“That was on the front side,” Lock explained. “So, yeah, that was not fun for a couple of weeks. Took a couple weeks off. It was in the preseason, though, so I missed the last two preseason games.”
Even though he’s not 100% healthy, Lock should be good to go against the Raiders, barring a setback, of course. The Seahawks then head into a bye in Week 11, and Darnold could return for their Week 12 rematch against the San Francisco 49ers.
At 5-4, the Seahawks are eighth in the NFC at the midway point of the season. Every game is now a must-win if they want to squeeze into the playoffs, especially since the teams ahead of them don’t seem to be slowing down.
Lock has played well in Darnold’s stead, completing 71.1% of his passes for 597 yards and five touchdowns. He hasn’t turned the ball over once, which has been the biggest positive for a Seahawks team that was struggling with giving the ball away.

title: How the Seahawks Gives Raiders' Fernando Mendoza a Rough First Start
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense is no stranger to tormenting young quarterbacks. Last season, the Seahawks gave Houston’s C.J. Stroud, Minnesota’s Max Brosmer and New England’s Drake Maye games to forget. This season, the Dark Side Defense has already given Maye, Los Angeles Chargers’ Justin Herbert and Kansas City’s Patrick Mahomes II a game to forget.
​The Seahawks will go on the road to take on the Las Vegas Raiders , who will be starting the 2026 NFL Draft’s first overall pick in quarterback Fernando Mendoza for the first time in his career. This comes after the Raiders traded veteran starting quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. The Dark Side Defense has the potential to give Mendoza a rough first start in his career.
​The Raiders come into Week 10 with the second-most productive passing offense and the fifth-most productive scoring offense. There are several key reasons for this impressive run, including the offensive philosophy from head coach and former Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak and Cousins’ stellar play. The Raiders’ offense has now to adjust to a dramatic quarterback switch from Cousins to Mendoza.
​Mendoza will likely rely on his tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer to quickly get the ball off for his first start. Bowers and Mayer have combined for nearly 1,000 yards and seven touchdowns this season. The Seahawks have been more efficient in the last few games at suppressing tight ends. Seattle held Cardinals tight end Trey McBride to one of his least productive performances this season.
​Second-year nickelback Nick Emmanwori has become a much more efficient dynamic defender . One of his biggest weaknesses last season was covering tight ends, but he showed he has become reliable at covering every type of pass-catcher. Emmanwori can show the league how to cover Bowers and suppress Mendoza.
​The Seahawks can limit Mendoza by taking away his best targets, but their main objective should be to pressure him constantly. Seattle possesses the league’s top-ranked total defense and passing defense. This is largely due to the elite secondary and solid contributors throughout the rest of the defense.
​The Seahawks rank 13th in sacks accounted for (23), but fourth in quarterback knockdowns (13.7%) and fifth in quarterback pressures (27%). While the Seahawks don’t have the edge rushers to consistently create sacks, they have defenders on the defensive line and blitzing linebackers/secondaries to constantly hit the quarterback in the backfield. Seattle possesses the players to wear down Mendoza, despite his solid size.
​Seattle could be without defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) in Week 10.  Edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) could be back after being limited in Wednesday’s practice, but another edge rusher Derick Hall (back) is on the injury list and could be limited or miss Sunday’s game,

title: 5 Burning Questions Ahead of Seahawks vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are getting ready for their Week 10 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders , who will hand the ball to No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza for his first career NFL start.
With the game getting closer , we spoke with Las Vegas Raiders On SI contributor Carter Landis, who spoke about the team and its current state of affairs.
I think it’s been impressive. Some teams could pack it in after a four-game losing streak, especially a team with the Raiders’ talent level, but he’s kept the energy up in the room. The team is 4-5 after losing to the 49ers, but there have been some impressive moments from young players, and the bones of the scheme are evident.
There have also been some gaffes, which you expect from a first-year head coach without many household names, but overall, there is an impressive culture being built.
I was truthfully surprised John Spytek strayed from the course that they talked to extensively about this offseason. The plan was for Kirk Cousins to start until Fernando Mendoza was ready, and that appears to be sooner rather than later. The Vikings were obviously desperate, and getting a top-100 pick out of that is encouraging.
That said, the Raiders don’t make this move if they don’t think Mendoza is ready. The No. 1 overall pick has been learning behind Cousins, but he faces two tough defenses to start his career. We’ll see how he responds.
The Raiders’ offensive line has been absolutely awesome in pass-protection. Last year’s unit couldn’t run-block or pass-block (they still can’t run-block). Getting an experienced offensive line coach like Rick Dennison to improve the floor of this group has led to elevated play from Jackson Powers-Johnson and DJ Glaze. The Raiders have only allowed 11 sacks this season, tied for the second-fewest in the NFL. That group will be crucial in keeping Mendoza’s pocket clean.
The defense taking advantage of its opportunities. That’s what led to early-season victories, and the Raiders haven’t done that much in their recent losses. Young defenders like Treydan Stukes and Hezekiah Masses will need to take the ball away and create short fields and easy opportunities for the Mendoza-led offense. If they let Drew Lock (I presume?) get comfortable, they may be in for their seventh-straight game allowing 30-plus.
It’s a struggling Seahawks offense against a struggling Raiders defense, so something has to give. I’ll defer to the Super Bowl champions against the team that is still working on a rebuild. Seahawks 31, Raiders 20.

title: Seahawks Rookie Report: Jadarian Price Coming Off Best Game Yet
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks and their 2026 NFL Draft class have had a rough stretch. For most of the season, the Seahawks have seen a lot of their rookies show they’re not ready to play or are on IR. The Seahawks are coming off a 17-3 bounce-back win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 .
​The win over the Cardinals might have been the best any of the rookies looked at any point during the season. Seattle is getting some investment from the 2026 Draft class, with the potential of more impact coming soon. The Seahawks go on the road in Week 10 to face the Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) in a game where they develop their momentum and their rookies.
​The Seahawks potentially got the best performance out of first-round pick Jadarian Price in the win over the Cardinals. Price wasn’t a dominant rusher, accounting for 24 yards on nine carries. He was, however, the team’s leading pass-catcher with 54 yards on four receptions . Price is showing he can be one of the team’s most dynamic and reliable offensive playmakers.
​The only other rookie to play in Week 9 was cornerback Avery Smith , who played six special teams reps. He played three special teams reps against the Bears and eight in the 20-3 Week 7 home win over the Kansas City Chiefs. He has yet to play a defensive snap this season, but he is building experience by being on the field.
​The Seahawks elevated defensive tackle Deven Eastern off the practice squad to fill in for depth. Seattle was without veteran defensive tackles Leonard Williams and Brandon Pili and could still be without them. Eastern remains a serious option as a rotational player if the Seahawks need some fresh legs.
​Guard Beau Stephens remains on the 53-man roster and ready to fill in as one of the top backup interior offensive linemen. The Seahawks chose to release Christian Hayne following the trade of Quenton Nelson and, now he is recovering from minor surgery. Stephens possesses the experience and the potential to be a starting guard, but he needs time to be developed.
​Cornerback Julian Neal remains on IR as he recovers from a severe hamstring injury. It is not known if he will be back soon or at all this season. There are only five rookies on their practice squad after the front office released Gary Smith III and moved up Eastern to the active roster.
Wide receiver Emmanuel Henderson Jr., cornerback Michael Dansby and cornerback Andre Fuller are the remaining players who the Seahawks drafted and are still on the practice squad. Edge rusher Aidan Hubbard and recently added defensive tackle Cole Brevard are the two undrafted rookies on the practice squad.
​One player who would easily help the Seahawks’ draft class is second-round pick in safety Bud Clark. It’s hard to know where Clark would fully fit into the Seahawks’ defense this season with Julian Love and Ty Okada playing great at safety, Nick Emmanwori playing at a Pro-Bowl level, and the cornerbacks being solid. Clark would likely be an alternate at multiple position groups, but he will have to wait until the offseason due to his season-ending broken ankle injury.

title: Six Players the Seahawks Should Note from College Football Week 10
full_text:
Throughout the College Football Season, we’ll be monitoring top performers who might be available to the Seattle Seahawks in the 2027 draft. We’ll focus on players that play positions that are likely, or at least possibly, going to be one the team considers going after. This should give us a chance to spotlight players that the team targets well ahead of time.
One of the biggest games of the season so far featured a memorable quarterback battle between two top prospects in Darian Mensah and CJ Carr. Carr got the win, and he also had the superior statline, although both players have plenty to be proud of after a game like that. Carr’s 29/40 for 319 yards and 3 touchdowns against a good defense will go a long way.
After seeing minimal action in some recent weeks due to injury, Frazier took the field for the Bulldogs and got back to doing what he does. It was 16 carries for 107 yards, showcasing the elite speed that he brings to the table. I want some straight line speed in this backfield, and no one will bring it better than Frazier, so sign me up next April.
The Elijah Arroyo experiment has gone terribly so far for the Seahawks, and it’s time to start thinking about trying again. Carter has the athletic, big play ability, along with some YAC skills, to be the receiving threat this team wants to pair with AJ Barner. Carter had 4 catches and 1 drop this last week, but went for 81 yards and 2 touchdowns.
The Kansas Jayhawks aren’t known for football most of the time, but they’ve got a real fun EDGE prospect to monitor. You could call this last week a breakout for him, as he recorded 6 tackles and 3 sacks, forcing a fumble and generating a total of 9 pressures. He’s not among the elite prospects in this draft, but he joins a deep group of interesting options.
The Kentucky-Tennessee game was another massive tilt in a weekend full of them, but it was quickly a one-sided affair. One of the reasons why was the play of Arion Carter, a low-key linebacker prospect who went crazy on Saturday. 13 tackles, 4 of them behind the line of scrimmage with 2 sacks, 5 pressures, and 13 coverage yards allowed. Very clean.
It wasn’t my favorite week for safeties, but Bolden did his thing for the Bulldogs as they rolled over the Rebels. 3 tackles and an interception, while allowing just 5 yards in coverage on a single target. Sometimes a safety is doing his job just by staying clean and not letting anything get past him. Look for Bolden to be a first round pick, and maybe not a low one.

title: Why The Seahawks Should Pursue Former All-Pro Wide Receiver
full_text:
If you’ve been following the NFL over the last couple of years, you’re probably at least somewhat familiar with the Brandon Aiyuk drama in San Francisco. I won’t get into the entire saga, but what’s important is where things stand right now. Aiyuk is forcing the 49ers to either pay him or release him, and they’re expected to release him soon.
Once the 49ers do this, there is expected to be a market for his services. Since the trade deadline has passed, this is the last chance teams will have to acquire a notable talent at the position. Past him, you’re stuck buying lottery tickets with guys like Odell Beckham Jr or Tyreek Hill coming off a massive injury. Expect there to be a line of teams.
At the front of that line will likely be the Los Angeles Rams, who are down Puka Nacua for at least four games and Davante Adams for a bit longer. Their top receiver as of this moment might be Tutu Atwell, which is untenable. So before we go any further in this conversation, keep in mind that if the Seahawks don’t get involved, there’s a good chance the Rams get him.
So, that’s reason number one. But there are others. Before the trade deadline, it was reported that the Seahawks wanted to add a wide receiver . Assuming they meant for the immediate term, to bolster their chances of winning right now, and not for 2027 and beyond when Cooper Kupp retires, Aiyuk could work for that. Let’s remember how good he was previously.
He made the All-Pro team in 2023, with nearly 1,350 yards as the top option on a 49ers team that nearly won the super bowl. He’s a former first round pick, who has been productive every year he was healthy and engaged. He mostly plays on the outside, which is a good fit on this team that already has slots. And after the way things went in San Fran, he’ll be cheap.
The reasons to stay away are relatively clear. While he does come from the Kyle Shanahan offense in San Francisco, he’d have to learn this offense on the fly in a couple of months. He last played football in 2024, a season cut short by injury, and he’s been persona non grata in San Fran for much of the time since. And there’s no getting around his eccentricities.
In his defense, I’ll say that his beef is clearly with the 49ers front office specifically. His teammates seem happy with him, and there’s reason to believe the team has painted him in a poor light. But there’s no denying his recent actions indicate he’s not all there. So there’s something of a risk here. But all you’re asking is him to keep it together for a few months.

title: Seahawks Injury Report Has Great News For Multiple Key Starters
full_text:
It’s time for the first injury report of the week courtesy of the Seattle Seahawks and Las Vegas Raiders. Obviously, the Seahawks are in a fairly injured state , and the fanbase is eager to see at least some of those players start going in the right direction so they can play again. We won’t get everything we want today, but we definitely got a few things we needed.
A.J. Barner (finger) was added to the report, quite possibly from the touchdown ‘catch’ last week, but is a full participant regardless. The highlight of the day is definitely Rashid Shaheed (knee) getting to full status, after not practicing at all last week . It’s a strong indication that he’ll be on the field this Sunday, to help an offense that could really use his downfield speed.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Jarran Reed both sat for non-injury reasons. That’s the easy stuff. The pool of limited players includes Anthony Bradford (knee), Derick Hall (back) , Drew Lock (right elbow, oblique), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), and Connor O’Toole (foot). Offhand, I would expect all five of those players to play on Sunday, but any injury is noteworthy.
Nwosu’s return to practice is particularly significant, as he attempted a similar timeline last week with a limited practice on Wednesday before getting banished back to DNP the next two days. Hopefully this time, whatever setback or occurrence caused him to hit the bench doesn’t happen and he’s able to progress. The other injuries strike me as management ones.
Finally, Charles Cross (ankle), Sam Darnold (ribs, quadricep), Quenton Nelson (knee), Brandon Pili (back), and Leonard Williams (stinger) were the DNPs of the day. Pili and Williams apparently did some light work before practice, so progress is being made and they still have a chance this week. I would assume the first three, however, are waiting for after the bye week.
The Raiders have been among the healthiest teams in the NFL this year, and they’re currently sitting quite pretty in terms of possible absences this weekend. The team had only four players listed on their report, and one of them was a full participant. That player, Ian Thomas (ankle), is a third string tight end who sees only occasional snaps.
Thomas Booker (ankle) and Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, back) are limited today, and that’s not an insignificant one-two, since they combine to be a significant chunk of the Raiders’ interior defensive line. Trey Zuhn (concussion) was also limited, the backup center who has gotten little action so far this year. Otherwise, the Raiders look quite healthy and ready to roll.

title: Seahawks Standing Pat At Trade Deadline is Good News for Rashid Shaheed
full_text:
Personally, I think the Seattle Seahawks sitting the trade deadline out was probably the right thing to do. I wouldn’t have objected to a move (although I would have objected to some), but I’m just not convinced a player acquisition moves the needle right now. Some may disagree, which I can certainly understand. But consider the implication of standing pat.
Per reports leading into the deadline , the Seahawks were believed to be on the lookout for a wide receiver. Whether those reports were accurate is debatable, but it’s fairly believable. Once you get past the great Jaxon Smith-Njigba, things aren’t great in the receiver room. The report even directly said they wanted a wide receiver to complement JSN.
Cooper Kupp is too old to get much done on the field, Tory Horton isn’t ready for a bigger role, and Montorie Foster Jr is a fun training camp story that hasn’t shown up in games yet. Yet still, the Seahawks did not make a trade. Perhaps they simply couldn’t find a deal worth making, but also consider the one Seattle wide receiver I didn’t mention in this section yet.
Rashid Shaheed injured his knee a couple weeks ago against the Kansas City Chiefs and has been absent from the field on gameday since. When the report about the Seahawks wanting a wide receiver came out, it was a reasonable assumption that the injury was serious. Given that the team was willing to come up empty-handed, perhaps that’s not the case.
Perhaps the desire to acquire a wide receiver was more about the long-term. Maybe they wanted someone young and promising who could spend the rest of this season acclimating themselves to the team, and then be able to slide right in to take Kupp’s job in 2027. A good idea, but not something so dire that it absolutely had to get done right this moment.
If this read is correct, then Rashid Shaheed should be back soon. As in, after the bye week at the latest. And once he gets back, he’ll be able to play effective football. Good enough to suffice as this offense tries to find itself on the back half of the season. Despite his low production thus far, Shaheed remains a great speed threat with excellent hands.
To my eyes, Shaheed is getting open and doing his job, he’s just not getting the ball very often due to JSN getting all the targets. He’s also not exactly a clean fit for this offense right now, with much of his value coming as a deep threat and this offense rarely pushing it down the field . Hopefully, when he gets back on the field, that changes.
